1	# Raycast integration — reference
2	
3	How `translate` plugs into [Raycast](https://raycast.com), the options we
4	weighed, how the shipped integration works, and how it compares to existing
5	translation extensions. This is present-tense reference reading; the actual code
6	lives in [`../raycast/`](../raycast/), and store-publishing is tracked in
7	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
8	
9	**Core principle: reuse the binary, don't reimplement.** Every tier below shells
10	out to the existing `translate` CLI (`--json`) and renders the result. No
11	translation, engine, or dictionary logic is duplicated in TypeScript/bash.
12	
13	## Integration tiers
14	
15	Raycast offers four ways to surface functionality. We ship the middle two.
16	
17	| Tier | Reuses binary? | Effort | Selection → translate | Persisted defaults | Rich UI / history | Streaming | Distribution |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **Quick Link** | ✗ (can't exec) | 5 min | via deeplink only | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | launcher only |
20	| **Script Command** (bash) — *shipped* | ✓ | ~0.5 h | ✗ (needs `pbpaste`) | ✗ (no prefs) | ✗ (plain text) | only `fullOutput` | Add Script Directory |
21	| **TS Extension** (`@raycast/api`) — *shipped* | ✓ | 1–2 d | ✓ `getSelectedText()` | ✓ preferences | ✓ List/Detail/Actions | ✓ (manual `spawn`) | `npm run dev` / store |
22	| **AI Extension** (tools) | ✓ | +0.5 d | AI-orchestrated | — | AI Chat | `AI.ask` | store; **Pro-gated** |
23	
24	- **Quick Links** open a URL/file/app/`raycast://` deeplink — they have no
25	  shell-exec surface, so they can't run the CLI directly. Useful only as a hotkey
26	  that deeplinks into a real command.
27	- **AI Extensions** expose "tools" the Raycast AI can call. Feasible (a tool file
28	  can `execFile` the binary and return its `--json`), but the AI API requires
29	  **Raycast Pro**, so it's an additive Pro-only layer — deferred.
30	
31	## How Raycast extensions work
32	
33	- **Manifest** (`package.json`): a `commands[]` array; each command has a
34	  required `mode`:
35	  - `view` — default-exports a React (TSX) component (our `Translate`).
36	  - `no-view` — default-exports an async function; runs and exits, no UI
37	    (our `Translate Selection` → `getSelectedText` → `Clipboard.paste` + `showHUD`).
38	  - `menu-bar` — a persistent `MenuBarExtra` (not used yet).
39	- **Running the binary:** extensions run in a Node runtime, so `child_process`
40	  works. We use `execFile` (typed wrapper in
41	  [`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
42	  rather than the `useExec` hook, because `useExec` buffers with a 10 s default
43	  timeout that LLM engines exceed (and its `timeout: 0` is coerced back to 10000).
44	  The CLI's **`--stream` flag** forces token streaming even when stdout is piped
45	  (which Raycast always is; without it the CLI treats non-TTY as buffered). A
46	  streaming `Detail` view can spawn `translate … --stream` and append `stdout`
47	  chunks into React state bound to `Detail.markdown`. Caveat: visible progressive
48	  output depends on the provider — ollama streams; **copilot-proxy currently buffers
49	  its claude `/v1/messages` responses**, so the result appears after first-token
50	  latency. The default live view uses `--json` (buffered, structured), which returns
51	  fast enough.
52	- **Preferences** (`getPreferenceValues()`): persisted per-extension settings —
53	  our `binaryPath`, `defaultTarget`, `engine`, `tier`.
54	- **Input/UI:** `getSelectedText()` (frontmost app's selection),
55	  `Clipboard.copy/paste`, `Action.CopyToClipboard`/`Action.Paste`; `List` +
56	  `List.Dropdown` (searchBarAccessory, `storeValue` to remember the last target);
57	  `Detail`/`List.Item.Detail` with `.Metadata` for structured fields; `showHUD`/
58	  `showToast` for feedback.
59	- **Tooling:** the `ray` CLI (ships in the extension's dev deps). `ray develop`
60	  (`npm run dev`) registers the extension with the running Raycast app and
61	  hot-reloads; **it persists in root search after you stop dev** — no store
62	  publish needed for personal use. `ray build`/`ray lint` type-check and lint.
63	
64	## Gotchas (learned the hard way)
65	
66	- **launchd PATH:** Raycast launches under launchd and does *not* inherit your
67	  shell PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `ENOENT` / `command not found`.
68	  Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path (preference first, then probe
69	  `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`). Always test
70	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
71	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
72	- **HOME / config, not shell env:** the CLI reads providers/keys from
73	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, *not* environment variables. A key exported
74	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd — put it in the config (`translate init`).
75	  We pass `HOME` through so the CLI finds its config.
76	- **Exit code is 0 even on engine failure** (auto-fallback), so we read
77	  `warnings[]` from `--json` rather than branching on exit codes. The extension
78	  surfaces warnings in the Detail pane / HUD; the plain-text scripts don't.
79	- **Extension icons must be a real PNG** (512×512) — emoji icons work only for
80	  Script Commands. `ray build`/`lint` complains otherwise.
81	- **A preference `default` only applies when no value is stored.** Changing a
82	  `default` in `package.json` does *not* reach an install that has already
83	  materialized that preference — Raycast keeps the stored value, and the new
84	  default is inert. Symptom: a behaviour you "fixed" in the manifest persists. See
85	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md).
86	  Corollary: read preferences through the generated `Preferences.<Command>` type,
87	  not a hand-written interface — the generated one makes the field required, so a
88	  code default that drifts from the manifest becomes a compile error.
89	- **The extension runs the *installed* binary, not your working tree.**
90	  `resolveBinary()` probes `~/.local/bin` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` → `/usr/local/bin`
91	  → `~/go/bin`, so `just raycast-dev` alone never picks up a CLI change. When a
92	  change spans both, the loop is `just check && just install && just raycast-dev`.
93	  Worse, an old binary fails *silently*: `translate` takes free text as its first
94	  argument, so an unknown subcommand gets translated and exits 0
95	  (`translate models` → "n. 模型…"). Never probe capability by exit status. See
96	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md).
97	- **The search bar refuses a long paste** ("The text you are trying to paste is
98	  too long"). That guard is in the Raycast app binary, not `@raycast/api`, so it
99	  can't be raised or caught, and it applies to every search-bar command. Long
100	  text needs a `Form.TextArea` — that is what the `translate-text` command is.
101	  Behind it, argv caps at `ARG_MAX` (1 MiB), so `src/lib/translate.ts` pipes to
102	  stdin above 128 KB. See
103	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md).
104	- **Command arguments are static manifest data** and can't be populated at
105	  runtime, so a language argument is necessarily a hand-synced subset. In-view
106	  `List.Dropdown`s can call `translate lang list --json` for the full table.
107	
108	## Competitive landscape (2026)
109	
110	The Raycast translation category is crowded, but the field is almost entirely
111	remote-API/cloud-LLM wrappers configured via extension preferences.
112	
113	| Extension | Backend | Streaming | TTS | History | Offline dict |
114	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
115	| gebeto/translate (Google) | Google web (keyless) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
116	| tisfeng/Easydict | 10 remote providers + Apple `say`/Shortcuts | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ (remote) |
117	| douo/openai-translator | multi-LLM incl. Ollama / custom endpoint | ✓ | ✗ (roadmap) | ✓ | ✗ |
118	| deepcast / itranslate | DeepL / multi (BYO API key) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
119	| Raycast built-in Translate | unstated | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (Pro-gated) |
120	
121	**What `translate` does that they don't:**
122	
123	- **Shells out to a dedicated local translator CLI** — no surveyed extension
124	  wraps a standalone translator binary (Easydict shells to `osascript`/Apple
125	  Shortcuts; none to a CLI like this).
126	- **Automatic multi-engine failover** — competitors that support multiple engines
127	  do *parallel aggregation*, not "try A, on failure fall back to B".
128	- **Offline CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries** via `translate define` — all
129	  competitors' dictionaries are remote.
130	- **Unified, searchable history** (`translate history [search]`).
131	- **Free local TTS** (`--speak`) — note openai-translator lists TTS as an
132	  unshipped roadmap item, so this is a real gap.
133	- **Fuzzy language resolution** (`translate lang resolve`, `chinees → zh`).
134	
135	Frame differentiation as **offline-resilient + auto-fallback + unified history**,
136	*not* "local LLM" (openai-translator already reaches Ollama) and *not* "study
137	modes" (Anki / Vocabulary Builder already exist in the store).
138	
139	## How ours is built
140	
141	- **Script Commands** — [`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/):
142	  `translate-text` (dropdown language + text, `fullOutput`), `translate-and-copy`
143	  (`silent`, copies; blank arg → clipboard), `define-word`. Install:
144	  `just raycast-scripts`, then add the directory in Raycast once.
145	- **TS extension** — [`../raycast/extension/`](../raycast/extension/): commands
146	  `translate` (view: type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
147	  Copy/Paste/Speak, typo "did you mean?" suggestions, opt-in selection prefill),
148	  `translate-selection` (no-view:
149	  grabs the selection/clipboard and opens Translate prefilled via `launchCommand` —
150	  editable, not blind-paste), `define` (view: dictionary lookup +
151	  LLM fallback + "did you mean" suggestions), `look-up-word` (view: the Define
152	  Word-style picker, below), `translate-text` (view: a `Form.TextArea` for
153	  passages the search bar refuses, below), and `history` (view: browse/search
154	  past translations). All share `src/lib/translate.ts` (binary resolve + typed
155	  `execFile` wrappers mirroring `internal/engine/engine.go`'s `TranslateResult`).
156	  Run: `just raycast-dev` (`build`/`lint` variants exist). Live translate is
157	  debounced + abortable to avoid an LLM call per keystroke, with an opt-in `⌘↵`
158	  streaming view (`spawnTranslateStream` → `translate … --stream` → live `Detail`).
159	  Typo suggestions reuse the engine's fuzzy `suggestions[]` (a shared
160	  `did-you-mean.tsx` component) — no CLI change; single-word lookups route to the
161	  offline dict, full sentences to the LLM which corrects implicitly. Default target,
162	  live-debounce, and tier are inherited from the CLI config (`config show --json`)
163	  when the matching Raycast preference is empty, so `config.toml` is the single
164	  source of truth (a Raycast preference overrides it).
165	
166	### `look-up-word` — the Define Word-style picker
167	
168	Modeled on Raycast's built-in **Define Word**: an empty search bar lists recent
169	history; typing shows ranked headword candidates with definition previews;
170	`⏎` pushes a full-page `Detail`.
171	
172	Three rules shape it, and each is worth preserving:
173	
174	1. **Typing is local-only.** The list is backed by `translate dict search --json`,
175	   which reads the dictionary databases and nothing else (~30 ms). An LLM call per
176	   keystroke would take ~6 s and be unusable, so the LLM fallback is deferred to
177	   `⏎` — either on a fuzzy candidate or on the explicit *Ask the LLM* row that
178	   appears when no local headword matched.
179	2. **Only `⏎` writes history.** `dict search` opens no history store at all, so the
180	   typing path *cannot* record; `DefineDetail` calls `define` without
181	   `--no-history`, so opening a word remembers it. The old `define` command passes
182	   `--no-history` because it looks up on every keystroke.
183	3. **Language is pickable before and after opening.** A command *argument*
184	   dropdown appears in the Raycast root bar; an in-view `List.Dropdown` (populated
185	   from `translate lang list --json`) changes it later. Both only steer the LLM
186	   fallback — the offline tiers are script-fixed (ECDICT en→zh, CC-CEDICT zh→en) —
187	   and the Detail metadata says so rather than letting the choice look ignored.
188	
189	`define` is kept alongside it, unchanged, so the two UXes can be compared.
190	New components: `lib/define-detail.tsx` (full-page definition, the only history
191	writer), `lib/history-detail.tsx` (a stored record as a page — no re-run, instant),
192	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx`. `lib/did-you-mean.tsx` is deliberately *not* reused
193	here: its `⏎` re-runs the search, whereas in this list `⏎` must define.
194	
195	### `translate-text` — the long-passage escape hatch
196	
197	Every other command takes its input in the search bar, which Raycast caps: a long
198	paste is refused outright, and the extension never even sees it. This command is a
199	`Form.TextArea` plus target/engine dropdowns; submitting pushes the same full-page
200	`Detail` (`lib/translation-detail.tsx`), with `⌘↵` for the streaming view.
201	
202	Nothing is prefilled — *Load Selection* (`⌘⇧S`) and *Load Clipboard* (`⌘⇧V`) are
203	explicit actions, keeping the lesson from `e87db06` that auto-grabbing input on
204	open is surprising. `⌘⇧A` reveals **Engine** and **Model**; both stay hidden by
205	default so the common case is two fields.
206	
207	The Model list comes from `translate models --json` — the models the configured
208	providers *declare*, one per tier. Deliberately not a live `/v1/models` probe:
209	copilot-proxy advertises ids it then refuses to serve, so a probed list would
210	offer choices that fail at request time. Picking a model also selects its
211	provider, since `llama3.2:3b` belongs to ollama regardless of chain order.
212	
213	Past 128 KB of UTF-8, `src/lib/translate.ts` stops putting the text in argv and
214	pipes it to stdin (`execWithStdin`), because macOS caps a whole argument list at
215	`ARG_MAX` = 1 MiB. The CLI already reads stdin when given no text argument, so
216	this needed no CLI change. The provider is the real ceiling long before either
217	limit: Google puts the text in a GET query string and fails around 180 KB.
218	
219	Result metadata (engine · model · direction) is a dim footer line at the end of
220	the markdown rather than a `Detail.Metadata` sidebar: the sidebar is a permanent
221	third of the window, which is a lot of width to spend on five short labels when
222	the whole point of the view is reading room.
223	
224	### Target language: the **Auto** entry
225	
226	Both target dropdowns (`translate`, `translate-text`) lead with
227	`Auto — <home> ⇄ <away>`, the dropdown equivalent of the TUI's `^g`. It is not
228	cosmetic:
229	
230	With `[general] pair = true` the CLI reroutes home-language input to `pair_with`
231	regardless of `--to`, so before this the dropdown was quietly lying — picking
232	"Chinese (Traditional)" and pasting Chinese returned *English*. Making the mode
233	explicit lets a concrete choice mean what it says: the extension now sends
234	`--no-pair` whenever a specific language is picked, and no `--to` at all for Auto.
235	`--no-pair` had to be added to the CLI for this; there was previously no way to
236	turn pair off for one run.
237	
238	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx` reads the pair from `config show --json`, so the entry
239	is labelled with the real codes and is omitted when no `pair_with` is configured.
240	
241	## Publishing & distribution
242	
243	The journey from local development to the store, and why we default to
244	local/personal for now.
245	
246	### Three distribution paths
247	
248	| Path | Review | Audience | How | Our stance |
249	|---|---|---|---|---|
250	| **Local dev** | none | just you | `just raycast-dev` (`ray develop`) — persists in root search after you stop dev | **current default** |
251	| **Private / org store** | none (org-gated) | your Raycast org | set `owner` in package.json → `npm run publish`; needs Raycast Pro/Team | option if sharing to a team |
252	| **Public store** | **human review** | everyone | `npm run publish` opens a PR to `raycast/extensions` → CI + Raycast-team review → merge auto-publishes | deferred → [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md) |
253	
254	### It is *not* like PyPI
255	
256	PyPI is self-service: register + `twine upload`, published instantly, no review.
257	The Raycast **public** store is curated — closer to Homebrew core:
258	
259	- `npm run publish` (= `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`) **authenticates with
260	  GitHub** and auto-opens a pull request into `github.com/raycast/extensions`.
261	- Automated CI checks run, then the **Raycast team reviews** and "request[s] changes
262	  when required"; on merge it auto-publishes. Turnaround is days, not seconds.
263	- Auth is **GitHub** (for the PR). Your **Raycast account** only supplies the
264	  validated `author` handle (ours: `da-wei_lee`).
265	
266	### Public-store requirements (checklist)
267	
268	Verified against developers.raycast.com. `✓` = done in this repo.
269	
270	- `✓` `author` = registered Raycast username; `license: "MIT"`; ≥1 category;
271	  one-sentence description; `platforms`; `package-lock.json`; `npm run build` +
272	  `ray lint` clean.
273	- `✓` **512×512 PNG icon** that reads in light + dark (not the default Raycast icon).
274	- `✓` **`CHANGELOG.md`** at the extension root (h2 headers; `{PR_MERGE_DATE}` placeholder).
275	- `✓` **`README.md`** at the extension root (setup/onboarding; media under a top-level
276	  `media/` folder).
277	- `☐` **≥3 (max 6) screenshots at 2000×1250 PNG** — captured from the *running*
278	  extension (a GUI step; not scriptable here).
279	- `☐` `npm run publish` (GitHub auth) + choose public vs private.
280	
281	### The binary-dependency hurdle
282	
283	The store guideline *"Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads"* is exactly
284	our case — the extension needs a user-installed `translate` (brew / `go install`).
285	"Calling known system binaries" is allowed, but a custom go-install CLI is a gray
286	area reviewers may push back on. Mitigations already in place:
287	
288	- Extension `README.md` documents the dependency + install commands.
289	- A graceful **binary-not-found onboarding** view (`src/lib/binary-not-found.tsx`) with
290	  copyable install commands + a jump to preferences — instead of a bare error.
291	- We do **not** bundle the ~22 MB Go binary (store discourages "heavy" binaries;
292	  shipping release binaries is a separate item — `backlog/release-binaries.md`).
293	
294	This friction is why the public store is deferred and local/private is the current
295	path; the analysis lives in [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
296

302	- Script Commands: https://github.com/raycast/script-commands
303	- Prepare / Publish / Teams: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store
304

# Pueue on this machine — evidence-backed inventory

Everything below was run read-only. **No task was added, killed, removed, cleaned, reset, or paused.** Where a fact could only be established by mutating state, I say so and cite the upstream v4.0.4 source instead.

---

## 1. Installation

```
$ which -a pueue pueued
/usr/local/bin/pueue
/usr/local/bin/pueued

$ pueue --version   → pueue 4.0.4
$ pueued --version  → pueued 4.0.4
```

Install method: **Homebrew** (Intel prefix `/usr/local`, not `/opt/homebrew` — this is an x86_64 Homebrew, confirmed by `.crates2.json`: `"target":"x86_64-apple-darwin"`).

```
/usr/local/bin/pueue  -> ../Cellar/pueue/4.0.4/bin/pueue
/usr/local/bin/pueued -> ../Cellar/pueue/4.0.4/bin/pueued
```

- `brew list pueue` → 16 files under `/usr/local/Cellar/pueue/4.0.4/` (binaries, `homebrew.mxcl.pueue.plist`, CHANGELOG.md, completions).
- Other bin dirs checked and **empty of pueue**: `/opt/homebrew/bin` (doesn't apply), `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`. No cargo install.
- Completions installed: `/usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_pueue`, `/usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/pueue`, plus a fish one in the Cellar. No man page (`man -w pueue` → "No manual entry").
- Useful local file: `/usr/local/Cellar/pueue/4.0.4/CHANGELOG.md` (contains the full 4.0.0 breaking-change writeup).

**Absolute path to hardcode/probe: `/usr/local/bin/pueue`** (note: `/opt/homebrew/bin/pueue` does *not* exist here, so an extension must probe both).

## 2. Daemon

Running, launched by **launchd via `brew services`**:

```
$ pgrep -fl pueued
3337 /usr/local/opt/pueue/bin/pueued --verbose

$ launchctl list | grep -i pueue
3337	0	homebrew.mxcl.pueue

$ brew services list | grep pueue

## 3. Command surface (pueue 4.0.4)

Top-level: `add, remove, switch, stash, enqueue, start, restart, pause, kill, send, edit, env, group, status, log, follow, wait, clean, reset, shutdown, parallel, completions, help`. There is **no `remote` subcommand**; shell completion generation is `completions` (not `complete`).

Global options: `-v/--verbose...`, `--color <auto|never|always>`, `-c/--config <CONFIG>` (or `$PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH`), `-p/--profile`, `-h`, `-V`. **Default subcommand when none given is `status`** (source: `pueue/src/bin/pueue.rs`).

Only **three** commands take `--json` (confirmed both in help and in `pueue.rs`'s `show_version_warning` match arms): `status`, `log`, `group`.

| Command | Flags that matter |
|---|---|
| `status` | `[QUERY]...` (DSL, see below), `-j/--json`, `-g/--group <GROUP>` |
| `log` | `[TASK_IDS]...`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--all`, `-j/--json`, `-l/--lines <N>`, `-f/--full` |
| `group` | `-j/--json`; subcommands `add`, `remove` |
| `add` | `-w/--working-directory`, `-e/--escape`, `-i/--immediate`, `--follow`, `-s/--stashed`, `-d/--delay`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--after <id>...`, `-o/--priority <N>`, `-l/--label`, `-p/--print-task-id` |
| `follow` | `[TASK_ID]`, `-l/--lines <N>` |
| `wait` | `[TASK_IDS]...`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--all`, `-q/--quiet`, `-s/--status <done\|success\|queued\|running>` |
| `restart` | `-a/--all-failed`, `-g/--failed-in-group`, `-k/--immediate`, `-s/--stashed`, `-i/--in-place`, `--not-in-place`, `-e/--edit` |
| `clean` | `-s/--successful-only`, `-g/--group` |
| `kill` | `[TASK_IDS]...`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--all`, `-s/--signal` |
| `pause` | `[TASK_IDS]...`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--all`, `-w/--wait` |
| `start` | `[TASK_IDS]...`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--all` |
| `stash` / `enqueue` | `[TASK_IDS]...`, `-g/--group`, `-a/--all`, `-d/--delay` |
| `remove` | `<TASK_IDS>...` (required; running/paused must be killed first) |
| `switch` | `<TASK_ID_1> <TASK_ID_2>` |
| `send` | `<TASK_ID> <INPUT>` |
| `edit` | `[TASK_IDS]...` — opens `$EDITOR`; `client.edit_mode` is `toml` here (single TOML file with `id/command/path/priority/label`) |
| `env` | `set`, `unset` |
| `parallel` | `[PARALLEL_TASKS]`, `-g/--group` (0 = unlimited) |
| `reset` | `-g/--groups`, `-f/--force` |
| `shutdown` | none |
| `completions` | `<bash\|elvish\|fish\|power-shell\|zsh\|nushell> [OUT_DIR]` |

`--delay` accepts seconds (`3600s`), durations (`3h`, `1week`), or date expressions (`2020-04-01T18:30:00`, `wednesday 10:30pm`, `4/1`).

### `status` QUERY DSL (server-side filtering, works together with `--json`)
```
[columns=[col,...]]?  [filter]*  [order_by col asc|desc]?  [first|last N]?
columns: id|status|command|label|path|enqueue_at|dependencies|start|end
filter columns: status|command|label|start|end|enqueue_at
ops: =  !=  <  >  %=   (%= means "contains")
status values accepted: queued|stashed|paused|running|success|failed
```
Verified: `pueue status --json 'status=Success last 5'` → exit 0; `pueue status --json 'status=Nope'` → exit 1 with a pest parse error listing the accepted status tokens.

## 4. JSON shapes

### Current live output (the queue is EMPTY right now — 0 tasks)

```
$ pueue status --json
{"tasks":{},"groups":{"default":{"status":"Running","parallel_tasks":1}}}

$ pueue group --json
{"default":{"status":"Running","parallel_tasks":1}}

$ pueue log --json            → {}
$ pueue log --json --lines 5  → {}
```

Output is **one line of compact JSON on stdout, terminated by `\n`** (verified with `od -c`: `...parallel_tasks":1}}}\n`). `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/state.json` matches exactly, so the daemon persists the same struct.

**Because there are no tasks I could not show a real task object without mutating state.** The shapes below are derived from the exact v4.0.4 sources (`pueue_lib/src/task.rs`, `state.rs`, `pueue/src/client/commands/state/mod.rs`, `commands/log/json.rs`), which serialize with plain serde (externally-tagged enums, chrono `DateTime<Local>` → RFC 3339 with offset). They are corroborated by a local, independently written reference doc observed on pueue 4.0.2 at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/json-schema.md` — same major version, and the CHANGELOG shows no state-format changes between 4.0.2 and 4.0.4.

### `pueue status --json` top level
```jsonc
{
  "tasks":  { "<id>": <Task> },   // BTreeMap<usize, Task> → keys are STRINGS ("0","1",...)
  "groups": { "<name>": { "status": "Running"|"Paused"|"Reset", "parallel_tasks": <int> } }
}
```
`parallel_tasks: 0` = unlimited. `GroupStatus` is a **plain string enum** — `"Running" | "Paused" | "Reset"` (`pueue_lib/src/state.rs`).

`pueue group --json` emits **just the inner map** (`{"<name>": {...}}`), not `{"groups": ...}` — different from `status`.

### The `Task` object — all fields (`pueue_lib/src/task.rs`, v4.0.4)
```rust
pub struct Task {
    pub id: usize,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Local>,
    pub original_command: String,
    pub command: String,
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub envs: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub group: String,
    pub dependencies: Vec<usize>,
    pub priority: i32,
    pub label: Option<String>,
    pub status: TaskStatus,
}
```
→ JSON keys, in order: `id` (int), `created_at` (string), `original_command`, `command`, `path` (string), `envs` (object), `group` (string, `"default"` if unset), `dependencies` (int array, `[]` if none), `priority` (int, `0` default), `label` (string **or null**), `status` (tagged object).

Notes:
- **`envs` is a full snapshot of the submitting shell's environment**, included verbatim in `status --json`. This is the single biggest payload concern for a polling client — a few hundred tasks × a full env is the reason upstream added `daemon.compress_state_file` ("~2MB state for 400 tasks"). It may also contain secrets.
- `id` appears **both** as the map key (string) and inside the object (number).
- There is **no top-level `start`/`end`/`enqueue_at`/`result`/`exit_code` field** on `Task` in v4 — they were moved *into* the status enum in 4.0.0 ("Breaking: Refactor internal task state… moved into the `TaskStatus` enum"). Any v3-era example you find with `"status":"Done","result":"Success","exit_code":0` at the top level is **wrong for this version**.

### `status` encoding — nested tagged enum, NOT a flat string
`TaskStatus` is a Rust struct-enum with default (externally tagged) serde:

```jsonc
{"Stashed": {"enqueue_at": null}}
{"Stashed": {"enqueue_at": "2026-04-27T11:01:06.893055+08:00"}}   // delayed via --delay
{"Queued":  {"enqueued_at": "2026-04-27T11:01:06.893055+08:00"}}
{"Running": {"enqueued_at": "...", "start": "..."}}
{"Paused":  {"enqueued_at": "...", "start": "..."}}
{"Locked":  {"previous_status": { ...another TaskStatus object... }}}   // recursive!
{"Done":    {"enqueued_at": "...", "start": "...", "end": "...", "result": <TaskResult>}}
```

`TaskResult` is *also* externally tagged, mixing bare strings and objects:

| JSON | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"Success"` | exit 0 |
| `{"Failed": 1}` | non-zero exit; int is the exit code (`Failed(i32)`) |
| `{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error string>"}` | couldn't spawn (bad cwd, typo'd binary) |
| `"Killed"` | `pueue kill`, or daemon shutdown |
| `"Errored"` | internal IO error |
| `"DependencyFailed"` | an `--after` parent failed; task never ran |

So a client must handle *four* shapes: bare string status keys don't exist at all — always `Object.keys(status)[0]` for the variant, and `typeof result === "string" ? result : Object.keys(result)[0]`. Treat **anything terminal that isn't `"Success"` as failure** (allowlist, not denylist) — `FailedToSpawn` and `Errored` are easy to miss.

Timestamps: chrono `DateTime<Local>` → **RFC 3339 with microseconds and a numeric local offset**, e.g. `2026-04-27T11:01:06.893055+08:00` (not `Z`, not epoch). `enqueue_at` (Stashed) vs `enqueued_at` (everything else) — **note the one-letter difference; this is a real footgun.** Only `Done` has `end`; `Queued`/`Stashed` have no `start`.

### `pueue log --json`
```jsonc
{
  "<id>": {
    "task":   { ...same Task object... },
    "output": "<string>"
  }
}
```
Source: `pueue/src/client/commands/log/json.rs` defines `struct TaskLog { task: Task, output: String }` over a `BTreeMap<usize, TaskLog>`.

Two important behaviors from that file:
1. **`task.envs = HashMap::new()` is applied before serializing** — so `log --json` returns `"envs": {}` while `status --json` returns the full env. (Asymmetry worth knowing.)
2. When `client.read_local_logs: true` (the case here), the client **reads the log file from disk itself** and does not ask the daemon to ship bytes; when false it decompresses snappy frames sent by the daemon.

Line count: `--full` → whole file; `--lines N` → last N; **neither given → last 15 lines** (`fn determine_log_line_amount` returns `Some(15)`). This applies to `--json` too. Help text warns: "the json cannot be streamed! … using `--full` can use all of your machine's RAM."

`pueue log <nonexistent-id> --json` → `{}` with **exit 0** (verified).

### `--group` + `--json` interaction
`pueue status --json -g <group>` **does** filter `tasks` (the group is folded into the query filter: `apply_filters` → `.filter(|task| task.group == *group)`), but the `groups` map in the payload is **not** filtered — you still get every group. Verified against a nonexistent group name: exit 0, full state returned, no error about the unknown group (the "group doesn't exist" error only fires on the human table path).

### Non-JSON structured output
`pueue add -p/--print-task-id` prints only the integer id on stdout — the cheapest machine-readable "add" path. Otherwise it prints `New task added (id N).` (+ `It will be enqueued at <time>` for delayed, + `The group of this task is currently paused!`). The daemon-side struct is `AddedTaskResponse { task_id, enqueue_at, group_is_paused }` but that is CBOR-on-the-wire, not exposed as JSON.

## 6. Runtime / behavior facts

**Exit codes** — measured:

| Invocation | Exit |
|---|---|
| `pueue status --json` (daemon up) | 0 |
| `pueue group --json` | 0 |
| `pueue log 99999` / `pueue log 99999 --json` | **0** (prints `There are no finished tasks for your specified ids` to stderr / `{}` to stdout) |
| `pueue status --json 'status=Nope'` (bad query) | 1 |
| `pueue -c /nonexistent/pueue.yml status --json` | 1 |
| `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH=/nope/pueue.yml pueue status` | 1 |
| `pueue follow 99999` | 1 |

Convention: **0 = ok, 1 = everything else.** There are no distinct codes. Sources of the `1`: `color_eyre` bubbling out of `main` (prints an `Error:` block with `0:`/`1:` cause chain, a `Location:` line, and a backtrace hint), or an explicit `std::process::exit(1)` in `handle_response` on a `Response::Failure` / in `follow`. Also relevant: `pueue wait --status success` calls `std::process::exit(1)` the moment any watched task fails.

**Surprising:** `pueue parallel` with no argument prints `ERROR pueue::client::commands: Received unhandled response message` to stderr and **still exits 0**. It is not a usable "read current parallelism" command — use `pueue group --json` for that.

**Daemon-not-running** — I did **not** stop the daemon (that would mutate state and interrupt a service the user has running), and there is no way to simulate it without writing a throwaway config file. From `pueue_lib/src/network/socket/unix.rs` + `pueue/src/bin/pueue.rs`, the exact behavior is:
```
Error:
   0: Failed to initialize client.
   1: I/O error at path "/Users/david/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue_david.socket" \
      while connecting to daemon. Did you start it?:
      No such file or directory (os error 2)
```
on **stderr**, stdout empty, **exit 1** (`color_eyre` from `main`). Two distinct failure modes to detect:
- config file missing entirely → `bail!("Couldn't find a configuration file. Did you start the daemon yet?")` — this fires *before* any connection attempt.
- config present, socket gone/refused → the `connecting to daemon. Did you start it?` message above (`ECONNREFUSED` if the socket file exists but nothing listens, `ENOENT` if the file is gone).
There is **no `--json` error envelope** — errors are always human-formatted prose on stderr. A client must branch on exit code, not parse stdout.

**ANSI on stderr — surprising and worth planning for:** `color_eyre` error blocks are emitted **with ANSI escapes even when stderr is a pipe**, and neither `--color never` nor `NO_COLOR=1` suppresses them (verified via `| cat -v` for all three cases: `^[[91mFailed to read configuration.^[[0m`). Meanwhile normal stdout output correctly drops color when not a TTY. So: strip ANSI from any stderr you surface to the user.

**Speed** — 20 sequential `pueue status --json` runs against the empty queue (process spawn included):
```
min 22.1 ms   median 28.1 ms   max 44.0 ms
```
(`/usr/bin/time -p` rounds this to `real 0.01–0.02`.) That is process startup dominated; expect it to grow with `envs` payload size once tasks exist.

**No push/subscribe for state.** The wire protocol has a streaming response (`Response::Stream`) but it is used **only** for log following. Concretely:
- `pueue wait` **polls**: `loop { get_state(client); ...; sleep(2000ms) }` — a fixed **2 s** interval (250 ms only if `PUEUED_TEST_ENV_VARIABLE` is set). It re-requests the *entire* `State` each tick, diffs statuses in the client, and prints human-readable transition lines to stdout unless `-q`. It exits when all watched tasks hit the target status. So `wait` is a long-running process, but it is not a push subscription — and its stdout is prose, not JSON.
- `pueue follow` **does stream stdout continuously** (tail -f semantics), but for log text only, never for state. Two implementations: with `client.read_local_logs: true` (this machine), `local_follow` opens the log file directly and `io::copy`s new bytes to stdout every **250 ms**, re-asking the daemon whether the task is still running every **500 ms**; it exits when the task stops, prints `Pueue: Log file has gone away. Has the task been removed?` if the file vanishes, and `Pueue: The task to be followed doesn't exist.` + exit 1 for a bad id (verified). With `read_local_logs: false` it uses a real daemon-pushed `StreamRequest`/`Response::Stream` loop until `Response::Close`.
- `pueue add --immediate --follow` combines both, printing the "New task added" line to **stderr** so stdout stays pure log.

Net: **a client must poll `pueue status --json`** (or watch `state.json` / the `task_logs/` dir for mtime changes as a cheaper trigger — the daemon persists `state.json` on every change).

## 7. Log output

- Human: `pueue log <ids>` — last **15** lines per task by default; `--lines N`; `--full` for everything; `-g/--group`, `-a/--all` to select sets. Prints a header table per task plus the output.
- JSON: the output **is embedded** in `pueue log --json` as `.["<id>"].output` (a single string, stdout and stderr interleaved). It is *not* in `pueue status --json` at all — status explicitly excludes output ("This does not include the output of tasks. Use `log -j` if you want everything").
- On disk: **`{pueue_directory}/task_logs/{task_id}.log`**, i.e. here `/Users/david/Library/Application Support/pueue/task_logs/<id>.log`. From `pueue_lib/src/log.rs`: `get_log_path()` = `pueue_dir.join("task_logs").join(format!("{task_id}.log"))`, and `create_log_file_handles` returns **two handles to the same file** for stdout and stderr — so stdout and stderr are **merged into one plain-text file, uncompressed, unstructured**, with no timestamps or stream markers. Snappy compression is applied only in-flight when shipping logs to a *remote* client; local files are raw.
- **This directory is currently empty** — no task has produced a log since the last clean/reset, so I have no on-disk sample to show.
- Because `client.read_local_logs: true`, a Raycast extension can read `task_logs/<id>.log` directly and skip the daemon entirely for log display (that is exactly what `pueue log --json` and `pueue follow` do here). Log files are deleted with the task (`clean_log_handles` on remove/clean), and `restart --in-place` overwrites them.

## Things worth flagging

1. **No tasks exist right now** (`tasks: {}`, `task_logs/` empty, `state.json` 73 bytes). Every task-object claim above is from the v4.0.4 Rust source, not from live output.
2. **v4 moved timestamps and results inside the status enum.** Nested tagged enums, two levels deep (`status.Done.result.Failed`), plus a recursive `Locked.previous_status`. Any v3 documentation or example you find will mislead you.
3. **`enqueue_at` (Stashed) vs `enqueued_at` (all others)** — different spellings for near-identical concepts.
4. **`envs` (full environment snapshot) is in `status --json` but blanked in `log --json`.** Payload size and secret-leak implications for a polling UI.
5. **Homebrew here is `/usr/local`, not `/opt/homebrew`** — an Apple-Silicon-assuming path constant would break on this machine.
6. **Config lives in `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/`, not `~/.config/pueue/`** on macOS, and that same directory doubles as the data dir, socket dir, and log dir.
7. **`pueue log <bad id>` exits 0**, but `pueue follow <bad id>` exits 1. Exit codes are 0/1 only, with no structured error output — and stderr carries unsuppressable ANSI codes.
8. **`pueue parallel` with no args is broken** (logs "Received unhandled response message", exits 0).
9. **No watch/subscribe API.** `wait` polls every 2 s and emits prose; `follow` streams log text only. Polling `status --json` (~25 ms) or watching `state.json` mtime are the only options.
10. **`pueue status --json --group X` filters tasks but not the returned `groups` map**, and silently returns success for a group that doesn't exist.
```

## 3. `src/lib/translate.ts` — the shell-out layer

612 lines. This is the file to adapt most directly. Architecture: one module owning binary resolution + one exported `runX()` per CLI subcommand, each returning a typed interface that mirrors the Go struct's JSON tags.

### Binary resolution — probe + cache + preference-first

```ts
const PROBE_DIRS = [
  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
  "/opt/homebrew/bin",
  "/usr/local/bin",
  join(homedir(), "go", "bin"),
];

let cachedBin: string | undefined;

/**
 * Resolve an ABSOLUTE path to the translate binary. Raycast runs under launchd
 * with a restricted PATH that does not inherit the shell rc, so a bare
 * `translate` throws ENOENT — we probe known install dirs (preference first).
 */
export function resolveBinary(): string {
  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
  if (prefs.binaryPath && existsSync(prefs.binaryPath)) return prefs.binaryPath;
  if (cachedBin) return cachedBin;
  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
    const candidate = join(dir, "translate");
    if (existsSync(candidate)) {
      cachedBin = candidate;
      return candidate;
    }
  }
  throw new Error(
    "translate CLI not found. Set the binary path in extension preferences, or install it (just install / brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate).",
  );
}

/** True when an error came from resolveBinary failing to locate the CLI. */
export function isBinaryMissing(e: unknown): boolean {
  return e instanceof Error && e.message.startsWith("translate CLI not found");
}
```

Key points: the preference is checked **before** the cache (so changing it takes effect immediately), `existsSync` validates the preference (a bad path falls through to the probe), the cache is module-level so it lives for one command run only. Errors are identified by **message prefix** — `isBinaryMissing()` is the string-sniffing predicate every command uses to route to `<BinaryNotFound />`. Same pattern for `isNoDictEntry()`.

### execFile wrapping and env

```ts
const pexecFile = promisify(execFile);

function baseEnv(): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
  // Ensure the CLI can locate its config.toml (providers/API keys) under launchd.
  return { ...process.env, HOME: process.env.HOME ?? homedir() };
}
```

`baseEnv()` is passed to **every** spawn/exec. Note it does **not** touch `PATH` — the absolute path from `resolveBinary()` makes PATH irrelevant. The only fixup is `HOME`, so the CLI finds `~/.config/translate/config.toml`.

Every call site is a thin async wrapper over `pexecFile(bin, args, { timeout, maxBuffer, env: baseEnv(), signal })` followed by `JSON.parse(stdout)`. Representative shapes:

| Function | args | timeout | maxBuffer | cached | abortable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runTranslate` | `[text, --to, --json, …]` | scaled (see below) | 16 MB | no | yes |
| `runDefine` | `["define", word, "--json", …]` | 60 s | 16 MB | no | yes |
| `runDictSearch` | `["dict","search",q,"--limit",N,"--json"]` | 10 s | 8 MB | no | yes |
| `runHistory` | `["history","--json","--limit",N]` or `["history","search",q,"--json"]` | 30 s | 32 MB | no | yes |
| `runLangs` | `["lang","list","--json"]` | 10 s | 1 MB | **yes** | no |
| `runModels` | `["models","--json"]` | 10 s | 1 MB | **yes** | no |
| `readConfig` | `["config","show","--json"]` | 10 s | 4 MB | **yes** | no |
| `speak`/`speakText` | fire-and-forget raw `execFile` with empty callback | none | — | no | no |

The three cached ones use a module-level `let cachedX` and are lazily populated once per command run. Two of them (`runModels`, `runLangs`) **swallow all errors and return a fallback** so an older installed binary degrades rather than crashes:

```ts
export async function runLangs(): Promise<LangInfo[]> {
  if (cachedLangs) return cachedLangs;
  try {
    const bin = resolveBinary();
    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["lang", "list", "--json"], {
      timeout: 10_000, maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024, env: baseEnv(),
    });
    const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as LangInfo[];
    if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.length > 0) {
      cachedLangs = parsed;
      return cachedLangs;
    }
  } catch {
    /* older CLI or no binary — fall through to the static list */
  }
  cachedLangs = LANGS.map((l) => ({ code: l.value, name: l.title }));
  return cachedLangs;
}
```

### Timeout handling — scaled to input size

```ts
/**
 * How long to let a translation run, scaled to the input.
 *
 * A document-sized translation legitimately takes minutes — measured against
 * copilot-proxy: 10 KB of prose took 61 s, 20 KB took 96 s. A flat 60 s killed
 * exactly the long inputs Translate Text exists for. ~10 ms per character with a
 * 1-minute floor and a 10-minute ceiling (matching the CLI's own backstop).
 */
function requestTimeout(text: string): number {
  return Math.min(600_000, Math.max(60_000, text.length * 10));
}
```

The documented reason `useExec` is **not** used at all (`docs/raycast-extension.md`): *"`useExec` buffers with a 10 s default timeout that LLM engines exceed (and its `timeout: 0` is coerced back to 10000)."* For `pueue` most calls are sub-second, so a flat short timeout is likely fine — but the pattern of a named `requestTimeout()` helper is worth keeping.

### stdin fallback for large input

```ts
/**
 * Above this many UTF-8 bytes, text goes to the CLI on stdin instead of argv.
 *
 * macOS caps a whole argument list at ARG_MAX (1 MiB) and fails the spawn with
 * E2BIG — measured: 900 KB via argv works, 1.1 MB is "argument list too long".
 * The CLI reads stdin when it gets no text argument, and the pipe has no such
 * limit, so long documents take that route. The threshold leaves plenty of room
 * for multi-byte text (a CJK character is 3 bytes).
 */
const ARGV_SAFE_BYTES = 128 * 1024;

function needsStdin(text: string): boolean {
  return Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8") > ARGV_SAFE_BYTES;
}

/**
 * Run the CLI with `input` written to stdin and no text argument, resolving with
 * stdout. Mirrors pexecFile's rejection shape (message + `stderr`) so callers
 * can keep inspecting stderr the same way.
 */
function execWithStdin(
  bin: string,
  args: string[],
  input: string,
  opts: { timeout?: number; signal?: AbortSignal } = {},
): Promise<string> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
    let out = "";
    let err = "";
    let settled = false;

    const finish = (fn: () => void) => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      opts.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
      fn();
    };
    const kill = (reason: string) =>
      finish(() => {
        if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
        reject(Object.assign(new Error(reason), { stderr: err }));
      });
    const onAbort = () => kill("aborted");
    const timer = opts.timeout
      ? setTimeout(() => kill(`timed out after ${opts.timeout}ms`), opts.timeout)
      : (undefined as unknown as NodeJS.Timeout);

    opts.signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });

    child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
    child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
    child.stdout?.on("data", (d: string) => (out += d));
    child.stderr?.on("data", (d: string) => (err += d));
    child.on("error", (e) =>
      finish(() => reject(Object.assign(e, { stderr: err }))),
    );
    child.on("close", (code) =>
      finish(() =>
        code === 0
          ? resolve(out)
          : reject(
              Object.assign(new Error(`translate exited ${code}: ${err.trim()}`), {
                stderr: err,
              }),
            ),
      ),
    );

    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
      /* the child may exit before we finish writing — the close handler reports it */
    });
    child.stdin?.end(input, "utf8");
  });
}
```

The `settled` guard + `finish()` wrapper is the reusable bit: it makes the promise idempotent across the timeout/abort/error/close races and always clears the timer and removes the abort listener. Rejections deliberately carry `.stderr` so callers can sniff it the same way they do for `pexecFile` rejections.

### The main runner, showing arg assembly + the two exec paths

```ts
export async function runTranslate(
  text: string,
  opts: TranslateOptions = {},
): Promise<TranslateResult> {
  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
  const bin = resolveBinary();
  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, prefs.defaultTarget);
  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
  // With no text argument the CLI reads stdin, which sidesteps ARG_MAX.
  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
  args.push("--json");
  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
  const engine = opts.engine ?? prefs.engine;
  if (engine) args.push("--engine", engine);
  const tier = opts.tier ?? prefs.tier;
  if (tier) args.push("--tier", tier);
  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");

  const timeout = requestTimeout(text);
  if (viaStdin) {
    const stdout = await execWithStdin(bin, args, text, { timeout, signal: opts.signal });
    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
  }
  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
    timeout, // LLM engines routinely exceed useExec's 10s default
    maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
    env: baseEnv(),
    signal: opts.signal, // cancel a superseded call when the user keeps typing
  });
  return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
}
```

Note the `opts.X ?? prefs.X` precedence pattern (explicit call option beats preference) repeated per flag.

### Error handling — tagged domain errors from stderr

```ts
const NO_DICT_ENTRY = "no dictionary entry";

export async function runDefine(word: string, opts: DefineOptions = {}): Promise<TranslateResult> {
  const bin = resolveBinary();
  const args = ["define", word, "--json"];
  if (opts.smart) args.push("--smart");
  if (opts.to) args.push("--to", opts.to);
  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");
  try {
    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
      timeout: 60_000, maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024, env: baseEnv(), signal: opts.signal,
    });
    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
  } catch (e) {
    const stderr = String((e as { stderr?: string }).stderr ?? "");
    if (stderr.includes(NO_DICT_ENTRY)) {
      throw new Error(`${NO_DICT_ENTRY}: ${word}`);
    }
    throw e;
  }
}

/** True when `define` exited on a hard dictionary miss (no JSON was emitted). */
export function isNoDictEntry(e: unknown): boolean {
  return e instanceof Error && e.message.startsWith(NO_DICT_ENTRY);
}
```

There is **no** central error-toast helper (`showFailureToast` from `@raycast/utils` is not used anywhere). Errors propagate through `usePromise`'s `error` and each view renders them itself via `List.EmptyView` or markdown.

### Fire-and-forget helper

```ts
export function speakText(text: string, lang?: string): void {
  const bin = resolveBinary();
  const args = ["speak", text];
  if (lang) args.push("--lang", lang);
  execFile(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() }, () => {
    /* ignore — best-effort audio */
  });
}
```

Directly relevant to `pueue`: this is the right shape for side-effecting commands (`pueue start`/`pause`/`kill`), except you'd want to surface failures rather than swallow them.

### Streaming spawn helper

```ts
export interface StreamHandlers {
  onData: (chunk: string) => void;
  onDone: (code: number | null) => void;
  onError: (err: Error) => void;
}

export function spawnTranslateStream(
  text: string,
  opts: TranslateOptions,
  h: StreamHandlers,
): () => void {
  const bin = resolveBinary();
  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, undefined);
  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
  args.push("--stream", "--no-history");
  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
  if (opts.engine) args.push("--engine", opts.engine);
  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
  if (opts.tier) args.push("--tier", opts.tier);
  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);

  const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
  child.stdout?.on("data", (d: Buffer | string) => h.onData(d.toString()));
  child.on("close", (code) => h.onDone(code));
  child.on("error", (err) => h.onError(err));
  if (viaStdin) {
    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
      /* reported via the close/error handlers above */
    });
    child.stdin?.end(text, "utf8");
  }
  return () => {
    if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
  };
}
```

**Returns a cancel function** — the consumer (`stream-view.tsx`) returns it straight from `useEffect` as the cleanup. This maps perfectly onto `pueue follow` / `pueue log --follow` for live task output.

## 4. `src/lib/binary-not-found.tsx` — verbatim

```tsx
import {
  ActionPanel,
  Action,
  Icon,
  List,
  openExtensionPreferences,
} from "@raycast/api";

const INSTALL_BREW = "brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate";
const INSTALL_GO = "go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest";

/**
 * Actionable empty state shown when the `translate` binary can't be found — instead
 * of a bare error. Offers copyable install commands and a jump to preferences (to
 * set a custom binary path). Raycast runs under a restricted PATH, so the binary
 * living at ~/.local/bin etc. isn't on the extension's PATH — hence the probe/preference.
 */
export function BinaryNotFound() {
  return (
    <List.EmptyView
      icon={Icon.Download}
      title="translate CLI not found"
      description="Install the translate binary, then reopen. If it lives in a non-standard location, set its path in preferences."
      actions={
        <ActionPanel>
          <Action.CopyToClipboard
            title="Copy Homebrew Install Command"
            content={INSTALL_BREW}
          />
          <Action.CopyToClipboard
            title="Copy Go Install Command"
            content={INSTALL_GO}
          />
          <Action
            title="Open Extension Preferences"
            icon={Icon.Gear}
            onAction={openExtensionPreferences}
          />
          <Action.OpenInBrowser
            title="Open the Homebrew Tap"
            url="https://github.com/daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap"
          />
        </ActionPanel>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

Important structural constraint: it returns a bare `<List.EmptyView>`, so it must be rendered **inside** a `<List>`. Two call conventions exist in the codebase — inline as a child of the command's own `<List>` (translate/define/history), or wrapped in a fresh minimal one with an early return (look-up-word):

```tsx
if (error && isBinaryMissing(error)) {
  return (
    <List>
      <BinaryNotFound />
    </List>
  );
}
```

There's no `Detail` equivalent component; `translation-detail.tsx` and `define-detail.tsx` each duplicate a small `errorMarkdown()` that hand-rolls the same message as markdown. That duplication is a wart worth fixing in the new extension.

## 5. Command entry points

**Confirmed: no command uses `mode: "menu-bar"` and `MenuBarExtra` appears nowhere.** `grep -rn "MenuBarExtra\|menu-bar\|menubar"` across all `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.json` (excluding node_modules) returned zero hits. Modes used: 5 × `view`, 1 × `no-view`. `docs/raycast-extension.md` mentions `menu-bar` only to say "(not used yet)".

Also confirmed: **`useExec` is never used** (only mentioned in a comment); **`useCachedPromise`, `useFetch`, `useForm`, `useLocalStorage`, `showFailureToast` are never used**. The only `@raycast/utils` import anywhere is `usePromise`.

### `src/translate.tsx` — `mode: view`, the flagship
- **Components**: `List` with `searchText`/`onSearchTextChange` (controlled search bar), `isShowingDetail={!!data?.translation}`, `searchBarAccessory={<LanguageDropdown/>}`, one `List.Item` with `List.Item.Detail` (markdown + `.Metadata`), `List.EmptyView` for each of 4 states.
- **Data**: `usePromise(fn, [debouncedText, to, engine], { abortable })` where `abortable = useRef<AbortController>()`. Returns `undefined` early for empty input.
- **Loading**: `isLoading={isLoading || pending}` where `pending = text.trim().length > 0 && text.trim() !== debouncedText.trim()` — keeps the bar up during the debounce window. This is a nice trick worth copying.
- **States**: error → `isBinaryMissing(error) ? <BinaryNotFound/> : <List.EmptyView icon={Icon.Warning}/>`; no data → intro EmptyView; suggestions → `<DidYouMean/>`; success → the item; else → "No translation" EmptyView.
- **Launch context**: `LaunchProps<{ launchContext?: { seed?: string; to?: string } }>` — received from `translate-selection`'s `launchCommand`.
- **Shortcuts**: `⌘↵` push StreamView, `⌘I` copy source, `⌘E` engine submenu (`ActionPanel.Submenu` with checkmark icons toggling state).
- **Actions**: `Action.CopyToClipboard`, `Action.Paste`, `Action.Push`, plain `Action` with `onAction` + `showHUD`.

### `src/translate-selection.tsx` — `mode: no-view`
Default-exports an `async function` (not a component). Reads `getSelectedText()` in a try, falls back to `Clipboard.readText()`, then `launchCommand({ name: "translate", type: LaunchType.UserInitiated, context: { seed, to } })` in a try/catch that ends in `showHUD` on failure. 40 lines. This is the canonical no-view pattern.

### `src/translate-text.tsx` — `mode: view`, `Form`-based
- **Components**: `Form` with `Form.TextArea`, `Form.Description` (used as a live char counter *and* as a keyboard-hint line), `Form.Separator`, `Form.Dropdown` × 3 (target always visible; engine + model behind a `showAdvanced` state toggle).
- **Data**: no `usePromise` at the top level. Two `useEffect`s: one loads `runModels()` into state, one does the config-inheritance. Submission pushes a child view via `useNavigation().push(...)` — that child (`TranslationDetail` / `StreamView`) owns the actual async work.
- **Validation**: `if (!trimmed) showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: "Nothing to translate" })` — no `Form.TextArea` `error` prop, no `useForm`.
- **Shortcuts**: `⌘↵` streaming submit, `⌘⇧S` load selection, `⌘⇧V` load clipboard, `⌘⇧X` clear, `⌘⇧A` toggle advanced. Primary action (`Translate`) is unbound (plain `↵`).
- **Degradation**: when `models.length === 0` it renders an explicit `Form.Description` explaining the installed CLI is probably stale, instead of an empty dropdown.

### `src/look-up-word.tsx` — `mode: view`, the richest list
- **Components**: `List` with **multiple `List.Section`s** (Dictionary / Did you mean? / No dictionary match / Dictionary data / Recent), each conditionally rendered with `? … : null`. `searchBarAccessory` dropdown. `accessories={[{ text }]}` and `accessories={[{ tag }]}`.
- **Data**: **two parallel `usePromise` calls** with **separate abort refs** (`searchAbort`, `historyAbort`), errors merged via `const error = search.error ?? history.error`, loading merged via `search.isLoading || history.isLoading || pending`.
- **Adaptive debounce**: 180 ms, or 300 ms when the query matches a CJK regex (`/[\p{Script=Han}\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}\p{Script=Hangul}]/u`) because an IME emits intermediate candidates.
- **Min-query gate**: `MIN_QUERY = 2` — below that it shows history instead of searching.
- **Refresh-after-mutation**: `const onRecorded = () => history.revalidate()` is threaded down into the pushed `DefineDetail`, which calls it from `usePromise`'s `onData` callback. The comment notes Raycast keeps the list mounted underneath so the revalidate lands while the Detail is still open. **This is the exact pattern you want for pueue** (act on a task → refresh the list).
- **Shortcuts**: `⌘↵` use-this-word, `⌘I` copy, `⌘L` look up again, `⌘R` reload.
- A shared `rowActions(c: Candidate)` function returns the `<ActionPanel>` so multiple sections reuse identical actions.

### `src/define.tsx` — `mode: view`, the simple single-result list
Simplest full example: one `useState` search text → 500 ms `useDebouncedValue` → one `usePromise` with abortable → four-branch render. 149 lines. Good template.

### `src/history.tsx` — `mode: view`, static list, no search wiring
- `usePromise` with an **empty dep array** — loads once, exposes `revalidate` bound to `⌘R`.
- Does **not** control `searchText`; instead it feeds Raycast's built-in client-side filtering via `keywords={[h.input, h.output, h.source_lang, h.target_lang, h.engine ?? ""]}` on each `List.Item`. That's the "let Raycast filter" pattern — likely the right call for a pueue task list.
- `isShowingDetail={entries.length > 0}` and per-item `List.Item.Detail` with `.Metadata`.

## 6. Shared UI helpers — generic vs domain-specific

| File | Reusability | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/hooks.ts` | **100% generic** | 11-line `useDebouncedValue<T>`. Copy verbatim. |
| `lib/binary-not-found.tsx` | **Generic shape, translate-specific strings** | Swap the 2 install-command constants, the title/description, and the tap URL. Structure unchanged. |
| `lib/did-you-mean.tsx` | **Generic** | `{ suggestions: string[], onPick: (s) => void }` — a `List.Section` where the first item gets `Icon.Checkmark` + a `"closest"` accessory and the rest get `Icon.MagnifyingGlass`. Nothing translate-specific in the code; only the doc-comment is. Directly reusable for e.g. fuzzy task-label matching. |
| `lib/stream-view.tsx` | **Generic minus one import** | The `useRef` accumulator + `setMd(acc.current)` + `return cancel` from `useEffect` pattern is exactly right for `pueue follow`. Only `spawnTranslateStream` is domain-specific; parameterize it (pass the spawn fn or the args) and the component is fully generic. |
| `lib/history-detail.tsx` | **Mostly generic** | `Detail` + `Detail.Metadata` + copy/paste actions over a plain record; renders **without re-running anything** (instant). Exports three genuinely generic utilities: `oneline(s, n)` (collapse whitespace + ellipsize — used all over `look-up-word.tsx`), `formatTS(ts)` (safe `new Date().toLocaleString()` with fallback), `renderEntry`. The `HistoryEntry` type and the "Look up Again" action are domain-specific. |
| `lib/translation-detail.tsx` | **Reusable skeleton** | Pattern: a pushed `Detail` that owns its own `usePromise`, computes `markdown = error ? errorMarkdown(error) : data ? render(data) : "Translating…"`, and conditionally renders actions only when `data` exists (`{data ? <>…</> : null}` inside `ActionPanel`). Also the deliberate design note: a dim `*a · b · c*` footer line **instead of** a `Detail.Metadata` sidebar, because "the sidebar is a permanent third of the window". |
| `lib/define-detail.tsx` | **Reusable skeleton, domain body** | Same pushed-Detail pattern plus two things worth stealing: (a) the `onRecorded` callback fired from `usePromise`'s `onData` to refresh the parent list; (b) `launchCommand` from within a Detail action to jump to a sibling command with context. The `Metadata` sub-component and `definitionText()` are dictionary-specific. |
| `lib/language-dropdown.tsx` | **Structure generic, content specific** | Three exports. `useLanguages()` is a genuinely reusable "start from a static fallback list so the dropdown never paints empty, then swap in the live list from the CLI" hook. `usePair()`/`autoLabel()` are translate-only. The `LanguageDropdown` component has one subtle, portable trick: |

```tsx
// A value that isn't in the list would silently reset the dropdown, so keep
// whatever the config resolved to (e.g. a code the CLI knows and we don't).
const known =
  props.value === AUTO_TARGET || langs.some((l) => l.code === props.value);
…
{!known && props.value ? (
  <List.Dropdown.Item title={props.value} value={props.value} />
) : null}
```

For pueue the analogue is a **group dropdown** populated from `pueue status --json`'s groups, with the same static-fallback-then-live-swap and unknown-value-preservation.

## 7. Preferences pattern

**Declaration.** Two levels: top-level `preferences[]` (extension-wide, appear in every command) and per-command `commands[].preferences[]`. Types used here: `textfield` (with optional `placeholder`) and `dropdown` (with `default` + `data[]` of `{title, value}`). All are `required: false`.

**Reading.** `ray build`/`ray develop` generates `raycast-env.d.ts` (gitignored) with:
- `type ExtensionPreferences = { … }` — top-level prefs, optional fields for non-required textfields, but **a required union type for a dropdown with a `default`** (`"tier": "" | "default" | "fast" | "max"`).
- `declare namespace Preferences { export type Translate = ExtensionPreferences & { "prefill": "selection" | "clipboard" | "none" } … }` — one PascalCase alias per command.
- `declare namespace Arguments { export type TranslateSelection = { "to": "en" | "zh-TW" | … } … }`

Both namespaces are **globally declared** — no import needed:

```tsx
const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.Translate>();
…
export default function Command(props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.LookUpWord }>) {
```

The hard rule (from `pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`, and repeated in `docs/`, `README.md`, and an inline comment in `translate.tsx`):

> Read preferences through the generated `Preferences.<Command>` type. **Never hand-write a preferences interface** — the hand-written one makes fields optional and re-opens exactly this gap.

The bug it prevents: a hand-written `interface Prefs { prefill?: string }` shadowed the generated type, letting `prefs.prefill ?? "selection"` silently contradict the manifest's `"default": "none"`. With the generated type the field is required, so drift is a compile error.

Note `lib/translate.ts` itself still uses a **hand-written** `interface Prefs { binaryPath?; defaultTarget?; engine?; tier? }` — that's a deliberate exception (a lib module that isn't scoped to one command) but arguably the same trap; in the new extension prefer `Preferences` (the global alias for `ExtensionPreferences`) there.

**The "inherit from CLI config when the preference is empty" mechanism.** Three-tier fallback chain: *command argument → Raycast preference → CLI config → hardcoded default*. Implemented as `useState(initial-from-arg-or-pref)` + a mount-time `useEffect` that patches state from `readConfig()`. Verbatim, from `look-up-word.tsx` (the minimal form):

```tsx
const [to, setTo] = useState(props.arguments?.to || prefs.defaultTarget || "");

useEffect(() => {
  if (to) return;
  readConfig()
    .then((cfg) => {
      if (cfg.general?.default_target) setTo(cfg.general.default_target);
    })
    .catch(() => {
      /* fall back below */
    })
    .finally(() => setTo((t) => t || "en"));
}, []);
```

The `.finally(() => setTo((t) => t || "en"))` is the key detail: a functional update that only fires if nothing else set it, so it covers both the throw path and the "config had no value" path in one line.

And the two-field version from `translate.tsx`, which also inherits the debounce:

```tsx
const prefDebounce = Number(prefs.liveDebounceMs);
const [debounceMs, setDebounceMs] = useState(
  prefDebounce > 0 ? Math.max(250, prefDebounce) : 700,
);
…
// Inherit the default target + debounce from the CLI config (~/.config/translate)
// when the matching Raycast preference is empty. Falls back to "en"/700ms.
useEffect(() => {
  if (to && prefs.liveDebounceMs) return; // nothing to inherit
  readConfig()
    .then((cfg) => {
      if (!to && cfg.general?.default_target) setTo(cfg.general.default_target);
      if (!prefs.liveDebounceMs && cfg.general?.debounce_ms)
        setDebounceMs(Math.max(250, cfg.general.debounce_ms));
    })
    .catch(() => { /* fall back to defaults */ })
    .finally(() => setTo((t) => t || "en"));
}, []);
```

Backed by:

```ts
/** The effective CLI config (subset we care about) from `config show --json`. */
export interface CliConfig {
  general?: { default_target?: string; debounce_ms?: number; /* … */ };
}
let cachedConfig: CliConfig | undefined;

export async function readConfig(): Promise<CliConfig> {
  if (cachedConfig) return cachedConfig;
  const bin = resolveBinary();
  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["config", "show", "--json"], {
    timeout: 10_000, maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024, env: baseEnv(),
  });
  cachedConfig = JSON.parse(stdout) as CliConfig;
  return cachedConfig;
}
```

Note `readConfig` (unlike `runLangs`/`runModels`) does **not** swallow errors — callers `.catch()` individually. For pueue the analogue is `pueue status --json`'s group list / `~/.config/pueue/pueue.yml`, though pueue has no `config show --json`, so you'd likely drop this tier or read the YAML directly.

## 8. Tooling

### Justfile recipes (all four, verbatim)

```make
# make the Raycast script-commands executable + show how to add them
raycast-scripts:
    chmod +x raycast/script-commands/*.sh
    @echo "Add in Raycast → Settings → Extensions → Script Commands → Add Script Directory:"
    @echo "  {{justfile_directory()}}/raycast/script-commands"

# run the TS extension in dev (registers it in Raycast; persists after you stop)
raycast-dev:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run dev

# type-check / build the extension bundle (does NOT install into Raycast)
raycast-build:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run build

# lint the extension with the Raycast eslint config
raycast-lint:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run lint
```

The `([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) &&` idiom makes every recipe self-bootstrapping. The Justfile has no `raycast-fix-lint` even though `package.json` defines `fix-lint`.

### Exact `ray` commands
`ray develop` (registers with the running Raycast app, hot-reloads, **stays installed after you stop dev**), `ray build`, `ray lint`, `ray lint --fix`, `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`. The `ray` binary ships inside `@raycast/api` (it's not in `node_modules/.bin` as a standalone symlink; npm scripts resolve it).

### tsconfig.json — verbatim
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/tsconfig",
  "include": ["src/**/*", "raycast-env.d.ts"],
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["ES2023"],
    "module": "commonjs",
    "target": "ES2022",
    "strict": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "resolveJsonModule": true
  }
}
```
(This is the stock Raycast template tsconfig, unmodified.)

### .eslintrc.json — verbatim
```json
{
  "root": true,
  "extends": ["@raycast"]
}
```

### Prettier
**No prettier config file exists** (`.prettierrc*` / `prettier.config.*` — none found). `prettier@^3.5.3` is a devDependency and `@raycast/eslint-config` wires it via `eslint-config-prettier`; formatting is all defaults (visible in the source: 2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas, 80-col wrap).

### Docs/assets checklist
- `extension/CHANGELOG.md` — **yes**, single `## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}` section with a bulleted per-command summary. The `{PR_MERGE_DATE}` placeholder is the store convention.
- `extension/README.md` — **yes**, 3.7 KB: Requirements (install commands + the launchd/Accessibility caveats in a blockquote), Commands (one bullet each with shortcuts), Preferences (with the stored-default warning).
- `raycast/README.md` — **yes**, a separate track-comparison README one level up.
- `assets/extension-icon.png` — **yes**, verified 512×512 8-bit RGBA PNG, with `extension-icon.svg` kept as source.
- `metadata/` — **no** (the outstanding store blocker).
- `package-lock.json` — **yes**, committed (a store requirement).

## 9. Testing / CI

**None, for the extension.**
- No `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, no `jest.config*`, no `vitest*` anywhere under `raycast/`.
- No `test` script in `extension/package.json`.
- No `.github/` directory at all — **zero GitHub Actions** in the repo.
- The only tests are Go: `just test` → `go test ./cmd/... ./internal/...`.
- `just check` = `fmt vet build` — Go only; it does **not** invoke `raycast-build` or `raycast-lint`.

So the extension's entire quality gate is manual: `just raycast-build` (tsc via `ray build`) + `just raycast-lint`. The release flow in `AGENTS.md` is Go-tag-driven and never mentions the extension.

## 10. Docs worth reading

**Named for raycast:**

| File | One-line summary |
|---|---|
| `docs/raycast-extension.md` (19 KB) | **The one to read first.** Present-tense reference: the four Raycast integration tiers and why two shipped; how manifests/modes/preferences/`ray` work; a "Gotchas (learned the hard way)" section (launchd PATH, HOME-not-env, exit-0-on-failure, PNG icon requirement, stored-preference-defaults, installed-vs-working-tree binary, search-bar paste cap, static command arguments); a competitive-landscape table; a per-command build narrative; and a full "Publishing & distribution" section with the store checklist. |
| `backlog/raycast-extension.md` (4.2 KB) | Status `P?` — research on publishing: local-dev vs private-org vs public store, the "avoid asking users to install external tools" review headwind, what's already in place (registered author `da-wei_lee`, MIT, 512px icon, CHANGELOG, README, binary-not-found view) and what isn't (3–6 screenshots at 2000×1250). Decision: deferred, local/personal is the current path. |
| `pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md` | `spawn translate ENOENT` from Raycast but works in a terminal — Raycast launches under launchd and never sources your shell rc, so PATH lacks `~/.local/bin` etc.; fix is always resolving an absolute path (preference → 4-dir probe), and always testing *from Raycast* because a terminal's PATH masks the bug. |
| `pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md` | New dropdowns come back empty / `unknown flag` after adding CLI surface — `just raycast-dev` rebuilds the *extension*, never the *binary*; the loop must be `just check && just install && just raycast-dev`. Also: never probe capability by exit status (an unknown subcommand got *translated* and exited 0), and degrade visibly rather than showing an empty list. |
| `pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md` | "The text you are trying to paste is too long" — the guard lives in the Raycast **app binary** (proven with `strings`), not `@raycast/api`, so it can't be raised, configured, or even observed; long input needs a `Form.TextArea`. Behind it: `ARG_MAX` 1 MiB on the exec (hence the 128 KB stdin switch) and provider-side limits (~180 KB for Google). |
| `pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md` | A manifest preference `default` change has no effect on an existing install — Raycast persists a value once materialized and a `default` only applies when nothing is stored. Three compounding causes (stored value, stale `ray develop` bundle, a code default contradicting the manifest via a hand-written prefs interface shadowing the generated `Preferences.<Command>`). Also notes `getSelectedText()` falls back to a copy-and-read-pasteboard path, so `"selection"` can look like clipboard prefill. |

**Not named for raycast but heavily raycast-relevant:**

| File | Summary |
|---|---|
| `backlog/look-up-word.md` (6.3 KB) | Status `shipped`. The design record for the `look-up-word` command: why Raycast's built-in Define Word shape needed two new CLI capabilities (prefix headword search with previews; `define` writing history), and the three invariants — typing is local-only, only `⏎` writes history, language pickable before and after. |
| `pitfalls/llm-stream-truncation-silently-rendered-as-complete.md` (9 KB) | The timeout story behind `requestTimeout()` — a flat 60 s whole-request client timeout truncated long translations; the fix scaled the deadline, and "Raycast scales its exec timeout to match". |

| `AGENTS.md` | The project-knowledge-harness contract: `TODO.md` as the single priority/effort index, `backlog/<slug>.md` for `P?`/`[L]`/`[XL]` items, `pitfalls/<slug>.md` titled by *symptom* not root cause, with a verbatim-error "Symptoms (grep this section)" line. Plus the Go release/versioning flow. |

---

## Notes for the pueue port

Things that will differ, based on what I read:

1. **`resolveBinary()` probe dirs** — pueue installs via cargo (`~/.cargo/bin`) and Homebrew (`/opt/homebrew/bin`), so the list changes; and you need **two** binaries (`pueue` client and `pueued` daemon), so either a `resolveBinary(name)` parameter or two cached slots.
2. **Daemon-not-running is a second onboarding state** distinct from binary-not-found — `pueue status` fails when `pueued` isn't up. That warrants a sibling of `binary-not-found.tsx` with a "Start the daemon" `Action` rather than just copy-install-command actions.
3. **Mutating actions** (`start`/`pause`/`kill`/`remove`/`restart`) have no analogue here except the fire-and-forget `speak()`. The reusable half is `look-up-word.tsx`'s `onRecorded → revalidate()` plumbing.
4. **`mode: "menu-bar"` is genuinely unprecedented in this codebase** — there is no `MenuBarExtra` code to copy, and the manifest has no `interval` field anywhere. You'd be writing that from scratch.
5. The **timeout scaling** and the **128 KB stdin fallback** are almost certainly unnecessary for pueue (short JSON in, short JSON out) — but `execWithStdin`'s `settled`/`finish` race-guard is worth keeping for `pueue add` with a long command string.
