```text
Below is a concise extraction of the Menu Bar Commands API and related lifecycle/behavior from the provided page. Verbatim quotations from the source are in quotes (kept under 125 characters each). All other wording is a brief restatement.

High-level
- Purpose: create macOS menu bar extras via the MenuBarExtra React component (menu-bar commands are not available on Windows).
  - Quote: "Menubar commands aren't available on Windows."
- A menu-bar command is configured in package.json with "mode": "menu-bar". Background refresh is enabled by adding an interval (e.g., "interval": "5m").

MenuBarExtra (component)
- What it does: adds an item to the menu bar; returns null to remove the item.
  - Quote: "`menu-bar` commands don't always need to return a `MenuBarExtra`."
- Children: MenuBarExtra.Item, MenuBarExtra.Submenu, MenuBarExtra.Separator, MenuBarExtra.Section.
- Behavior: if children are non-empty, the MenuBarExtra provides a menu.

MenuBarExtra props (key ones called out)
- icon — image shown in the menu bar (Image.ImageLike).
- title — string displayed in the menu bar.
- tooltip — string shown on hover.
- isLoading — boolean that prevents Raycast from unloading the command while async work runs; if used you must set it to false when done.

MenuBarExtra.Item
- Purpose: an item inside a MenuBarExtra or submenu.
- Typical props:
  - title (required for display in lists)
  - icon (optional)
  - subtitle (optional)
  - tooltip (optional)
  - onAction (handler invoked when user clicks the item)
  - shortcut (keyboard shortcut used while parent menu is open)
  - alternate (an alternate MenuBarExtra.Item shown when Option (⌥) is pressed)
- Disabled items: an Item with only title (or title+icon but no onAction) is rendered disabled.
- Alternate limitations (quoted and paraphrased):
  - Quote (short): "The `alternate` item may not have a custom shortcut."
  - Quote (short): "The `alternate` item may not also specify an alternate."
  - Quote (short): "A parent item that provides an `alternate` may not use ⌥ (opt) as a modifier."

MenuBarExtra.Submenu
- Purpose: groups items that reveal children when interacted with.
- Props: title (required), children, icon (optional).
- Submenus with no children render as disabled.

MenuBarExtra.Section
- Purpose: groups related menu items and inserts a separator between sections.
- Props: title (optional), children.

MenuBarExtra.ActionEvent (for onAction handlers)
- Property: type — reports event kind; allowed values are:
  - Quote: `"left-click"` or `"right-click"`

Lifecycle and running behavior (summary)
- Events that can place an item in the menu bar:
  1. From root search: Raycast loads and runs the command; it waits for MenuBarExtra.isLoading to switch to false, then may unload.
     - Important constraint (quoted, shortened): "If your command returns a `MenuBarExtra`, it *must* either not set `isLoading`..."
       - Note: the original continues to explain the required isLoading behavior; the page stresses you must set isLoading to false when async work finishes.
  2. At set interval: when background refresh is configured and active, Raycast runs the command on that schedule; environment.launchType can be used to detect background launches.
     - Quote (short): "environment.launchType"
  3. When user clicks the command's icon/title in the macOS menu bar: Raycast loads the command and keeps it in memory while the menu is open; it unloads when the menu closes or an item is clicked.
  4. When Raycast is restarted: previously placed items are restored from Raycast's database (not by re-running the command).
  5. When the menu-bar command is re-enabled in preferences (behaves like restart).
- Note on background refresh activation: adding an "interval" key to the command object in package.json enables periodic runs (example given: "interval": "5m").

Best practices and constraints
- Use Cache API and Utilities to provide quick feedback and make actions reliable.
- Ensure you set isLoading to false when command finishes.
- Avoid very long titles in MenuBarExtra, Submenu, or Item (keep labels short).
  - Quote (short): "avoid setting long titles in `MenuBarExtra`"
- Do not place identical MenuBarExtra.Item elements at the same level (their onAction handlers may not run correctly).
  - Quote (short): "don't put identical `MenuBarExtra.Item`s at the same level"

Other notes
- macOS ultimately decides whether an extra is shown; many items may cause the OS to hide some icons.
- Development helper: background-run action is exposed in development mode for testing commands configured to run in the background.

Sources (from the provided page)
- The page sections: Getting Started, Lifecycle, Best practices, API Reference (MenuBarExtra, Item, Submenu, Section), Types (ActionEvent).

- Produce short example components for common patterns (simple item, item with action, submenu, background refresh).

```text
Summary — Pueue (v2.0.0)

What it is
- A command-line task manager for running long-lived shell commands, handling a queue for sequential and parallel execution.
- As stated: "Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks."

Key features / concepts
- Queueing and scheduling: add tasks, reorder them, set dependencies, and schedule by time.
- Parallelism & groups: run multiple tasks concurrently; define groups (multiple queues) with independent parallel limits.
- Process interaction: inspect output, send stdin to running tasks, pause/resume, restart, and kill tasks.
- Persistence & background daemon: a background daemon (pueued) persists queue and logs across crashes; commands run in their working directories and inherit environment.
- Simplicity focus: built for interactive single-user use, not as a heavy-duty distributed scheduler. As the README notes, "Pueue is considered feature-complete :tada:."

Installation
- Package manager (preferred when available).
- Prebuilt binaries on the release page (download both pueue and pueued and add to PATH).
- Via cargo: cargo install --locked pueue
- From source: git clone ...; cargo build --release --locked --path ./pueue

Platform notes
- Cross-platform: Linux and macOS are fully supported and battle-tested; Windows is supported as well.
- macOS is explicitly listed as "fully supported and on par with Linux."

JSON and automation
- Several commands support JSON output for integration. Example: status and log can produce JSON; there is also a format-status helper to render JSON tasks.
- Logs are persisted on disk and can be followed (follow) or shown (log). There is a callback hook for notifications.

Docs & links
- Quick start and detailed topics on the project wiki: Get-started, Configuration, Groups, Advanced usage, Connect-to-remote.
- Source, releases, packaging info, badges, and architecture guide available on the GitHub repo.

Notable constraints / out of scope
- Not intended for distributed or multi-user job scheduling, heavy programmatic scheduling, or tight system integration. The README emphasizes keeping the design simple and user-focused.

Short helpful quote (<=125 chars):
- "Simply put, it's a tool that 'p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.'"

Links referenced in the README: GitHub repo, release page, wiki pages (Get-started, Configuration, Groups, Advanced usage, Connect-to-remote), Architecture.md.
```

`for c in status log add follow wait group edit restart clean parallel completions; do echo "########## pueue help $c ##########"; pueue help $c 2>&1; echo; done`

```text
########## pueue help status ##########
Display the current status of all tasks

Usage: pueue status [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...

Arguments:
  [QUERY]...
          Users can specify a custom query to filter for specific values, order by a column
          or limit the amount of tasks listed.
          
          Syntax:
             [column_selection]? [filter]* [order_by]? [limit]?
          
          where:
            - column_selection := `columns=[column]([column],)*`
            - column := `id | status | command | label | path | enqueue_at | dependencies | start |
            end`
            - filter := `[filter_column] [filter_op] [filter_value]`
              (note: not all columns support all operators, see "Filter columns" below.)
            - filter_column := `status | command | label | start | end | enqueue_at`
            - filter_op := `= | != | < | > | %=`
              (`%=` means 'contains', as in the test value is a substring of the column value)
            - order_by := `order_by [column] [order_direction]`
            - order_direction := `asc | desc`
            - limit := `[limit_type]? [limit_count]`
            - limit_type := `first | last`
            - limit_count := a positive integer
          
          Filter columns:
            - `status` supports the operators `=`, `!=`
              against test values that are:
                - strings like `queued`, `stashed`, `paused`, `running`, `success`, `failed`
            - `command`, `label` support the operators `=`, `!=`, `%=`
              against test values that are:
                - strings like `some text`
            - `start`, `end`, `enqueue_at` contain a datetime
              which support the operators `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`
              against test values that are:
                - date like `YYYY-MM-DD`
                - time like `HH:mm:ss` or `HH:mm`
                - datetime like `YYYY-MM-DDHH:mm:ss`
                  (note there is currently no separator between the date and the time)
          
          Examples:
            - `status=running`
            - `command%=echo`
            - `label=mytask`
            - `columns=id,status,command status=running start > 2023-05-2112:03:17 order_by command
            first 5`
          
          The formal syntax is defined here:
          https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/commands/state/query/syntax.pest
          
          More documentation is on the query syntax PR:
          https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/issues/350#issue-1359083118

Options:
  -j, --json
          Print the current state as json to stdout. This does not include the output of tasks. Use
          `log -j` if you want everything

  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Only show tasks of a specific group

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help log ##########
Display the log output of finished tasks.

Only the last few lines will be shown by default. If you want to follow the output of a task, please
use the \"follow\" subcommand.

Usage: pueue log [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          View the task output of these specific tasks

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          View the outputs of this specific group's tasks

  -a, --all
          Show the logs of all groups' tasks

  -j, --json
          Print the resulting tasks and output as json.
          
          By default only the last lines will be returned unless --full is provided. Take care, as
          the json cannot be streamed! If your logs are really huge, using --full can use all of
          your machine's RAM.

  -l, --lines <LINES>
          Only print the last X lines of each task's output.
          
          This is done by default if you're looking at multiple tasks.

  -f, --full
          Show the whole output

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help add ##########
Enqueue a task for execution.

There're many different options when scheduling a task. Check the individual option help texts for
more information. Furthermore, please remember that scheduled commands are executed via your system
shell. This means that the command needs proper shell escaping. The safest way to preserve shell
escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:

pueue add 'ls $HOME && echo \"Some string\"'

Usage: pueue add [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <COMMAND>...
          The command to be added

Options:
  -w, --working-directory <working-directory>
          Specify current working directory

  -e, --escape
          Escape any special shell characters (" ", "&", "!", etc.).
          Beware: This implicitly disables nearly all shell specific syntax ("&&", "&>").

  -i, --immediate
          Immediately start the task

      --follow
          Immediately follow a task, if it's started with --immediate

  -s, --stashed
          Create the task in Stashed state.
          
          Useful to avoid immediate execution if the queue is empty.

  -d, --delay <delay>
          Prevents the task from being enqueued until 'delay' elapses. See "enqueue" for accepted
          formats

  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Assign the task to a group.
          
          Groups kind of act as separate queues. All groups run in parallel and you can specify the
          amount of parallel tasks for each group. If no group is specified, the default group will
          be used.
          
          Create groups via the `pueue group` subcommand

  -a, --after <after>...
          Start the task once all specified tasks have successfully finished.
          
          As soon as one of the dependencies fails, this task will fail as well.

  -o, --priority <PRIORITY>
          Start this task with a higher priority.
          
          The higher the number, the faster it will be processed.

  -l, --label <LABEL>
          Add some information for yourself.
          
          This string will be shown in the "status" table. There's no additional logic connected to
          it.

  -p, --print-task-id
          Only return the task id instead of a text.
          
          This is useful when working with dependencies in scripts.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help follow ##########
Follow the output of a currently running task. This command works like "tail -f"

Usage: pueue follow [OPTIONS] [TASK_ID]

Arguments:
  [TASK_ID]
          The id of the task you want to watch.
          
          If no or multiple tasks are running, you have to specify the id. If only a single task is
          running, you can omit the id.

Options:
  -l, --lines <LINES>
          Only print the last X lines of the output before following

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help wait ##########
Wait until tasks are finished.

By default, this will wait for all tasks in the default group to finish.

Note: This will also wait for all tasks that aren't somehow 'Done'. Includes: [Paused, Stashed,
Locked, Queued, ...]

Usage: pueue wait [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          This allows you to wait for specific tasks to finish

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Wait for all tasks in a specific group

  -a, --all
          Wait for all tasks across all groups and the default group

  -q, --quiet
          Don't show any log output while waiting

  -s, --status <STATUS>
          Wait for tasks to reach a specific task status

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help group ##########
Use this to add or remove groups.

By default, this will simply display all known groups.

Usage: pueue group [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add     Add a group by name
  remove  Remove a group by name. This will move all tasks in this group to the default group!
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -j, --json
          Print the list of groups as json

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help edit ##########
Adjust editable properties of a task.

Only stashed or queued tasks can be edited. A temporary folder folder/file will be opened by your
$EDITOR to edit the tasks.

Usage: pueue edit [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          The ids of all tasks that should be edited

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help restart ##########
Restart failed or successful task(s).

By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place. You
can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.

Usage: pueue restart [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          Restart these specific tasks

Options:
  -a, --all-failed
          Restart all failed tasks across all groups.
          
          This is nice for usage in combination with `-i/--in-place` (or the respective config
          option).

  -g, --failed-in-group <FAILED_IN_GROUP>
          Like `--all-failed`, but only restart tasks failed tasks of a specific group

  -k, --immediate
          Immediately start the tasks, no matter how many open slots there are. This will ignore any
          dependencies tasks may have

  -s, --stashed
          Set the restarted task to a "Stashed" state. Useful to avoid immediate execution

  -i, --in-place
          Restart the task by reusing the already existing tasks. This will overwrite any previous
          logs of the restarted tasks.
          
          This can also be enabled by default via the `restart_in_place` config option.

      --not-in-place
          Restart the task by creating a new identical tasks. Only necessary if you have the
          `restart_in_place` configuration set to true

  -e, --edit
          Edit the task before restarting

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help clean ##########
Remove all finished tasks from the list

Usage: pueue clean [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -s, --successful-only  Only clean tasks that finished successfully
  -g, --group <GROUP>    Only clean tasks of a specific group
  -h, --help             Print help

########## pueue help parallel ##########
Set the amount of allowed parallel tasks

By default, adjusts the amount of the default group.

No tasks will be stopped, if this is lowered. This limit is only considered when tasks are
scheduled.

Usage: pueue parallel [OPTIONS] [PARALLEL_TASKS]

Arguments:
  [PARALLEL_TASKS]
          The amount of allowed parallel tasks.
          
          Setting this to 0 means an unlimited amount of parallel tasks.

Options:
  -g, --group <group>
          Set the amount for a specific group

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

```text
# translate — dev tasks (run `just` to list)

# show available recipes
default:
    @just --list

# build the binary into ./translate
build:
    go build -o translate .

# run: `just run "hola mundo" --to en`  ·  `just run` for the TUI
run *ARGS:
    go run . {{ARGS}}

# launch the interactive TUI
tui:
    go run .

# dictionary lookup: `just define ephemeral`
define WORD:
    go run . define {{WORD}}

# guided config wizard
init:
    go run . init

# gofmt, vet, and build
check: fmt vet build

# format the source tree
fmt:
    gofmt -w cmd internal main.go

# static analysis (scoped to the Go tree; skips raycast/extension/node_modules)
vet:
    go vet . ./cmd/... ./internal/...

# tidy go.mod / go.sum
tidy:
    go mod tidy

# run tests
test:
    go test ./cmd/... ./internal/...

# install into ~/.local/bin (first on PATH; override with DIR=…)
install DIR="~/.local/bin": build
    mkdir -p {{DIR}}
    install -m 0755 translate {{DIR}}/translate

# remove build artifacts
clean:
    rm -f translate

# make the Raycast script-commands executable + show how to add them
raycast-scripts:
    chmod +x raycast/script-commands/*.sh
    @echo "Add in Raycast → Settings → Extensions → Script Commands → Add Script Directory:"
    @echo "  {{justfile_directory()}}/raycast/script-commands"

# run the TS extension in dev (registers it in Raycast; persists after you stop)
raycast-dev:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run dev

# type-check / build the extension bundle (does NOT install into Raycast)
raycast-build:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run build

# lint the extension with the Raycast eslint config
raycast-lint:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run lint

137	export function resolveBinary(): string {
138	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
139	  if (prefs.binaryPath && existsSync(prefs.binaryPath)) return prefs.binaryPath;
140	  if (cachedBin) return cachedBin;
141	  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {

143	    if (existsSync(candidate)) {

168	 * The CLI reads stdin when it gets no text argument, and the pipe has no such
169	 * limit, so long documents take that route. The threshold leaves plenty of room
170	 * for multi-byte text (a CJK character is 3 bytes).

180	 *
181	 * A document-sized translation legitimately takes minutes — measured against
182	 * copilot-proxy: 10 KB of prose took 61 s, 20 KB took 96 s. A flat 60 s killed
183	 * exactly the long inputs Translate Text exists for. ~10 ms per character with a
184	 * 1-minute floor and a 10-minute ceiling (matching the CLI's own backstop).
185	 */
186	function requestTimeout(text: string): number {
187	  return Math.min(600_000, Math.max(60_000, text.length * 10));
188	}
189	
190	/**
191	 * Run the CLI with `input` written to stdin and no text argument, resolving with
192	 * stdout. Mirrors pexecFile's rejection shape (message + `stderr`) so callers
193	 * can keep inspecting stderr the same way.
194	 */
195	function execWithStdin(
196	  bin: string,
197	  args: string[],
198	  input: string,
199	  opts: { timeout?: number; signal?: AbortSignal } = {},
200	): Promise<string> {
201	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
202	    const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
203	    let out = "";
204	    let err = "";
205	    let settled = false;
206	
207	    const finish = (fn: () => void) => {
208	      if (settled) return;
209	      settled = true;
210	      clearTimeout(timer);
211	      opts.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
212	      fn();
213	    };
214	    const kill = (reason: string) =>
215	      finish(() => {
216	        if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
217	        reject(Object.assign(new Error(reason), { stderr: err }));
218	      });
219	    const onAbort = () => kill("aborted");
220	    const timer = opts.timeout
221	      ? setTimeout(
222	          () => kill(`timed out after ${opts.timeout}ms`),
223	          opts.timeout,
224	        )
225	      : (undefined as unknown as NodeJS.Timeout);
226	
227	    opts.signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
228	
229	    child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
230	    child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
231	    child.stdout?.on("data", (d: string) => (out += d));
232	    child.stderr?.on("data", (d: string) => (err += d));
233	    child.on("error", (e) =>
234	      finish(() => reject(Object.assign(e, { stderr: err }))),
235	    );
236	    child.on("close", (code) =>
237	      finish(() =>
238	        code === 0
239	          ? resolve(out)
240	          : reject(
241	              Object.assign(
242	                new Error(`translate exited ${code}: ${err.trim()}`),
243	                {
244	                  stderr: err,
245	                },
246	              ),
247	            ),
248	      ),
249	    );
250	
251	    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
252	      /* the child may exit before we finish writing — the close handler reports it */
253	    });
254	    child.stdin?.end(input, "utf8");
255	  });
256	}
257	
258	export interface TranslateOptions {
259	  to?: string;
260	  from?: string;
261	  engine?: string;
262	  tier?: string;
263	  /** Exact model id, overriding engine/tier selection. */
264	  model?: string;
265	  /**
266	   * Direction. Tri-state on purpose:
267	   *   undefined → leave it to the config ([general] pair)
268	   *   true      → --pair: detect and route between the pair languages
269	   *   false     → --no-pair: always translate into `to`
270	   *
271	   * This matters because [general] pair = true silently overrides --to for
272	   * home-language input, so "translate into X" is only true with --no-pair.
273	   */
274	  pair?: boolean;
275	  noHistory?: boolean;
276	  signal?: AbortSignal;
277	}
278	
279	/**
280	 * Turns a target + pair choice into CLI flags.
281	 *
282	 * AUTO_TARGET means "no --to at all": the CLI's own home target and pair_with
283	 * decide the direction. Anything else falls back to the Raycast preference, and
284	 * finally to nothing (letting the CLI config's default_target apply).
285	 */
286	function directionArgs(
287	  to: string | undefined,
288	  pair: boolean | undefined,
289	  prefTarget: string | undefined,
290	): { to?: string; pair?: boolean } {
291	  if (to === AUTO_TARGET) return { to: undefined, pair: true };
292	  return { to: to || prefTarget || undefined, pair };
293	}
294	
295	export async function runTranslate(
296	  text: string,
297	  opts: TranslateOptions = {},
298	): Promise<TranslateResult> {
299	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
300	  const bin = resolveBinary();
301	  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, prefs.defaultTarget);
302	  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
303	  // With no text argument the CLI reads stdin, which sidesteps ARG_MAX.
304	  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
305	  // In auto/pair mode we deliberately send no --to: the CLI's own home target
306	  // plus [general] pair_with decide the direction.
307	  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
308	  args.push("--json");
309	  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
310	  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
311	  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
312	  const engine = opts.engine ?? prefs.engine;
313	  if (engine) args.push("--engine", engine);
314	  const tier = opts.tier ?? prefs.tier;
315	  if (tier) args.push("--tier", tier);
316	  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
317	  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");
318	
319	  const timeout = requestTimeout(text);
320	  if (viaStdin) {
321	    const stdout = await execWithStdin(bin, args, text, {
322	      timeout,
323	      signal: opts.signal,
324	    });
325	    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
326	  }
327	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
328	    timeout, // LLM engines routinely exceed useExec's 10s default
329	    maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
330	    env: baseEnv(),
331	    signal: opts.signal, // cancel a superseded call when the user keeps typing
332	  });
333	  return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
334	}
335	
336	let cachedModels: ModelInfo[] | undefined;
337	
338	/**
339	 * `translate models --json` — the models the configured providers declare, one
340	 * per tier, cached per command run. Deliberately not a live /v1/models probe:
341	 * copilot-proxy advertises ids it then refuses to serve, so a probed list would
342	 * offer choices that fail at request time. Empty on an older CLI.
343	 */
344	export async function runModels(): Promise<ModelInfo[]> {
345	  if (cachedModels) return cachedModels;
346	  try {
347	    const bin = resolveBinary();
348	    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["models", "--json"], {
349	      timeout: 10_000,
350	      maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,
351	      env: baseEnv(),
352	    });
353	    const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as ModelInfo[];
354	    cachedModels = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [];
355	  } catch {
356	    cachedModels = []; // older CLI without `models`, or no binary
357	  }
358	  return cachedModels;
359	}
360	
361	export interface DefineOptions {
362	  /** Definition language for the LLM fallback. A dictionary hit ignores it — the
363	   *  offline tiers are script-fixed (CC-CEDICT zh→en, ECDICT en→zh). */
364	  to?: string;
365	  /** Force smart-dict, i.e. fall back to the LLM when the dictionary misses. */
366	  smart?: boolean;
367	  /** Suppress the history row. Browsing must not record; opening a word should. */
368	  noHistory?: boolean;
369	  signal?: AbortSignal;
370	}
371	
372	const NO_DICT_ENTRY = "no dictionary entry";
373	
374	/**
375	 * `translate define <word> --json`. The top-level payload is a TranslateResult
376	 * whose `.dictionary` holds the entry (on a dict hit); on a miss it falls back
377	 * to an LLM definition in `.translation` with a `warnings[]` note.
378	 *
379	 * A *hard* miss (the plain dictionary with no LLM fallback and nothing close
380	 * enough to suggest) exits 1 with a bare stderr line and no JSON at all — that
381	 * is re-thrown as a tagged error so callers can render it as "no entry" rather
382	 * than as a crash. See isNoDictEntry.
383	 *
384	 * Unless noHistory is set this writes a history row, which is what makes
385	 * "opening a word remembers it" true.
386	 */
387	export async function runDefine(
388	  word: string,
389	  opts: DefineOptions = {},
390	): Promise<TranslateResult> {
391	  const bin = resolveBinary();
392	  const args = ["define", word, "--json"];
393	  if (opts.smart) args.push("--smart");
394	  if (opts.to) args.push("--to", opts.to);
395	  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");
396	  try {
397	    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
398	      timeout: 60_000,
399	      maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
400	      env: baseEnv(),
401	      signal: opts.signal,
402	    });
403	    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
404	  } catch (e) {
405	    const stderr = String((e as { stderr?: string }).stderr ?? "");
406	    if (stderr.includes(NO_DICT_ENTRY)) {
407	      throw new Error(`${NO_DICT_ENTRY}: ${word}`);
408	    }
409	    throw e;
410	  }
411	}
412	
413	/** True when `define` exited on a hard dictionary miss (no JSON was emitted). */
414	export function isNoDictEntry(e: unknown): boolean {
415	  return e instanceof Error && e.message.startsWith(NO_DICT_ENTRY);
416	}
417	
418	/**
419	 * `translate dict search <q> --limit N --json` — ranked headword candidates with
420	 * one-line definition previews.
421	 *
422	 * Local data only: no network, no LLM, single-digit milliseconds on an indexed
423	 * dictionary. That is the point — it is safe to run on every keystroke, and the
424	 * expensive LLM fallback is deferred to the moment a word is actually opened.
425	 * It also opens no history store, so typing can never pollute history.
426	 *
427	 * Finding nothing is not an error: `candidates` comes back empty and exit is 0.
428	 */
429	export async function runDictSearch(
430	  q: string,
431	  limit = 12,
432	  signal?: AbortSignal,
433	): Promise<DictSearchResult> {
434	  const bin = resolveBinary();
435	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(
436	    bin,
437	    ["dict", "search", q, "--limit", String(limit), "--json"],
438	    {
439	      timeout: 10_000,
440	      maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
441	      env: baseEnv(),
442	      signal,
443	    },
444	  );
445	  const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as DictSearchResult;
446	  return { ...parsed, candidates: parsed.candidates ?? [] };
447	}
448	
449	let cachedLangs: LangInfo[] | undefined;
450	
451	/**
452	 * `translate lang list --json` — the CLI's full language table (35 entries),
453	 * cached per command run. Falls back to the hardcoded LANGS subset when the
454	 * installed binary predates the subcommand, so an older CLI still works.
455	 */
456	export async function runLangs(): Promise<LangInfo[]> {
457	  if (cachedLangs) return cachedLangs;
458	  try {
459	    const bin = resolveBinary();
460	    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["lang", "list", "--json"], {
461	      timeout: 10_000,
462	      maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,
463	      env: baseEnv(),
464	    });
465	    const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as LangInfo[];
466	    if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.length > 0) {
467	      cachedLangs = parsed;
468	      return cachedLangs;
469	    }
470	  } catch {
471	    /* older CLI or no binary — fall through to the static list */
472	  }
473	  cachedLangs = LANGS.map((l) => ({ code: l.value, name: l.title }));
474	  return cachedLangs;
475	}
476	
477	/**
478	 * `translate history --json` (recent) or `translate history search <q> --json`.
479	 * Both return an array of HistoryEntry. Local + fast (no network).
480	 */
481	export async function runHistory(
482	  query?: string,
483	  limit = 200,
484	  signal?: AbortSignal,
485	): Promise<HistoryEntry[]> {
486	  const bin = resolveBinary();
487	  const q = query?.trim();
488	  const args = q
489	    ? ["history", "search", q, "--json"]
490	    : ["history", "--json", "--limit", String(limit)];
491	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
492	    timeout: 30_000,
493	    maxBuffer: 32 * 1024 * 1024,
494	    env: baseEnv(),
495	    signal,
496	  });
497	  const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout);
498	  return Array.isArray(parsed) ? (parsed as HistoryEntry[]) : [];
499	}
500	
501	/**
502	 * Fire-and-forget TTS via `translate <text> --to <lang> --speak`. This runs a
503	 * real translation (it speaks the translated side), so it passes --no-history:
504	 * pressing Speak is not a lookup and should not add a history row.
505	 */
506	export function speak(text: string, to: string): void {
507	  const bin = resolveBinary();
508	  execFile(
509	    bin,
510	    [text, "--to", to, "--speak", "--no-history"],
511	    { env: baseEnv() },
512	    () => {
513	      /* ignore — best-effort audio */
514	    },
515	  );
516	}
517	
518	/**
519	 * Fire-and-forget TTS via `translate speak <text>` — pronounces the text as-is.
520	 * Unlike speak() this neither translates nor records, which is what you want for
521	 * "how is this word pronounced".
522	 */
523	export function speakText(text: string, lang?: string): void {
524	  const bin = resolveBinary();
525	  const args = ["speak", text];
526	  if (lang) args.push("--lang", lang);
527	  execFile(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() }, () => {
528	    /* ignore — best-effort audio */
529	  });
530	}

532	/** The effective CLI config (subset we care about) from `config show --json`. */
533	export interface CliConfig {
534	  general?: {
535	    default_target?: string;
536	    default_source?: string;
537	    debounce_ms?: number;
538	    engine?: string;
539	    tier?: string;
540	    live_translate?: boolean;
541	    /** Bidirectional mode: home-language input goes to pair_with instead. */
542	    pair?: boolean;
543	    pair_with?: string;
544	  };
545	}
546	
547	let cachedConfig: CliConfig | undefined;
548	
549	/**
550	 * Read the CLI's effective config via `translate config show --json` (cached per
551	 * command run). Lets the extension inherit the default target / debounce from
552	 * ~/.config/translate/config.toml when the Raycast preferences are left empty.
553	 */
554	export async function readConfig(): Promise<CliConfig> {
555	  if (cachedConfig) return cachedConfig;
556	  const bin = resolveBinary();
557	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["config", "show", "--json"], {
558	    timeout: 10_000,
559	    maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024,
560	    env: baseEnv(),
561	  });
562	  cachedConfig = JSON.parse(stdout) as CliConfig;
563	  return cachedConfig;
564	}
565	
566	export interface StreamHandlers {
567	  onData: (chunk: string) => void;
568	  onDone: (code: number | null) => void;
569	  onError: (err: Error) => void;
570	}
571	
572	/**
573	 * Spawn `translate <text> --to <lang> [--engine] --stream` and stream plain-text
574	 * stdout chunks (the `--stream` flag forces streaming over a pipe). Returns a
575	 * cancel function that kills the child (call it on unmount). Whether output arrives
576	 * progressively depends on the provider — ollama streams; copilot-proxy buffers its
577	 * claude responses. `--no-history` avoids duplicating a history row the live view
578	 * may already have recorded.
579	 */
580	export function spawnTranslateStream(
581	  text: string,
582	  opts: TranslateOptions,
583	  h: StreamHandlers,
584	): () => void {
585	  const bin = resolveBinary();
586	  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, undefined);
587	  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
588	  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
589	  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
590	  args.push("--stream", "--no-history");
591	  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
592	  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
593	  if (opts.engine) args.push("--engine", opts.engine);
594	  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
595	  if (opts.tier) args.push("--tier", opts.tier);
596	  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
597	
598	  const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
599	  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
600	  child.stdout?.on("data", (d: Buffer | string) => h.onData(d.toString()));
601	  child.on("close", (code) => h.onDone(code));
602	  child.on("error", (err) => h.onError(err));
603	  if (viaStdin) {
604	    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
605	      /* reported via the close/error handlers above */
606	    });
607	    child.stdin?.end(text, "utf8");
608	  }
609	  return () => {
610	    if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
611	  };
612	}

1	import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
2	
3	/** Debounce a value so an expensive call only fires after the user pauses typing. */
4	export function useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
5	  const [debounced, setDebounced] = useState(value);
6	  useEffect(() => {
7	    const id = setTimeout(() => setDebounced(value), delayMs);
8	    return () => clearTimeout(id);
9	  }, [value, delayMs]);
10	  return debounced;
11	}

  -a, --all
          Enqueue all stashed tasks across all groups

  -d, --delay <delay>
          Delay enqueuing these tasks until 'delay' elapses. See DELAY FORMAT below

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

DELAY FORMAT:

    The --delay argument must be either a number of seconds or a "date expression" similar to GNU
    "date -d" with some extensions. It does not attempt to parse all natural language, but is
    incredibly flexible. Here are some supported examples.

    2020-04-01T18:30:00   // RFC 3339 timestamp
    2020-4-1 18:2:30      // Optional leading zeros
    2020-4-1 5:30pm       // Informal am/pm time
    2020-4-1 5pm          // Optional minutes and seconds
    April 1 2020 18:30:00 // English months
    1 Apr 8:30pm          // Implies current year
    4/1                   // American form date
    wednesday 10:30pm     // The closest wednesday in the future at 22:30
    wednesday             // The closest wednesday in the future
    4 months              // 4 months from today at 00:00:00
    1 week                // 1 week at the current time
    1days                 // 1 day from today at the current time
    1d 03:00              // The closest 3:00 after 1 day (24 hours)
    3h                    // 3 hours from now
    3600s                 // 3600 seconds from now

########## pueue help start ##########
Resume operation of specific tasks or groups of tasks.

Without any parameters this resumes the default group and all its tasks. Can also be used
force-start specific tasks, which **ignores** any group parallelism limits or dependencies a task my
have!

Usage: pueue start [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          Start these specific tasks. Paused tasks will resumed. Queued/Stashed tasks will be
          force-started

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Resume a specific group and all paused tasks in it.
          
          The group will be set to running and its paused tasks will be resumed.

  -a, --all
          Resume all groups!
          
          All groups will be set to running and paused tasks will be resumed.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help pause ##########
Either pause running tasks or specific groups of tasks.

By default, pauses the default group and all its tasks. A paused queue (group) won't start any new
tasks.

Usage: pueue pause [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          Pause these specific tasks

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Pause a specific group

  -a, --all
          Pause all groups!

  -w, --wait
          Pause the specified groups, but let already running tasks finish by themselves

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

########## pueue help kill ##########
Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups.

Kills all tasks of the default group when no ids or a specific group are provided.

Usage: pueue kill [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          Kill these specific tasks

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Kill all running tasks in a group. This also pauses the group

  -a, --all
          Kill all running tasks across ALL groups. This also pauses all groups

  -s, --signal <SIGNAL>
          Send a UNIX signal instead of simply killing the process.

          states, use at your own descretion.
          
          This argument also excepts the integer representation as well as the signal short name.

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

287	        <List.EmptyView

291	        />

296	
297	/**
298	 * History rows worth showing next to live results: the ones whose input or output
299	 * contains what was typed. Already in memory, so this costs nothing.
300	 */
301	function matchingHistory(entries: HistoryEntry[], q: string): HistoryEntry[] {
302	  const needle = q.toLowerCase();
303	  return entries
304	    .filter(
305	      (h) =>
306	        h.input.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
307	        h.output.toLowerCase().includes(needle),
308	    )
309	    .slice(0, HISTORY_WITH_RESULTS);
310	}
311	
312	/** Pull the `translate …` command out of a notes hint, for the copy action. */
313	function commandFromNotes(notes: string): string {
314	  const m = notes.match(/`([^`]+)`/);
315	  return m ? m[1] : notes;
316	}

- Add an `interval` property to a command in the manifest (example shown).  
- Interval format: seconds (s), minutes (m), hours (h) or days (d). Example values: `10m`, `12h`, `1d`.  
- "The minimum value is 10 seconds (`10s`), which should be used cautiously" (minimum allowed interval).

How often / scheduling behavior
- The interval requests background runs every X (s/m/h/d), but scheduling is not exact: macOS may vary times to optimize energy and battery.  
- "Note that the actual scheduling is not exact and might vary within a tolerance level."

Run conditions (when launched / launch type)
- Commands run in background without the user manually opening them.  
- Use the global `environment.launchType` to detect background runs (LaunchType.Background vs user). Quoted usage: "console.log("launchType", environment.launchType);" (example shows checking launch type).

Execution model / how long they run
- For no-view commands the command runs until the main async function Promise resolves.  
- For menu-bar commands the React component runs until `isLoading` is set to `false`.  
- To avoid overlapping launches, "commands are terminated after a timeout that is dynamically adjusted to the interval."  
- Also: "Raycast auto-terminates the command if it exceeds its maximum execution time."

State, errors, and defensive programming
- If commands share state, use defensive programming to handle errors, data races, incomplete or inaccessible stored state.  
- For development, there are actions to run in background and show full errors for debugging.

Activation by user / defaults
- "When a user installs the command via the Store, background refresh is initially *disabled* and is activated either when the user opens the command for the first time or enables background refresh in preferences."  
  (Installed-from-store commands start disabled until user opens or enables them.)

Updating UI from background
- Example shows using updateCommandMetadata to change the command subtitle from a background run. Quoted snippet: "await updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle: `Unread Notifications: ${count}` });"

Notes / best practices (brief)
- Prefer larger intervals to reduce energy use.  
- For network calls, respect rate limits and retry appropriately.  
- Finish quickly; for menu-bar commands set `isLoading` false as early as possible.

If you want, I can extract the exact example JSON and TypeScript snippets as quoted lines (each kept ≤125 characters) or produce a compact checklist you can paste into a manifest.

```text
Quoted signatures and short excerpts (each quote <=125 chars):

- "export async function launchCommand(options: LaunchOptions): Promise<void>;"
- "export async function updateCommandMetadata(metadata: { subtitle?: string | null }): Promise<void>;"
- "The actual manifest file is not modified, so the update applies as long as the command remains installed."

Summary (paraphrased; not verbatim):

- launchCommand
  - Purpose: programmatically start another Raycast command. Throws if the command is missing or disabled. If the target is in another extension, the user sees a permission prompt. Useful for user‑triggered opens or forcing background refreshes.
  - Parameters: one LaunchOptions object (see below).
  - Return: a Promise that resolves when the command has been launched (does not indicate target completion).

- updateCommandMetadata
  - Purpose: change manifest-declared properties for the current command at runtime. Currently only subtitle can be updated; pass null to clear it.
  - Parameters: object with optional subtitle?: string | null.
  - Note: the manifest file itself is not changed; the update lasts while the command remains installed.
  - Return: a Promise that resolves when the metadata update completes.

- Types referenced on this page
  - LaunchContext: represents the context object passed for programmatic launches.
  - LaunchOptions: decides which command to launch and what arguments/context it receives. Two variants described below.

- IntraExtensionLaunchOptions (launching within the same extension)
  - name (required): string — command name as in the extension manifest.
  - type (required): LaunchType — either UserInitiated or Background.
  - arguments: optional Arguments object (as defined in manifest).
  - context: optional JSON-serializable object accessible as LaunchProps/LaunchContext (Dates and Buffers supported).
  - fallbackText: optional string to send as fallback text.

- InterExtensionLaunchOptions (launching a command in another extension)
  - extensionName (required): string — target extension name from its manifest.
  - ownerOrAuthorName (required): string — owner/author as in target manifest.
  - name (required): string — command name in target manifest.
  - type (required): LaunchType.
  - arguments: optional Arguments object.
  - context: optional JSON-serializable object (accessible as LaunchProps/LaunchContext).
  - fallbackText: optional string.

Notes about LaunchProps / LaunchContext:
- The page uses LaunchContext to name the object passed as context and says that context is "accessible as LaunchProps"; treat LaunchProps as the runtime access point for the passed context inside the launched command.

References (from supplied content): command API page excerpts and the quoted signatures above.

19	/**
20	 * The full-page definition for one word — the payoff of pressing ⏎ on a
21	 * candidate. A whole Detail with markdown beats a List detail pane once the
22	 * definition (or the LLM fallback's prose) runs long.
23	 *
24	 * This is also the ONLY place the extension writes history: `runDefine` is called
25	 * without --no-history, so a word is remembered when you open it, never while you
26	 * type. onRecorded lets the pushing list refresh its recent-lookups section.
27	 */
28	export function DefineDetail(props: {
29	  word: string;
30	  to: string;
31	  onRecorded?: () => void;
32	}) {
33	  const { word, to } = props;
34	  const { data, isLoading, error } = usePromise(
35	    async (w: string, target: string): Promise<TranslateResult> =>
36	      // smart: fall back to the LLM when the offline dictionary has no entry.
37	      runDefine(w, { to: target, smart: true }),
38	    [word, to],
39	    { onData: () => props.onRecorded?.() },
40	  );
41	
42	  const markdown = error
43	    ? errorMarkdown(word, error)
44	    : data
45	      ? renderDefinition(data, word)
46	      : `# ${word}\n\nLooking up…`;
47	
48	  return (
49	    <Detail
50	      isLoading={isLoading}
51	      navigationTitle={word}
52	      markdown={markdown}
53	      metadata={data ? <Metadata result={data} to={to} /> : undefined}
54	      actions={
55	        <ActionPanel>
56	          {data ? (
57	            <Action.CopyToClipboard
58	              title="Copy Definition"
59	              content={definitionText(data, word)}
60	            />
61	          ) : null}
62	          <Action.CopyToClipboard
63	            title="Copy Word"
64	            content={word}
65	            shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd"], key: "i" }}
66	          />
67	          {data ? (
68	            <Action.Paste
69	              title="Paste Definition"
70	              content={definitionText(data, word)}
71	            />
72	          ) : null}
73	          <Action
74	            title="Speak"
75	            icon={Icon.SpeakerHigh}
76	            onAction={async () => {
77	              // Pronounce the headword itself — `translate speak` neither
78	              // translates nor records, unlike the Translate command's Speak.
79	              speakText(word);
80	              await showHUD("Speaking…");
81	            }}
82	          />
83	          <Action
84	            title="Open in Translate"
85	            icon={Icon.Text}
86	            shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"], key: "t" }}
87	            onAction={async () => {
88	              await launchCommand({
89	                name: "translate",
90	                type: LaunchType.UserInitiated,
91	                context: { seed: word, to },
92	              });
93	            }}
94	          />
95	        </ActionPanel>
96	      }
97	    />
98	  );
99	}

101	function errorMarkdown(word: string, error: Error): string {
102	  if (isNoDictEntry(error)) {
103	    return [
104	      `# ${word}`,
105	      "",
106	      "No dictionary entry, and no LLM fallback is configured.",
107	      "",
108	      "Configure a provider in `~/.config/translate/config.toml` (or run `translate init`) to define unknown words with an LLM.",
109	    ].join("\n");
110	  }
111	  if (isBinaryMissing(error)) {
112	    return [
113	      "# translate CLI not found",
114	      "",
115	      "Set the binary path in the extension preferences, or install it:",
116	      "",
117	      "```sh",
118	      "brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate",
119	      "```",
120	    ].join("\n");
121	  }
122	  return `# ${word}\n\nLookup failed.\n\n\`\`\`\n${String(error.message ?? error)}\n\`\`\``;
123	}
124	
125	/** The plain text a Copy/Paste action should produce. */
126	function definitionText(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
127	  const d = r.dictionary;
128	  if (!d) return r.translation;
129	  const lines: string[] = [];
130	  for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
131	    for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) lines.push(def.definition);
132	  }
133	  return lines.length > 0 ? lines.join("\n") : r.translation || word;
134	}

136	/** Renders a dictionary entry, or the LLM fallback's prose, as markdown. */
137	export function renderDefinition(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
138	  const d = r.dictionary;
139	  if (d) {
140	    const lines = [`# ${d.word || word}`];
141	    if (d.phonetic) lines.push(`*/${d.phonetic}/*`);
142	    lines.push("");
143	    for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
144	      lines.push(`## ${m.part_of_speech}`);
145	      for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) {
146	        lines.push(
147	          `- ${def.definition}${def.example ? `\n  - _${def.example}_` : ""}`,
148	        );
149	      }
150	      lines.push("");
151	    }
152	    return lines.join("\n");
153	  }
154	  // No dictionary entry — the LLM fallback's definition lives in `translation`.
155	  const lines = [`# ${word}`, "", r.translation, ""];
156	  if (r.warnings?.length) lines.push("---", ...r.warnings.map((w) => `> ${w}`));
157	  return lines.join("\n");
158	}

161	  const { result: r, to } = props;
162	  // A dictionary hit reports the language its glosses are actually written in,
163	  // which is fixed by the data (ECDICT is en→zh, CC-CEDICT is zh→en). Say so
164	  // rather than letting the picked target look ignored.
165	  const scriptFixed =
166	    r.engine === "dictionary" && !!r.target && r.target !== to;
167	  return (

169	      <Detail.Metadata.Label title="Engine" text={r.engine ?? "—"} />
170	      {r.dictionary?.phonetic ? (
171	        <Detail.Metadata.Label title="Phonetic" text={r.dictionary.phonetic} />
172	      ) : null}
173	      {r.model ? <Detail.Metadata.Label title="Model" text={r.model} /> : null}
174	      <Detail.Metadata.Label
175	        title="Definition language"
176	        text={

178	            ? `${r.target} — the offline dictionary is zh↔en; “${to}” applies to the LLM fallback`
179	            : r.target || to
180	        }
181	      />
182	      {r.dictionary?.source_url ? (

185	          target={r.dictionary.source_url}
186	          text="link"
187	        />
188	      ) : null}
189	    </Detail.Metadata>
190	  );
191	}

61	export function renderEntry(h: HistoryEntry): string {
62	  return [`# ${h.input}`, "", h.output].join("\n");

71	  const flat = s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();

=== CHANGELOG v4 section ===
Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## \[4.0.5\] - unreleased

### Fix

## \[4.0.4\] - 2026-03-02

### Fix

- Test fixes for armv7/armhf architectures
- Update dependencies to s390x builds

## \[4.0.3\] - 2026-03-01

### Fix

- `pueue add` Canonicalize `--working-directory` paths.
- `pueue start` can force-start stashed tasks. #659

### Maintenance

- Replace deprecated `command-group` with `process-wrap` v9. Minimum Rust version updated to 1.87.

## \[4.0.2\] - 2025-12-19

### Maintenance

- Bump dependencies
- Ditch deprecated `rustls_pemfile` library and directly use `rustls-pki-types`.
- Switch to `assert_cmd::cargo_bin` in tests to migrate from deprecated Cargo::cargo_bin #651

## \[4.0.1\] - 2025-07-07

### Fixed

- Fix extraneous double quotes being added to --config and --profile flags in Windows service install. #630
- Fix --config/--path flags causing Windows service start to fail. #631
- Removed forgotten debug log statement.

## \[4.0.0\] - 2025-03-09

This release aims to further improve Pueue and to rectify some old design decisions.
Large portions of both the library and the executables' code have been refactored and the protocol has been reworked, which completely breaks backwards compatibility.

Read the `Change` section for more details.

### Removing internal channel communication

TLDR: Commands that start/stop/pause tasks now only return when the task is actually started/stopped/paused.
`kill`ing commands still takes a short while, as the process needs to be cleaned up properly.

---

Until recently, Pueue managed subprocess (task) states in a dedicated thread.
Client commands affecting subprocesses, such as `pueue start --immediate`, were relayed to this special thread via an `mpsc` channel for processing.

This setup caused short delays before the instructions were executed.
For instance, tasks would begin a few hundred milliseconds after the client received an `Ok` from the daemon, despite using the `--immediate` flag.
This behavior was unintuitive and often led to commands like `pueue add --immediate install_something && pueue send 0 'y\n'` failing, as the task had not started by the time `pueue send` was called.

The new state design resolves this issue by allowing Pueue to manipulate subprocess states directly within the client message handlers, eliminating any delays.

### New editing

Task editing was a bit tedious until recently.
One could only edit a single task at a time and you had to specify which properties you wanted to add.
Each property was then opened in a new `$EDITOR` session, which meant that users had to open and close editors up to four times to edit a single task.

After a lot of consideration, tasks editing has been redesigned, provoding two ways that allow simple and convenient editing of multiple tasks at once.

#### File based approach

For this, a temporary directory is created for every task to edit and a new file for every property, resulting in the following structure:

```
   📁 0/
   │ * command
   │ * label
   │ * path
   └ * priority
   📁 1/
   │ * command
   │ * label
   │ * path
   └ * priority
```

You can then just navigate the resulting file structure and edit the properties you want in the editor of your choice.
This solution is obviously flawed if your editor doesn't provide an in-editor file tree like `helix`.

This mode is enabled by setting `client.edit_mode` to `files`.

#### Toml based approach

In this mode, all tasks to be edited are serialized into a single `toml` file that's then opened in the editor of your choice.

```toml
[1]
id = 1
command = "ls"
path = "/tmp"
priority = 0
```

This mode is very convenient for editing simple tasks, but has the drawback that users need to know the TOML format and have to make sure to not mess up character escaping.
For example, multi-line commands or commands that contain special/reserved characters in TOML will need special care.

Based on some feedback, this mode is apparently the most asked for, so this is enabled by default.
It can also be explicitly set via `client.edit_mode: "toml"`.

### Runtime invariants

TLDR: A new task state representation has been introduced, which is significantly cleaner and fixes some bugs.
However, it breaks compatibility with old states, so ensure there are no important tasks in your queue before updating. You'll also need to recreate groups.
```

```text
1	# Raycast integration — reference
2	
3	How `translate` plugs into [Raycast](https://raycast.com), the options we
4	weighed, how the shipped integration works, and how it compares to existing
5	translation extensions. This is present-tense reference reading; the actual code
6	lives in [`../raycast/`](../raycast/), and store-publishing is tracked in
7	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
8	
9	**Core principle: reuse the binary, don't reimplement.** Every tier below shells
10	out to the existing `translate` CLI (`--json`) and renders the result. No
11	translation, engine, or dictionary logic is duplicated in TypeScript/bash.
12	
13	## Integration tiers
14	
15	Raycast offers four ways to surface functionality. We ship the middle two.
16	
17	| Tier | Reuses binary? | Effort | Selection → translate | Persisted defaults | Rich UI / history | Streaming | Distribution |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **Quick Link** | ✗ (can't exec) | 5 min | via deeplink only | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | launcher only |
20	| **Script Command** (bash) — *shipped* | ✓ | ~0.5 h | ✗ (needs `pbpaste`) | ✗ (no prefs) | ✗ (plain text) | only `fullOutput` | Add Script Directory |
21	| **TS Extension** (`@raycast/api`) — *shipped* | ✓ | 1–2 d | ✓ `getSelectedText()` | ✓ preferences | ✓ List/Detail/Actions | ✓ (manual `spawn`) | `npm run dev` / store |
22	| **AI Extension** (tools) | ✓ | +0.5 d | AI-orchestrated | — | AI Chat | `AI.ask` | store; **Pro-gated** |
23	
24	- **Quick Links** open a URL/file/app/`raycast://` deeplink — they have no
25	  shell-exec surface, so they can't run the CLI directly. Useful only as a hotkey
26	  that deeplinks into a real command.
27	- **AI Extensions** expose "tools" the Raycast AI can call. Feasible (a tool file
28	  can `execFile` the binary and return its `--json`), but the AI API requires
29	  **Raycast Pro**, so it's an additive Pro-only layer — deferred.
30	
31	## How Raycast extensions work
32	
33	- **Manifest** (`package.json`): a `commands[]` array; each command has a
34	  required `mode`:
35	  - `view` — default-exports a React (TSX) component (our `Translate`).
36	  - `no-view` — default-exports an async function; runs and exits, no UI
37	    (our `Translate Selection` → `getSelectedText` → `Clipboard.paste` + `showHUD`).
38	  - `menu-bar` — a persistent `MenuBarExtra` (not used yet).
39	- **Running the binary:** extensions run in a Node runtime, so `child_process`
40	  works. We use `execFile` (typed wrapper in
41	  [`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
42	  rather than the `useExec` hook, because `useExec` buffers with a 10 s default
43	  timeout that LLM engines exceed (and its `timeout: 0` is coerced back to 10000).
44	  The CLI's **`--stream` flag** forces token streaming even when stdout is piped
45	  (which Raycast always is; without it the CLI treats non-TTY as buffered). A
46	  streaming `Detail` view can spawn `translate … --stream` and append `stdout`
47	  chunks into React state bound to `Detail.markdown`. Caveat: visible progressive
48	  output depends on the provider — ollama streams; **copilot-proxy currently buffers
49	  its claude `/v1/messages` responses**, so the result appears after first-token
50	  latency. The default live view uses `--json` (buffered, structured), which returns
51	  fast enough.
52	- **Preferences** (`getPreferenceValues()`): persisted per-extension settings —
53	  our `binaryPath`, `defaultTarget`, `engine`, `tier`.
54	- **Input/UI:** `getSelectedText()` (frontmost app's selection),
55	  `Clipboard.copy/paste`, `Action.CopyToClipboard`/`Action.Paste`; `List` +
56	  `List.Dropdown` (searchBarAccessory, `storeValue` to remember the last target);
57	  `Detail`/`List.Item.Detail` with `.Metadata` for structured fields; `showHUD`/
58	  `showToast` for feedback.
59	- **Tooling:** the `ray` CLI (ships in the extension's dev deps). `ray develop`
60	  (`npm run dev`) registers the extension with the running Raycast app and
61	  hot-reloads; **it persists in root search after you stop dev** — no store
62	  publish needed for personal use. `ray build`/`ray lint` type-check and lint.
63	
64	## Gotchas (learned the hard way)
65	
66	- **launchd PATH:** Raycast launches under launchd and does *not* inherit your
67	  shell PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `ENOENT` / `command not found`.
68	  Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path (preference first, then probe
69	  `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`). Always test
70	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
71	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
72	- **HOME / config, not shell env:** the CLI reads providers/keys from
73	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, *not* environment variables. A key exported
74	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd — put it in the config (`translate init`).
75	  We pass `HOME` through so the CLI finds its config.
76	- **Exit code is 0 even on engine failure** (auto-fallback), so we read
77	  `warnings[]` from `--json` rather than branching on exit codes. The extension
78	  surfaces warnings in the Detail pane / HUD; the plain-text scripts don't.
79	- **Extension icons must be a real PNG** (512×512) — emoji icons work only for
80	  Script Commands. `ray build`/`lint` complains otherwise.
81	- **A preference `default` only applies when no value is stored.** Changing a
82	  `default` in `package.json` does *not* reach an install that has already
83	  materialized that preference — Raycast keeps the stored value, and the new
84	  default is inert. Symptom: a behaviour you "fixed" in the manifest persists. See
85	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md).
86	  Corollary: read preferences through the generated `Preferences.<Command>` type,
87	  not a hand-written interface — the generated one makes the field required, so a
88	  code default that drifts from the manifest becomes a compile error.
89	- **The extension runs the *installed* binary, not your working tree.**
90	  `resolveBinary()` probes `~/.local/bin` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` → `/usr/local/bin`
91	  → `~/go/bin`, so `just raycast-dev` alone never picks up a CLI change. When a
92	  change spans both, the loop is `just check && just install && just raycast-dev`.
93	  Worse, an old binary fails *silently*: `translate` takes free text as its first
94	  argument, so an unknown subcommand gets translated and exits 0
95	  (`translate models` → "n. 模型…"). Never probe capability by exit status. See
96	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md).
97	- **The search bar refuses a long paste** ("The text you are trying to paste is
98	  too long"). That guard is in the Raycast app binary, not `@raycast/api`, so it
99	  can't be raised or caught, and it applies to every search-bar command. Long
100	  text needs a `Form.TextArea` — that is what the `translate-text` command is.
101	  Behind it, argv caps at `ARG_MAX` (1 MiB), so `src/lib/translate.ts` pipes to
102	  stdin above 128 KB. See
103	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md).
104	- **Command arguments are static manifest data** and can't be populated at
105	  runtime, so a language argument is necessarily a hand-synced subset. In-view
106	  `List.Dropdown`s can call `translate lang list --json` for the full table.
107	
108	## Competitive landscape (2026)
109	
110	The Raycast translation category is crowded, but the field is almost entirely
111	remote-API/cloud-LLM wrappers configured via extension preferences.
112	
113	| Extension | Backend | Streaming | TTS | History | Offline dict |
114	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
115	| gebeto/translate (Google) | Google web (keyless) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
116	| tisfeng/Easydict | 10 remote providers + Apple `say`/Shortcuts | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ (remote) |
117	| douo/openai-translator | multi-LLM incl. Ollama / custom endpoint | ✓ | ✗ (roadmap) | ✓ | ✗ |
118	| deepcast / itranslate | DeepL / multi (BYO API key) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
119	| Raycast built-in Translate | unstated | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (Pro-gated) |
120	
121	**What `translate` does that they don't:**
122	
123	- **Shells out to a dedicated local translator CLI** — no surveyed extension
124	  wraps a standalone translator binary (Easydict shells to `osascript`/Apple
125	  Shortcuts; none to a CLI like this).
126	- **Automatic multi-engine failover** — competitors that support multiple engines
127	  do *parallel aggregation*, not "try A, on failure fall back to B".
128	- **Offline CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries** via `translate define` — all
129	  competitors' dictionaries are remote.
130	- **Unified, searchable history** (`translate history [search]`).
131	- **Free local TTS** (`--speak`) — note openai-translator lists TTS as an
132	  unshipped roadmap item, so this is a real gap.
133	- **Fuzzy language resolution** (`translate lang resolve`, `chinees → zh`).
134	
135	Frame differentiation as **offline-resilient + auto-fallback + unified history**,
136	*not* "local LLM" (openai-translator already reaches Ollama) and *not* "study
137	modes" (Anki / Vocabulary Builder already exist in the store).
138	
139	## How ours is built
140	
141	- **Script Commands** — [`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/):
142	  `translate-text` (dropdown language + text, `fullOutput`), `translate-and-copy`
143	  (`silent`, copies; blank arg → clipboard), `define-word`. Install:
144	  `just raycast-scripts`, then add the directory in Raycast once.
145	- **TS extension** — [`../raycast/extension/`](../raycast/extension/): commands
146	  `translate` (view: type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
147	  Copy/Paste/Speak, typo "did you mean?" suggestions, opt-in selection prefill),
148	  `translate-selection` (no-view:
149	  grabs the selection/clipboard and opens Translate prefilled via `launchCommand` —
150	  editable, not blind-paste), `define` (view: dictionary lookup +
151	  LLM fallback + "did you mean" suggestions), `look-up-word` (view: the Define
152	  Word-style picker, below), `translate-text` (view: a `Form.TextArea` for
153	  passages the search bar refuses, below), and `history` (view: browse/search
154	  past translations). All share `src/lib/translate.ts` (binary resolve + typed
155	  `execFile` wrappers mirroring `internal/engine/engine.go`'s `TranslateResult`).
156	  Run: `just raycast-dev` (`build`/`lint` variants exist). Live translate is
157	  debounced + abortable to avoid an LLM call per keystroke, with an opt-in `⌘↵`
158	  streaming view (`spawnTranslateStream` → `translate … --stream` → live `Detail`).
159	  Typo suggestions reuse the engine's fuzzy `suggestions[]` (a shared
160	  `did-you-mean.tsx` component) — no CLI change; single-word lookups route to the
161	  offline dict, full sentences to the LLM which corrects implicitly. Default target,
162	  live-debounce, and tier are inherited from the CLI config (`config show --json`)
163	  when the matching Raycast preference is empty, so `config.toml` is the single
164	  source of truth (a Raycast preference overrides it).
165	
166	### `look-up-word` — the Define Word-style picker
167	
168	Modeled on Raycast's built-in **Define Word**: an empty search bar lists recent
169	history; typing shows ranked headword candidates with definition previews;
170	`⏎` pushes a full-page `Detail`.
171	
172	Three rules shape it, and each is worth preserving:
173	
174	1. **Typing is local-only.** The list is backed by `translate dict search --json`,
175	   which reads the dictionary databases and nothing else (~30 ms). An LLM call per
176	   keystroke would take ~6 s and be unusable, so the LLM fallback is deferred to
177	   `⏎` — either on a fuzzy candidate or on the explicit *Ask the LLM* row that
178	   appears when no local headword matched.
179	2. **Only `⏎` writes history.** `dict search` opens no history store at all, so the
180	   typing path *cannot* record; `DefineDetail` calls `define` without
181	   `--no-history`, so opening a word remembers it. The old `define` command passes
182	   `--no-history` because it looks up on every keystroke.
183	3. **Language is pickable before and after opening.** A command *argument*
184	   dropdown appears in the Raycast root bar; an in-view `List.Dropdown` (populated
185	   from `translate lang list --json`) changes it later. Both only steer the LLM
186	   fallback — the offline tiers are script-fixed (ECDICT en→zh, CC-CEDICT zh→en) —
187	   and the Detail metadata says so rather than letting the choice look ignored.
188	
189	`define` is kept alongside it, unchanged, so the two UXes can be compared.
190	New components: `lib/define-detail.tsx` (full-page definition, the only history
191	writer), `lib/history-detail.tsx` (a stored record as a page — no re-run, instant),
192	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx`. `lib/did-you-mean.tsx` is deliberately *not* reused
193	here: its `⏎` re-runs the search, whereas in this list `⏎` must define.
194	
195	### `translate-text` — the long-passage escape hatch
196	
197	Every other command takes its input in the search bar, which Raycast caps: a long
198	paste is refused outright, and the extension never even sees it. This command is a
199	`Form.TextArea` plus target/engine dropdowns; submitting pushes the same full-page
200	`Detail` (`lib/translation-detail.tsx`), with `⌘↵` for the streaming view.
201	
202	Nothing is prefilled — *Load Selection* (`⌘⇧S`) and *Load Clipboard* (`⌘⇧V`) are
203	explicit actions, keeping the lesson from `e87db06` that auto-grabbing input on
204	open is surprising. `⌘⇧A` reveals **Engine** and **Model**; both stay hidden by
205	default so the common case is two fields.
206	
207	The Model list comes from `translate models --json` — the models the configured
208	providers *declare*, one per tier. Deliberately not a live `/v1/models` probe:
209	copilot-proxy advertises ids it then refuses to serve, so a probed list would
210	offer choices that fail at request time. Picking a model also selects its
211	provider, since `llama3.2:3b` belongs to ollama regardless of chain order.
212	
213	Past 128 KB of UTF-8, `src/lib/translate.ts` stops putting the text in argv and
214	pipes it to stdin (`execWithStdin`), because macOS caps a whole argument list at
215	`ARG_MAX` = 1 MiB. The CLI already reads stdin when given no text argument, so
216	this needed no CLI change. The provider is the real ceiling long before either
217	limit: Google puts the text in a GET query string and fails around 180 KB.
218	
219	Result metadata (engine · model · direction) is a dim footer line at the end of
220	the markdown rather than a `Detail.Metadata` sidebar: the sidebar is a permanent
221	third of the window, which is a lot of width to spend on five short labels when
222	the whole point of the view is reading room.
223	
224	### Target language: the **Auto** entry
225	
226	Both target dropdowns (`translate`, `translate-text`) lead with
227	`Auto — <home> ⇄ <away>`, the dropdown equivalent of the TUI's `^g`. It is not
228	cosmetic:
229	
230	With `[general] pair = true` the CLI reroutes home-language input to `pair_with`
231	regardless of `--to`, so before this the dropdown was quietly lying — picking
232	"Chinese (Traditional)" and pasting Chinese returned *English*. Making the mode
233	explicit lets a concrete choice mean what it says: the extension now sends
234	`--no-pair` whenever a specific language is picked, and no `--to` at all for Auto.
235	`--no-pair` had to be added to the CLI for this; there was previously no way to
236	turn pair off for one run.
237	
238	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx` reads the pair from `config show --json`, so the entry
239	is labelled with the real codes and is omitted when no `pair_with` is configured.
240	
241	## Publishing & distribution
242	
243	The journey from local development to the store, and why we default to
244	local/personal for now.
245	
246	### Three distribution paths
247	
248	| Path | Review | Audience | How | Our stance |
249	|---|---|---|---|---|
250	| **Local dev** | none | just you | `just raycast-dev` (`ray develop`) — persists in root search after you stop dev | **current default** |
251	| **Private / org store** | none (org-gated) | your Raycast org | set `owner` in package.json → `npm run publish`; needs Raycast Pro/Team | option if sharing to a team |
252	| **Public store** | **human review** | everyone | `npm run publish` opens a PR to `raycast/extensions` → CI + Raycast-team review → merge auto-publishes | deferred → [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md) |
253	
254	### It is *not* like PyPI
255	
256	PyPI is self-service: register + `twine upload`, published instantly, no review.
257	The Raycast **public** store is curated — closer to Homebrew core:
258	
259	- `npm run publish` (= `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`) **authenticates with
260	  GitHub** and auto-opens a pull request into `github.com/raycast/extensions`.
261	- Automated CI checks run, then the **Raycast team reviews** and "request[s] changes
262	  when required"; on merge it auto-publishes. Turnaround is days, not seconds.
263	- Auth is **GitHub** (for the PR). Your **Raycast account** only supplies the
264	  validated `author` handle (ours: `da-wei_lee`).
265	
266	### Public-store requirements (checklist)
267	
268	Verified against developers.raycast.com. `✓` = done in this repo.
269	
270	- `✓` `author` = registered Raycast username; `license: "MIT"`; ≥1 category;
271	  one-sentence description; `platforms`; `package-lock.json`; `npm run build` +
272	  `ray lint` clean.
273	- `✓` **512×512 PNG icon** that reads in light + dark (not the default Raycast icon).
274	- `✓` **`CHANGELOG.md`** at the extension root (h2 headers; `{PR_MERGE_DATE}` placeholder).
275	- `✓` **`README.md`** at the extension root (setup/onboarding; media under a top-level
276	  `media/` folder).
277	- `☐` **≥3 (max 6) screenshots at 2000×1250 PNG** — captured from the *running*
278	  extension (a GUI step; not scriptable here).
279	- `☐` `npm run publish` (GitHub auth) + choose public vs private.
280	
281	### The binary-dependency hurdle
282	
283	The store guideline *"Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads"* is exactly
284	our case — the extension needs a user-installed `translate` (brew / `go install`).
285	"Calling known system binaries" is allowed, but a custom go-install CLI is a gray
286	area reviewers may push back on. Mitigations already in place:
287	
288	- Extension `README.md` documents the dependency + install commands.
289	- A graceful **binary-not-found onboarding** view (`src/lib/binary-not-found.tsx`) with
290	  copyable install commands + a jump to preferences — instead of a bare error.
291	- We do **not** bundle the ~22 MB Go binary (store discourages "heavy" binaries;
292	  shipping release binaries is a separate item — `backlog/release-binaries.md`).
293	
294	This friction is why the public store is deferred and local/private is the current
295	path; the analysis lives in [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
296	
297	## References
298	
299	- Raycast API — manifest, commands, UI: https://developers.raycast.com/
300	- `useExec`: https://developers.raycast.com/utilities/react-hooks/useexec
301	- AI Extensions: https://developers.raycast.com/ai
302	- Script Commands: https://github.com/raycast/script-commands
303	- Prepare / Publish / Teams: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store
