**Transport: unix socket** (`use_unix_socket: true`). Socket path is `runtime_directory/pueue_{username}.socket`; on macOS `dirs::runtime_dir()` is None so it falls back to `pueue_directory` → `/Users/david/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue_david.socket`. TCP would be `127.0.0.1:6924` with TLS + the cert pair, but is not in use.

**Shared secret**: yes — `pueue_directory/shared_secret`, 512 bytes, mode 0640. `pueue.rs` calls `read_shared_secret(...)` and sends it on **every** connection, including unix-socket ones. A client that shells out to `pueue` doesn't care, but a client speaking the socket protocol directly would.

**Env vars**: none required — `env | grep -i pueue` is empty and everything resolves from defaults. `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH` is honored by both binaries (verified: `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH=/nope/pueue.yml pueue status --json` → exit 1, `Failed to read configuration.`); the `-c` flag overrides it. `-p/--profile` selects a named block under `profiles:` (empty here).

## 6. Runtime / behavior facts

**Exit codes** — measured:

| Invocation | Exit |
|---|---|
| `pueue status --json` (daemon up) | 0 |
| `pueue group --json` | 0 |
| `pueue log 99999` / `pueue log 99999 --json` | **0** (prints `There are no finished tasks for your specified ids` to stderr / `{}` to stdout) |
| `pueue status --json 'status=Nope'` (bad query) | 1 |
| `pueue -c /nonexistent/pueue.yml status --json` | 1 |
| `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH=/nope/pueue.yml pueue status` | 1 |
| `pueue follow 99999` | 1 |

Convention: **0 = ok, 1 = everything else.** There are no distinct codes. Sources of the `1`: `color_eyre` bubbling out of `main` (prints an `Error:` block with `0:`/`1:` cause chain, a `Location:` line, and a backtrace hint), or an explicit `std::process::exit(1)` in `handle_response` on a `Response::Failure` / in `follow`. Also relevant: `pueue wait --status success` calls `std::process::exit(1)` the moment any watched task fails.

**Surprising:** `pueue parallel` with no argument prints `ERROR pueue::client::commands: Received unhandled response message` to stderr and **still exits 0**. It is not a usable "read current parallelism" command — use `pueue group --json` for that.

**Daemon-not-running** — I did **not** stop the daemon (that would mutate state and interrupt a service the user has running), and there is no way to simulate it without writing a throwaway config file. From `pueue_lib/src/network/socket/unix.rs` + `pueue/src/bin/pueue.rs`, the exact behavior is:
```
Error:
   0: Failed to initialize client.
   1: I/O error at path "/Users/david/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue_david.socket" \
      while connecting to daemon. Did you start it?:
      No such file or directory (os error 2)
```
on **stderr**, stdout empty, **exit 1** (`color_eyre` from `main`). Two distinct failure modes to detect:
- config file missing entirely → `bail!("Couldn't find a configuration file. Did you start the daemon yet?")` — this fires *before* any connection attempt.
- config present, socket gone/refused → the `connecting to daemon. Did you start it?` message above (`ECONNREFUSED` if the socket file exists but nothing listens, `ENOENT` if the file is gone).
There is **no `--json` error envelope** — errors are always human-formatted prose on stderr. A client must branch on exit code, not parse stdout.

**ANSI on stderr — surprising and worth planning for:** `color_eyre` error blocks are emitted **with ANSI escapes even when stderr is a pipe**, and neither `--color never` nor `NO_COLOR=1` suppresses them (verified via `| cat -v` for all three cases: `^[[91mFailed to read configuration.^[[0m`). Meanwhile normal stdout output correctly drops color when not a TTY. So: strip ANSI from any stderr you surface to the user.

**Speed** — 20 sequential `pueue status --json` runs against the empty queue (process spawn included):
```
min 22.1 ms   median 28.1 ms   max 44.0 ms
```
(`/usr/bin/time -p` rounds this to `real 0.01–0.02`.) That is process startup dominated; expect it to grow with `envs` payload size once tasks exist.

**No push/subscribe for state.** The wire protocol has a streaming response (`Response::Stream`) but it is used **only** for log following. Concretely:
- `pueue wait` **polls**: `loop { get_state(client); ...; sleep(2000ms) }` — a fixed **2 s** interval (250 ms only if `PUEUED_TEST_ENV_VARIABLE` is set). It re-requests the *entire* `State` each tick, diffs statuses in the client, and prints human-readable transition lines to stdout unless `-q`. It exits when all watched tasks hit the target status. So `wait` is a long-running process, but it is not a push subscription — and its stdout is prose, not JSON.
- `pueue follow` **does stream stdout continuously** (tail -f semantics), but for log text only, never for state. Two implementations: with `client.read_local_logs: true` (this machine), `local_follow` opens the log file directly and `io::copy`s new bytes to stdout every **250 ms**, re-asking the daemon whether the task is still running every **500 ms**; it exits when the task stops, prints `Pueue: Log file has gone away. Has the task been removed?` if the file vanishes, and `Pueue: The task to be followed doesn't exist.` + exit 1 for a bad id (verified). With `read_local_logs: false` it uses a real daemon-pushed `StreamRequest`/`Response::Stream` loop until `Response::Close`.
- `pueue add --immediate --follow` combines both, printing the "New task added" line to **stderr** so stdout stays pure log.

Net: **a client must poll `pueue status --json`** (or watch `state.json` / the `task_logs/` dir for mtime changes as a cheaper trigger — the daemon persists `state.json` on every change).

## 7. Log output

- Human: `pueue log <ids>` — last **15** lines per task by default; `--lines N`; `--full` for everything; `-g/--group`, `-a/--all` to select sets. Prints a header table per task plus the output.
- JSON: the output **is embedded** in `pueue log --json` as `.["<id>"].output` (a single string, stdout and stderr interleaved). It is *not* in `pueue status --json` at all — status explicitly excludes output ("This does not include the output of tasks. Use `log -j` if you want everything").
- On disk: **`{pueue_directory}/task_logs/{task_id}.log`**, i.e. here `/Users/david/Library/Application Support/pueue/task_logs/<id>.log`. From `pueue_lib/src/log.rs`: `get_log_path()` = `pueue_dir.join("task_logs").join(format!("{task_id}.log"))`, and `create_log_file_handles` returns **two handles to the same file** for stdout and stderr — so stdout and stderr are **merged into one plain-text file, uncompressed, unstructured**, with no timestamps or stream markers. Snappy compression is applied only in-flight when shipping logs to a *remote* client; local files are raw.
- **This directory is currently empty** — no task has produced a log since the last clean/reset, so I have no on-disk sample to show.
- Because `client.read_local_logs: true`, a Raycast extension can read `task_logs/<id>.log` directly and skip the daemon entirely for log display (that is exactly what `pueue log --json` and `pueue follow` do here). Log files are deleted with the task (`clean_log_handles` on remove/clean), and `restart --in-place` overwrites them.

## 8. Node.js / Raycast on this machine

```
$ node --version → v24.13.1   (mise: ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.1/bin/node, shimmed at /usr/local/bin/node)
$ npm  --version → 11.8.0
$ which ray      → ray not found
```
- **No `ray` CLI on PATH** and no global npm packages beyond `@playwright/cli`, `corepack`, `npm`. `ray` normally comes from the `@raycast/api` devDependency inside an extension (`node_modules/.bin/ray`), so it will appear once an extension is scaffolded.
- `/Applications/Raycast.app` is installed. Raycast ships its own Node: `~/Library/Application Support/com.raycast.macos/NodeJS/runtime/22.22.2` (extensions run on **Node 22**, not the mise 24).
- `~/.config/raycast/extensions/` holds 8 UUID-named installed extensions plus one **local dev extension named `translate`** (bundled `.js` per command + `package.json` + `assets/`, `cli.pid`, `dev.log`) — a working local example of a Raycast extension that shells out to a local CLI, at `/Users/david/.config/raycast/extensions/translate/package.json`. There is a symlink `~/.config/raycast/extensions/node_modules -> /Applications/Raycast.app/Contents/Resources/RaycastNodeExtensions_RaycastNodeExtensions.bundle/Contents/Resources/api/node_modules`.
- The target repo `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension` is an **empty git repo** — branch `main` with zero commits; only `.claude/` and `.specstory/` exist. No pueue extension exists yet.

## Things worth flagging

1. **No tasks exist right now** (`tasks: {}`, `task_logs/` empty, `state.json` 73 bytes). Every task-object claim above is from the v4.0.4 Rust source, not from live output.
2. **v4 moved timestamps and results inside the status enum.** Nested tagged enums, two levels deep (`status.Done.result.Failed`), plus a recursive `Locked.previous_status`. Any v3 documentation or example you find will mislead you.
3. **`enqueue_at` (Stashed) vs `enqueued_at` (all others)** — different spellings for near-identical concepts.
4. **`envs` (full environment snapshot) is in `status --json` but blanked in `log --json`.** Payload size and secret-leak implications for a polling UI.
5. **Homebrew here is `/usr/local`, not `/opt/homebrew`** — an Apple-Silicon-assuming path constant would break on this machine.
6. **Config lives in `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/`, not `~/.config/pueue/`** on macOS, and that same directory doubles as the data dir, socket dir, and log dir.
7. **`pueue log <bad id>` exits 0**, but `pueue follow <bad id>` exits 1. Exit codes are 0/1 only, with no structured error output — and stderr carries unsuppressable ANSI codes.
8. **`pueue parallel` with no args is broken** (logs "Received unhandled response message", exits 0).
9. **No watch/subscribe API.** `wait` polls every 2 s and emits prose; `follow` streams log text only. Polling `status --json` (~25 ms) or watching `state.json` mtime are the only options.
10. **`pueue status --json --group X` filters tasks but not the returned `groups` map**, and silently returns success for a group that doesn't exist.

```text
# pueue-ui

an experimental web ui for [pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue)

![screenshot](.github/images/status.webp)

> [!CAUTION]
> the api is completely unsafe and CANNOT not be made available over the internet,

## status

- [ ] status page
- [ ] task details page
  - [ ] logs
- [ ] task management (add, kill, pause, resume, restart, etc.)

## arch

one needs a tcp connection to communicate with the pueued daemon, meaning that it can't be done in the browser alone.

therefore there's two components; a node server for communicating with the daemon and a vue frontend for displaying
data.
```

```text
=== services-menu.tsx ===
/**
 * Menu bar command for quickly controlling brew services.
 *
 * Homebrew has no way to notify us when a service's state changes, so the menu
 * is kept fresh by polling on the command's `interval` (configurable in the
 * command preferences) and by an optimistic `mutate` after each action.
 */

import { Color, Icon, LaunchType, MenuBarExtra, launchCommand, showHUD } from "@raycast/api";
import {
  ALL_SERVICES,
  applyServiceAction,
  brewServiceIsRunning,
  ensureError,
  getErrorMessage,
  runServiceCommand,
  SERVICE_ACTION_COPY,
  type Service,
  type ServiceAction,
} from "./utils";
import { useBrewServices } from "./hooks/useBrewServices";
import { serviceStatusIcon, type ServicesMutate } from "./components/serviceActions";

const MENU_ICON = { source: "services-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.PrimaryText };

const ACTION_ICONS: Record<ServiceAction, Icon> = {
  start: Icon.Play,
  stop: Icon.Stop,
  restart: Icon.ArrowClockwise,
};

async function handleAction(action: ServiceAction, name: string, mutate: ServicesMutate) {
  const copy = SERVICE_ACTION_COPY[action];
  const target = name === ALL_SERVICES ? "all services" : name;
  try {
    await mutate(runServiceCommand(action, name), {
      optimisticUpdate: (services) => applyServiceAction(services ?? [], action, name),
    });
    await showHUD(`${copy.past} ${target}`);
  } catch (err) {
    await showHUD(`Failed to ${copy.verb.toLowerCase()} ${target}: ${getErrorMessage(ensureError(err))}`);
  }
}

export default function Command() {
  const { isLoading, data, revalidate, mutate } = useBrewServices();

  const services = data ?? [];
  const running = services.filter(brewServiceIsRunning);

  return (
    <MenuBarExtra
      icon={MENU_ICON}
      title={running.length > 0 ? `${running.length}` : undefined}
      tooltip="Homebrew Services"
      isLoading={isLoading}
    >
      <MenuBarExtra.Section title="All Services">
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Start All"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.start}
          onAction={() => handleAction("start", ALL_SERVICES, mutate)}
        />
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Stop All"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.stop}
          onAction={() => handleAction("stop", ALL_SERVICES, mutate)}
        />
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Restart All"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.restart}
          onAction={() => handleAction("restart", ALL_SERVICES, mutate)}
        />
      </MenuBarExtra.Section>

      <MenuBarExtra.Section title="Services">
        {services.map((service) => (
          <ServiceSubmenu key={service.name} service={service} mutate={mutate} />
        ))}
        {!isLoading && services.length === 0 && <MenuBarExtra.Item title="No services found" />}
```

```text
===== pueued.ts =====
import { Buffer } from "node:buffer"
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import path from "node:path"
import { connect, type TLSSocket } from "node:tls"

import { decode } from "cbor-x/decode-no-eval"
import { encode } from "cbor-x/encode"
import { useLogger } from "evlog"
import { type H3Event } from "nitro/h3"

import { type PueuedStatusResponse } from "../types/pueue.types.ts"

const PACKET_SIZE = 1280

const buildMessageParts = (data: Uint8Array): [Uint8Array, Uint8Array[]] => {
  const size = data.byteLength
  const header = Buffer.alloc(8)
  header.writeBigUInt64BE(BigInt(size))

  if (size < PACKET_SIZE) {
    return [header, [data]]
  }

  const packets: Uint8Array[] = []
  for (let i = 0; i < size; i += PACKET_SIZE) {
    packets.push(data.subarray(i, i + PACKET_SIZE))
  }
  return [header, packets]
}

const sendMessage = (socket: TLSSocket, message: Uint8Array) => {
  const { promise, resolve } = Promise.withResolvers<Uint8Array>()

  let incomingSize = -1
  let incomingData: Buffer | null = null
  let readSize = 0
  const handler = (incoming: Buffer) => {
    if (incomingSize === -1) {
      incomingSize = Number(incoming.readBigUInt64BE())
      incomingData = Buffer.alloc(incomingSize)
    } else {
      readSize += incoming.copy(incomingData!, readSize, 0, PACKET_SIZE)
    }

    if (readSize === incomingSize) {
      resolve(new Uint8Array(incomingData!))
      socket.removeListener("data", handler)
    }
  }
  socket.addListener("data", handler)

  const [header, parts] = buildMessageParts(message)
  socket.write(header)
  for (const part of parts) {
    socket.write(part)
  }

  return promise
}

const loadSharedSecret = () =>
  readFileSync(path.join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA!, "pueue", "shared_secret"))
let sharedSecret: Buffer | undefined

let connection: Promise<TLSSocket> | null = null

const initConnection = async (event: H3Event) => {
  const logger = useLogger(event)

  const { promise, resolve, reject: _reject } = Promise.withResolvers<TLSSocket>()
  connection = promise

  const socket = connect(
    {
      host: "127.0.0.1",
      port: 6925,
      timeout: 1000, // TODO: make configurable
      rejectUnauthorized: false,
    },
    () => {
      logger.set({ pueued: { status: "connected" } })
    },
  )

  socket.on("close", async () => {
    ;(await connection)?.destroySoon()
    connection = null
    logger.set({ pueued: { status: "closed" } })
  })
  socket.on("error", async (error) => {
    ;(await connection)?.destroySoon()
    connection = null
    logger.set({ pueued: { status: "error" } })
    logger.error(error)
  })

  sharedSecret ??= loadSharedSecret()
  const versionBuffer = await sendMessage(socket, sharedSecret)
  logger.set({ pueued: { version: new TextDecoder().decode(versionBuffer) } })

  resolve(socket)
}

export const usePueued = (event: H3Event) => {
  // const logger = useLogger(event)

  if (connection == null) void initConnection(event)

  const getStatus = async () => {
    const data = await sendMessage(await connection!, encode("Status"))

    return decode(data).Status as PueuedStatusResponse
  }

  return { getStatus } as const
}

===== pueue.types.ts =====
export type PueuedStatusStashed = {
  Stashed: {
    enqueued_at: string
  }
}

export type PueuedStatusQueued = {
  Queued: {
    enqueued_at: string
  }
}

export type PueuedStatusRunning = {
  Running: {
    enqueued_at: string
    start: string
  }
}

export type PueuedStatusPaused = {
  Paused: {
    enqueued_at: string
    start: string
  }
}

export type PueuedStatusDone = {
  Done: {
    enqueued_at: string
    start: string
    end: string
    result: "Success" | { Failed: number }
  }
}

export type PueuedStatus =
  | PueuedStatusStashed
  | PueuedStatusQueued
  | PueuedStatusRunning
  | PueuedStatusPaused
  | PueuedStatusDone
export type PueuedStatusName = keyof (PueuedStatusStashed &
  PueuedStatusQueued &
  PueuedStatusRunning &
  PueuedStatusPaused &
  PueuedStatusDone)

export type PueuedTask<S extends PueuedStatus = PueuedStatus> = {
  id: number
  priority: number
  group: string | null
  label: string | null
  status: S
  command: string
  original_command: string
  dependencies: unknown[]
  created_at: string
  path: string
  envs: Record<string, string>
}
```

```text
=== brew paths.ts ===
/**
 * Homebrew path utilities.
 *
 * Provides functions for resolving brew installation paths.
 */

import { execSync } from "child_process";
import { join as path_join } from "path";
import { cpus } from "os";
import { preferences } from "../preferences";

/**
 * The Homebrew prefix directory.
 * Determined by:
 * 1. Custom brew path preference (if set)
 * 2. Running `brew --prefix` command
 * 3. Fallback based on CPU architecture
 */
export const brewPrefix = (() => {
  if (preferences.customBrewPath && preferences.customBrewPath.length > 0)
    return path_join(preferences.customBrewPath, "..", "..");
  try {
    return execSync("brew --prefix", { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
  } catch {
    const firstCpu = cpus()[0];
    return firstCpu?.model?.includes("Apple") ? "/opt/homebrew" : "/usr/local";
  }
})();

/**
 * Get a path relative to the brew prefix.
 */
export const brewPath = (suffix: string): string => path_join(brewPrefix, suffix);

/**
 * Get the path to the brew executable.
 */
export const brewExecutable = (): string => brewPath("bin/brew");

=== brew services.ts (detect) ===
/**
 * Homebrew services utilities.
 *
 * Provides functions for listing and controlling brew services
 * (start/stop/restart), backed by `brew services`.
 */

import { ParseError } from "../errors";
import { actionsLogger, fetchLogger } from "../logger";
import { execBrew } from "./commands";

/**
 * A brew service status as reported by `brew services list`.
 *
 * Known values include "started", "stopped", "none", "error", "scheduled",
 * "other" and "unknown", but brew may report others so this stays a string.
 */
export type ServiceStatus =
  | "started"
  | "stopped"
  | "none"
  | "error"
  | "scheduled"
  | "other"
  | "unknown"
  | (string & {});

/**
 * A brew service, as returned by `brew services list --json`.
 */
export interface Service {
  name: string;
  status: ServiceStatus;
  /** User the service runs as, or null when not running. */
  user: string | null;
  /** Path to the service's plist file. */
  file: string;
  /** Exit code of the last run, or null when unavailable. */
  exit_code: number | null;
}

/** Sentinel used by brew to target every service. */
export const ALL_SERVICES = "--all";

/**
 * Fetch the list of brew services.
 *
 * Uses the JSON output for robust parsing.
 */
export async function brewFetchServices(cancel?: AbortSignal): Promise<Service[]> {
  fetchLogger.log("Fetching brew services");
  const result = await execBrew("services list --json", cancel ? { signal: cancel } : undefined);

  const stdout = result.stdout.trim();
  if (stdout.length === 0) {
    return [];
  }

  try {
    const services = JSON.parse(stdout) as Service[];
    fetchLogger.log("Fetched brew services", { count: services.length });
    return services;
  } catch (err) {
    fetchLogger.error("Failed to parse brew services output", { error: `${err}` });
    throw new ParseError("Failed to parse brew services output", { cause: err as Error });
  }
}
```

```text
use std::collections::HashMap;

use chrono::{DateTime, Local};
use handlebars::{Handlebars, RenderError};
use pueue_lib::{
    Settings, Task, TaskResult, TaskStatus,
    log::{get_log_path, read_last_log_file_lines},
};

use crate::{
    daemon::internal_state::state::LockedState, internal_prelude::*,
    process_helper::compile_shell_command,
};

/// Users can specify a callback that's fired whenever a task finishes.
/// The callback is performed by spawning a new subprocess.
pub fn spawn_callback(settings: &Settings, state: &mut LockedState, task: &Task) {
    // Return early, if there's no callback specified
    let Some(template_string) = &settings.daemon.callback else {
        return;
    };

    // Build the command to be called from the template string in the configuration file.
    let callback_command = match build_callback_command(settings, state, task, template_string) {
        Ok(callback_command) => callback_command,
        Err(err) => {
            error!("Failed to create callback command from template with error: {err}");
            return;
        }
    };

    let mut command = compile_shell_command(settings, &callback_command);

    // Spawn the callback subprocess and log if it fails.
    let spawn_result = command.spawn();
    let child = match spawn_result {
        Err(error) => {
            error!("Failed to spawn callback with error: {error}");
            return;
        }
        Ok(child) => child,
    };

    debug!("Spawned callback for task {}", task.id);
    state.callbacks.push(child);
}

/// Take the callback template string from the configuration and insert all parameters from the
/// finished task.
pub fn build_callback_command(
    settings: &Settings,
    state: &mut LockedState,
    task: &Task,
    template_string: &str,
) -> Result<String, RenderError> {
    // Init Handlebars. We set to strict, as we want to show an error on missing variables.
    let mut handlebars = Handlebars::new();
    handlebars.set_strict_mode(true);
    handlebars.register_escape_fn(handlebars::no_escape);

    // Add templating variables.
    let mut parameters = HashMap::new();
    parameters.insert("id", task.id.to_string());
    parameters.insert("command", task.command.clone());
    parameters.insert("path", (*task.path.to_string_lossy()).to_owned());

    // Add group information to template
    // This includes how many stashed and queued tasks are left in the group.
    parameters.insert("group", task.group.clone());
    let queued_tasks = state
        .filter_tasks_of_group(Task::is_queued, &task.group)
        .matching_ids
        .len();
    parameters.insert("queued_count", queued_tasks.to_string());
    let stashed_tasks = state
        .filter_tasks_of_group(|task| task.is_stashed(), &task.group)
        .matching_ids
        .len();
    parameters.insert("stashed_count", stashed_tasks.to_string());

    // Result takes the TaskResult Enum strings, unless it didn't finish yet.
    if let TaskStatus::Done { result, .. } = &task.status {
        parameters.insert("result", result.to_string());
    } else {
        parameters.insert("result", "None".into());
    }

    // Format and insert start and end times.
    let print_time = |time: Option<DateTime<Local>>| {
        time.map(|time| time.timestamp().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default()
    };
    let (start, end) = task.start_and_end();
    parameters.insert("start", print_time(start));
    parameters.insert("end", print_time(end));

    // Read the last lines of the process' output and make it available.
    if let Ok(output) = read_last_log_file_lines(
        task.id,
        &settings.shared.pueue_directory(),
        settings.daemon.callback_log_lines,
    ) {
        parameters.insert("output", output);
    } else {
        parameters.insert("output", "".to_string());
    }

    let out_path = get_log_path(task.id, &settings.shared.pueue_directory());
    // Using Display impl of PathBuf which isn't necessarily a perfect
    // representation of the path but should work for most cases here
    parameters.insert("output_path", out_path.display().to_string());

    // Get the exit code

        match result {
            TaskResult::Success => parameters.insert("exit_code", "0".into()),
            TaskResult::Failed(code) => parameters.insert("exit_code", code.to_string()),
            _ => parameters.insert("exit_code", "None".into()),
        };
```

```text
/// Look at all running callbacks and check if they're still running.
/// Handle finished callbacks and log their outcome.
pub fn check_callbacks(state: &mut LockedState) {
    let mut finished = Vec::new();
    for (id, child) in state.callbacks.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        match child.try_wait() {
            // Handle a child error.
            Err(error) => {
                error!("Callback failed with error {error:?}");
                finished.push(id);
            }
            // Child process did not exit yet.
            Ok(None) => continue,
            Ok(exit_status) => {
                info!("Callback finished with exit code {exit_status:?}");
                finished.push(id);
            }
        }
    }
```

```text
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use chrono::{DateTime, Local, LocalResult};
use pueue_lib::{
    Client,
    settings::Settings,
    state::{PUEUE_DEFAULT_GROUP, State},
    task::Task,
};

use crate::{
    client::{commands::get_state, display_helper::get_group_headline, style::OutputStyle},
    internal_prelude::*,
};

mod query;
mod table_builder;

use query::apply_query;
use table_builder::TableBuilder;

/// Simply request and print the state.
pub async fn state(
    client: &mut Client,
    settings: Settings,
    style: &OutputStyle,
    query: Vec<String>,
    json: bool,
    group: Option<String>,
) -> Result<()> {
    let state = get_state(client).await?;
    let tasks = state.tasks.values().cloned().collect();

    let output = print_state(state, tasks, style, &settings, json, group, Some(query))?;
    println!("{output}");

    Ok(())
}

/// Get the output for the state of the daemon in a nicely formatted table.
/// If there are multiple groups, each group with a task will have its own table.
///
/// We pass the tasks as a separate parameter and as a list.
/// This allows us to print the tasks in the order passed to the `format-status` subcommand.
fn print_state(
    mut state: State,
    mut tasks: Vec<Task>,
    style: &OutputStyle,
    settings: &Settings,
    json: bool,
    group: Option<String>,
    query: Option<Vec<String>>,
) -> Result<String> {
    let mut output = String::new();

    let mut table_builder = TableBuilder::new(settings, style);

    if let Some(query) = &query {
        let query_result = apply_query(&query.join(" "), &group)?;
        table_builder.set_visibility_by_rules(&query_result.selected_columns);
        tasks = query_result.apply_filters(tasks);
        tasks = query_result.order_tasks(tasks);
        tasks = query_result.limit_tasks(tasks);
    }

    // If the json flag is specified, print the state as json and exit.
    if json {
        if query.is_some() {
            state.tasks = tasks.into_iter().map(|task| (task.id, task)).collect();
        }
        output.push_str(&serde_json::to_string(&state).unwrap());
        return Ok(output);
    }

    if let Some(group) = group {
        print_single_group(state, tasks, style, group, table_builder, &mut output);
        return Ok(output);
    }

    print_all_groups(state, tasks, style, table_builder, &mut output);

/// Print some log output in JSON serialized form.
///
/// If the log isn't read from the disk but rather received from the daemon, we have to
/// convert the received [TaskLogResponse] into a proper JSON serializable format.
/// Output in [TaskLogResponse], is usually compressed, so we need to decompress it first.
pub fn print_log_json(
    task_log_messages: BTreeMap<usize, TaskLogResponse>,
    settings: &Settings,
    lines: Option<usize>,
) {
    let mut tasks: BTreeMap<usize, Task> = BTreeMap::new();
    let mut task_log: BTreeMap<usize, String> = BTreeMap::new();
    for (id, message) in task_log_messages {
        tasks.insert(id, message.task);

        if settings.client.read_local_logs {
            let output = get_local_log(settings, id, lines);
            task_log.insert(id, output);
        } else {
            let output = get_remote_log(message.output);
            task_log.insert(id, output);
        }
    }

    // Now assemble the final struct that will be returned
    let mut json = BTreeMap::new();
    for (id, mut task) in tasks {
        let (id, output) = task_log.remove_entry(&id).unwrap();
```

# TOPIC A — Raycast: what "widget" options actually exist

## A1. Does Raycast have a "widget" concept? **No — not for extensions.**

I queried the live Raycast docs directly (GitBook `?ask=` endpoint, which searches the current docs corpus) with "Is there a widget surface for Raycast extensions?". The docs answered:

> "widgets or arbitrary *desktop surfaces*" — [docs response, developers.raycast.com/information/manifest](https://developers.raycast.com/information/manifest) (the docs report they cannot find any page describing these)

and confirmed the complete list of extension entry points:

> "No — there is no separate 'widget' surface described in the docs. The closest thing is a menu-bar command using a 'Menu Bar Extra' UI."

### The complete, exhaustive list of extension entry points (2026)

| Entry point | Manifest declaration | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **View command** | `"mode": "view"` | "A value of `view` indicates that the command will show a main view when performed." ([manifest](https://developers.raycast.com/information/manifest)) |
| **No-view command** | `"mode": "no-view"` | "`no-view` means that the command does not push a view to the main navigation stack in Raycast." ([manifest](https://developers.raycast.com/information/manifest)) |
| **Menu bar command** | `"mode": "menu-bar"` | "`menu-bar` indicates that this command will return a Menu Bar Extra" ([manifest](https://developers.raycast.com/information/manifest)) — **macOS only**: "Menubar commands aren't available on Windows." ([menu-bar-commands](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/menu-bar-commands)) |
| **AI Tools** | `"tools": [...]` array | "Tools don't show up in root search and users can't directly interact with them." Invoked by Raycast AI. ([getting-started docs response](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/getting-started)) |
| **Script Commands** | separate repo, metadata comments | Shell/Python/etc. scripts, not TS extensions. ([raycast/script-commands](https://github.com/raycast/script-commands)) |

**That's it.** There is no:
- Desktop widget surface
- macOS Notification Center / Control Center widget API for extensions
- "Live Activity"-style surface
- Raycast Companion / Sidebar API
- Floating-window API for extensions

### What the "widget" search results actually were (all red herrings)

- **[Raycast Manual — Widgets & Controls](https://manual.raycast.com/ios/widgets-and-controls)** — this is **iOS only** (home screen / lock screen / Control Center widgets for the Raycast iOS app). Not an extension surface, not macOS.
- **[ZoranJambor/raycast-extension-show-widgets-on-desktop](https://github.com/ZoranJambor/raycast-extension-show-widgets-on-desktop)** — a community extension that *toggles the macOS system setting* "Show widgets on Desktop". It does not create widgets.
- **Raycast Notes** — a first-party Raycast feature (floating note window), not an extension API surface. Its own changelog stream lives at [raycast.com/changelog/windows/0-46](https://www.raycast.com/changelog/windows/0-46).
- **"Floating window"** — appears in Raycast v1.103.0 (Sept 15, 2025) as *"Floating window will now follow the current space"*, referring to Raycast Notes' own floating window, not an extension API. ([raycast.com/changelog](https://www.raycast.com/changelog))

### 2026 Raycast news — nothing widget-shaped shipped for extensions

**["The New Raycast" (May 14, 2026)](https://www.raycast.com/blog/the-new-raycast)** — ground-up macOS rebuild, public beta. New things announced:
- Visual refresh for macOS Tahoe ("Liquid Glass")
- Root Search expanded to files/folders/contacts (custom indexer)
- Built-in global dictation
- Hotkey recorder improvements (single-tap modifiers, L/R modifiers)
- AI revamp: Quick AI + AI Chat share a composer; local "skills"; AI Profile; GPT-5.4 mini free in beta
- Window Management: new **"Toggle Grid Overlay"** command (a desktop overlay, but a *first-party window-management command*, not an extension API)
- Tags for Snippets/Quicklinks/AI Commands, Clipboard History format preservation, Translator custom commands, redesigned Settings
- Missing in beta: Cloud Sync; still forthcoming: larger fonts, local LLMs

**[Glaze (July 1, 2026)](https://alternativeto.net/news/2026/7/raycast-launches-glaze-a-new-ai-tool-for-creating-custom-desktop-apps-from-prompts/)** — "an AI tool for creating custom desktop apps from prompts". This is a *separate product*, not a widget system for extensions. (The canonical blog URL `raycast.com/blog/glaze` 404'd for me; only the third-party writeup was reachable.)

> ⚠️ **Caveat on freshness:** the [developer API changelog](https://developers.raycast.com/misc/changelog) returned entries only through **1.103.0 (2025-09-15)** on fetch, and [raycast.com/changelog](https://www.raycast.com/changelog) returned no 2026 entries. This may be caching in the fetch layer rather than genuine absence. The live `?ask=` docs query (which does hit current content) independently confirmed no widget surface exists, so the conclusion holds, but if you want belt-and-braces, re-check the changelog manually.

### AI Extensions are Pro-gated

> "To use AI APIs or AI Extensions, you need to subscribe to [Raycast Pro](https://raycast.com/pro)."
> — [developers.raycast.com/ai/getting-started](https://developers.raycast.com/ai/getting-started)

Tools were introduced in **API 1.93.0 (2025-02-26)**: *"They turn a regular extension into an AI Extension."* Tool preferences added in **1.94.0 (2025-03-19)** (also: Node 22 / React 19). ([API changelog](https://developers.raycast.com/misc/changelog))

Adding a tool: *"edit the `package.json` file manually and add a new entry to the `tools` array"*; *"The description is passed to AI to help it understand how to use the tool."* ([create-an-ai-extension](https://developers.raycast.com/ai/create-an-ai-extension))

## A2. Menu Bar Commands in depth

Source: [developers.raycast.com/api-reference/menu-bar-commands](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/menu-bar-commands)

### Component tree
- `MenuBarExtra` — root. Returning `null` removes the item from the menu bar. *"`menu-bar` commands don't always need to return a `MenuBarExtra`."*
- `MenuBarExtra.Item` — `title` (required), `icon`, `subtitle`, `tooltip`, `onAction`, `shortcut`, `alternate`
- `MenuBarExtra.Submenu` — `title` (required), `icon`, `children`. Submenus with no children render **disabled**.
- `MenuBarExtra.Section` — `title` (optional), `children`; inserts a separator.
- `MenuBarExtra.Separator`

### MenuBarExtra props
- `icon: Image.ImageLike` — the menu bar image
- `title: string` — **the text displayed in the menu bar** (this is how you show a badge/count — see below)
- `tooltip: string` — hover text
- `isLoading: boolean` — *"Indicates to Raycast that it should not unload the command, as it is still executing."*

### Badge/count: there is no badge API — you use `title`

There is no dedicated badge or count property. The idiomatic pattern (used by the first-party-adjacent Brew extension) is to put the count in `title` and pass `undefined` when zero, which hides the text entirely:

```tsx
<MenuBarExtra
  icon={MENU_ICON}
  title={running.length > 0 ? `${running.length}` : undefined}
  tooltip="Homebrew Services"
  isLoading={isLoading}
>
```
— [extensions/brew/src/services-menu.tsx](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/blob/main/extensions/brew/src/services-menu.tsx)

### Title length limits — soft guidance only, no hard number

> "avoid setting long titles in `MenuBarExtra`, `MenuBarExtra.Submenu` or `MenuBarExtra.Item`"

Also, macOS itself may hide your item:

> macOS ultimately decides whether an extra is shown; many items may cause the OS to hide some icons.

### Alternate item constraints (verbatim)

> "The `alternate` item may not have a custom shortcut."
> "The `alternate` item may not also specify an alternate."
> "A parent item that provides an `alternate` may not use ⌥ (opt) as a modifier."

### `MenuBarExtra.ActionEvent`
`onAction` receives an event whose `type` is `"left-click"` or `"right-click"`.

### Lifecycle — the 5 events that place/refresh the item

1. **From root search** — Raycast loads and runs the command; waits for `isLoading` to become `false`, then may unload. *"Same as any other commands, `menu-bar` commands can be run directly from Raycast's root search."*
2. **At the set interval** — *"Raycast will run the command at set intervals."* Detect via `environment.launchType`.
3. **When the user clicks the menu bar icon** — *"Raycast will load the command code, execute it and keep it in memory while the menu is open."* It unloads when the menu closes or an item is clicked.
4. **When Raycast restarts** — ⚠️ crucial: *"that item will be restored from Raycast's database - *not* by loading and executing the command."* So the last-rendered title/icon is what you see until the next interval fires.
5. **When the command is re-enabled in preferences** — *"This case should work the same as when Raycast is restarted."*

### The `isLoading` contract (verbatim, marked "danger" in the docs)

> "it *must* either not set `isLoading` - in which case Raycast will render and immediately unload the command,"
> "or set it to `true` while it's performing an async task (such as an API call) and then set it to `false` once it's done."

### Best practices (verbatim)

> "make generous use of the [Cache API] and our [Utilities] in order to provide quick feedback"
> "make sure you set `isLoading` to false when your command finishes executing"
> "don't put identical `MenuBarExtra.Item`s at the same level (direct children of `MenuBarExtra` or in the same `Submenu`) as their `onAction` handlers will not be executed correctly"

## A3. `interval` / background refresh

Sources: [background-refresh](https://developers.raycast.com/information/lifecycle/background-refresh), [manifest](https://developers.raycast.com/information/manifest)

### Which modes support it

> "Raycast supports scheduling commands with mode `no-view` and `menu-bar`."

`view` commands **cannot** be scheduled.

### ⚠️ The two docs pages disagree on the minimum interval

| Page | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| [background-refresh](https://developers.raycast.com/information/lifecycle/background-refresh) | "The minimum value is 10 seconds (`10s`), which should be used cautiously, also see the section on best practices." |
| [manifest](https://developers.raycast.com/information/manifest) | "every X seconds (s), minutes (m), hours (h) or days (d)." … "The minimum value is 1 minute (1m)." |

I re-queried both pages independently via the live `?ask=` endpoint and got the same contradictory answers, so this is a genuine docs inconsistency, not a fetch artifact. **Treat `1m` as the safe floor** (that's what the manifest validator documents, and it's what the Brew extension ships with). Format examples given: `90s`, `1m`, `10m`, `12h`, `1d`.

### Scheduling is NOT exact

> "Note that the actual scheduling is not exact and might vary within a tolerance level."

macOS varies the times to optimize energy/battery.

### Time budget — yes, there is one, and it's dynamic

> "To prevent overlapping background launches of the same command, commands are terminated after a timeout that is dynamically adjusted to the interval."
> "Raycast auto-terminates the command if it exceeds its maximum execution time."

Execution model:
- **`no-view`**: runs until the main async function's Promise resolves.
- **`menu-bar`**: the React component runs until `isLoading` is set to `false`. **Yes, the whole React tree re-runs on every background tick.**

### Does it run when Raycast's window is closed? Yes.

> Commands run in background without the user manually opening them.

This is the entire point — background refresh drives the menu bar item while the main Raycast window is shut. It runs inside Raycast's managed Node child process, not launchd directly (Raycast.app itself is the launchd-launched process).

### Background refresh is OFF by default for store installs

> "When a user installs the command via the Store, background refresh is initially *disabled* and is activated either when the user opens the command for the first time or enables background refresh in preferences."

This is a significant UX consideration: **a freshly-installed menu bar command will not appear until the user runs it once.**

### Detecting a background run

```ts
console.log("launchType", environment.launchType);  // LaunchType.Background | LaunchType.UserInitiated
```

### Passing data from the background run to the UI

**Cache API** — [developers.raycast.com/api-reference/cache](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/cache)
```ts
constructor(options: Cache.Options): Cache
get(key: string): string | undefined
has(key: string): boolean
set(key: string, data: string)
remove(key: string): boolean
clear((options = { notifySubscribers: true }));
subscribe(subscriber: Cache.Subscriber): Cache.Subscription
```
- Disk-backed LRU with an in-memory index. `Cache.Options`: `namespace?: string` (isolate per-command), `capacity?: number` (**default 10 MB**, LRU-evicts beyond).
- Values must be strings — `JSON.stringify` yourself.
- Shared across an extension's commands by default.
- `Cache.Subscriber` receives `(key: string | undefined, data: string | undefined)`.
- Note API 1.89.0 (2025-01-15): *"Clearing the cache will now delete all the files"* inside the folder rather than the folder itself.

**LocalStorage API** — [developers.raycast.com/api-reference/storage](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/storage)
```ts
async function getItem(key: string): Promise<Value | undefined>;
async function setItem(key: string, value: Value): Promise<void>;
async function removeItem(key: string): Promise<void>;
async function allItems(): Promise<Values>;
async function clear(): Promise<void>;
// Value = string | number | boolean
```
> "All commands in an extension have shared access to the stored data. Extensions can *not* access the storage of other extensions."
> "The API is not meant to store large amounts of data. For this, use Node's built-in APIs to write files."

### Defensive programming warning

> If commands share state, use defensive programming to handle errors, data races, incomplete or inaccessible stored state.

## A4. `launchCommand`, `updateCommandMetadata`, `showHUD`, `showToast`, `confirmAlert`, `Clipboard`, `open`

### `launchCommand` — [api-reference/command](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/command)
```ts
export async function launchCommand(options: LaunchOptions): Promise<void>;
```
- Throws if the command is missing or disabled. Cross-extension launches show a **user permission prompt**.
- Resolves when launched, **not** when the target completes.
- `IntraExtensionLaunchOptions`: `name` (required), `type: LaunchType` (required), `arguments?`, `context?` (JSON-serializable; Dates & Buffers supported), `fallbackText?`
- `InterExtensionLaunchOptions`: adds `extensionName` + `ownerOrAuthorName` (both required)
- Documented use case: *"forcing background refreshes"* — i.e. after an action, kick the menu bar command to re-run.

Real-world usage in the Brew menu bar command: it imports `launchCommand` and `LaunchType` alongside `MenuBarExtra` ([services-menu.tsx](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/blob/main/extensions/brew/src/services-menu.tsx)).

### `updateCommandMetadata` — the subtitle-on-root-search trick
```ts
export async function updateCommandMetadata(metadata: { subtitle?: string | null }): Promise<void>;
```
> "The actual manifest file is not modified, so the update applies as long as the command remains installed."

Only `subtitle` is updatable today; pass `null` to clear. Canonical example from the background-refresh docs:
```ts
await updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle: `Unread Notifications: ${count}` });
```

### `showHUD` — [api-reference/feedback/hud](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/feedback/hud)
```ts
async function showHUD(title: string, options?: { clearRootSearch?: boolean; popToRootType?: PopToRootType }): Promise<void>
```
> "showHUD closes the main window when called, so you can use the same options as `closeMainWindow`."

This is the right feedback primitive for menu bar item actions (Brew uses exactly this: `await showHUD(\`${copy.past} ${target}\`)`).

### `showToast` — [api-reference/feedback/toast](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/feedback/toast)
```ts
async function showToast(options: Toast.Options): Promise<Toast>
```
> "Creates and shows a Toast with the given [options]."
> "The `showToast()` will fallback to [showHUD()] if the Raycast window is closed."

- `Toast.Options`: `title` (required), `message?`, `style?`, `primaryAction?`, `secondaryAction?`
- `Toast.Style`: `Animated`, `Success`, `Failure`
- `Toast` instance: `.hide()`, `.show()`, mutable `.style` / `.title` / `.message`
- `Toast.ActionOptions`: `title` (required), `onAction: (toast: Toast) => void` (required), `shortcut?`

**Important for menu bar work:** because of the HUD fallback, `showToast` is safe to call from a menu-bar command even when the main window is closed.

### `confirmAlert` — [api-reference/feedback/alert](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/feedback/alert)
```ts
async function confirmAlert(options: Alert.Options): Promise<boolean>;
```
- `Alert.Options`: `title` (required), `message?`, `icon?`, `primaryAction?`, `dismissAction?`, `rememberUserChoice?`
- `rememberUserChoice: true` shows "Do not show this message again" and persists the answer
- `Alert.ActionStyle`: *"Use Alert.ActionStyle.Default for confirmations of a positive action."* / *"Use Alert.ActionStyle.Destructive for confirmations of a destructive action (eg. deleting a file)."*
- Returns `true` for primary action, `false` for dismiss

### `Clipboard` — [api-reference/clipboard](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/clipboard)
```ts
async function copy(content: string | number | Content, options?: CopyOptions): Promise<void>;
async function paste(content: string | Content): Promise<void>;
async function clear(): Promise<void>;
async function read(options?: { offset?: number }): Promise<ReadContent>;
async function readText(options?: { offset?: number }): Promise<string | undefined>;
```

### `open` — [api-reference/utilities](https://developers.raycast.com/api-reference/utilities)
```ts
async function open(target: string, application?: Application | string): Promise<void>;
```
`target` = file, folder, or URL. `application` = app name, bundle id, or absolute app path.

## A5. Store rules for extensions requiring a user-installed CLI + running daemon

Source: [developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store)

### Verbatim guideline text

> "Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads and try to automate as much as possible from the extension,"
> "especially if you are targeting non-developers."
> "See the [Speedtest](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/pull/302) extension that downloads a CLI in the background"
> "If you do end up downloading executable binaries in the background, please make sure it's done from a server"
> "that you don't have access to."
> "Otherwise, we cannot guarantee that you won't replace the binary with malicious code after the review."
> "Add additional integrity checks through hashes."
> "Don't bundle opaque binaries where sources are unavailable or where it's unclear how they have been built."
> "Don't bundle heavy binary dependencies in the extension – this would lead to an increased extension download size."

### "Examples for interacting with binaries" (verbatim bullets)

> "✅ Calling known system binaries"
> "✅ Binary downloaded or installed from a trusted location with additional integrity checking through hashes"
> "(that is, verify whether the downloaded binary really matches the expected binary)"
> "✅ Binary extracted from an npm package and copied to assets, with traceable sources how the binary is built;"
> "❌ Any binary with unavailable sources or unclear builds just added to the assets folder"

**Interpretation for a Pueue extension:** "✅ Calling known system binaries" is the relevant lane — calling a user's already-installed `pueue`/`pueued` from Homebrew is explicitly sanctioned. The "avoid asking users to perform additional downloads" clause is soft guidance ("try to", "especially if you are targeting non-developers") and is clearly not enforced as a hard rule, given the precedent extensions below all require pre-installed CLIs.

### Precedent: extensions in the store that wrap a local daemon/CLI

I enumerated `raycast/extensions/extensions/*` via the GitHub API. **Present:** `brew`, `docker`, `colima`, `orbstack`, `yabai`. **Absent:** `ollama`, `lima`, `podman`, `homebrew`.

| Extension | Author | Commands | Menu bar? | How it finds the binary / detects "down" |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[Brew](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/tree/main/extensions/brew)** | `nhojb` | `installed`, `search`, `outdated`, `upgrade`, `manage-services` (all `view`), **`services-menu` (`menu-bar`, `interval: 1m`)**, `clean-up`, `clear-cache` (`no-view`) | ✅ **Yes** — the single best precedent | 3-tier resolution in [`utils/brew/paths.ts`](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/blob/main/extensions/brew/src/utils/brew/paths.ts): (1) `customBrewPath` preference; (2) `execSync("brew --prefix")`; (3) arch-based fallback `/opt/homebrew` (Apple CPU) vs `/usr/local`. Then `brewExecutable() = brewPath("bin/brew")` — **calls the absolute path**, never bare `brew`. Parses `brew services list --json`. Has a typed error taxonomy incl. `BrewNotFoundError`. |
| **[Docker](https://www.raycast.com/priithaamer/docker)** | `priithaamer` (45,631 installs) | `container_list`, `projects_list`, `image_list` — all `view` | ❌ No | Uses **`@priithaamer/dockerode`** (a fork of dockerode) — talks to the **Docker socket directly**, no CLI shell-out. |
| **[Colima](https://www.raycast.com/MiskaMyasa/colima)** | `MiskaMyasa` (Denis Zaitsev) | `list-instances`, `list-containers`, `list-images`, `pull-image`, `run-container` — all `view` | ❌ No | *"checks for both dependencies on launch and shows installation links if anything is missing"*. Requires Colima (`brew install colima`) + Docker CLI (`brew install docker`). **Zero preferences** — relies on default PATH. Shows per-instance "status, CPU, memory, disk, runtime, and architecture". |
| **[OrbStack](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/tree/main/extensions/orbstack)** | `nicholasq` | `machine_list`, `machine_create` — both `view` | ❌ No | Plain `@raycast/api` + `@raycast/utils`, shells out to `orb`. |
| **[Yabai](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/tree/main/extensions/yabai)** | `krzysztoff1` | 30+ commands, mostly `no-view`; **`screens-menu-bar` (`menu-bar`, no interval)**; incl. `start`/`stop`/`restart` for the daemon itself | ✅ Yes (no interval — refreshes only on click/root-search) | Uses **`execa`**. Exposes a preference: `yabaiPath` — *"Location to the Yabai installation (Defaults to `/opt/homebrew/bin/yabai` on M1 Macs, and `/usr/local/bin/yabai` otherwise)"* |

**Pattern to copy:** Brew's `paths.ts` (preference → `--prefix` probe → arch fallback → always invoke absolute path) is the most robust precedent, and its `services-menu` is a near-exact structural analogue of a Pueue menu bar command (poll on `interval`, `title` = count of running items, optimistic `mutate` after each action, `showHUD` for feedback).

Note the Brew menu bar file's own header comment, which describes exactly the constraint a Pueue extension faces:

> "Homebrew has no way to notify us when a service's state changes, so the menu is kept fresh by polling on the command's `interval` (configurable in the command preferences) and by an optimistic `mutate` after each action."

Also notable: Brew makes the interval **user-configurable via command preferences**, which is a good pattern.

## A6. Known issues with menu bar commands

### PATH — the single biggest gotcha

Raycast extensions run in a *"managed child Node.js process"* ([store docs response](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store)). The docs **do not document what `PATH` contains** — I asked the live docs directly and got: *"I cannot find information about the **exact `PATH` contents**"*.

Empirically, it's broken:
- **[raycast/extensions#170 — "[API Bug] env.PATH is undefined"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/170)** — extensions do not reliably receive `PATH`.
- **[Stack Overflow — "Running Custom Bash Script Works in Terminal But Not RayCast"](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76451345/running-custom-bash-script-works-in-terminal-but-not-raycast)** — Raycast (non-interactive GUI context) lacks the interactive shell's PATH, so Homebrew binaries in `/opt/homebrew/bin` are simply not found.
- **[apple.stackexchange — GUI apps and launchd PATH](https://apple.stackexchange.com/questions/51305/executables-in-bin-and-usr-bin-are-not-found-in-path)** — macOS GUI apps inherit environment from launchd, not shell rc files.
- **[Node child_process docs](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)** — `spawn` fails `ENOENT` if the command isn't in the spawned process's PATH; it uses `options.env.PATH` or `process.env.PATH`, falling back to `/usr/bin:/bin`.

**Workaround used by real extensions:** absolute paths (Brew), or an explicit path preference (Yabai). Both.

### CPU / memory / battery

- **[#22995 — "[Music] Currently Playing Track background refresh memory ..."](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/22995)** — background refresh causing growing memory per run.
- **[#22946 — "Coffee Extension consumes a lot of RAM and CPU and has memory ..."](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/22946)** — high RAM/CPU, memory-leak behaviour.
- Docs guidance: prefer larger intervals to reduce energy use; set `isLoading` false as early as possible.

### Menu bar item not updating / stuck

- **[#20031 — "[Battery Menu Bar] ... Not updating"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/20031)**
- **[#14659 — "[Todoist] 'Menu Bar Tasks' fails in background reload"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/14659)**
- **[#14250 — "Menu bar icon stuck"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/14250)** (plus #14248, #14251) — icons persisting/not disappearing. Root cause is architectural: lifecycle event #4 means the item is **restored from Raycast's database, not by re-running the command**, so a stale render can survive restarts. Typical workarounds reported: quit/restart Raycast, disable/re-enable the command, remove the dev-installed extension.

### Development
- There's a *"run in background"* action exposed in dev mode to test interval-scheduled commands, plus a "show full errors" debugging action.
- The menu bar item persisting after `ray develop` stops is a manifestation of the same DB-restore behaviour; no documented clean teardown.

### Max refresh frequency
Governed by `interval` (see the 10s vs 1m contradiction above) plus macOS's energy-driven tolerance jitter plus the dynamic termination timeout. There is no documented hard ceiling on frequency other than the minimum interval.

# TOPIC B — Pueue

## B7. What Pueue is, version, core concepts

**Repo:** [github.com/Nukesor/pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) — Apache-2.0, **6,272 stars**, last push 2026-07-18 (very much alive).

**Current version: v4.0.4, released 2026-03-02.** ([GitHub releases](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases)) Tag history: v4.0.4, v4.0.3, v4.0.2 (2025-12-19), v4.0.1 (2025-07-07), v4.0.0, v4.0.0-rc.{1,2,3}, then v3.4.1 … v3.0.0. Companion crate **pueue-lib v0.31.0** published 2026-03-01.

> ⚠️ The `raw.githubusercontent.com` README fetch returned a **stale/cached v2.0.0** copy. Trust the releases API (v4.0.4), not that README header.

**Description:** *"Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks."* — *"a tool that processes a queue of shell commands."* The project declares itself *"feature-complete 🎉"*.

**Explicitly out of scope** (per README): distributed/multi-user job scheduling, heavy programmatic scheduling, tight system integration.

### Core concepts

- **Tasks** — a shell command run by the daemon. Pueue runs your input as `sh -c $command` in the background (see Pitfalls below). Tasks carry: id, created_at, original_command, command, path (cwd), envs, group, dependencies, priority, label, status. Environment variables are captured at `add` time.
- **Groups** ([wiki/Groups](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Groups)) — *"Grouping tasks can be useful, whenever your tasks utilize different system resources."* *"If no group is specified, the task will just be added to the default queue."* Each group has its **own parallelism limit** and its **own Running/Paused state**. Commands: `pueue group add <name>` / `pueue group remove <name>` / `pueue group` / `pueue add -g <group> -- '<cmd>'` / `pueue parallel -g <group> <n>` / `pueue status --group <NAME>` / `pueue pause -g <group>` / `pueue start -g <group>`.
- **Parallelism** — `pueue parallel 3` globally, or `-g <group>`. Env vars `PUEUE_WORKER_ID` and `PUEUE_GROUP` are injected into tasks so you can map workers to external resources (e.g. GPU indices).
- **Dependencies** — `pueue add --after/-a <ids>`. A task runs only if its dependencies succeeded; otherwise it gets `TaskResult::DependencyFailed`. Wiki recommends `pause_on_failure` to avoid cascading failures, and restarting with `--in-place`.
- **Labels** — `label: Option<String>` on each task.
- **Priorities** — `priority: i32` on each task.
- **Statuses** — see B8.
- **Stashing** — tasks can be stashed (not queued) and later enqueued; optionally with a scheduled `enqueue_at` time.

### Basic commands ([wiki/Get-started](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Get-started))
`pueued` / `pueued -d` (daemonize) / `pueue shutdown` / `pueue add` / `pueue status` (or bare `pueue`) / `pueue log [id]` / `pueue follow $id` (`-e` for stderr) / `pueue pause` / `pueue start` / `pueue kill` / `pueue restart` / `pueue stash` / `pueue enqueue` / `pueue send` / `pueue parallel N` / `pueue wait` / `pueue clean` / `pueue reset` / `pueue edit` / `pueue switch` / `pueue env` / `pueue remove` / `pueue format-status` / `pueue completions $shell $dir`.

Most commands accept multiple IDs or shell ranges: `pueue log 0 1 2 3 15 19`, `pueue log {0..3}`.

## B8. The JSON / machine-readable interface

### Which commands support `--json` — exactly three

From [`pueue/src/client/cli.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/cli.rs), all with `#[arg(short, long)] json: bool`:

| Subcommand | Doc comment (verbatim from source) |
|---|---|
| `status` | `/// Print the current state as json to stdout.` `/// This does not include the output of tasks.` `/// Use \`log -j\` if you want everything.` |
| `log` | `/// Print the resulting tasks and output as json.` `/// By default only the last lines will be returned unless --full is provided.` `/// Take care, as the json cannot be streamed!` `/// If your logs are really huge, using --full can use all of your machine's RAM.` |
| `group` | `/// Print the list of groups as json.` |

There is also `pueue format-status`, which takes JSON on stdin and renders the human table — e.g. `pueue status --json | jq -c '.tasks' | pueue format-status` ([wiki/Advanced-usage](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Advanced-usage)).

### `pueue status --json` returns the whole `State`, serialized with `serde_json`

From [`pueue/src/client/commands/state/mod.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/commands/state/mod.rs):
```rust
// If the json flag is specified, print the state as json and exit.
if json {
    if query.is_some() {
        state.tasks = tasks.into_iter().map(|task| (task.id, task)).collect();
    }
    output.push_str(&serde_json::to_string(&state).unwrap());
    return Ok(output);
}
```
Note: `--query` filtering **is** applied to the JSON output (the tasks map is rebuilt from the filtered/ordered/limited set). `--group` is **not** applied to JSON — the `group` branch is only reached in the non-JSON path.

### The `State` struct ([`pueue_lib/src/state.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/state.rs))

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct State {
    pub tasks: BTreeMap<usize, Task>,
    pub groups: BTreeMap<String, Group>,
}

#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct Group {
    pub status: GroupStatus,
    pub parallel_tasks: usize,
}

#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Copy, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub enum GroupStatus {
    Running,
    Paused,
    Reset,
}
```

### The `Task` struct ([`pueue_lib/src/task.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/task.rs))

```rust
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct Task {
    pub id: usize,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Local>,
    pub original_command: String,
    pub command: String,
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub envs: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub group: String,
    pub dependencies: Vec<usize>,
    pub priority: i32,
    pub label: Option<String>,
    pub status: TaskStatus,
}
```

### `TaskStatus` — **externally tagged** (no serde attributes)

```rust
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Display, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TaskStatus {
    /// Used while the command of a task is edited (to prevent starting the task)
    Locked { previous_status: Box<TaskStatus> },
    /// The task has been manually stashed. It won't be executed until it's manually enqueued
    Stashed { enqueue_at: Option<DateTime<Local>> },
    /// The task is queued and waiting for a free slot
    Queued { enqueued_at: DateTime<Local> },
    /// The task is started and running
    Running {
        enqueued_at: DateTime<Local>,
        start: DateTime<Local>,
    },
    /// A previously running task has been paused
    Paused {
        enqueued_at: DateTime<Local>,
        start: DateTime<Local>,
    },
    /// Task finished. The actual result of the task is handled by the [TaskResult] enum.
    Done {
        enqueued_at: DateTime<Local>,
        start: DateTime<Local>,
        end: DateTime<Local>,
        result: TaskResult,
    },
}
```

I verified by grepping the file: **there are no `#[serde(tag=...)]`, `#[serde(rename=...)]` or `#[serde(untagged)]` attributes anywhere in `task.rs`.** So serde's **default externally-tagged representation** applies. Concretely the JSON is:

```jsonc
"status": { "Queued":  { "enqueued_at": "2026-07-26T10:00:00+02:00" } }
"status": { "Running": { "enqueued_at": "...", "start": "..." } }
"status": { "Paused":  { "enqueued_at": "...", "start": "..." } }
"status": { "Stashed": { "enqueue_at": null } }        // note: enqueue_at, NOT enqueued_at
"status": { "Locked":  { "previous_status": { "Queued": { "enqueued_at": "..." } } } }  // recursive!
"status": { "Done": { "enqueued_at": "...", "start": "...", "end": "...",
                      "result": "Success" } }
"status": { "Done": { ..., "result": { "Failed": 127 } } }
```

⚠️ **Trap:** `Stashed` uses `enqueue_at` (future scheduled time, nullable) while every other variant uses `enqueued_at`. Easy to typo.
⚠️ **Trap:** `Locked.previous_status` is a **recursive `TaskStatus`**, so a naive discriminated-union type must handle nesting.

### `TaskResult` — also externally tagged

```rust
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Display, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum TaskResult {
    /// Task exited with 0
    Success,
    /// The task failed in some other kind of way (error code != 0)
    Failed(i32),
    /// The task couldn't be spawned. Probably a typo in the command
    FailedToSpawn(String),
    /// Task has been actively killed by either the user or the daemon on shutdown
    Killed,
    /// Some kind of IO error. This should barely ever happen. Please check the daemon logs.
    Errored,
    /// A dependency of the task failed.
    DependencyFailed,
}
```

JSON forms: unit variants serialize as bare strings (`"Success"`, `"Killed"`, `"Errored"`, `"DependencyFailed"`); newtype variants as `{"Failed": 127}` and `{"FailedToSpawn": "…"}`.

### `pueue log --json` shape

From [`pueue/src/client/commands/log/json.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/commands/log/json.rs):
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct TaskLog {
    pub task: Task,
    pub output: String,
}
```
Emitted as a `BTreeMap<usize, TaskLog>` — i.e. `{"0": {"task": {...}, "output": "..."}}`. Output from the daemon is **snappy-compressed** (`snap::read::FrameDecoder`) and decompressed client-side; when `client.read_local_logs` is true it's read straight off disk instead.

### Breaking changes in the JSON shape — **v3 → v4 is a hard break**

From [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), v4.0.0:

> "**Breaking**: Refactor internal task state."
> "Important: This completely breaks pre v4.0 states."
> "The Pueue daemon needs to be restarted and the state will be wiped clean."
> "Send log output to `stderr` instead of `stdout`"
> "Switch `cbor` handling library, breaking backwards-compatible communication on a data format level."
> "Switch protocol message representation, completely breaking backwards compatibility."
> "Redesigned task editing process"

What changed concretely: in **v3**, `Task` had flat sibling fields (`start`, `end`, `enqueue_at`, `result`) alongside a simpler `status` enum whose variants were mostly unit-like (`"Queued"`, `"Running"`, `"Done"` etc.). In **v4** all of those timestamps and the result were **moved into the `TaskStatus` enum's variant payloads**, making every status variant a struct variant. This is why `{"Queued": {"enqueued_at": ...}}` (v4) replaces bare `"Queued"` (v3).

Also from v4: logs go to stderr, but *"JSON and task log output remain on stdout"* — good for scripting.

**There is no versioned/stable status format.** No `schema_version` field exists in `State`. The wire protocol is explicitly not backwards compatible. Any consumer must pin to v4.x semantics and detect version drift itself (the daemon does send its version during the handshake — see B9).

v3.0.0's breaking changes were behavioural, not schema-level:
> "Tasks are now started in a process group, and `pueue kill` will kill all processes in the group [#372]"
> "The `--children` cli flag has been deprecated (signals go to the whole group, always)."

## B9. Talking to the daemon directly (instead of shelling out)

**Yes — and there is a working TypeScript implementation to copy from.**

### Transport & auth ([docs/Architecture.md](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/docs/Architecture.md))

> "Listen on the daemon's socket"
> "Performs authorization (secret & certificate)"
> "send confirmation, which is also the daemon's version."
> "Receive the incoming message and deserialize it"
> "All functions used for handling client messages can be found in [daemon::network::message_handler]."

The daemon accepts **Unix domain sockets OR TLS-encrypted TCP** (one at a time, per config). Each connection spawns a tokio task. Auth is a **shared secret** read from a file + (for TCP) a self-signed cert. **The auth response body is the daemon's version string** — handy for version detection.

### Wire protocol ([`pueue_lib/src/network/protocol.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/network/protocol.rs))

- **Framing:** 8-byte **big-endian u64 length header**, then payload.
  `WriteBytesExt::write_u64::<BigEndian>(&mut header, message_size).unwrap();`
- **Chunking:** payload written in `PACKET_SIZE` = **1280**-byte chunks: `for chunk in payload.chunks(PACKET_SIZE) {`
- **Serialization: CBOR** via `ciborium` + serde — `into_writer(&message, &mut payload)` / `from_reader(payload_bytes.as_slice())`. **Not JSON.**
- **DoS guard:** `receive_bytes_with_max_size(max_size: Option<usize>)`; handshake reads are capped at ~4 MiB; warns above 20 MiB.
- Helpers: `send_request<T: Into<Request>>`, `send_response`, `receive_request`, `receive_response`.

### `Request` enum ([`pueue_lib/src/message/request.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/message/request.rs))

```rust
#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub enum Request {
    Add(AddRequest),
    Remove(Vec<usize>),
    Switch(SwitchRequest),
    Stash(StashRequest),
    Enqueue(EnqueueRequest),
    Start(StartRequest),
    Restart(RestartRequest),
    Pause(PauseRequest),
    Kill(KillRequest),
    Send(SendRequest),
    EditRequest(Vec<usize>),
    EditRestore(Vec<usize>),
    EditedTasks(Vec<EditableTask>),
    Env(EnvRequest),
    Group(GroupRequest),
    Parallel(ParallelRequest),
    /// Request the daemon's state
    Status,
    Log(LogRequest),
    Stream(StreamRequest),
    Reset(ResetRequest),
    Clean(CleanRequest),
    DaemonShutdown(ShutdownRequest),
}
```
Note `Status` is a **unit variant** → encodes as the bare CBOR string `"Status"`.

### `Response` enum ([`pueue_lib/src/message/response.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/message/response.rs))

```
AddedTask(AddedTaskResponse)   // { task_id, enqueue_at, group_is_paused }
Edit(Vec<EditableTask>)
Status(Box<State>)             // ← the whole State
Log(BTreeMap<usize, TaskLogResponse>)   // TaskLogResponse { task, output_complete, output: Option<Vec<u8>> }
Group(GroupResponse)           // { groups: BTreeMap<String, Group> }
Stream(StreamResponse)         // { logs: BTreeMap<usize, String> }
Success(String)
Failure(String)
Close
```

Note `Request::Stream` gives you a **continuous log stream** — no polling needed for `follow`-style output.

### Config keys relevant to connecting ([wiki/Configuration](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Configuration))

Config file on macOS: **`~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml`**. Override with `-c` or `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH` (CLI flag wins).

Shared section:
- `use_unix_socket: true` — *"(Unix only) Whether the daemon should listen on a Unix- or a TCP-socket."*
- `unix_socket_path: ~/.local/share/pueue/pueue_your_user.socket` — *"Defaults to `runtime_directory/pueue_$USER.socket`."* Default socket mode `0o700`.
- `host: "localhost"`, `port: "6924"`
- `daemon_cert` / `daemon_key` — TLS for TCP
- `shared_secret_path: ~/.local/share/pueue/shared_secret` — *"The path to the file, which contains the secret used for authentication with the daemon."*
- `pueue_directory: ~/.local/share/pueue`, `runtime_directory: null`
- **Profiles** are supported in one file; select with `pueue --profile remote status`.

### **No** documented JSON-RPC or HTTP interface

There is no HTTP/REST/JSON-RPC endpoint. The only interfaces are: (a) the CLI, (b) the CBOR-over-socket protocol.

### Existing TypeScript/Node client — one exists, unpublished

**[beeequeue/pueue-ui](https://github.com/beeequeue/pueue-ui)** — TypeScript, Vue + Nitro, MIT, last push **2026-07-24** (2 days ago), 1 star, "wip"/"experimental". Its `server/lib/pueued.ts` is a **complete working Node implementation of the pueue wire protocol**:

```ts
import { connect, type TLSSocket } from "node:tls"
import { decode } from "cbor-x/decode-no-eval"
import { encode } from "cbor-x/encode"

const PACKET_SIZE = 1280

const buildMessageParts = (data: Uint8Array): [Uint8Array, Uint8Array[]] => {
  const size = data.byteLength
  const header = Buffer.alloc(8)
  header.writeBigUInt64BE(BigInt(size))
  ...
}
```
Auth handshake — the secret is sent as a raw length-prefixed message and the reply is the version string:
```ts
sharedSecret ??= loadSharedSecret()
const versionBuffer = await sendMessage(socket, sharedSecret)
logger.set({ pueued: { version: new TextDecoder().decode(versionBuffer) } })
```
Status request:
```ts
const data = await sendMessage(await connection!, encode("Status"))
return decode(data).Status as PueuedStatusResponse
```

It also has hand-written TypeScript types for the v4 JSON/CBOR shape in `server/types/pueue.types.ts` (`PueuedStatusQueued`, `…Running`, `…Paused`, `…Done`, `…Stashed`, `PueuedTask`, `PueuedStatusResponse`) — these match the Rust source exactly, **except** the file has a typo `parrallel_tasks` (should be `parallel_tasks`), omits `Locked`, and models `result` as only `"Success" | { Failed: number }` (missing `FailedToSpawn`/`Killed`/`Errored`/`DependencyFailed`).

Its README carries a relevant warning:
> "one needs a tcp connection to communicate with the pueued daemon, meaning that it can't be done in the browser alone."
> "the api is completely unsafe and CANNOT not be made available over the internet, unless you want people to be able to run arbitrary commands on your machine."

Also note it uses `node:tls` + `rejectUnauthorized: false` on `127.0.0.1:6925` and loads the secret from `process.env.LOCALAPPDATA` (Windows-only path) — so it's TCP-mode and Windows-centric; a Unix-socket path would use `node:net` instead.

**There is no `pueue` package on npm.** No official or established Node client exists. Other language bindings found: `daviddwlee84/PueueWrapper` (Python), `xFA25E/pueue` (Emacs), `Mephistophiles/pueue-lib` (stale Rust fork, 2022).

## B10. Existing GUI / menu-bar / integration front-ends

### **No Raycast extension for Pueue exists.** Confirmed four ways:

1. `gh search code 'pueue repo:raycast/extensions'` → **only false positive** was a base64 substring inside `extensions/clockify/package-lock.json` (`...PueUee+d5NBRxz3Fd...` in an integrity hash). No real matches.
2. `gh search repos 'pueue raycast'` → **zero results**.
3. Raycast store search for "pueue" → *"no extension named 'pueue' and no entries matching 'task queue' or 'queue'"* ([raycast.com/store](https://www.raycast.com/store))
4. Web searches across raycast.com and GitHub → nothing. ([search confirmation](https://www.raycast.com/store))

**Conclusion: you would not be duplicating work. This would be the first Raycast extension for Pueue.**

### Menu bar / launcher tooling: essentially nothing
- **No SwiftBar plugin** for pueue (checked [swiftbar/SwiftBar](https://github.com/swiftbar/SwiftBar))
- **No xbar plugin** for pueue (checked [matryer/xbar-plugins](https://github.com/matryer/xbar-plugins))
- **No Alfred workflow** for pueue ([alfredapp.com/workflows](https://www.alfredapp.com/workflows/))
- `pueue-bar` is a 2021 empty shell

### Built-in "fuzzy TUI" shipped in the wiki
[wiki/Advanced-usage](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Advanced-usage) documents a shell function `pf` using `jq` + `fzf` + `bat`, with keybindings Ctrl-p/s/r/k/l/f for pause/start/restart/kill/log/follow, auto-reloading. This is the current de-facto interactive UX and is a useful feature-parity reference.
