## B11. Callback / hook mechanism — **yes, fully supported**

Config key: **`daemon.callback`** in `pueue.yml`. Default in the generated config:
```yaml
callback: "\"Task {{ id }}\nCommand: {{ command }}\nPath: {{ path }}\nFinished with status '{{ result }}'\""
callback_log_lines: 10
```
> *"The command that will be called after a task finishes. Can be parameterized"*
> *"The amount of stdout/stderr lines that are available in the callback."*
> — [wiki/Configuration](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Configuration)

> *"Make sure to restart the daemon after you make changes to `pueue.yml`."* — [wiki/Advanced-usage](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Advanced-usage)

### Complete templating variable list — from the source, not the docs

[`pueue/src/daemon/callbacks.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/daemon/callbacks.rs) uses **Handlebars in strict mode** (`handlebars.set_strict_mode(true)`, `register_escape_fn(no_escape)`) — so **a typo'd variable is a hard render error**, and values are not HTML-escaped. The full parameter set inserted:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `{{ id }}` | `task.id` |
| `{{ command }}` | `task.command` |
| `{{ path }}` | task cwd (lossy UTF-8) |
| `{{ group }}` | `task.group` |
| **`{{ queued_count }}`** | number of still-**queued** tasks in the same group |
| **`{{ stashed_count }}`** | number of still-**stashed** tasks in the same group |
| `{{ result }}` | `TaskResult` Display string, or `"None"` if not `Done` |
| `{{ start }}` | **Unix timestamp** as string, or `""` |
| `{{ end }}` | **Unix timestamp** as string, or `""` |
| `{{ output }}` | last `callback_log_lines` lines of the task's output (`""` on read failure) |
| **`{{ output_path }}`** | absolute path to the task's log file |
| `{{ exit_code }}` | `"0"` on Success, the code on `Failed(code)`, `"None"` otherwise |

> ⚠️ The wiki's variable list (`id, command, path, result, exit_code, group, output, start, end`) is **incomplete** — it omits `queued_count`, `stashed_count`, and `output_path`, all of which are in the source.

Execution: the callback is spawned as a **new subprocess** via `compile_shell_command(settings, &callback_command)` — i.e. it goes through the same `shell_command` config (default `["zsh", "-c", "{{ pueue_command_string }}"]` on macOS-ish setups). `check_callbacks` reaps them and logs exit codes. Callbacks fire **whenever a task finishes**.

macOS notification example from the wiki: set `callback` to an `osascript ... display notification` invocation with templated values. Multi-line callbacks can use a YAML block.

Other daemon options relevant to notifications/behaviour:
- `pause_group_on_failure: false` — pause queued tasks in the failed task's group
- `pause_all_on_failure: false` — pause everything on any failure
- `shell_command: ["zsh", "-c", "{{ pueue_command_string }}"]`
- `env_vars: {…}` — *"These variables will be injected into all tasks."*

---

## B12. Pueue on macOS

### Support level
README: macOS is *"fully supported and on par with Linux"* — Linux and macOS both described as "fully supported and battle-tested"; Windows also supported.

### Install
```
brew install pueue
```
[formulae.brew.sh/formula/pueue](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/pueue) — Homebrew has **v4.0.4**.

### Autostart — **the Homebrew formula ships a launchd service**

From [formulae.brew.sh/api/formula/pueue.json](https://formulae.brew.sh/api/formula/pueue.json):
```json
"run": ["$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/pueue/bin/pueued", "--verbose"],
"run_type": "immediate",
"keep_alive": { "always": false },
"working_dir": "$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/var",
"log_path": "$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/var/log/pueued.log",
"error_log_path": "$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/var/log/pueued.log"
```

So `brew services start pueue` works and is the standard macOS setup. Notes:
- `brew services` is a thin launchd wrapper; without `sudo` it writes to `~/Library/LaunchAgents` and starts **at user login**; with `sudo` it writes to `/Library/LaunchDaemons` and starts **at boot**. ([Homebrew discussion #4215](https://github.com/orgs/Homebrew/discussions/4215))
- `keep_alive: always=false` means **launchd will not restart pueued if it dies**.
- Logs land at `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/var/log/pueued.log` (i.e. `/opt/homebrew/var/log/pueued.log` on Apple Silicon).

Manual alternatives: `pueued` (foreground) or `pueued -d` / `pueued --daemonize`. Shutdown: `pueue shutdown`. The [Get-started wiki](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Get-started) only documents systemd (Linux) and the new Windows service subcommands (`pueued service install|uninstall|start|stop`, 4.0+) — **it has no macOS/launchd section**, so brew services is the practical answer.

### Config location on macOS
`~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml` (auto-generated on first daemon start).

### Known issues / pitfalls ([wiki/Common-Pitfalls-and-Debugging](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Common-Pitfalls-and-Debugging))

> *"Pueue takes your input and uses it exactly as is to create a new `sh -c $command` in the background."*
> *"A single `&` somewhere in your command detaches the process, causing the Pueue task to finish immediately."*
> *"Pueue doesn't support aliases in your shell's `.*rc` files"* (it has its own aliasing)
> *"All programs that require some kind of display/window manager won't work"*
> *"Try to run the command without adding it to Pueue."* (debug via `sh -c '$COMMAND'` first)
> *"Sometimes processes may wait for user input."* → use `pueue send "y\n"`

Shell escaping: wrap the whole command in single quotes to survive your interactive shell, e.g. `pueue add 'echo "&& rm /tmp"'`, `pueue add 'ls /tmp/Hello\ World.md'`. There's also a `--escape` flag that disables shell-syntax handling.

Scripting caveat (marked deprecated for 4.0.0 but still on the wiki): the daemon processes requests asynchronously and the TaskManager has its own update loop, so scripts may need a brief sleep before observing a state change. **This matters for optimistic-UI patterns** — an action's effect may not be visible in the very next `status` call.

**No macOS-specific bugs are documented** in the pitfalls page (the platform-specific caveats listed are all Windows, and marked fixed in 4.0+).

---

# Key cross-cutting facts for the decision at hand

1. **"Widget" doesn't exist in Raycast.** The only persistent always-visible surface for an extension is a **`mode: "menu-bar"` command with an `interval`**. Everything else requires the user to open Raycast.
2. **The menu bar item can show a count via `title`** — no badge API, but `title={n > 0 ? String(n) : undefined}` is the established idiom (Brew does exactly this).
3. **Polling is the only option** — Pueue has no push mechanism to a GUI *except* `Request::Stream` (log streaming) and the `callback` hook (which spawns an arbitrary subprocess on task completion and could, e.g., invoke a Raycast deeplink). Interval floor is `1m` per the manifest docs (`10s` per the background-refresh docs — contradictory).
4. **PATH is the #1 implementation hazard.** Copy Brew's `paths.ts` pattern (preference → probe → arch fallback → absolute path).
5. **v4-only JSON shape.** Externally-tagged enums, recursive `Locked`, and the `enqueue_at` vs `enqueued_at` asymmetry. No schema version field. v3 clients will not work.
6. **Shelling out to `pueue status --json` is far simpler than the CBOR socket protocol** — but `beeequeue/pueue-ui` proves the socket route is viable in Node with `cbor-x` if you want to avoid CLI-spawn latency, and it also gives you the daemon version for free from the auth handshake.
7. **"Daemon down" detection** has no first-class API: `pueue status` simply fails to connect. Precedent extensions (Colima, Brew) detect by catching the CLI failure and surfacing an install/start affordance.
8. **First mover.** No Raycast extension, no SwiftBar/xbar plugin, no Alfred workflow, no macOS menu bar app for Pueue exists.

application?: Application | string): Promise<void>;\n```\n`target` = file, folder, or URL. `application` = app name, bundle id, or absolute app path.\n\n---\n\n## A5. Store rules for extensions requiring a user-installed CLI + running daemon\n\nSource: [developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store)\n\n### Verbatim guideline text\n\n> \"Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads and try to automate as much as possible from the extension,\"\n> \"especially if you are targeting non-developers.\"\n> \"See the [Speedtest](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/pull/302) extension that downloads a CLI in the background\"\n> \"If you do end up downloading executable binaries in the background, please make sure it's done from a server\"\n> \"that you don't have access to.\"\n> \"Otherwise, we cannot guarantee that you won't replace the binary with malicious code after the review.\"\n> \"Add additional integrity checks through hashes.\"\n> \"Don't bundle opaque binaries where sources are unavailable or where it's unclear how they have been built.\"\n> \"Don't bundle heavy binary dependencies in the extension – this would lead to an increased extension download size.\"\n\n### \"Examples for interacting with binaries\" (verbatim bullets)\n\n> \"✅ Calling known system binaries\"\n> \"✅ Binary downloaded or installed from a trusted location with additional integrity checking through hashes\"\n> \"(that is, verify whether the downloaded binary really matches the expected binary)\"\n> \"✅ Binary extracted from an npm package and copied to assets, with traceable sources how the binary is built;\"\n> \"❌ Any binary with unavailable sources or unclear builds just added to the assets folder\"\n\n**Interpretation for a Pueue extension:** \"✅ Calling known system binaries\" is the relevant lane — calling a user's already-installed `pueue`/`pueued` from Homebrew is explicitly sanctioned. The \"avoid asking users to perform additional downloads\" clause is soft guidance (\"try to\", \"especially if you are targeting non-developers\") and is clearly not enforced as a hard rule, given the precedent extensions below all require pre-installed CLIs.\n\n### Precedent: extensions in the store that wrap a local daemon/CLI\n\nI enumerated `raycast/extensions/extensions/*` via the GitHub API. **Present:** `brew`, `docker`, `colima`, `orbstack`, `yabai`. **Absent:** `ollama`, `lima`, `podman`, `homebrew`.\n\n| Extension | Author | Commands | Menu bar? | How it finds the binary / detects \"down\" |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **[Brew](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/tree/main/extensions/brew)** | `nhojb` | `installed`, `search`, `outdated`, `upgrade`, `manage-services` (all `view`), **`services-menu` (`menu-bar`, `interval: 1m`)**, `clean-up`, `clear-cache` (`no-view`) | ✅ **Yes** — the single best precedent | 3-tier resolution in [`utils/brew/paths.ts`](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/blob/main/extensions/brew/src/utils/brew/paths.ts): (1) `customBrewPath` preference; (2) `execSync(\"brew --prefix\")`; (3) arch-based fallback `/opt/homebrew` (Apple CPU) vs `/usr/local`. Then `brewExecutable() = brewPath(\"bin/brew\")` — **calls the absolute path**, never bare `brew`. Parses `brew services list --json`. Has a typed error taxonomy incl. `BrewNotFoundError`. |\n| **[Docker](https://www.raycast.com/priithaamer/docker)** | `priithaamer` (45,631 installs) | `container_list`, `projects_list`, `image_list` — all `view` | ❌ No | Uses **`@priithaamer/dockerode`** (a fork of dockerode) — talks to the **Docker socket directly**, no CLI shell-out. |\n| **[Colima](https://www.raycast.com/MiskaMyasa/colima)** | `MiskaMyasa` (Denis Zaitsev) | `list-instances`, `list-containers`, `list-images`, `pull-image`, `run-container` — all `view` | ❌ No | *\"checks for both dependencies on launch and shows installation links if anything is missing\"*. Requires Colima (`brew install colima`) + Docker CLI (`brew install docker`). **Zero preferences** — relies on default PATH. Shows per-instance \"status, CPU, memory, disk, runtime, and architecture\". |\n| **[OrbStack](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/tree/main/extensions/orbstack)** | `nicholasq` | `machine_list`, `machine_create` — both `view` | ❌ No | Plain `@raycast/api` + `@raycast/utils`, shells out to `orb`. |\n| **[Yabai](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/tree/main/extensions/yabai)** | `krzysztoff1` | 30+ commands, mostly `no-view`; **`screens-menu-bar` (`menu-bar`, no interval)**; incl. `start`/`stop`/`restart` for the daemon itself | ✅ Yes (no interval — refreshes only on click/root-search) | Uses **`execa`**. Exposes a preference: `yabaiPath` — *\"Location to the Yabai installation (Defaults to `/opt/homebrew/bin/yabai` on M1 Macs, and `/usr/local/bin/yabai` otherwise)\"* |\n\n**Pattern to copy:** Brew's `paths.ts` (preference → `--prefix` probe → arch fallback → always invoke absolute path) is the most robust precedent, and its `services-menu` is a near-exact structural analogue of a Pueue menu bar command (poll on `interval`, `title` = count of running items, optimistic `mutate` after each action, `showHUD` for feedback).\n\nNote the Brew menu bar file's own header comment, which describes exactly the constraint a Pueue extension faces:\n\n> \"Homebrew has no way to notify us when a service's state changes, so the menu is kept fresh by polling on the command's `interval` (configurable in the command preferences) and by an optimistic `mutate` after each action.\"\n\nAlso notable: Brew makes the interval **user-configurable via command preferences**, which is a good pattern.\n\n---\n\n## A6. Known issues with menu bar commands\n\n### PATH — the single biggest gotcha\n\nRaycast extensions run in a *\"managed child Node.js process\"* ([store docs response](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store)). The docs **do not document what `PATH` contains** — I asked the live docs directly and got: *\"I cannot find information about the **exact `PATH` contents**\"*.\n\nEmpirically, it's broken:\n- **[raycast/extensions#170 — \"[API Bug] env.PATH is undefined\"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/170)** — extensions do not reliably receive `PATH`.\n- **[Stack Overflow — \"Running Custom Bash Script Works in Terminal But Not RayCast\"](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76451345/running-custom-bash-script-works-in-terminal-but-not-raycast)** — Raycast (non-interactive GUI context) lacks the interactive shell's PATH, so Homebrew binaries in `/opt/homebrew/bin` are simply not found.\n- **[apple.stackexchange — GUI apps and launchd PATH](https://apple.stackexchange.com/questions/51305/executables-in-bin-and-usr-bin-are-not-found-in-path)** — macOS GUI apps inherit environment from launchd, not shell rc files.\n- **[Node child_process docs](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html)** — `spawn` fails `ENOENT` if the command isn't in the spawned process's PATH; it uses `options.env.PATH` or `process.env.PATH`, falling back to `/usr/bin:/bin`.\n\n**Workaround used by real extensions:** absolute paths (Brew), or an explicit path preference (Yabai). Both.\n\n### CPU / memory / battery\n\n- **[#22995 — \"[Music] Currently Playing Track background refresh memory ...\"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/22995)** — background refresh causing growing memory per run.\n- **[#22946 — \"Coffee Extension consumes a lot of RAM and CPU and has memory ...\"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/22946)** — high RAM/CPU, memory-leak behaviour.\n- Docs guidance: prefer larger intervals to reduce energy use; set `isLoading` false as early as possible.\n\n### Menu bar item not updating / stuck\n\n- **[#20031 — \"[Battery Menu Bar] ... Not updating\"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/20031)**\n- **[#14659 — \"[Todoist] 'Menu Bar Tasks' fails in background reload\"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/14659)**\n- **[#14250 — \"Menu bar icon stuck\"](https://github.com/raycast/extensions/issues/14250)** (plus #14248, #14251) — icons persisting/not disappearing. Root cause is architectural: lifecycle event #4 means the item is **restored from Raycast's database, not by re-running the command**, so a stale render can survive restarts. Typical workarounds reported: quit/restart Raycast, disable/re-enable the command, remove the dev-installed extension.\n\n### Development\n- There's a *\"run in background\"* action exposed in dev mode to test interval-scheduled commands, plus a \"show full errors\" debugging action.\n- The menu bar item persisting after `ray develop` stops is a manifestation of the same DB-restore behaviour; no documented clean teardown.\n\n### Max refresh frequency\nGoverned by `interval` (see the 10s vs 1m contradiction above) plus macOS's energy-driven tolerance jitter plus the dynamic termination timeout. There is no documented hard ceiling on frequency other than the minimum interval.\n\n---\n\n# TOPIC B — Pueue\n\n## B7. What Pueue is, version, core concepts\n\n**Repo:** [github.com/Nukesor/pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) — Apache-2.0, **6,272 stars**, last push 2026-07-18 (very much alive).\n\n**Current version: v4.0.4, released 2026-03-02.** ([GitHub releases](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases)) Tag history: v4.0.4, v4.0.3, v4.0.2 (2025-12-19), v4.0.1 (2025-07-07), v4.0.0, v4.0.0-rc.{1,2,3}, then v3.4.1 … v3.0.0. Companion crate **pueue-lib v0.31.0** published 2026-03-01.\n\n> ⚠️ The `raw.githubusercontent.com` README fetch returned a **stale/cached v2.0.0** copy. Trust the releases API (v4.0.4), not that README header.\n\n**Description:** *\"Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.\"* — *\"a tool that processes a queue of shell commands.\"* The project declares itself *\"feature-complete 🎉\"*.\n\n**Explicitly out of scope** (per README): distributed/multi-user job scheduling, heavy programmatic scheduling, tight system integration.\n\n### Core concepts\n\n- **Tasks** — a shell command run by the daemon. Pueue runs your input as `sh -c $command` in the background (see Pitfalls below). Tasks carry: id, created_at, original_command, command, path (cwd), envs, group, dependencies, priority, label, status. Environment variables are captured at `add` time.\n- **Groups** ([wiki/Groups](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Groups)) — *\"Grouping tasks can be useful, whenever your tasks utilize different system resources.\"* *\"If no group is specified, the task will just be added to the default queue.\"* Each group has its **own parallelism limit** and its **own Running/Paused state**. Commands: `pueue group add <name>` / `pueue group remove <name>` / `pueue group` / `pueue add -g <group> -- '<cmd>'` / `pueue parallel -g <group> <n>` / `pueue status --group <NAME>` / `pueue pause -g <group>` / `pueue start -g <group>`.\n- **Parallelism** — `pueue parallel 3` globally, or `-g <group>`. Env vars `PUEUE_WORKER_ID` and `PUEUE_GROUP` are injected into tasks so you can map workers to external resources (e.g. GPU indices).\n- **Dependencies** — `pueue add --after/-a <ids>`. A task runs only if its dependencies succeeded; otherwise it gets `TaskResult::DependencyFailed`. Wiki recommends `pause_on_failure` to avoid cascading failures, and restarting with `--in-place`.\n- **Labels** — `label: Option<String>` on each task.\n- **Priorities** — `priority: i32` on each task.\n- **Statuses** — see B8.\n- **Stashing** — tasks can be stashed (not queued) and later enqueued; optionally with a scheduled `enqueue_at` time.\n\n### Basic commands ([wiki/Get-started](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Get-started))\n`pueued` / `pueued -d` (daemonize) / `pueue shutdown` / `pueue add` / `pueue status` (or bare `pueue`) / `pueue log [id]` / `pueue follow $id` (`-e` for stderr) / `pueue pause` / `pueue start` / `pueue kill` / `pueue restart` / `pueue stash` / `pueue enqueue` / `pueue send` / `pueue parallel N` / `pueue wait` / `pueue clean` / `pueue reset` / `pueue edit` / `pueue switch` / `pueue env` / `pueue remove` / `pueue format-status` / `pueue completions $shell $dir`.\n\nMost commands accept multiple IDs or shell ranges: `pueue log 0 1 2 3 15 19`, `pueue log {0..3}`.\n\n---\n\n## B8. The JSON / machine-readable interface\n\n### Which commands support `--json` — exactly three\n\nFrom [`pueue/src/client/cli.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/cli.rs), all with `#[arg(short, long)] json: bool`:\n\n| Subcommand | Doc comment (verbatim from source) |\n|---|---|\n| `status` | `/// Print the current state as json to stdout.` `/// This does not include the output of tasks.` `/// Use \\`log -j\\` if you want everything.` |\n| `log` | `/// Print the resulting tasks and output as json.` `/// By default only the last lines will be returned unless --full is provided.` `/// Take care, as the json cannot be streamed!` `/// If your logs are really huge, using --full can use all of your machine's RAM.` |\n| `group` | `/// Print the list of groups as json.` |\n\nThere is also `pueue format-status`, which takes JSON on stdin and renders the human table — e.g. `pueue status --json | jq -c '.tasks' | pueue format-status` ([wiki/Advanced-usage](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Advanced-usage)).\n\n### `pueue status --json` returns the whole `State`, serialized with `serde_json`\n\nFrom [`pueue/src/client/commands/state/mod.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/commands/state/mod.rs):\n```rust\n// If the json flag is specified, print the state as json and exit.\nif json {\n    if query.is_some() {\n        state.tasks = tasks.into_iter().map(|task| (task.id, task)).collect();\n    }\n    output.push_str(&serde_json::to_string(&state).unwrap());\n    return Ok(output);\n}\n```\nNote: `--query` filtering **is** applied to the JSON output (the tasks map is rebuilt from the filtered/ordered/limited set). `--group` is **not** applied to JSON — the `group` branch is only reached in the non-JSON path.\n\n### The `State` struct ([`pueue_lib/src/state.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/state.rs))\n\n```rust\n#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize, Serialize)]\npub struct State {\n    pub tasks: BTreeMap<usize, Task>,\n    pub groups: BTreeMap<String, Group>,\n}\n\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]\npub struct Group {\n    pub status: GroupStatus,\n    pub parallel_tasks: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Copy, Deserialize, Serialize)]\npub enum GroupStatus {\n    Running,\n    Paused,\n    Reset,\n}\n```\n\n### The `Task` struct ([`pueue_lib/src/task.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/task.rs))\n\n```rust\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]\npub struct Task {\n    pub id: usize,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Local>,\n    pub original_command: String,\n    pub command: String,\n    pub path: PathBuf,\n    pub envs: HashMap<String, String>,\n    pub group: String,\n    pub dependencies: Vec<usize>,\n    pub priority: i32,\n    pub label: Option<String>,\n    pub status: TaskStatus,\n}\n```\n\n### `TaskStatus` — **externally tagged** (no serde attributes)\n\n```rust\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Display, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub enum TaskStatus {\n    /// Used while the command of a task is edited (to prevent starting the task)\n    Locked { previous_status: Box<TaskStatus> },\n    /// The task has been manually stashed. It won't be executed until it's manually enqueued\n    Stashed { enqueue_at: Option<DateTime<Local>> },\n    /// The task is queued and waiting for a free slot\n    Queued { enqueued_at: DateTime<Local> },\n    /// The task is started and running\n    Running {\n        enqueued_at: DateTime<Local>,\n        start: DateTime<Local>,\n    },\n    /// A previously running task has been paused\n    Paused {\n        enqueued_at: DateTime<Local>,\n        start: DateTime<Local>,\n    },\n    /// Task finished. The actual result of the task is handled by the [TaskResult] enum.\n    Done {\n        enqueued_at: DateTime<Local>,\n        start: DateTime<Local>,\n        end: DateTime<Local>,\n        result: TaskResult,\n    },\n}\n```\n\nI verified by grepping the file: **there are no `#[serde(tag=...)]`, `#[serde(rename=...)]` or `#[serde(untagged)]` attributes anywhere in `task.rs`.** So serde's **default externally-tagged representation** applies. Concretely the JSON is:\n\n```jsonc\n\"status\": { \"Queued\":  { \"enqueued_at\": \"2026-07-26T10:00:00+02:00\" } }\n\"status\": { \"Running\": { \"enqueued_at\": \"...\", \"start\": \"...\" } }\n\"status\": { \"Paused\":  { \"enqueued_at\": \"...\", \"start\": \"...\" } }\n\"status\": { \"Stashed\": { \"enqueue_at\": null } }        // note: enqueue_at, NOT enqueued_at\n\"status\": { \"Locked\":  { \"previous_status\": { \"Queued\": { \"enqueued_at\": \"...\" } } } }  // recursive!\n\"status\": { \"Done\": { \"enqueued_at\": \"...\", \"start\": \"...\", \"end\": \"...\",\n                      \"result\": \"Success\" } }\n\"status\": { \"Done\": { ..., \"result\": { \"Failed\": 127 } } }\n```\n\n⚠️ **Trap:** `Stashed` uses `enqueue_at` (future scheduled time, nullable) while every other variant uses `enqueued_at`. Easy to typo.\n⚠️ **Trap:** `Locked.previous_status` is a **recursive `TaskStatus`**, so a naive discriminated-union type must handle nesting.\n\n### `TaskResult` — also externally tagged\n\n```rust\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Display, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub enum TaskResult {\n    /// Task exited with 0\n    Success,\n    /// The task failed in some other kind of way (error code != 0)\n    Failed(i32),\n    /// The task couldn't be spawned. Probably a typo in the command\n    FailedToSpawn(String),\n    /// Task has been actively killed by either the user or the daemon on shutdown\n    Killed,\n    /// Some kind of IO error. This should barely ever happen. Please check the daemon logs.\n    Errored,\n    /// A dependency of the task failed.\n    DependencyFailed,\n}\n```\n\nJSON forms: unit variants serialize as bare strings (`\"Success\"`, `\"Killed\"`, `\"Errored\"`, `\"DependencyFailed\"`); newtype variants as `{\"Failed\": 127}` and `{\"FailedToSpawn\": \"…\"}`.\n\n### `pueue log --json` shape\n\nFrom [`pueue/src/client/commands/log/json.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue/src/client/commands/log/json.rs):\n```rust\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]\npub struct TaskLog {\n    pub task: Task,\n    pub output: String,\n}\n```\nEmitted as a `BTreeMap<usize, TaskLog>` — i.e. `{\"0\": {\"task\": {...}, \"output\": \"...\"}}`. Output from the daemon is **snappy-compressed** (`snap::read::FrameDecoder`) and decompressed client-side; when `client.read_local_logs` is true it's read straight off disk instead.\n\n### Breaking changes in the JSON shape — **v3 → v4 is a hard break**\n\nFrom [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md), v4.0.0:\n\n> \"**Breaking**: Refactor internal task state.\"\n> \"Important: This completely breaks pre v4.0 states.\"\n> \"The Pueue daemon needs to be restarted and the state will be wiped clean.\"\n> \"Send log output to `stderr` instead of `stdout`\"\n> \"Switch `cbor` handling library, breaking backwards-compatible communication on a data format level.\"\n> \"Switch protocol message representation, completely breaking backwards compatibility.\"\n> \"Redesigned task editing process\"\n\nWhat changed concretely: in **v3**, `Task` had flat sibling fields (`start`, `end`, `enqueue_at`, `result`) alongside a simpler `status` enum whose variants were mostly unit-like (`\"Queued\"`, `\"Running\"`, `\"Done\"` etc.). In **v4** all of those timestamps and the result were **moved into the `TaskStatus` enum's variant payloads**, making every status variant a struct variant. This is why `{\"Queued\": {\"enqueued_at\": ...}}` (v4) replaces bare `\"Queued\"` (v3).\n\nAlso from v4: logs go to stderr, but *\"JSON and task log output remain on stdout\"* — good for scripting.\n\n**There is no versioned/stable status format.** No `schema_version` field exists in `State`. The wire protocol is explicitly not backwards compatible. Any consumer must pin to v4.x semantics and detect version drift itself (the daemon does send its version during the handshake — see B9).\n\nv3.0.0's breaking changes were behavioural, not schema-level:\n> \"Tasks are now started in a process group, and `pueue kill` will kill all processes in the group [#372]\"\n> \"The `--children` cli flag has been deprecated (signals go to the whole group, always).\"\n\n---\n\n## B9. Talking to the daemon directly (instead of shelling out)\n\n**Yes — and there is a working TypeScript implementation to copy from.**\n\n### Transport & auth ([docs/Architecture.md](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/docs/Architecture.md))\n\n> \"Listen on the daemon's socket\"\n> \"Performs authorization (secret & certificate)\"\n> \"send confirmation, which is also the daemon's version.\"\n> \"Receive the incoming message and deserialize it\"\n> \"All functions used for handling client messages can be found in [daemon::network::message_handler].\"\n\nThe daemon accepts **Unix domain sockets OR TLS-encrypted TCP** (one at a time, per config). Each connection spawns a tokio task. Auth is a **shared secret** read from a file + (for TCP) a self-signed cert. **The auth response body is the daemon's version string** — handy for version detection.\n\n### Wire protocol ([`pueue_lib/src/network/protocol.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/network/protocol.rs))\n\n- **Framing:** 8-byte **big-endian u64 length header**, then payload.\n  `WriteBytesExt::write_u64::<BigEndian>(&mut header, message_size).unwrap();`\n- **Chunking:** payload written in `PACKET_SIZE` = **1280**-byte chunks: `for chunk in payload.chunks(PACKET_SIZE) {`\n- **Serialization: CBOR** via `ciborium` + serde — `into_writer(&message, &mut payload)` / `from_reader(payload_bytes.as_slice())`. **Not JSON.**\n- **DoS guard:** `receive_bytes_with_max_size(max_size: Option<usize>)`; handshake reads are capped at ~4 MiB; warns above 20 MiB.\n- Helpers: `send_request<T: Into<Request>>`, `send_response`, `receive_request`, `receive_response`.\n\n### `Request` enum ([`pueue_lib/src/message/request.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/message/request.rs))\n\n```rust\n#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]\npub enum Request {\n    Add(AddRequest),\n    Remove(Vec<usize>),\n    Switch(SwitchRequest),\n    Stash(StashRequest),\n    Enqueue(EnqueueRequest),\n    Start(StartRequest),\n    Restart(RestartRequest),\n    Pause(PauseRequest),\n    Kill(KillRequest),\n    Send(SendRequest),\n    EditRequest(Vec<usize>),\n    EditRestore(Vec<usize>),\n    EditedTasks(Vec<EditableTask>),\n    Env(EnvRequest),\n    Group(GroupRequest),\n    Parallel(ParallelRequest),\n    /// Request the daemon's state\n    Status,\n    Log(LogRequest),\n    Stream(StreamRequest),\n    Reset(ResetRequest),\n    Clean(CleanRequest),\n    DaemonShutdown(ShutdownRequest),\n}\n```\nNote `Status` is a **unit variant** → encodes as the bare CBOR string `\"Status\"`.\n\n### `Response` enum ([`pueue_lib/src/message/response.rs`](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/pueue_lib/src/message/response.rs))\n\n```\nAddedTask(AddedTaskResponse)   // { task_id, enqueue_at, group_is_paused }\nEdit(Vec<EditableTask>)\nStatus(Box<State>)             // ← the whole State\nLog(BTreeMap<usize, TaskLogResponse>)   // TaskLogResponse { task, output_complete, output: Option<Vec<u8>> }\nGroup(GroupResponse)           // { groups: BTreeMap<String, Group> }\nStream(StreamResponse)         // { logs: BTreeMap<usize, String> }\nSuccess(String)\nFailure(String)\nClose\n```\n\nNote `Request::Stream` gives you a **continuous log stream** — no polling needed for `follow`-style output.\n\n### Config keys relevant to connecting ([wiki/Configuration](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Configuration))\n\nConfig file on macOS: **`~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml`**. Override with `-c` or `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH` (CLI flag wins).\n\nShared section:\n- `use_unix_socket: true` — *\"(Unix only) Whether the daemon should listen on a Unix- or a TCP-socket.\"*\n- `unix_socket_path: ~/.local/share/pueue/pueue_your_user.socket` — *\"Defaults to `runtime_directory/pueue_$USER.socket`.\"* Default socket mode `0o700`.\n- `host: \"localhost\"`, `port: \"6924\"`\n- `daemon_cert` / `daemon_key` — TLS for TCP\n- `shared_secret_path: ~/.local/share/pueue/shared_secret` — *\"The path to the file, which contains the secret used for authentication with the daemon.\"*\n- `pueue_directory: ~/.local/share/pueue`, `runtime_directory: null`\n- **Profiles** are supported in one file; select with `pueue --profile remote status`.\n\n### **No** documented JSON-RPC or HTTP interface\n\nThere is no HTTP/REST/JSON-RPC endpoint. The only interfaces are: (a) the CLI, (b) the CBOR-over-socket protocol.\n\n### Existing TypeScript/Node client — one exists, unpublished\n\n**[beeequeue/pueue-ui](https://github.com/beeequeue/pueue-ui)** — TypeScript, Vue + Nitro, MIT, last push **2026-07-24** (2 days ago), 1 star, \"wip\"/\"experimental\". Research is in. Quick verdict before I design:

**Feasible — and you'd be first.** No Raycast extension, xbar/SwiftBar plugin, or Alfred workflow for Pueue exists (verified four ways: `gh search code repo:raycast/extensions`, repo search, store search, web). `jakevossen5/pueue-bar` is an empty 2021 shell.

Two corrections to the premise worth stating up front:

- **Raycast has no "widget" API.** Not for extensions — no desktop surface, no Notification Center widget, nothing new in "The New Raycast" (May 2026) or Glaze. The only always-visible surface is a **`mode: "menu-bar"` command** (`MenuBarExtra` + manifest `interval`). That's the real target.
- **Your local pueue is v4.0.4**, whose JSON shape is a hard break from v3: timestamps and results moved *inside* the status enum as externally-tagged Rust enums — `{"Done":{"start":…,"end":…,"result":{"Failed":127}}}`, plus a recursive `{"Locked":{"previous_status":…}}` and an `enqueue_at`/`enqueued_at` spelling asymmetry. Any v3-era example you find is wrong.

The closest structural precedent is Homebrew's `services-menu` in `raycast/extensions` — menu-bar, `interval: 1m`, count in `title`, optimistic refresh after each action. Its own header comment states the exact constraint we have: no push notification of state changes, so poll.

Four decisions shape the design:

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**What should v1 cover?**

Options:
- **Menu bar + full command set (Recommended)** - menu-bar 'Pueue Status' (counts + per-task actions) PLUS view commands: Tasks list (search/filter/detail/log), Add Task form, Groups. The menu bar is the glanceable surface; the list view is where you actually work. ~1200 LOC.
- **Menu bar only** - Just the MenuBarExtra: running/queued/failed counts in the title, submenu per task with start/pause/kill/restart/copy, group pause/start. Smallest useful thing, ~300 LOC, ships in a day.
- **View commands only, no menu bar** - Skip the persistent surface entirely — just a searchable Tasks list + Add Task + Logs inside Raycast. Zero background polling, zero battery cost.

**How should the extension talk to pueued?**

Options:
- **Shell out to `pueue --json` (Recommended)** - execFile an absolute-path `pueue status/log/group --json`. Measured 22–44 ms on your machine. Only 3 commands emit JSON; mutations (start/kill/add) are exit-code-only. Simple, survives daemon protocol changes.
- **Speak the CBOR unix socket directly** - Node net + cbor-x, 8-byte BE length header, shared-secret handshake that returns the daemon version. No process spawn, gives log streaming via Request::Stream. Prior art exists (beeequeue/pueue-ui). But it hard-couples to an explicitly unstable wire protocol.
- **Shell out now, socket later behind a flag** - Ship the CLI path; leave a seam so a socket transport can be swapped in if the ~25 ms spawn cost ever matters.

**Where is this headed?**

Options:
- **Public Raycast store (Recommended)** - Nobody has published one. Store rules explicitly bless '✅ Calling known system binaries' — brew-installed pueue qualifies. Costs: 512×512 icon, CHANGELOG, README, 3–6 screenshots at 2000×1250, and a human review of days.
- **Personal / local only** - `ray develop` registers it and it persists in root search after you stop dev. No icon, no screenshots, no review. Can be published later without rework.
- **Build store-ready, decide at the end** - Follow every store requirement while building (icon, CHANGELOG, README, lockfile) but don't run publish until you've used it for a while.

**Pueue can run a shell command whenever a task finishes (`daemon.callback` in pueue.yml, Handlebars-templated with id/command/result/exit_code/output_path). Want to use it?**

Options:
- **Document it, don't touch the config (Recommended)** - README shows a copy-paste callback snippet for osascript notifications, and the extension offers a 'Copy callback config' action. Your pueue.yml stays untouched — the extension never writes to it.
- **Yes, wire it up in-extension** - An extension action that edits ~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml to set a callback, then prompts to restart the daemon. Gives real push notifications on task completion instead of up-to-60s polling lag.
- **Skip entirely** - Menu bar polling is enough; no notification story in v1.


**Answer:** Menu bar + full command set (Recommended), shell out to `pueue --json` (unix socket as backlog), Build store-ready, decide at the end, Document it, don't touch the config (Recommended)". Read the answers carefully — they may request clarification, changes, or that you not proceed — and follow what they actually say.

2. **Transport**: shell out to the `pueue` CLI with `--json`. A direct CBOR unix-socket transport is a *backlog item only* — but structure `src/lib/` so it could be swapped in later behind one module boundary.
3. **Distribution**: build store-ready (icon, CHANGELOG, README, committed package-lock.json, metadata/ screenshots slot), but defer the actual `publish` decision.
4. **Notifications**: pueue's `daemon.callback` hook is **documented in the README + offered as a copy-to-clipboard action**. The extension must **never write to the user's pueue.yml**.

## Verified facts about the environment (from a prior investigation — trust these)

**Pueue on this machine**: v4.0.4, Homebrew at **`/usr/local/bin/pueue`** and `/usr/local/bin/pueued` (Intel prefix — `/opt/homebrew/bin` does NOT exist here, so probe both). Daemon runs via `brew services` / launchd (`homebrew.mxcl.pueue`, pid file at the config dir). Config at **`~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml`** (NOT `~/.config/pueue/`) — on macOS that same dir is also the data dir, socket dir, and log dir. Node 24 on PATH via mise; Raycast runs extensions on its own bundled **Node 22**. `/Applications/Raycast.app` installed; `~/.config/raycast/extensions/` has a working local dev extension. `ray` is not on PATH (it ships inside `@raycast/api`).

**Only three commands emit JSON**: `status`, `log`, `group`. Everything else (`add`, `start`, `pause`, `kill`, `restart`, `remove`, `stash`, `enqueue`, `clean`, `parallel`, `switch`, `send`, `env`, `reset`) is exit-code + prose only.

**`pueue status --json`** → `{"tasks": {"<id>": Task}, "groups": {"<name>": {"status":"Running"|"Paused"|"Reset", "parallel_tasks": int}}}`. Compact single line + `\n`. Empty queue → `{"tasks":{},"groups":{"default":{"status":"Running","parallel_tasks":1}}}`. Measured latency **22–44 ms, median 28 ms** on an empty queue.

**`pueue group --json`** returns just the inner map `{"<name>": {...}}` — a DIFFERENT top-level shape from `status`. Easy trap.

**Task object** (v4.0.4, `pueue_lib/src/task.rs`): `id` (int, also the map key as a string), `created_at`, `original_command`, `command`, `path`, `envs` (object), `group`, `dependencies` (int[]), `priority` (int), `label` (string|null), `status`.

**`status` is a nested externally-tagged enum** — there is NO flat `"status":"Running"` string:
```
{"Stashed": {"enqueue_at": null | "<ts>"}}
{"Queued":  {"enqueued_at": "<ts>"}}
{"Running": {"enqueued_at": "<ts>", "start": "<ts>"}}
{"Paused":  {"enqueued_at": "<ts>", "start": "<ts>"}}
{"Locked":  {"previous_status": <recursive TaskStatus>}}
{"Done":    {"enqueued_at","start","end", "result": <TaskResult>}}
```
`TaskResult` is ALSO externally tagged and mixes bare strings with objects: `"Success"`, `{"Failed": <int exit code>}`, `{"FailedToSpawn": "<string>"}`, `"Killed"`, `"Errored"`, `"DependencyFailed"`. Timestamps are chrono `DateTime<Local>` → RFC3339 with microseconds and a numeric offset (`2026-04-27T11:01:06.893055+08:00`), never `Z`, never epoch. **Note `enqueue_at` (Stashed only) vs `enqueued_at` (everything else)** — a one-letter footgun.

**`envs` is a full snapshot of the submitting shell's environment**, present in `status --json` (blanked to `{}` in `log --json`). Upstream cites ~2 MB state for 400 tasks. It may contain secrets. This matters for a command that polls every minute.

**`pueue log --json`** → `{"<id>": {"task": Task, "output": "<string>"}}`. Defaults to the **last 15 lines**; `--lines N`; `--full` (docs warn it can exhaust RAM). Because `client.read_local_logs: true` here, logs can also be read straight off disk at `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/task_logs/<id>.log` (stdout+stderr merged, plain text, uncompressed). `pueue log <bad-id> --json` → `{}` with **exit 0**.

**`pueue status --json --group X`** filters `tasks` but NOT the returned `groups` map, and silently succeeds for a nonexistent group.

**`pueue status` accepts a server-side query DSL** that composes with `--json`: `[columns=[...]] [filter]* [order_by col asc|desc] [first|last N]`, filter columns `status|command|label|start|end|enqueue_at`, ops `= != < > %=` (`%=` is "contains"), status tokens `queued|stashed|paused|running|success|failed`. A bad query → exit 1 with a pest parse error.

**Exit codes are 0/1 only**, no structured errors. Errors are human prose on **stderr**, and `color_eyre` emits **ANSI escapes even when stderr is a pipe** — `--color never` and `NO_COLOR=1` do NOT suppress them. Any stderr surfaced to the user must be ANSI-stripped.

**Daemon-down** produces two distinguishable failures, both exit 1: config file missing → `Couldn't find a configuration file. Did you start the daemon yet?`; config present but socket gone/refused → `I/O error at path "…/pueue_<user>.socket" while connecting to daemon. Did you start it?` (ENOENT or ECONNREFUSED).

**No push/subscribe for state.** `pueue wait` polls internally every 2 s and prints prose. `pueue follow <id>` DOES stream log text continuously (250 ms disk poll locally; exits when the task stops; exit 1 + `The task to be followed doesn't exist.` for a bad id). So: state must be polled; log output can be streamed via `spawn`.

**Gotchas**: `pueue parallel` with no args is broken (logs "Received unhandled response message", exits 0) — read parallelism from `group --json` instead. `pueue add -p/--print-task-id` prints just the integer id. `pueue remove` refuses running/paused tasks (must kill first). Pueue runs commands as `sh -c $command`, so a trailing `&` detaches and the task "finishes" instantly. The daemon processes requests asynchronously with its own update loop, so **a state change may not be visible in the very next `status` call** — this directly affects optimistic-UI/refresh-after-action timing.

## Verified facts about the Raycast API (2026)

- **No widget surface exists.** Extension entry points are exactly: `mode: "view"`, `mode: "no-view"`, `mode: "menu-bar"` (macOS only), AI `tools[]` (Raycast **Pro**-gated), and Script Commands.
- `MenuBarExtra` props: `icon`, `title`, `tooltip`, `isLoading`. **No badge API** — the count goes in `title`, and `title={n > 0 ? String(n) : undefined}` hides it at zero (the Brew extension's idiom). Children: `.Item` (`title`, `icon`, `subtitle`, `tooltip`, `onAction`, `shortcut`, `alternate`), `.Submenu`, `.Section`, `.Separator`. Empty submenus render disabled. Returning `null` removes the item entirely.
- **`isLoading` contract (docs mark this "danger")**: either never set it (Raycast renders and immediately unloads), or set `true` during async work and `false` when done. Getting this wrong hangs or truncates the command.
- **Don't put two identical `MenuBarExtra.Item`s at the same level** — their `onAction` handlers misfire.
- **Background refresh**: manifest `interval` on a command, allowed only for `no-view` and `menu-bar`. **The docs contradict themselves on the floor** — the background-refresh page says `10s`, the manifest page says `1m`. Treat `1m` as the safe floor (Brew ships `1m`). Scheduling is inexact (macOS energy jitter). Commands are auto-terminated after a timeout dynamically scaled to the interval. For `menu-bar`, **the whole React tree re-runs on every tick** until `isLoading` goes false.
- **Background refresh is DISABLED by default for store installs** until the user runs the command once or enables it in preferences. A fresh install shows nothing in the menu bar — this needs to be in the README.
- **When Raycast restarts, the menu bar item is restored from Raycast's database, not by re-running the command** — so a stale render survives restarts until the next interval fires. There are open upstream issues about stuck/stale menu bar icons (#14250, #20031, #14659).
- `Cache` (disk-backed LRU, string values, default 10 MB, `namespace` option, `subscribe()`) is the documented way to hand data from a background tick to the UI. `LocalStorage` (`string|number|boolean`) is for small settings; docs say don't use it for bulk data.
- `launchCommand({name, type: LaunchType, context})` — documented use case includes **forcing a background refresh** of a sibling command. Resolves when launched, not when the target finishes.
- `updateCommandMetadata({subtitle})` puts live text under a command's name in root search; not persisted to the manifest.
- `showToast` **falls back to `showHUD` when the Raycast window is closed**, so it's safe to call from menu-bar actions. `confirmAlert` supports `rememberUserChoice` and `Alert.ActionStyle.Destructive`.
- **PATH is the #1 hazard**: Raycast runs extensions in a managed Node child process under launchd with no shell rc, so a bare `pueue` throws ENOENT. Every real extension resolves an absolute path. The best precedent is the Brew extension's `src/utils/brew/paths.ts`: preference → `execSync("brew --prefix")` probe → arch-based fallback (`/opt/homebrew` vs `/usr/local`) → always invoke the absolute path. Yabai exposes a `yabaiPath` preference for the same reason.
- Store rules: "✅ Calling known system binaries" is explicitly allowed; "Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads" is soft guidance ("try to", "especially if you are targeting non-developers"). Precedent store extensions requiring a pre-installed CLI/daemon: **brew** (has a `menu-bar` `services-menu` with `interval: 1m` — the closest structural analogue), **colima**, **orbstack**, **yabai** (also has a `menu-bar` command, no interval), **docker** (talks to the socket via a dockerode fork instead).

## The reference extension to mine for patterns

`/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui/raycast/extension/` — a mature working extension by the same author (Raycast handle **`da-wei_lee`**) that shells out to a local Go CLI. **Read these files yourself** and reuse their patterns:

- `src/lib/translate.ts` (612 lines) — `resolveBinary()` (preference checked *before* the module-level cache, `existsSync` validation, probe list), `isBinaryMissing(e)` as a message-prefix predicate, `baseEnv()` which passes `HOME` through so the CLI finds its config, `promisify(execFile)` wrappers with per-call `timeout`/`maxBuffer`/`signal`, a module-level cache for static lookups that **swallows errors and returns a static fallback** so an older binary degrades instead of crashing, and `execWithStdin`'s `settled`/`finish()` race-guard.
- `src/lib/binary-not-found.tsx` — a `List.EmptyView` onboarding view with copyable install commands + `openExtensionPreferences`. Note it returns a bare `List.EmptyView`, so it must be rendered inside a `<List>`; there is no `Detail` equivalent and two views duplicate an `errorMarkdown()` helper instead — **fix that duplication in the new extension**.
- `src/lib/stream-view.tsx` — `useRef` accumulator + `spawn` + returning the cancel function from `useEffect`. Maps directly onto `pueue follow`.
- `src/look-up-word.tsx` — two parallel `usePromise` calls with **separate abort refs**, merged `error`/`isLoading`, and the `onRecorded → revalidate()` callback threaded into a pushed Detail so the parent list refreshes after a mutation while the Detail is still open. **This is the exact pattern for act-on-a-task-then-refresh.**
- `src/history.tsx` — does NOT control `searchText`; feeds Raycast's built-in client-side filtering via `keywords={[...]}` per item. Likely right for a task list.
- `src/lib/language-dropdown.tsx` — the "static fallback list so the dropdown never paints empty, then swap in the live list" hook, plus preserving an unknown current value as a synthetic dropdown item so it doesn't silently reset. The analogue here is a **group dropdown**.
- `src/lib/hooks.ts` — an 11-line generic `useDebouncedValue<T>`.
- Preferences: `ray build` generates `raycast-env.d.ts` with globally-declared `Preferences.<Command>` and `Arguments.<Command>` namespaces. **Hard rule from their pitfalls doc: never hand-write a preferences interface** — the generated type makes fields required so a code default that drifts from the manifest becomes a compile error. (Their own `lib/translate.ts` violates this; don't copy that part.)
- Stack: `@raycast/api ^1.103.6` (locks to 1.104.23), `@raycast/utils ^2.2.2`, react 19, typescript 5.8, `@raycast/eslint-config`, no prettier config file, stock Raycast tsconfig, no tests, no CI. Scripts: `build: ray build`, `dev: ray develop`, `lint: ray lint`, `fix-lint: ray lint --fix`, `publish: npx @raycast/api@latest publish`.
- The repo uses a **project-knowledge-harness** convention worth replicating: `TODO.md` as a priority/effort-tagged index, `backlog/<slug>.md` for large deferred items, `pitfalls/<slug>.md` titled by *symptom* with a grep-able verbatim-error section, `docs/<topic>.md` for present-tense reference, and a `Justfile` whose recipes self-bootstrap with `([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) &&`.

139	  if (prefs.binaryPath && existsSync(prefs.binaryPath)) return prefs.binaryPath;
140	  if (cachedBin) return cachedBin;
141	  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
142	    const candidate = join(dir, "translate");
143	    if (existsSync(candidate)) {
144	      cachedBin = candidate;
145	      return candidate;
146	    }
147	  }
148	  throw new Error(
149	    "translate CLI not found. Set the binary path in extension preferences, or install it (just install / brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate).",
150	  );
151	}
152	
153	/** True when an error came from resolveBinary failing to locate the CLI. */
154	export function isBinaryMissing(e: unknown): boolean {
155	  return e instanceof Error && e.message.startsWith("translate CLI not found");
156	}
157	
158	function baseEnv(): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
159	  // Ensure the CLI can locate its config.toml (providers/API keys) under launchd.
160	  return { ...process.env, HOME: process.env.HOME ?? homedir() };
161	}
162	
163	/**
164	 * Above this many UTF-8 bytes, text goes to the CLI on stdin instead of argv.
165	 *
166	 * macOS caps a whole argument list at ARG_MAX (1 MiB) and fails the spawn with
167	 * E2BIG — measured: 900 KB via argv works, 1.1 MB is "argument list too long".
168	 * The CLI reads stdin when it gets no text argument, and the pipe has no such
169	 * limit, so long documents take that route. The threshold leaves plenty of room
170	 * for multi-byte text (a CJK character is 3 bytes).
171	 */
172	const ARGV_SAFE_BYTES = 128 * 1024;
173	
174	function needsStdin(text: string): boolean {
175	  return Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8") > ARGV_SAFE_BYTES;
176	}
177	
178	/**
179	 * How long to let a translation run, scaled to the input.
180	 *
181	 * A document-sized translation legitimately takes minutes — measured against
182	 * copilot-proxy: 10 KB of prose took 61 s, 20 KB took 96 s. A flat 60 s killed
183	 * exactly the long inputs Translate Text exists for. ~10 ms per character with a
184	 * 1-minute floor and a 10-minute ceiling (matching the CLI's own backstop).
185	 */
186	function requestTimeout(text: string): number {
187	  return Math.min(600_000, Math.max(60_000, text.length * 10));
188	}
189	
190	/**
191	 * Run the CLI with `input` written to stdin and no text argument, resolving with
192	 * stdout. Mirrors pexecFile's rejection shape (message + `stderr`) so callers
193	 * can keep inspecting stderr the same way.
194	 */
195	function execWithStdin(
196	  bin: string,
197	  args: string[],
198	  input: string,
199	  opts: { timeout?: number; signal?: AbortSignal } = {},
200	): Promise<string> {
201	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
202	    const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
203	    let out = "";
204	    let err = "";
205	    let settled = false;
206	
207	    const finish = (fn: () => void) => {
208	      if (settled) return;
209	      settled = true;
210	      clearTimeout(timer);
211	      opts.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
212	      fn();
213	    };
214	    const kill = (reason: string) =>
215	      finish(() => {
216	        if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
217	        reject(Object.assign(new Error(reason), { stderr: err }));
218	      });
219	    const onAbort = () => kill("aborted");
220	    const timer = opts.timeout
221	      ? setTimeout(
222	          () => kill(`timed out after ${opts.timeout}ms`),
223	          opts.timeout,
224	        )
225	      : (undefined as unknown as NodeJS.Timeout);
226	
227	    opts.signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
228	
229	    child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
230	    child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
231	    child.stdout?.on("data", (d: string) => (out += d));
232	    child.stderr?.on("data", (d: string) => (err += d));
233	    child.on("error", (e) =>
234	      finish(() => reject(Object.assign(e, { stderr: err }))),
235	    );
236	    child.on("close", (code) =>
237	      finish(() =>
238	        code === 0
239	          ? resolve(out)
240	          : reject(
241	              Object.assign(
242	                new Error(`translate exited ${code}: ${err.trim()}`),
243	                {
244	                  stderr: err,
245	                },
246	              ),
247	            ),
248	      ),
249	    );
250	
251	    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
252	      /* the child may exit before we finish writing — the close handler reports it */
253	    });
254	    child.stdin?.end(input, "utf8");
255	  });
256	}
257	
258	export interface TranslateOptions {
259	  to?: string;
260	  from?: string;
261	  engine?: string;
262	  tier?: string;
263	  /** Exact model id, overriding engine/tier selection. */
264	  model?: string;
265	  /**
266	   * Direction. Tri-state on purpose:
267	   *   undefined → leave it to the config ([general] pair)
268	   *   true      → --pair: detect and route between the pair languages
269	   *   false     → --no-pair: always translate into `to`
270	   *
271	   * This matters because [general] pair = true silently overrides --to for
272	   * home-language input, so "translate into X" is only true with --no-pair.
273	   */
274	  pair?: boolean;
275	  noHistory?: boolean;
276	  signal?: AbortSignal;
277	}
278	
279	/**
280	 * Turns a target + pair choice into CLI flags.
281	 *
282	 * AUTO_TARGET means "no --to at all": the CLI's own home target and pair_with
283	 * decide the direction. Anything else falls back to the Raycast preference, and
284	 * finally to nothing (letting the CLI config's default_target apply).
285	 */
286	function directionArgs(
287	  to: string | undefined,
288	  pair: boolean | undefined,
289	  prefTarget: string | undefined,
290	): { to?: string; pair?: boolean } {
291	  if (to === AUTO_TARGET) return { to: undefined, pair: true };
292	  return { to: to || prefTarget || undefined, pair };
293	}
294	
295	export async function runTranslate(
296	  text: string,
297	  opts: TranslateOptions = {},
298	): Promise<TranslateResult> {
299	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
300	  const bin = resolveBinary();
301	  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, prefs.defaultTarget);
302	  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
303	  // With no text argument the CLI reads stdin, which sidesteps ARG_MAX.
304	  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
305	  // In auto/pair mode we deliberately send no --to: the CLI's own home target
306	  // plus [general] pair_with decide the direction.
307	  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
308	  args.push("--json");
309	  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
310	  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
311	  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
312	  const engine = opts.engine ?? prefs.engine;
313	  if (engine) args.push("--engine", engine);
314	  const tier = opts.tier ?? prefs.tier;
315	  if (tier) args.push("--tier", tier);
316	  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
317	  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");
318	
319	  const timeout = requestTimeout(text);
320	  if (viaStdin) {
321	    const stdout = await execWithStdin(bin, args, text, {
322	      timeout,
323	      signal: opts.signal,
324	    });
325	    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
326	  }
327	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
328	    timeout, // LLM engines routinely exceed useExec's 10s default
329	    maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
330	    env: baseEnv(),
331	    signal: opts.signal, // cancel a superseded call when the user keeps typing
332	  });
333	  return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
334	}
335	
336	let cachedModels: ModelInfo[] | undefined;
337	
338	/**
339	 * `translate models --json` — the models the configured providers declare, one
340	 * per tier, cached per command run. Deliberately not a live /v1/models probe:
341	 * copilot-proxy advertises ids it then refuses to serve, so a probed list would
342	 * offer choices that fail at request time. Empty on an older CLI.
343	 */
344	export async function runModels(): Promise<ModelInfo[]> {
345	  if (cachedModels) return cachedModels;
346	  try {
347	    const bin = resolveBinary();
348	    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["models", "--json"], {
349	      timeout: 10_000,
350	      maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,
351	      env: baseEnv(),
352	    });
353	    const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as ModelInfo[];
354	    cachedModels = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [];
355	  } catch {
356	    cachedModels = []; // older CLI without `models`, or no binary
357	  }
358	  return cachedModels;
359	}
360	
361	export interface DefineOptions {
362	  /** Definition language for the LLM fallback. A dictionary hit ignores it — the
363	   *  offline tiers are script-fixed (CC-CEDICT zh→en, ECDICT en→zh). */
364	  to?: string;
365	  /** Force smart-dict, i.e. fall back to the LLM when the dictionary misses. */
366	  smart?: boolean;
367	  /** Suppress the history row. Browsing must not record; opening a word should. */
368	  noHistory?: boolean;
369	  signal?: AbortSignal;
370	}
371	
372	const NO_DICT_ENTRY = "no dictionary entry";
373	
374	/**
375	 * `translate define <word> --json`. The top-level payload is a TranslateResult
376	 * whose `.dictionary` holds the entry (on a dict hit); on a miss it falls back
377	 * to an LLM definition in `.translation` with a `warnings[]` note.
378	 *
379	 * A *hard* miss (the plain dictionary with no LLM fallback and nothing close
380	 * enough to suggest) exits 1 with a bare stderr line and no JSON at all — that
381	 * is re-thrown as a tagged error so callers can render it as "no entry" rather
382	 * than as a crash. See isNoDictEntry.
383	 *
384	 * Unless noHistory is set this writes a history row, which is what makes
385	 * "opening a word remembers it" true.
386	 */
387	export async function runDefine(
388	  word: string,
389	  opts: DefineOptions = {},
390	): Promise<TranslateResult> {
391	  const bin = resolveBinary();
392	  const args = ["define", word, "--json"];
393	  if (opts.smart) args.push("--smart");
394	  if (opts.to) args.push("--to", opts.to);
395	  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");
396	  try {
397	    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
398	      timeout: 60_000,
399	      maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
400	      env: baseEnv(),
401	      signal: opts.signal,
402	    });
403	    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
404	  } catch (e) {
405	    const stderr = String((e as { stderr?: string }).stderr ?? "");
406	    if (stderr.includes(NO_DICT_ENTRY)) {
407	      throw new Error(`${NO_DICT_ENTRY}: ${word}`);
408	    }
409	    throw e;
410	  }
411	}
412	
413	/** True when `define` exited on a hard dictionary miss (no JSON was emitted). */
414	export function isNoDictEntry(e: unknown): boolean {
415	  return e instanceof Error && e.message.startsWith(NO_DICT_ENTRY);
416	}
417	
418	/**
419	 * `translate dict search <q> --limit N --json` — ranked headword candidates with
420	 * one-line definition previews.
421	 *
422	 * Local data only: no network, no LLM, single-digit milliseconds on an indexed
423	 * dictionary. That is the point — it is safe to run on every keystroke, and the
424	 * expensive LLM fallback is deferred to the moment a word is actually opened.
425	 * It also opens no history store, so typing can never pollute history.
426	 *
427	 * Finding nothing is not an error: `candidates` comes back empty and exit is 0.
428	 */
429	export async function runDictSearch(
430	  q: string,
431	  limit = 12,
432	  signal?: AbortSignal,
433	): Promise<DictSearchResult> {
434	  const bin = resolveBinary();
435	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(
436	    bin,
437	    ["dict", "search", q, "--limit", String(limit), "--json"],
438	    {
439	      timeout: 10_000,
440	      maxBuffer: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
441	      env: baseEnv(),
442	      signal,
443	    },
444	  );
445	  const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as DictSearchResult;
446	  return { ...parsed, candidates: parsed.candidates ?? [] };
447	}
448	
449	let cachedLangs: LangInfo[] | undefined;
450	
451	/**
452	 * `translate lang list --json` — the CLI's full language table (35 entries),
453	 * cached per command run. Falls back to the hardcoded LANGS subset when the
454	 * installed binary predates the subcommand, so an older CLI still works.
455	 */
456	export async function runLangs(): Promise<LangInfo[]> {
457	  if (cachedLangs) return cachedLangs;
458	  try {
459	    const bin = resolveBinary();
460	    const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["lang", "list", "--json"], {
461	      timeout: 10_000,
462	      maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024,
463	      env: baseEnv(),
464	    });
465	    const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout) as LangInfo[];
466	    if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.length > 0) {
467	      cachedLangs = parsed;
468	      return cachedLangs;
469	    }
470	  } catch {
471	    /* older CLI or no binary — fall through to the static list */
472	  }
473	  cachedLangs = LANGS.map((l) => ({ code: l.value, name: l.title }));
474	  return cachedLangs;
475	}
476	
477	/**
478	 * `translate history --json` (recent) or `translate history search <q> --json`.
479	 * Both return an array of HistoryEntry. Local + fast (no network).
480	 */
481	export async function runHistory(
482	  query?: string,
483	  limit = 200,
484	  signal?: AbortSignal,
485	): Promise<HistoryEntry[]> {
486	  const bin = resolveBinary();
487	  const q = query?.trim();
488	  const args = q
489	    ? ["history", "search", q, "--json"]
490	    : ["history", "--json", "--limit", String(limit)];
491	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
492	    timeout: 30_000,
493	    maxBuffer: 32 * 1024 * 1024,
494	    env: baseEnv(),
495	    signal,
496	  });
497	  const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout);
498	  return Array.isArray(parsed) ? (parsed as HistoryEntry[]) : [];
499	}

501	/**
502	 * Fire-and-forget TTS via `translate <text> --to <lang> --speak`. This runs a
503	 * real translation (it speaks the translated side), so it passes --no-history:
504	 * pressing Speak is not a lookup and should not add a history row.
505	 */
506	export function speak(text: string, to: string): void {
507	  const bin = resolveBinary();
508	  execFile(
509	    bin,
510	    [text, "--to", to, "--speak", "--no-history"],
511	    { env: baseEnv() },
512	    () => {
513	      /* ignore — best-effort audio */
514	    },
515	  );
516	}
517	
518	/**
519	 * Fire-and-forget TTS via `translate speak <text>` — pronounces the text as-is.
520	 * Unlike speak() this neither translates nor records, which is what you want for
521	 * "how is this word pronounced".
522	 */
523	export function speakText(text: string, lang?: string): void {
524	  const bin = resolveBinary();
525	  const args = ["speak", text];
526	  if (lang) args.push("--lang", lang);
527	  execFile(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() }, () => {
528	    /* ignore — best-effort audio */
529	  });
530	}

532	/** The effective CLI config (subset we care about) from `config show --json`. */
533	export interface CliConfig {
534	  general?: {
535	    default_target?: string;
536	    default_source?: string;
537	    debounce_ms?: number;
538	    engine?: string;
539	    tier?: string;
540	    live_translate?: boolean;
541	    /** Bidirectional mode: home-language input goes to pair_with instead. */
542	    pair?: boolean;
543	    pair_with?: string;
544	  };
545	}
546	
547	let cachedConfig: CliConfig | undefined;
548	
549	/**
550	 * Read the CLI's effective config via `translate config show --json` (cached per
551	 * command run). Lets the extension inherit the default target / debounce from
552	 * ~/.config/translate/config.toml when the Raycast preferences are left empty.
553	 */
554	export async function readConfig(): Promise<CliConfig> {
555	  if (cachedConfig) return cachedConfig;
556	  const bin = resolveBinary();
557	  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, ["config", "show", "--json"], {
558	    timeout: 10_000,
559	    maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024,
560	    env: baseEnv(),
561	  });
562	  cachedConfig = JSON.parse(stdout) as CliConfig;
563	  return cachedConfig;

566	export interface StreamHandlers {
567	  onData: (chunk: string) => void;
568	  onDone: (code: number | null) => void;
569	  onError: (err: Error) => void;
570	}
571	
572	/**
573	 * Spawn `translate <text> --to <lang> [--engine] --stream` and stream plain-text
574	 * stdout chunks (the `--stream` flag forces streaming over a pipe). Returns a
575	 * cancel function that kills the child (call it on unmount). Whether output arrives
576	 * progressively depends on the provider — ollama streams; copilot-proxy buffers its
577	 * claude responses. `--no-history` avoids duplicating a history row the live view
578	 * may already have recorded.
579	 */
580	export function spawnTranslateStream(
581	  text: string,
582	  opts: TranslateOptions,
583	  h: StreamHandlers,
584	): () => void {
585	  const bin = resolveBinary();
586	  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, undefined);
587	  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
588	  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
589	  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
590	  args.push("--stream", "--no-history");
591	  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
592	  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
593	  if (opts.engine) args.push("--engine", opts.engine);
594	  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
595	  if (opts.tier) args.push("--tier", opts.tier);
596	  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
597	
598	  const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
599	  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
600	  child.stdout?.on("data", (d: Buffer | string) => h.onData(d.toString()));
601	  child.on("close", (code) => h.onDone(code));
602	  child.on("error", (err) => h.onError(err));
603	  if (viaStdin) {
604	    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
605	      /* reported via the close/error handlers above */
606	    });
607	    child.stdin?.end(text, "utf8");
608	  }
609	  return () => {
610	    if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
611	  };
612	}

4	
5	/** A pushed Detail that streams `translate … --stream` output token-by-token.
6	 *  Opt-in from the Translate view (⌘↵) — useful for long text and streaming
7	 *  engines; on a buffering provider it simply appears after first-token latency. */
8	export function StreamView({
9	  text,
10	  to,
11	  engine,
12	  model,
13	  pair,
14	}: {
15	  text: string;
16	  to?: string;
17	  engine?: string;
18	  model?: string;
19	  pair?: boolean;
20	}) {
21	  const [md, setMd] = useState("");
22	  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
23	  const acc = useRef("");
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    acc.current = "";
27	    setMd("");
28	    setIsLoading(true);
29	    const cancel = spawnTranslateStream(
30	      text,
31	      { to, engine: engine || undefined, model, pair },
32	      {
33	        onData: (chunk) => {
34	          acc.current += chunk;
35	          setMd(acc.current);
36	        },
37	        onDone: () => setIsLoading(false),
38	        onError: (err) => {
39	          acc.current += `\n\n> error: ${err.message}`;
40	          setMd(acc.current);
41	          setIsLoading(false);
42	        },
43	      },
44	    );
45	    return cancel;
46	  }, [text, to, engine, model, pair]);
47	
48	  return (
49	    <Detail
50	      isLoading={isLoading}
51	      markdown={md || "…"}
52	      navigationTitle={to ? `Translate → ${to}` : "Translate"}
53	      actions={
54	        <ActionPanel>
55	          <Action.CopyToClipboard title="Copy Translation" content={md} />
56	          <Action.Paste title="Paste Translation" content={md} />
57	        </ActionPanel>
58	      }
59	    />
60	  );
61	}

31	const HISTORY_LIMIT = 200;

35	/**
36	 * Below this the prefix scan is both slowest (a one-letter range covers ~60k

39	const MIN_QUERY = 2;

41	/**

44	 * input gets a little longer because an IME emits intermediate candidates.

46	const DEBOUNCE_MS = 180;
47	const DEBOUNCE_MS_CJK = 300;

49	const CJK =
50	  /[\p{Script=Han}\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}\p{Script=Hangul}]/u;
51	
52	export default function Command(
53	  props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.LookUpWord }>,
54	) {
55	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.LookUpWord>();
56	  const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
57	  // Command argument (picked in the Raycast root bar) → Raycast preference →
58	  // the CLI config's default_target → "en".
59	  const [to, setTo] = useState(
60	    props.arguments?.to || prefs.defaultTarget || "",
61	  );
62	
63	  useEffect(() => {
64	    if (to) return;
65	    readConfig()
66	      .then((cfg) => {
67	        if (cfg.general?.default_target) setTo(cfg.general.default_target);
68	      })
69	      .catch(() => {
70	        /* fall back below */
71	      })
72	      .finally(() => setTo((t) => t || "en"));
73	  }, []);
74	
75	  const trimmed = query.trim();
76	  const debounced = useDebouncedValue(
77	    trimmed,
78	    CJK.test(trimmed) ? DEBOUNCE_MS_CJK : DEBOUNCE_MS,
79	  );
80	  const searchAbort = useRef<AbortController>();
81	  const historyAbort = useRef<AbortController>();
82	
83	  const search = usePromise(

85	      if (q.length < MIN_QUERY) return undefined;

87	    },
88	    [debounced],
89	    { abortable: searchAbort },

91	
92	  const history = usePromise(
93	    async (): Promise<HistoryEntry[]> =>
94	      runHistory(undefined, HISTORY_LIMIT, historyAbort.current?.signal),
95	    [],
96	    { abortable: historyAbort },

155	      onSearchTextChange={setQuery}
156	      searchBarPlaceholder="Look up a word…"
157	      searchBarAccessory={<LanguageDropdown value={to} onChange={setTo} />}
158	    >

261	                    target={

295	}
296	
297	/**
298	 * History rows worth showing next to live results: the ones whose input or output
299	 * contains what was typed. Already in memory, so this costs nothing.
300	 */
301	function matchingHistory(entries: HistoryEntry[], q: string): HistoryEntry[] {
302	  const needle = q.toLowerCase();
303	  return entries
304	    .filter(
305	      (h) =>
306	        h.input.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
307	        h.output.toLowerCase().includes(needle),
308	    )
309	    .slice(0, HISTORY_WITH_RESULTS);
310	}
311	
312	/** Pull the `translate …` command out of a notes hint, for the copy action. */
313	function commandFromNotes(notes: string): string {
314	  const m = notes.match(/`([^`]+)`/);
315	  return m ? m[1] : notes;
316	}

13	 * static LANGS subset so the dropdown is never empty on first paint, then swaps

15	 */
16	export function useLanguages(): LangInfo[] {
17	  const [langs, setLangs] = useState<LangInfo[]>(() =>
18	    LANGS.map((l) => ({ code: l.value, name: l.title })),
19	  );

22	      .then(setLangs)
23	      .catch(() => {
24	        /* keep the static list */
25	      });
26	  }, []);

28	}
29	
30	/** The configured pair, or null when [general] pair_with isn't set. */
31	export interface PairInfo {
32	  home: string;
33	  away: string;
34	  /** Whether [general] pair is on, i.e. whether this is already the default. */
35	  enabled: boolean;
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * Reads the configured bidirectional pair, so a target picker can offer "Auto"
40	 * with real language codes in its label instead of a vague word.
41	 */
42	export function usePair(): PairInfo | null {
43	  const [pair, setPair] = useState<PairInfo | null>(null);
44	  useEffect(() => {
45	    readConfig()
46	      .then((cfg) => {
47	        const g = cfg.general;
48	        if (g?.pair_with && g.default_target) {
49	          setPair({
50	            home: g.default_target,
51	            away: g.pair_with,
52	            enabled: !!g.pair,
53	          });
54	        }
55	      })
56	      .catch(() => {
57	        /* no pair offered */
58	      });
59	  }, []);
60	  return pair;
61	}
62	
63	/** The label for the Auto entry, e.g. "Auto — zh-TW ⇄ en". */
64	export function autoLabel(pair: PairInfo | null): string {
65	  return pair
66	    ? `Auto — ${pair.home} ⇄ ${pair.away}`
67	    : "Auto (detect direction)";
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Target-language picker with an "Auto" entry — the dropdown equivalent of the
72	 * TUI's ^g.
73	 *
74	 * Auto is not cosmetic. With [general] pair = true the CLI already reroutes
75	 * home-language input to pair_with, so picking "Chinese" and pasting Chinese
76	 * gives you English. Making Auto explicit means picking a language can mean what
77	 * it says: a concrete choice sends --no-pair and always translates *into* it.
78	 */
79	export function LanguageDropdown(props: {
80	  value: string;
81	  onChange: (code: string) => void;
82	  /** Show the Auto entry (target pickers) or not (definition-language pickers). */
83	  auto?: PairInfo | null;
84	}) {
85	  const langs = useLanguages();
86	  // A value that isn't in the list would silently reset the dropdown, so keep
87	  // whatever the config resolved to (e.g. a code the CLI knows and we don't).
88	  const known =
89	    props.value === AUTO_TARGET || langs.some((l) => l.code === props.value);
90	  return (
91	    <List.Dropdown
92	      tooltip="Target language — Auto follows the configured pair, like ^g in the TUI"
93	      value={props.value}
94	      onChange={props.onChange}
95	    >
96	      {props.auto !== undefined ? (
97	        <List.Dropdown.Item
98	          title={autoLabel(props.auto)}
99	          value={AUTO_TARGET}
100	          keywords={["auto", "pair", "bidirectional"]}
101	        />
102	      ) : null}
103	      {!known && props.value ? (
104	        <List.Dropdown.Item title={props.value} value={props.value} />
105	      ) : null}
106	      {langs.map((l) => (
107	        <List.Dropdown.Item

1	import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
2	
3	/** Debounce a value so an expensive call only fires after the user pauses typing. */
4	export function useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
5	  const [debounced, setDebounced] = useState(value);
6	  useEffect(() => {
7	    const id = setTimeout(() => setDebounced(value), delayMs);
8	    return () => clearTimeout(id);
9	  }, [value, delayMs]);
10	  return debounced;
11	}

125	/** The plain text a Copy/Paste action should produce. */
126	function definitionText(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
127	  const d = r.dictionary;
128	  if (!d) return r.translation;
129	  const lines: string[] = [];
130	  for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
131	    for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) lines.push(def.definition);
132	  }
133	  return lines.length > 0 ? lines.join("\n") : r.translation || word;
134	}

136	/** Renders a dictionary entry, or the LLM fallback's prose, as markdown. */
137	export function renderDefinition(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
138	  const d = r.dictionary;
139	  if (d) {
140	    const lines = [`# ${d.word || word}`];
141	    if (d.phonetic) lines.push(`*/${d.phonetic}/*`);
142	    lines.push("");
143	    for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
144	      lines.push(`## ${m.part_of_speech}`);
145	      for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) {
146	        lines.push(
147	          `- ${def.definition}${def.example ? `\n  - _${def.example}_` : ""}`,
148	        );
149	      }
150	      lines.push("");
151	    }
152	    return lines.join("\n");
153	  }
154	  // No dictionary entry — the LLM fallback's definition lives in `translation`.
155	  const lines = [`# ${word}`, "", r.translation, ""];
156	  if (r.warnings?.length) lines.push("---", ...r.warnings.map((w) => `> ${w}`));
157	  return lines.join("\n");
158	}

163	  // which is fixed by the data (ECDICT is en→zh, CC-CEDICT is zh→en). Say so
164	  // rather than letting the picked target look ignored.
165	  const scriptFixed =
166	    r.engine === "dictionary" && !!r.target && r.target !== to;
167	  return (
168	    <Detail.Metadata>
169	      <Detail.Metadata.Label title="Engine" text={r.engine ?? "—"} />
170	      {r.dictionary?.phonetic ? (
171	        <Detail.Metadata.Label title="Phonetic" text={r.dictionary.phonetic} />
172	      ) : null}
173	      {r.model ? <Detail.Metadata.Label title="Model" text={r.model} /> : null}
174	      <Detail.Metadata.Label
175	        title="Definition language"
176	        text={
177	          scriptFixed
178	            ? `${r.target} — the offline dictionary is zh↔en; “${to}” applies to the LLM fallback`
179	            : r.target || to
180	        }
181	      />
182	      {r.dictionary?.source_url ? (
183	        <Detail.Metadata.Link
184	          title="Source"
185	          target={r.dictionary.source_url}
186	          text="link"
187	        />
188	      ) : null}
189	    </Detail.Metadata>
190	  );

- **Translate** — type-to-translate with a target-language dropdown, debounced live
