=== README head ===
# Translate

Translate, define, and speak text from Raycast — backed by the local
[`translate`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/translate) CLI. Multi-engine
auto-fallback (local LLM via copilot-proxy / Ollama, keyless Google, offline
CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries), unified history, and free TTS.

## Requirements

This extension **shells out to the `translate` CLI** — it does not translate on its
own. Install the binary first:

```sh
brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
# or, with a Go toolchain:
go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest
```

On first run, `translate init` sets up your providers/config
(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`). The extension auto-detects the binary in
`~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, and `~/go/bin`; if it lives
elsewhere, set **“translate binary path”** in the extension preferences. (If it
isn’t found, the extension shows an install-instructions screen instead of failing.)

> **Note:** Raycast runs under a restricted `PATH` and reads no shell env, so API
> keys must live in `translate`’s config file (via `translate init`), not in
> `~/.zshrc`. “Translate Selection” and selection-prefill need macOS **Accessibility**
> permission for Raycast (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).

## Commands

- **Translate** — type to translate; pick the target language; ⌘↵ for a streaming
  view; actions for Copy / Paste / Speak and an engine override.
- **Translate Text** — a multi-line box for whole paragraphs. Raycast's search bar
  refuses a long paste ("the text you are trying to paste is too long"), and that
  limit is the app's, not ours — so long text gets its own form. ⌘⇧S loads the
  selection, ⌘⇧V the clipboard, ⌘↵ streams, ⌘⇧A reveals engine + model.
- **Translate Selection** — grabs your selection (or clipboard) and opens Translate
  prefilled and editable.
- **Look up Word** — a dictionary picker: an empty search bar lists your recent
  lookups, typing shows ranked headword candidates with definition previews, and ↵
  opens a full definition page (which is also what records the lookup in history).
  Pick the definition language before opening the command or from the dropdown
  inside it. Typing only reads the local dictionary — the LLM is called when you
  open a word, not while you type.
- **Define** — single-result dictionary lookup with phonetics and meanings (offline
  dictionaries, LLM fallback, and suggestions).
- **History** — browse and search your past translations.

For the best **Look up Word** experience run `translate dict update all` once
(offline CC-CEDICT + ECDICT); existing installs should also run
`translate dict reindex`, which makes Chinese lookups ~20× faster without
re-downloading anything.

Every target dropdown leads with **Auto**, which follows the bidirectional pair
configured in `translate` (`pair` + `pair_with`) — the equivalent of `^g` in the
TUI. Picking a specific language instead always translates *into* it.

## Preferences

```text
Interact with the Pueue daemon

Use the `--help` long form to get detailed help output on each subcommand!

Usage: pueue [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add          Enqueue a task for execution
  remove       Remove tasks from the list. Running or paused tasks need to be killed first
  switch       Switches the queue position of two commands
  stash        Stash a task. Stashed tasks won't be automatically started
  enqueue      Enqueue stashed tasks. They'll be handled normally afterwards
  start        Resume operation of specific tasks or groups of tasks
  restart      Restart failed or successful task(s)
  pause        Either pause running tasks or specific groups of tasks
  kill         Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups
  send         Send something to a task. Useful for sending confirmations such as 'y\n'
  edit         Adjust editable properties of a task
  env          Use this to add or remove environment variables from tasks
  group        Use this to add or remove groups
  status       Display the current status of all tasks
  log          Display the log output of finished tasks
  follow       Follow the output of a currently running task. This command works like "tail -f"
  wait         Wait until tasks are finished
  clean        Remove all finished tasks from the list
  reset        Kill all tasks, clean up afterwards and reset EVERYTHING!
  shutdown     Remotely shut down the daemon. Should only be used if the daemon isn't started by a
               service manager
  parallel     Set the amount of allowed parallel tasks
  completions  Generates shell completion files
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv)

      --color <COLOR>
          Colorize the output; auto enables color output when connected to a tty
          
          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, never, always]

  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          If provided, Pueue only uses this config file.
          
          This path can also be set via the "PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH" environment variable. The
          commandline option overwrites the environment variable!

  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          The name of the profile that should be loaded from your config file

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
=== STATUS HELP ===
Display the current status of all tasks

Usage: pueue status [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...

Arguments:
  [QUERY]...
          Users can specify a custom query to filter for specific values, order by a column
          or limit the amount of tasks listed.
          
          Syntax:
             [column_selection]? [filter]* [order_by]? [limit]?
          
          where:
            - column_selection := `columns=[column]([column],)*`
            - column := `id | status | command | label | path | enqueue_at | dependencies | start |
            end`
            - filter := `[filter_column] [filter_op] [filter_value]`
              (note: not all columns support all operators, see "Filter columns" below.)
            - filter_column := `status | command | label | start | end | enqueue_at`
            - filter_op := `= | != | < | > | %=`
              (`%=` means 'contains', as in the test value is a substring of the column value)
            - order_by := `order_by [column] [order_direction]`
            - order_direction := `asc | desc`
            - limit := `[limit_type]? [limit_count]`
            - limit_type := `first | last`
            - limit_count := a positive integer
          
          Filter columns:
            - `status` supports the operators `=`, `!=`
              against test values that are:
                - strings like `queued`, `stashed`, `paused`, `running`, `success`, `failed`
            - `command`, `label` support the operators `=`, `!=`, `%=`
              against test values that are:
                - strings like `some text`
            - `start`, `end`, `enqueue_at` contain a datetime
              which support the operators `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`
              against test values that are:
                - date like `YYYY-MM-DD`
                - time like `HH:mm:ss` or `HH:mm`
                - datetime like `YYYY-MM-DDHH:mm:ss`

Enqueue a task for execution.

There're many different options when scheduling a task. Check the individual option help texts for
more information. Furthermore, please remember that scheduled commands are executed via your system
shell. This means that the command needs proper shell escaping. The safest way to preserve shell
escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:

Usage: pueue add [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>...

Arguments:
  <COMMAND>...
          The command to be added

Options:

          Specify current working directory

  -e, --escape

          Beware: This implicitly disables nearly all shell specific syntax ("&&", "&>").

  -i, --immediate

      --follow
          Immediately follow a task, if it's started with --immediate

  -s, --stashed

          Useful to avoid immediate execution if the queue is empty.

  -d, --delay <delay>

          formats

  -g, --group <GROUP>

          amount of parallel tasks for each group. If no group is specified, the default group will
          be used.

  -a, --after <after>...

  -o, --priority <PRIORITY>

=== restart ===
Restart failed or successful task(s).

By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place. You
can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.

Usage: pueue restart [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:
  [TASK_IDS]...
          Restart these specific tasks

Options:
  -a, --all-failed
          Restart all failed tasks across all groups.
          
          This is nice for usage in combination with `-i/--in-place` (or the respective config
          option).

  -g, --failed-in-group <FAILED_IN_GROUP>
          Like `--all-failed`, but only restart tasks failed tasks of a specific group

  -k, --immediate
          Immediately start the tasks, no matter how many open slots there are. This will ignore any
          dependencies tasks may have

  -s, --stashed
          Set the restarted task to a "Stashed" state. Useful to avoid immediate execution

  -i, --in-place
          Restart the task by reusing the already existing tasks. This will overwrite any previous
          logs of the restarted tasks.
          
          This can also be enabled by default via the `restart_in_place` config option.

      --not-in-place
          Restart the task by creating a new identical tasks. Only necessary if you have the
          `restart_in_place` configuration set to true

  -e, --edit
          Edit the task before restarting

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
=== kill ===
Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups.

Kills all tasks of the default group when no ids or a specific group are provided.

Usage: pueue kill [OPTIONS] [TASK_IDS]...

Arguments:

          Kill these specific tasks

Options:
  -g, --group <GROUP>
          Kill all running tasks in a group. This also pauses the group

  -a, --all
          Kill all running tasks across ALL groups. This also pauses all groups

/**
 * Homebrew path utilities.
 *
 * Provides functions for resolving brew installation paths.
 */

import { execSync } from "child_process";
import { join as path_join } from "path";
import { cpus } from "os";
import { preferences } from "../preferences";

/**
 * The Homebrew prefix directory.
 * Determined by:
 * 1. Custom brew path preference (if set)
 * 2. Running `brew --prefix` command
 * 3. Fallback based on CPU architecture
 */
export const brewPrefix = (() => {
  if (preferences.customBrewPath && preferences.customBrewPath.length > 0)
    return path_join(preferences.customBrewPath, "..", "..");
  try {
    return execSync("brew --prefix", { encoding: "utf8" }).trim();
  } catch {
    const firstCpu = cpus()[0];
    return firstCpu?.model?.includes("Apple") ? "/opt/homebrew" : "/usr/local";
  }
})();

/**
 * Get a path relative to the brew prefix.
 */
export const brewPath = (suffix: string): string => path_join(brewPrefix, suffix);

/**
 * Get the path to the brew executable.
 */
export const brewExecutable = (): string => brewPath("bin/brew");
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
/**
 * Menu bar command for quickly controlling brew services.
 *
 * Homebrew has no way to notify us when a service's state changes, so the menu
 * is kept fresh by polling on the command's `interval` (configurable in the
 * command preferences) and by an optimistic `mutate` after each action.
 */

import { Color, Icon, LaunchType, MenuBarExtra, launchCommand, showHUD } from "@raycast/api";
import {
  ALL_SERVICES,
  applyServiceAction,
  brewServiceIsRunning,
  ensureError,
  getErrorMessage,
  runServiceCommand,
  SERVICE_ACTION_COPY,
  type Service,
  type ServiceAction,
} from "./utils";
import { useBrewServices } from "./hooks/useBrewServices";
import { serviceStatusIcon, type ServicesMutate } from "./components/serviceActions";

const MENU_ICON = { source: "services-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.PrimaryText };

const ACTION_ICONS: Record<ServiceAction, Icon> = {
  start: Icon.Play,
  stop: Icon.Stop,
  restart: Icon.ArrowClockwise,
};

async function handleAction(action: ServiceAction, name: string, mutate: ServicesMutate) {
  const copy = SERVICE_ACTION_COPY[action];
  const target = name === ALL_SERVICES ? "all services" : name;
  try {
    await mutate(runServiceCommand(action, name), {
      optimisticUpdate: (services) => applyServiceAction(services ?? [], action, name),
    });
    await showHUD(`${copy.past} ${target}`);
  } catch (err) {
    await showHUD(`Failed to ${copy.verb.toLowerCase()} ${target}: ${getErrorMessage(ensureError(err))}`);
  }
}

export default function Command() {
  const { isLoading, data, revalidate, mutate } = useBrewServices();

  const services = data ?? [];
  const running = services.filter(brewServiceIsRunning);

  return (
    <MenuBarExtra
      icon={MENU_ICON}
      title={running.length > 0 ? `${running.length}` : undefined}
      tooltip="Homebrew Services"
      isLoading={isLoading}
    >
      <MenuBarExtra.Section title="All Services">
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Start All"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.start}
          onAction={() => handleAction("start", ALL_SERVICES, mutate)}
        />
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Stop All"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.stop}
          onAction={() => handleAction("stop", ALL_SERVICES, mutate)}
        />
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Restart All"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.restart}
          onAction={() => handleAction("restart", ALL_SERVICES, mutate)}
        />
      </MenuBarExtra.Section>

      <MenuBarExtra.Section title="Services">
        {services.map((service) => (
          <ServiceSubmenu key={service.name} service={service} mutate={mutate} />
        ))}
        {!isLoading && services.length === 0 && <MenuBarExtra.Item title="No services found" />}
      </MenuBarExtra.Section>

      <MenuBarExtra.Section>
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Open Manage Services"
          icon={Icon.AppWindowList}
          onAction={() => launchCommand({ name: "manage-services", type: LaunchType.UserInitiated })}
        />
        <MenuBarExtra.Item title="Refresh" icon={Icon.ArrowClockwise} onAction={() => revalidate()} />
      </MenuBarExtra.Section>
    </MenuBarExtra>
  );
}

function ServiceSubmenu(props: { service: Service; mutate: ServicesMutate }) {
  const { service, mutate } = props;
  const running = brewServiceIsRunning(service);

  return (
    <MenuBarExtra.Submenu title={service.name} icon={serviceStatusIcon(service.status)}>
      {running ? (
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Stop"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.stop}
          onAction={() => handleAction("stop", service.name, mutate)}
        />
      ) : (
        <MenuBarExtra.Item
          title="Start"
          icon={ACTION_ICONS.start}
          onAction={() => handleAction("start", service.name, mutate)}
        />
      )}
      <MenuBarExtra.Item
        title="Restart"
        icon={ACTION_ICONS.restart}
        onAction={() => handleAction("restart", service.name, mutate)}
      />
    </MenuBarExtra.Submenu>
  );
}

//////// ../src/hooks/useBrewServices.ts
/**
 * Hook for fetching brew services.
 */

import { showToast, Toast } from "@raycast/api";
import { useCachedPromise } from "@raycast/utils";
import { brewFetchServices, Service, isBrewLockError, getErrorMessage, fetchLogger } from "../utils";

/**
 * Hook to fetch and cache brew services.
 *
 * @returns Object containing loading state, data, and a revalidate function.
 */
export function useBrewServices() {
  return useCachedPromise(
    async (): Promise<Service[]> => {
      return await brewFetchServices();
    },
    [],
    {
      keepPreviousData: true,
      onError: async (error) => {
        fetchLogger.error("Failed to fetch services", {
          errorType: error.name,
          message: error.message,
          isLockError: isBrewLockError(error),
        });

        const isLock = isBrewLockError(error);
        await showToast({
          style: Toast.Style.Failure,
          title: isLock ? "Brew is Busy" : "Failed to fetch services",
          message: isLock ? "Another brew process is running. Please wait and try again." : getErrorMessage(error),
        });
      },
    },
  );
}

//////// ../src/components/serviceActions.tsx
/**
 * Action panel and status helpers for managing brew services.
 */

import { Action, ActionPanel, Color, Icon, Image, Keyboard } from "@raycast/api";
import { MutatePromise } from "@raycast/utils";
import { homedir } from "os";
import {
  ALL_SERVICES,
  applyServiceAction,
  brewServiceIsRunning,
  ensureError,
  runServiceCommand,
  SERVICE_ACTION_COPY,
  showActionToast,
  showBrewFailureToast,
  type Service,
  type ServiceAction,
} from "../utils";

export type ServicesMutate = MutatePromise<Service[], undefined>;

/** Map a service status to a list icon. */
export function serviceStatusIcon(status: string): Image.ImageLike {
  switch (status) {
    case "started":
      return { source: Icon.CheckCircle, tintColor: Color.Green };
    case "scheduled":
      return { source: Icon.Clock, tintColor: Color.Blue };
    case "stopped":
    case "none":
      return { source: Icon.Circle, tintColor: Color.SecondaryText };
    case "error":
      return { source: Icon.XMarkCircle, tintColor: Color.Red };
    default:
      return { source: Icon.QuestionMarkCircle, tintColor: Color.Orange };
  }
}

/**
 * Run a service action with an optimistic list update, showing progress.
 *
 * The list flips to the expected state immediately via `mutate`, then
 * reconciles against a fresh `brew services list` in the background.
 */
async function runServiceAction(action: ServiceAction, name: string, mutate: ServicesMutate): Promise<void> {
  const copy = SERVICE_ACTION_COPY[action];
  const target = name === ALL_SERVICES ? "all services" : name;

  const run = () =>
    mutate(runServiceCommand(action, name), {
      optimisticUpdate: (services) => applyServiceAction(services ?? [], action, name),
    });

  const toast = showActionToast({ title: `${copy.gerund} ${target}`, cancelable: false });
  try {
    await run();
    await toast.showSuccessHUD(`${copy.past} ${target}`);
  } catch (err) {
    toast.hide();
    await showBrewFailureToast(`Failed to ${copy.verb.toLowerCase()} ${target}`, ensureError(err), {
      retryAction: run,
    });
  }
}

function ServiceActionItem(props: {
  action: ServiceAction;
  name: string;
  icon: Image.ImageLike;
  shortcut?: Keyboard.Shortcut;
  mutate: ServicesMutate;
}) {
  const { action, name } = props;
  const isAll = name === ALL_SERVICES;
  const title = isAll
    ? `${SERVICE_ACTION_COPY[action].verb} All Services`
    : `${SERVICE_ACTION_COPY[action].verb} Service`;
  return (
    <Action
      title={title}
      icon={props.icon}
      shortcut={props.shortcut}
      style={action === "stop" ? Action.Style.Destructive : undefined}
      onAction={() => runServiceAction(action, name, props.mutate)}
    />
  );
}

function AllServicesSection(props: { mutate: ServicesMutate }) {
  return (
    <ActionPanel.Section title="All Services">
      <ServiceActionItem
        action="start"
        name={ALL_SERVICES}
        icon={Icon.Play}
        shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"], key: "s" }}
        mutate={props.mutate}
      />
      <ServiceActionItem
        action="stop"
        name={ALL_SERVICES}
        icon={Icon.Stop}
        shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"], key: "x" }}
        mutate={props.mutate}
      />
      <ServiceActionItem
        action="restart"
        name={ALL_SERVICES}
        icon={Icon.ArrowClockwise}
        shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd", "shift"], key: "r" }}
        mutate={props.mutate}
      />
    </ActionPanel.Section>
  );
}

function PlistSection(props: { file: string }) {
  const path = props.file.replace(/^~/, homedir());
```

- [ ] **[S] Automate the Homebrew formula bump on release** — the tap formula (`daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` `Formula/translate.rb`) is currently hand-bumped (url + sha256) per tag. Add an on-tag GitHub Action (e.g. `dawidd6/action-homebrew-bump-formula`, needs a cross-repo PAT) so a new `vX.Y.Z` auto-updates the formula. Keeps build-from-source (no goreleaser/cask). See [backlog/homebrew-distribution.md](backlog/homebrew-distribution.md).
- [ ] **[M] Table/wrapped-prose-aware bilingual mode** — the `--bilingual`/`-2` reading view interleaves a translation per blank-line-delimited prose block, which breaks on tabular output (`ls -l`, `kubectl get`, `git status`) and on hard-wrapped prose split by blank lines. Add column/table detection (skip or column-align) and soft-wrap coalescing; consider per-span parsing via the `charmbracelet/x/ansi` tokenizer already imported. See [backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md](backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md).
- [ ] **[M] lingua-go detection upgrade behind the `Detector` seam** — whatlanggo is light/fast but weak on short and mixed-script text; lingua-go is more accurate but heavy (embedded n-gram models → bigger binary, slower init). Swap behind the existing `internal/lang` interface only if short-text detection proves insufficient. Detection is mostly a fallback (Google returns the source, LLM returns `DetectedSource`), so keeping it light is defensible.
- [ ] **[S] MyMemory fallback engine** — trivial flat JSON (`responseData.translatedText`, `matches[]`); wire as an easy secondary free path after Google. Limits: 5k chars/day anon (50k with `&de=email`), 500 B max per `q`, no source auto-detect.
- [ ] **[M] Azure Translator engine behind the engine seam** — the only supported Microsoft path (needs an Azure subscription key). Keyless Bing scraping (`ttranslatev3` + transient `IG`/`IID`/token) is too fragile/ToS-risky for v1. Leave the engine interface ready; add when a key is available.
- [ ] **[S] history --engine/--kind filter flags** — Raycast Look up Word and History both pull `history --json` and filter client-side (there is no way to ask for "only dictionary lookups" or "only single-word inputs"). Add filter flags to `translate history` and the `/v1/history` query so front-ends stop re-implementing the same predicate. See `internal/store/jsonl.go`, whose Recent/Search already read the whole file per call.
- [ ] **[M] Opportunistic translate serve fast path for the Raycast extension** — Probe `127.0.0.1:4155/healthz` once per command mount and route `dict search` / `define` through the running server when it answers, falling back to spawning otherwise. Saves the ~55 ms process start per keystroke. Never required and never prompted for — the cost is a second code path to keep in sync with the CLI. See `backlog/look-up-word.md`.
- [ ] **[S] Simplified to Traditional conversion for ECDICT glosses** — ECDICT defines English words in Simplified Chinese, so a zh-TW user sees Simplified glosses on every dictionary hit (the result now honestly reports `target: zh-CN` rather than echoing --to). Add an s2t conversion when the resolved target is zh-TW/zh-Hant. There is no converter in the repo yet — needs a dependency or a mapping table.
- [ ] **[S] Covering (word_lc, frq) index in ecdict.db** — A one-letter prefix in `dict search` covers ~60k rows and costs 275 ms with a cold page cache (33 ms warm) because the ranking sort reads the table. A covering index over (word_lc, frq) would let the ORDER BY run off the index. Needs a `dict update ecdict` rebuild, so it is not worth forcing now; the extension avoids the case with a 2-character minimum query.
- [ ] **[S] Rank prefix candidates by lemma frequency via entries.exchange** — Inflected forms have `frq = 0` in ECDICT, so `tests` / `testifying` sort below rare-but-ranked words in `dict search`. Their lemma is in the `exchange` column (`test` -> `s:tests/d:tested/i:testing`), so an unranked row could inherit its lemma rank plus a penalty. See `internal/engine/dictsearch.go` and `pitfalls/ecdict-prefix-search-ranks-obscure-words-first.md`.

==== pitfall: launchd path ====
# Raycast can't find `translate` (`spawn translate ENOENT` / "command not found") though it works in a terminal

**Symptoms** (grep this section): a Raycast Script Command prints `translate: command not found`; a Raycast TS extension throws `Error: spawn translate ENOENT`; the exact same command works fine in a terminal but not from Raycast root search; translation works from the shell but the Raycast command errors or shows nothing.
**First seen**: 2026-07 (anticipated — designed around, not yet hit in prod)
**Affects**: Raycast (macOS) Script Commands + TypeScript extensions on this host; any GUI/launchd-launched process that calls the `translate` binary by bare name.

## Symptom

Calling `translate` by bare name from Raycast fails, e.g. a script's
`translate "$2" --to "$1"` yields `command not found`, or an extension's
`execFile("translate", …)` / `spawn("translate")` throws:

```
Error: spawn translate ENOENT
```

The identical invocation succeeds in Terminal/iTerm, which makes it look like the
binary is "missing" only under Raycast.

## Root cause

Raycast is launched by the macOS GUI (launchd), and GUI-launched processes do
**not** source your interactive shell's rc files (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`). So
`process.env.PATH` inside a Raycast extension/script is the minimal launchd PATH
and does **not** include `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, or
`~/go/bin` — exactly where `translate` gets installed (`go install` / `just install`
→ `~/.local/bin`; Homebrew → `/opt/homebrew/bin`). A bare-name lookup then fails.

## Workaround

Resolve an **absolute** path to the binary instead of trusting PATH.

- Script Commands ([`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/)) —
  probe known dirs (already baked into every script):

  ```sh
  find_translate() {
    for d in "$HOME/.local/bin" /opt/homebrew/bin /usr/local/bin "$HOME/go/bin"; do
      [ -x "$d/translate" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$d/translate"; return 0; }
    done
    command -v translate 2>/dev/null && return 0
    return 1
  }
  ```

- TS extension ([`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
  — a `binaryPath` preference first, then the same 4-dir probe (`resolveBinary()`).

Probe order must keep `~/.local/bin` **first** — the blessed install location
(see sibling below) — so a stray copy elsewhere can't win.

## Prevention

- Never call bare `translate` from any Raycast surface; always resolve an absolute
  path (preference or probe).
- **Test from Raycast, not a terminal.** A terminal inherits your full PATH and
  will happily find the binary, masking the bug entirely.

## Related

- Sibling: [duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md](duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md)
  (why `~/.local/bin` must be first in the probe)
- Reference: [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) "Gotchas"
- Backlog: `TODO.md` P? "Publish the Raycast extension to the store" ·
  [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md)
==== pitfall: installed binary not working tree ====
# Raycast extension shows no models / "unknown flag" after adding a CLI feature

**Symptoms** (grep this section): a new dropdown in the Raycast extension is empty; the Model picker offers only "Default (engine + tier)"; a target/language choice fails with `translate: unknown flag: --no-pair`; `translate models` prints a *translation of the word "models"* instead of a model list; a CLI subcommand you just added behaves as if it doesn't exist; the extension works but ignores a flag you can see in `cmd/`.
**First seen**: 2026-07-26
**Affects**: the Raycast extension (and any front-end using `resolveBinary()`) whenever the repo is ahead of the installed `translate` binary.

## Symptom

After adding `translate models` and `--no-pair` to the CLI and running
`just raycast-dev`, the extension's Model dropdown contained only its own
placeholder, and picking a specific target language failed.

The confusing part is *how* the old binary fails. `translate` takes free text as
its first argument, so an unknown subcommand is not an error — it gets
**translated**:

```console
$ ~/.local/bin/translate models          # v0.5.2, no `models` command
n. 模型( model的名词复数 ); 模特儿; 模式; 典型
```

Exit status 0, plausible-looking output, no JSON. `runModels()` parses it, fails,
and returns `[]` — an empty dropdown with no error anywhere. A naive capability
probe (`translate models --json >/dev/null && echo yes`) reports **yes**.

Flags fail loudly, at least:

```console
$ ~/.local/bin/translate "hi" --to ja --no-pair
translate: unknown flag: --no-pair
```

## Root cause

`just raycast-dev` rebuilds the **extension**, not the **binary**. The extension
never runs `./translate` from the working tree — `resolveBinary()`
(`raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`) deliberately probes absolute install
directories, because Raycast runs under launchd with a restricted PATH (see
[`raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md)):

```
~/.local/bin → /opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin → ~/go/bin
```

So the extension talks to whatever was last installed:

```console
$ ~/.local/bin/translate --version
translate version v0.5.2                 # 4 days old
$ ./translate --version
translate version v0.5.3-0.20260726…+dirty
```

## Workaround

Install the working tree before testing extension features that depend on new CLI
surface:

```sh
just install            # → ~/.local/bin/translate, first in the probe order
translate --version     # confirm it is the dev build, not the tag
```

Beware a second copy shadowing it — `/usr/local/bin/translate` is the Homebrew
install and is also on the probe list, just later. See
[`duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md`](duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md).

## Prevention

- Treat `just install` as part of the loop when a change spans CLI **and**
  extension: `just check && just install && just raycast-dev`.
- Don't probe capability by exit status. `translate <unknown-subcommand>` exits 0
  because it translated the word. Check for the *shape* of the output (this is why
  `runModels`/`runLangs` parse and fall back rather than trusting the exit code).
- Degrade visibly. An empty list is indistinguishable from "nothing configured",
  so `translate-text.tsx` renders an explicit "the installed CLI is probably
  older" note instead of an empty dropdown.
- A published extension faces the same skew with users' installed binaries, only
  permanently — new CLI surface needs a fallback path, not just a newer README.

## Related

- [`raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md) — why the extension resolves an absolute install path at all.
- [`raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`](raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md) — the sibling "you rebuilt the wrong thing" trap (stale `ray develop` bundle).
- `AGENTS.md` — the release/versioning flow that makes the installed binary a tag, not `main`.

I need to correct something important about the syntax — the actual format is `columns=id,status` without square brackets, even though the help text shows `columns=[column]([column],)*` which is just grammar notation, not literal syntax. That's a gotcha worth noting. I've also confirmed that query arguments work both as a single quoted string like `'status=queued'` and as multiple unquoted arguments since clap collects and joins them, and separate arguments like `columns=id,status` work fine too.

Now I'm ready to write out the plan. Let me think through the design carefully — starting with the repo layout. The extension should live at the root because `ray build`, `ray develop`, and `ray lint` all expect the cwd to be the extension root where they can find `package.json` and write output files like `raycast-env.d.ts` and `.build`. The Raycast store's workflow copies the extension directory as-is into their monorepo, so a root layout maps directly. The knowledge-harness directories like `docs/`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, and `TODO.md` also belong at root alongside the extension, and there's no conflict since Raycast's build tools only care about `src/`, `assets/`, and related extension files.

When publishing to the Raycast store via `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`, the whole directory gets included, so I should recommend adding the harness directories to `.gitignore` or creating a `just store-export` recipe that copies only the publishable subset to avoid review noise. I'll go with the straightforward approach: keep everything at root, document the export workflow as a fallback if needed. For the package.json, I'm setting up the extension metadata with the name "pueue" and author "da-wei_lee", then defining the commands—a menu-bar item that updates every minute, the main tasks view, an add-task form with an optional command argument for quick entry, a groups view, and a quick-add command that takes a required command text parameter. I'm ruling out a separate logs view since that should be accessible from the Tasks panel. For preferences, I'll keep it simple with just a `pueuePath` setting and derive the daemon path from the same directory, which avoids cluttering the config. I'm also thinking through the right way to start the daemon on this machine—likely using `brew services start pueue` on launchd systems.

The safest approach is to detect whether the daemon is brew-services-managed by checking for the LaunchAgent plist, then offer the appropriate start command rather than guessing and potentially creating a duplicate daemon. The real issue is that a daemon spawned from Raycast inherits its environment, which means tasks would run with a degraded PATH. So I should only offer one-click start when the brew-services plist is detected, otherwise just provide copy-to-clipboard with a note about the environment inheritance problem. This is opinionated but defensible, and I'll document it clearly.

For the implementation, I can probe for the brew binary at `/usr/local/bin/brew` or `/opt/homebrew/bin/brew`, then run `brew services start pueue`. If that fails, fall back to copy-to-clipboard. That's cleaner than trying to handle launchctl bootstrap and kickstart separately.

For command preferences, I'll add a dropdown for display mode (running+queued / running only / none), a checkbox for showing groups, and a textfield for max tasks. But I need to correct something: Raycast's `interval` field in the manifest can't be overridden by a preference — the user can only change it through Raycast Settings directly. So I shouldn't add an interval preference since it wouldn't actually work.

Now I'm organizing the pueue library into separate modules: types for wire protocol definitions, normalize for pure utility functions like status classification and duration calculations, errors for the error taxonomy with ANSI stripping, and binary for resolving the pueue binary and daemon.

# Pueue Raycast Extension — Implementation Plan

## 0. Corrections to the brief (verified on this machine)

These change the design, so they come first.

| # | Premise | Verified reality |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "`--color never` and `NO_COLOR=1` do NOT suppress ANSI" | **True, and worse**: `--color` is a *global* option. `pueue status --color never --json` exits **2** with a clap error (`error: unexpected argument '--color' found`). It must go **before** the subcommand: `pueue --color never status --json`. |
| 2 | "Exit codes are 0/1 only" | **False.** clap argument errors exit **2**. A third error shape exists and must be handled, or a flag typo surfaces as a confusing "command failed". |
| 3 | Query DSL `columns=[...]` | **Brackets are grammar meta-notation, not literal.** `columns=[id]` → `Failed to parse query … expected column`. The working form is `columns=id,status`. (Irrelevant for `--json` anyway — column selection does not trim the JSON.) |
| 4 | "make `interval` a command preference (Brew does)" | **Brew does not**, and it *cannot work*. I read the installed manifest: `services-menu` hard-codes `"interval": "1m"` with no interval preference. `interval` is a manifest field; a preference cannot change it. Raycast itself renders a refresh-interval control in the command's settings. **Do not ship an interval preference — it would be a lie.** (The stale comment in brew's own `services-menu.tsx` says "configurable in the command preferences"; the manifest disagrees.) |
| 5 | (not mentioned) | `pueue kill -g GROUP` **also pauses the group** (verified in `--help`). `pueue group remove NAME` **moves all its tasks to `default`**. Both need loud confirmation copy. |
| 6 | "structure `src/lib/` so a socket transport could be swapped in later" | The seam only holds if **mutations are modelled as a discriminated data union**, not as argv arrays. See §3. |
| 7 | (not mentioned) | `new Date(null)` returns **1970-01-01, not `Invalid Date`**. Since `Stashed.enqueue_at` is `string \| null`, a naive `new Date(enqueueAt)` renders "1970" instead of "—". |
| 8 | (not mentioned) | The query DSL is applied by the **pueue client binary**, not the daemon. It reduces stdout size and Node-side `JSON.parse` cost, but not daemon→client traffic. Still worth exposing for huge queues. |

## 1. Repo layout

**Extension at the repo root.** Not a subdirectory.

Justification:
- `ray build` / `ray develop` / `ray lint` all resolve `./package.json`, write `./raycast-env.d.ts`, and emit `./.build` relative to cwd. A subdir means every command is `cd extension && …`.
- Store submission (`npm run publish`) forks `raycast/extensions` and copies the extension directory verbatim into `extensions/pueue/`. Root layout maps 1:1.

        ├── group-dropdown.tsx   # List.Dropdown seeded static → live
        ├── format.tsx           # icons/colors/duration/relative-time
        └── hooks.ts             # useDebouncedValue (11 lines, lifted verbatim)
```

**Publishing caveat.** `npm run publish` uploads the extension folder; `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `TODO.md`, `Justfile` would ride along and add review noise. Escape hatch: a `just store-export` recipe that `rsync`s a clean subset to `/tmp/pueue-store/` and runs publish from there. Don't do this pre-emptively — only if a reviewer objects.

Notes on choices:
- `@types/node` pinned to **`^22`** on purpose. Raycast's runtime is bundled Node 22 even though `node -v` in this shell is 24.13.1 — typing against 24 lets you write APIs that throw at runtime.
- No `interval` preference (§0 #4).
- No `subtitle` on commands — the extension is already titled "Pueue"; a `"Pueue"` subtitle on every row is pure noise here (brew needs it because "Search" alone is ambiguous).
- `tasks` takes a `query` **text argument**, not a dropdown: it's the escape hatch to the server-side DSL from root search, and the DSL values are unbounded.
- `quick-add`'s `label` argument is optional; the group and cwd come from `LocalStorage` written by the Add Task form.
- **Never hand-write a `Preferences` interface.** `ray build` generates `Preferences.Tasks`, `Preferences.QueueMenu`, `Arguments.Tasks`, etc. with required fields — so a code default that drifts from the manifest becomes a compile error. The reference's `lib/translate.ts` violates this with its local `interface Prefs`; do not copy that.

## 3. `src/lib/pueue/` — the transport seam

### 3.1 Why a directory, not one file

`translate.ts` is 612 lines and already at the edge. Pueue has ~15 mutations, 3 reads, a streaming surface, a 6-variant recursive enum, and a 4-way error taxonomy. More importantly, **the seam has to be a file boundary to be swappable**: `cli-transport.ts` is the only file a future CBOR socket transport replaces.

### 3.2 `types.ts` — the wire (1:1 with `pueue_lib` v4.0.4 serde)

```ts
/** Externally tagged, and it mixes bare strings with single-field objects. */
export type TaskResult =
  | "Success"
  | "Killed"
  | "Errored"
  | "DependencyFailed"
  | { Failed: number }          // exit code
  | { FailedToSpawn: string };  // spawn error message

/**
 * Externally tagged, recursive through `Locked`. There is NO flat
 * `"status": "Running"` string anywhere in a Task.
 *
 * NOTE the one-letter split: Stashed carries `enqueue_at` (when it WILL be
 * enqueued, nullable); every other variant carries `enqueued_at` (when it WAS).
 */
export type TaskStatus =
  | { Stashed: { enqueue_at: string | null } }
  | { Queued: { enqueued_at: string } }
  | { Running: { enqueued_at: string; start: string } }
  | { Paused: { enqueued_at: string; start: string } }
  | { Locked: { previous_status: TaskStatus } }
  | {
      Done: {
        enqueued_at: string;
        start: string;
        end: string;
        result: TaskResult;
      };
    };

/** Exactly what `status --json` puts in `tasks["<id>"]`. */
export interface RawTask {
  id: number;
  created_at: string;
  original_command: string;
  command: string;
  path: string;
  /** A full snapshot of the submitting shell's environment. May contain secrets. */
  envs: Record<string, string>;
  group: string;
  dependencies: number[];
  priority: number;
  label: string | null;
  status: TaskStatus;
}

/**
 * The app-facing task. `envs` is DROPPED at the parse boundary and never
 * reaches a component, a cache, or disk. See stripEnvs() for why.
 */
export type Task = Omit<RawTask, "envs">;

export type GroupStatus = "Running" | "Paused" | "Reset";
export interface Group {
  status: GroupStatus;
  parallel_tasks: number;
}

/** `status --json` top level. */
export interface State {
  tasks: Record<string, Task>;
  groups: Record<string, Group>;
}

/**
 * `group --json` returns the INNER map only — `{"default": {...}}`, NOT
 * `{"groups": {...}}`. Different top-level shape from `status --json`.
 * Feeding one parser to both is the single easiest bug in this codebase.
 */
export type GroupMap = Record<string, Group>;

/** `log --json` → `{"<id>": {task, output}}`. `task.envs` is blanked to {} here. */
export interface LogEntry {
  task: Task;
  output: string;
}
export type LogMap = Record<string, LogEntry>;

/** Timestamped read, so the UI can say how stale it is. */
export interface Snapshot {
  state: State;
  fetchedAt: number;
}
```

**Why `envs` is stripped at parse:**
1. `useCachedPromise` persists its result to the disk-backed `Cache`. Caching `envs` writes every secret in the submitting shell's environment to Raycast's cache directory in plaintext.
2. Upstream cites ~2 MB of state for 400 tasks, virtually all of it `envs`. The menu-bar command re-parses this every 60 s.
3. Nothing in the v1 UI needs it.

Explicit opt-in accessor for the one place it matters (a "Show Environment" action in the task detail), uncached:

```ts
/** Uncached, on-demand. Never call this from a render path. */
export async function taskEnvs(id: number): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
```

### 3.3 `normalize.ts` — flatten the enums (pure, no I/O, unit-testable)

```ts
import type { Task, TaskStatus, TaskResult } from "./types";

export type StatusKind =
  | "stashed" | "queued" | "running" | "paused" | "locked" | "done"
  | "unknown"; // a future pueue variant must degrade, not throw

export type ResultKind =
  | "success" | "failed" | "failed-to-spawn" | "killed" | "errored"
  | "dependency-failed" | "unknown";

const KINDS: Record<string, StatusKind> = {
  Stashed: "stashed", Queued: "queued", Running: "running",
  Paused: "paused", Locked: "locked", Done: "done",
};

export function statusKind(s: TaskStatus): StatusKind {
  const tag = Object.keys(s)[0];
  return KINDS[tag] ?? "unknown";
}

/** Locked wraps the status the task will return to. Unwrap it recursively. */
export function unwrapLocked(s: TaskStatus): TaskStatus {
  return "Locked" in s ? unwrapLocked(s.Locked.previous_status) : s;
}

/** The kind a Locked task will resume as — what to show as a secondary badge. */
export function underlyingKind(s: TaskStatus): StatusKind {
  return statusKind(unwrapLocked(s));
}

export function taskResult(s: TaskStatus): TaskResult | undefined {
  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
  return "Done" in u ? u.Done.result : undefined;
}

export function resultKind(r: TaskResult | undefined): ResultKind | undefined {
  if (r === undefined) return undefined;
  if (typeof r === "string") {
    switch (r) {
      case "Success": return "success";
      case "Killed": return "killed";
      case "Errored": return "errored";
      case "DependencyFailed": return "dependency-failed";
      default: return "unknown";
    }
  }
  if ("Failed" in r) return "failed";
  if ("FailedToSpawn" in r) return "failed-to-spawn";
  return "unknown";
}

/** The process exit code, only for `{ Failed: n }`. Success has none on the wire. */
export function exitCode(r: TaskResult | undefined): number | undefined {
  return r && typeof r === "object" && "Failed" in r ? r.Failed : undefined;
}

export const isDone = (t: Task) => underlyingKind(t.status) === "done";
export const isRunning = (t: Task) => underlyingKind(t.status) === "running";
export const isSuccess = (t: Task) => resultKind(taskResult(t.status)) === "success";
/** Anything that finished without Success — including Killed and DependencyFailed. */
export function isFailed(t: Task): boolean {
  const k = resultKind(taskResult(t.status));
  return k !== undefined && k !== "success";
}
/** Not finished: the queue still owes you something. */
export const isActive = (t: Task) =>
  !isDone(t) && underlyingKind(t.status) !== "stashed";

/* ---- timestamps -------------------------------------------------------- */

/**
 * Guarded parse. `new Date(null)` returns 1970-01-01, NOT Invalid Date, so a
 * Stashed task with `enqueue_at: null` would render as 1970 without this.
 * Chrono emits RFC3339 with microseconds and a numeric offset
 * ("2026-04-27T11:01:06.893055+08:00") — never Z, never epoch. V8 parses the
 * extra fractional digits and truncates to ms; verified.
 */
export function parseTs(s: string | null | undefined): Date | undefined {
  if (!s) return undefined;
  const d = new Date(s);
  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? undefined : d;
}

/** Handles the enqueue_at / enqueued_at split. Stashed may legitimately be undefined. */
export function enqueuedAt(s: TaskStatus): Date | undefined {
  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
  if ("Stashed" in u) return parseTs(u.Stashed.enqueue_at);
  if ("Queued" in u) return parseTs(u.Queued.enqueued_at);
  if ("Running" in u) return parseTs(u.Running.enqueued_at);
  if ("Paused" in u) return parseTs(u.Paused.enqueued_at);
  if ("Done" in u) return parseTs(u.Done.enqueued_at);
  return undefined;
}

export function startedAt(s: TaskStatus): Date | undefined {
  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
  if ("Running" in u) return parseTs(u.Running.start);
  if ("Paused" in u) return parseTs(u.Paused.start);
  if ("Done" in u) return parseTs(u.Done.start);
  return undefined;
}

export function endedAt(s: TaskStatus): Date | undefined {
  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
  return "Done" in u ? parseTs(u.Done.end) : undefined;
}

/** Wall-clock runtime: end−start for finished tasks, now−start for live ones. */
export function durationMs(t: Task, now = Date.now()): number | undefined {
  const start = startedAt(t.status);
  if (!start) return undefined;
  const end = endedAt(t.status);
  return (end ? end.getTime() : now) - start.getTime();
}

/** A short human label: "running", "failed (127)", "killed", "success". */
export function statusLabel(t: Task): string;
/** The token typed into the search bar to find this task — feeds List.Item keywords. */
export function statusKeywords(t: Task): string[];
```

`format.tsx` layers presentation on top (kept out of `normalize.ts` so the latter stays React-free):

```ts
export function statusIcon(t: Task): Image.ImageLike;
// running   → { source: Icon.CircleProgress,  tintColor: Color.Blue }
// paused    → { source: Icon.Pause,           tintColor: Color.Orange }
// queued    → { source: Icon.Clock,           tintColor: Color.SecondaryText }
// stashed   → { source: Icon.Tray,            tintColor: Color.SecondaryText }
// locked    → { source: Icon.Lock,            tintColor: Color.Purple }
// success   → { source: Icon.CheckCircle,     tintColor: Color.Green }
// failed    → { source: Icon.XMarkCircle,     tintColor: Color.Red }
// killed    → { source: Icon.Stop,            tintColor: Color.Red }
// depfailed → { source: Icon.MinusCircle,     tintColor: Color.Red }
export function formatDuration(ms: number | undefined): string; // "1.2s" / "3m 04s" / "1h 12m"
```

### 3.4 `errors.ts` — taxonomy + stderr normalizer

```ts
export type PueueErrorKind =
  | "binary-not-found"    // resolvePueue() failed, or spawn ENOENT
  | "config-missing"      // pueue has never run: no pueue.yml
  | "daemon-not-running"  // config present, socket gone or refused
  | "bad-query"           // the DSL string didn't parse
  | "bad-arguments"       // clap, exit 2 — an extension bug, surface verbatim
  | "timeout"
  | "command-failed";     // anything else

export class PueueError extends Error {
  readonly kind: PueueErrorKind;
  /** ANSI-stripped, eyre-noise-stripped, ready to render. */
  readonly detail: string;
  readonly exitCode: number | null;
  readonly argv: readonly string[];
}

export const isBinaryMissing = (e: unknown) =>
  e instanceof PueueError && e.kind === "binary-not-found";
/** True for both "never configured" and "socket unreachable" — both mean "start it". */
export const isDaemonDown = (e: unknown) =>
  e instanceof PueueError &&
  (e.kind === "daemon-not-running" || e.kind === "config-missing");
```

The normalizer, driven by the three verified shapes:

```ts
// eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex -- color_eyre emits raw SGR even when stderr is a pipe
const ANSI_SGR = /\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g;

/**
 * Turn pueue's stderr into one renderable message.
 *
 * color_eyre writes SGR escapes to stderr even when it is a pipe: neither
 * `--color never` (which is a GLOBAL flag and must precede the subcommand, or
 * clap exits 2) nor NO_COLOR=1 suppresses them. Verified against v4.0.4.
 * It then appends a "Location:" block naming a Rust source file and two
 * RUST_BACKTRACE hints, none of which mean anything to a Raycast user.
 */
export function cleanStderr(raw: string): string {
  const lines = raw.replace(ANSI_SGR, "").split("\n");
  const kept: string[] = [];
  for (const line of lines) {
    if (/^Location:\s*$/.test(line)) break;
    if (/^Backtrace omitted/.test(line)) break;
    if (/^Run with RUST_BACKTRACE/.test(line)) continue;
    kept.push(line);
  }
  return kept
    .join("\n")
    .replace(/^Error:\s*\n?/, "")
    // eyre numbers its cause chain "   0: " / "   1: ". Pest's own diagnostic
    // uses "      1 | " (pipe, not colon), so this leaves it intact.
    .replace(/^\s*\d+:\s+/gm, "")
    .replace(/^Pueue:\s*/gm, "")
    .trim();
}

export function classify(detail: string, exitCode: number | null): PueueErrorKind {
  if (/Failed to parse query/i.test(detail)) return "bad-query";
  if (exitCode === 2 && /^error:/im.test(detail)) return "bad-arguments";
  if (/Couldn't find a configuration file/i.test(detail)) return "config-missing";
  // The socket path ends in .socket; the config path ends in .yml. Discriminate
  // on the verb, which is unambiguous: "while connecting to daemon".
  if (/while connecting to daemon/i.test(detail)) return "daemon-not-running";
  if (/Did you start (it|the daemon)/i.test(detail)) return "daemon-not-running";
  if (/(ECONNREFUSED|ENOENT).*socket/i.test(detail)) return "daemon-not-running";
  return "command-failed";
}
```

### 3.5 `binary.ts` — PATH resolution

The #1 hazard. Raycast runs extensions under launchd with no shell rc, so bare `pueue` throws `spawn pueue ENOENT`. Modelled on brew's `paths.ts` (which I read from the installed sourcemap) plus the reference's `resolveBinary()`.

```ts
const PROBE_DIRS = [
  "/opt/homebrew/bin",              // Apple Silicon Homebrew
  "/usr/local/bin",                 // Intel Homebrew — the one that exists on this host
  join(homedir(), ".cargo", "bin"), // cargo install pueue
  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
  "/usr/bin",
  "/bin",
];

let cachedPueue: string | undefined;

/**
 * Absolute path to the `pueue` client.
 * The preference is checked BEFORE the module cache on purpose: a cached probe
 * result must never outlive the user changing the preference mid-session.
 * The preference is existsSync-validated so a stale path falls through to the
 * probe rather than producing an ENOENT with no explanation.
 */
export function resolvePueue(): string {
  const { pueuePath } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
  if (pueuePath && existsSync(pueuePath)) return pueuePath;
  if (cachedPueue && existsSync(cachedPueue)) return cachedPueue;
  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
    const c = join(dir, "pueue");
    if (existsSync(c)) return (cachedPueue = c);
  }
  throw new PueueError("binary-not-found", "pueue CLI not found");
}

/**
 * `pueued`, preferring the SIBLING of the resolved client — a Homebrew client
 * driving a cargo-built daemon is a version-skew bug waiting to happen.
 */
export function resolvePueued(): string | undefined {
  try {
    const sibling = join(dirname(resolvePueue()), "pueued");
    if (existsSync(sibling)) return sibling;
  } catch { /* fall through */ }
  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
    const c = join(dir, "pueued");
    if (existsSync(c)) return c;
  }
  return undefined;
}

/**
 * Pass HOME through so pueue can find its config dir. On macOS that is
 * ~/Library/Application Support/pueue (NOT ~/.config/pueue), and it doubles as
 * the data, socket, and log dir. Deliberately NOT setting NO_COLOR: it does
 * nothing to color_eyre's stderr (verified), and setting it would imply it does.
 */
export function baseEnv(): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
  const { configPath } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
  return {
    ...process.env,
    HOME: process.env.HOME ?? homedir(),
    ...(configPath ? { PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH: configPath } : {}),
  };
}

/**
 * The pueue data directory, for reading task_logs off disk.
 * 1. default macOS path
 * 2. if missing, one regex probe of pueue.yml for a non-null `pueue_directory`
 * 3. give up — callers fall back to `pueue log --json`
 * Deliberately no YAML dependency for one optional key.
 */
export function pueueDirectory(): string | undefined;
export function taskLogPath(id: number): string | undefined; // <dir>/task_logs/<id>.log

/** Homebrew's brew binary, for the one-click daemon start. undefined if absent. */
export function resolveBrew(): string | undefined;
/** True when the daemon is brew-services/launchd managed on this host. */
export function isBrewManagedDaemon(): boolean; // ~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.pueue.plist
```

### 3.6 `transport.ts` — the interface and the Mutation union

**This is the actual seam.** If mutations are `string[]` argv, a socket transport has to parse argv back into intent. Model them as data:

```ts
export type Mutation =
  | { op: "add"; command: string; group?: string; label?: string;
      priority?: number; workingDirectory?: string; after?: number[];
      delay?: string; stashed?: boolean; immediate?: boolean; escape?: boolean }
  | { op: "start";   ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean }
  | { op: "pause";   ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean; wait?: boolean }
  | { op: "kill";    ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean; signal?: string }
  | { op: "restart"; ids: number[]; inPlace?: boolean; stashed?: boolean; immediate?: boolean }
  | { op: "remove";  ids: number[] }
  | { op: "stash";   ids?: number[]; group?: string; delay?: string }
  | { op: "enqueue"; ids?: number[]; group?: string; delay?: string }
  | { op: "clean";   group?: string; successfulOnly?: boolean }
  | { op: "switch";  a: number; b: number }
  | { op: "parallel"; count: number; group?: string }
  | { op: "group-add"; name: string; parallel?: number }
  | { op: "group-remove"; name: string }
  | { op: "send"; id: number; input: string }
  | { op: "reset"; groups?: string[] };

export interface StatusOptions { group?: string; query?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }
export interface LogOptions { lines?: number; full?: boolean; signal?: AbortSignal }
export interface FollowHandlers {
  onData(chunk: string): void;
  onDone(code: number | null): void;
  onError(e: Error): void;
}

export interface PueueTransport {
  /** READ — `status --json`. The only call that returns tasks + groups together. */
  readState(o?: StatusOptions): Promise<State>;
  /** READ — `group --json`. DIFFERENT top-level shape; never route through readState's parser. */
  readGroups(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<GroupMap>;
  /** READ — `log --json`. Defaults to the last 15 lines; `full` can exhaust RAM. */
  readLogs(ids: number[], o?: LogOptions): Promise<LogMap>;
  /** WRITE — exit-code + prose only. Returns the new id for `add`, else void. */
  mutate(m: Mutation): Promise<number | void>;
  /** STREAM — the only push surface pueue has. Returns a cancel fn. */
  followLog(id: number, lines: number, h: FollowHandlers): () => void;
  /** Reachability + version, for onboarding and the >=4.0 guard. */
  probe(): Promise<{ version: string; reachable: boolean }>;
}

let active: PueueTransport | undefined;
export function transport(): PueueTransport {
  return (active ??= createCliTransport()); // swap point for a future socket transport
}
```

### 3.7 `cli-transport.ts` — the swappable implementation

```ts
const pexecFile = promisify(execFile);

/**
 * Global flags go BEFORE the subcommand. `pueue status --color never` exits 2
 * with a clap error — verified. `--color never` does not affect stderr (that is
 * color_eyre, which ignores it), but it does clean up the prose stdout of the
 * mutation commands, which we occasionally surface in a toast.
 */
function globalArgs(): string[] {
  const { configPath } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
  return ["--color", "never", ...(configPath ? ["--config", configPath] : [])];
}

/** Argv for one Mutation. The ONLY place argv is constructed. */
export function argvFor(m: Mutation): string[] {
  switch (m.op) {
    case "add": {
      const a = ["add"];
      if (m.workingDirectory) a.push("--working-directory", m.workingDirectory);
      if (m.group) a.push("--group", m.group);
      if (m.label) a.push("--label", m.label);
      if (m.priority !== undefined) a.push("--priority", String(m.priority));
      for (const id of m.after ?? []) a.push("--after", String(id));
      if (m.delay) a.push("--delay", m.delay);
      if (m.stashed) a.push("--stashed");
      if (m.immediate) a.push("--immediate");
      if (m.escape) a.push("--escape");
      a.push("--print-task-id");
      // The command goes LAST and as ONE argv element. pueue joins the variadic
      // <COMMAND>... with spaces and hands the result to `sh -c`, so we must not
      // shell-quote it ourselves — and must never build a shell string.
      a.push("--", m.command);
      return a;
    }
    case "kill": {
      const a = ["kill"];
      if (m.all) a.push("--all");
      if (m.group) a.push("--group", m.group);
      if (m.signal) a.push("--signal", m.signal);
      a.push(...(m.ids ?? []).map(String));
      return a;
    }
    /* … one case per variant … */
  }
}

const READ_TIMEOUT = 10_000;
const WRITE_TIMEOUT = 15_000;
/** status --json carries a full env snapshot per task: ~2 MB for 400 tasks. */
const STATUS_MAX_BUFFER = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

async function readState(o: StatusOptions = {}): Promise<State> {
  const bin = resolvePueue();
  const args = [...globalArgs(), "status", "--json"];
  if (o.group) args.push("--group", o.group);
  // The query is variadic <QUERY>...; pass it as ONE argv element.
  if (o.query?.trim()) args.push(o.query.trim());
  const { stdout } = await run(bin, args, {
    timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, maxBuffer: STATUS_MAX_BUFFER, signal: o.signal,
  });
  const raw = JSON.parse(stdout) as { tasks: Record<string, RawTask>; groups: GroupMap };
  // Guard against ever being handed `group --json`'s shape.
  if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || !("tasks" in raw)) {
    throw new PueueError("command-failed", "Unexpected status payload");
  }
  return { tasks: stripEnvs(raw.tasks), groups: raw.groups ?? {} };
}

/** Drop `envs` before anything can cache it to disk or render it. */
function stripEnvs(tasks: Record<string, RawTask>): Record<string, Task> {
  const out: Record<string, Task> = {};
  for (const [k, t] of Object.entries(tasks)) {
    const { envs: _drop, ...lean } = t;
    out[k] = lean;
  }
  return out;
}

async function readGroups(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<GroupMap> {
  const { stdout } = await run(resolvePueue(), [...globalArgs(), "group", "--json"], {
    timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024, signal,
  });
  const parsed = JSON.parse(stdout);
  // `group --json` returns the INNER map. If someone ever "fixes" it upstream to
  // match status, unwrap rather than break.
  return ("groups" in parsed ? parsed.groups : parsed) as GroupMap;
}

/**
 * `pueue follow <id>` — the only streaming surface. It tails the on-disk log at
 * a 250 ms poll and exits when the task stops. Exit 1 + "The task to be followed
 * doesn't exist." for a bad id. Returns a cancel fn for useEffect's teardown.
 */
function followLog(id: number, lines: number, h: FollowHandlers): () => void {
  const child = spawn(resolvePueue(),
    [...globalArgs(), "follow", String(id), "--lines", String(lines)],
    { env: baseEnv() });
  /* … same shape as the reference's spawnTranslateStream … */
  return () => { if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM"); };
}
```

`run()` is the shared wrapper: `pexecFile` with `env: baseEnv()`, per-call `timeout`/`maxBuffer`/`signal`, and a catch that turns `err.code === "ENOENT"` into `binary-not-found` and everything else into `new PueueError(classify(cleanStderr(err.stderr), err.code), …)`.

`probe()` is the module-level cached lookup with the reference's swallow-and-fall-back discipline — but note the reference's own pitfall: **never probe capability by exit status alone**; parse the shape. `pueue --version` prints `pueue 4.0.4`; match `/^pueue (\d+)\.(\d+)/` and treat an unparseable result as "unknown, assume 4".

### 3.8 `index.ts` — the public API views actually import

```ts
export * from "./types";
export * from "./normalize";
export { PueueError, isBinaryMissing, isDaemonDown, cleanStderr } from "./errors";
export { taskLogPath, pueueDirectory, resolveBrew, isBrewManagedDaemon } from "./binary";

export const status  = (o?: StatusOptions) => transport().readState(o);
export const groups  = (s?: AbortSignal)   => transport().readGroups(s);
export const logs    = (ids: number[], o?: LogOptions) => transport().readLogs(ids, o);
export const follow  = (id: number, lines: number, h: FollowHandlers) =>
  transport().followLog(id, lines, h);
export const mutate  = (m: Mutation) => transport().mutate(m);

/** Timestamped read for the menu bar — one cache entry holds data AND its age. */
export async function snapshot(o?: StatusOptions): Promise<Snapshot> {
  return { state: await status(o), fetchedAt: Date.now() };
}

/** Read the merged stdout+stderr log straight off disk. Falls back to the CLI. */
export async function readLogText(id: number, maxBytes = 512 * 1024): Promise<string>;

/** Uncached, on demand, never rendered by default. */
export async function taskEnvs(id: number): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
```

## 4. The menu-bar command (`src/queue-menu.tsx`)

### 4.1 Data

```tsx
const { data, isLoading, revalidate, mutate: mutateState } = useCachedPromise(
  async (query: string): Promise<Snapshot> => snapshot({ query }),
  [prefs.menuQuery ?? ""],
  { keepPreviousData: true, failureToastOptions: { title: "Pueue" } },
);
```

`useCachedPromise` is `Cache`-backed, so the first paint after a Raycast restart is the last successful state — no blank menu. Returning `{ state, fetchedAt }` from the fetch means **the age lives in the same cache entry as the data**; no second `Cache` mechanism, no drift between them.

### 4.2 `title` / `icon` / `tooltip`

```tsx
const running = tasks.filter(isRunning).length;
const queued  = tasks.filter(t => underlyingKind(t.status) === "queued").length;
const paused  = tasks.filter(t => underlyingKind(t.status) === "paused").length;
const failed  = tasks.filter(isFailed).length;

// Hidden at zero — no badge API exists, the count IS the title, and
// `undefined` is what removes it (the Brew idiom).
const title =
  prefs.titleCounts === "none"           ? undefined
  : prefs.titleCounts === "running-queued" ? (running || queued ? `${running}/${queued}` : undefined)
  : prefs.titleCounts === "active"         ? (running + queued + paused || undefined) && String(running + queued + paused)
  : running > 0 ? String(running) : undefined;
```

Order of precedence in the title: **running first**. Running is the only count that changes on its own; queued is a backlog you already know about.

Icon — one glyph, four tints, so the shape never moves in the menu bar:

| Condition | icon |
|---|---|
| binary missing / daemon down | `{ source: Icon.XMarkCircle, tintColor: Color.Red }` |
| any failed task | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.Red }` |
| every group paused | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.Orange }` |
| last fetch errored, showing cached data | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.SecondaryText }` |
| normal | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.PrimaryText }` |

`pueue-menubar.svg` must be a **monochrome template glyph** — a coloured asset looks wrong on a dark menu bar. `tintColor: Color.PrimaryText` is exactly what brew does.

Tooltip: `"Pueue — 2 running, 5 queued, 1 failed"`, or `"Pueue — daemon not running"`, or `"Pueue — stale, last update 14:32"`.

### 4.3 Structure

```
<MenuBarExtra icon={…} title={…} tooltip={…} isLoading={isLoading}>

  {/* only when errored — see 4.6 */}
  <Section>  Pueue daemon not running / Start Daemon / Copy … / Open Preferences </Section>

  <Section title={`Running (${running})`}>
    {top(runningTasks).map(t =>
      <Submenu key={t.id} title={`${t.id} · ${oneline(t.command, 48)}`} icon={statusIcon(t)}>
        <Item title="Follow Output"  onAction={openTasksAt(t)} />
        <Item title="Kill"           icon={Icon.Stop}
              alternate={<Item title="Kill (SIGINT)" onAction={…signal:"int"} />}
              onAction={act({op:"kill", ids:[t.id]})} />
        <Item title="Copy Command"   onAction={() => Clipboard.copy(t.command)} />
      </Submenu>)}
    {more(runningTasks)}
  </Section>

  <Section title={`Queued (${queued})`}>   … Start Now / Stash / Copy · ⌥ Remove </Section>
  <Section title={`Failed (${failed})`}>   … Show Log / Restart · ⌥ Restart in Place / Copy · ⌥ Remove </Section>

  {prefs.showGroups && (
    <Section title="Groups">
      {groupEntries.map(([name, g]) =>
        <Submenu key={name} title={`${name} — ${g.status.toLowerCase()} (${runningIn(name)}/${g.parallel_tasks})`}>
          <Item title={g.status === "Running" ? "Pause Group" : "Resume Group"} … />
          <Submenu title="Parallelism">
            {[1,2,3,4,6,8,0].map(n =>
              <Item key={n} title={n === 0 ? "Unlimited" : String(n)}
                    icon={n === g.parallel_tasks ? Icon.Checkmark : undefined} … />)}
          </Submenu>
        </Submenu>)}
    </Section>)}

  <Section>
    <Item title="Add Task…"  icon={Icon.Plus}          onAction={launch("add-task")} />
    <Item title="Open Tasks" icon={Icon.AppWindowList} onAction={launch("tasks")} />
    <Item title="Pause All"  icon={Icon.Pause}
          alternate={<Item title="Pause All (let running finish)" … wait:true />} … />
    <Item title="Start All"  icon={Icon.Play} … />
    <Item title="Clean Finished" icon={Icon.Trash}
          alternate={<Item title="Clean Successful Only" … />} … />   {/* ⌥-only, see 4.4 */}
  </Section>

  <Section>
    <Item title={`Updated ${fmtClock(data.fetchedAt)}`} />   {/* no onAction → disabled label */}
    <Item title="Refresh" icon={Icon.ArrowClockwise} onAction={() => revalidate()} />
  </Section>
</MenuBarExtra>
```

Rules honoured:
- **No two identical `Item`s at the same level.** Every title is prefixed with the task id, and the per-task actions live inside per-task `Submenu`s — which also keeps the top level short.
- **Empty submenus render disabled**, which is fine and self-documenting for an empty Groups list.
- `maxItemsPerSection` (default 7) with a trailing `…and N more` item that `launchCommand`s the Tasks view. A 400-task queue must not become 400 menu items on every 60 s tick.
- The `Updated HH:MM` disabled item is the mitigation for the restore-from-database problem (§4.5).

### 4.4 One-click vs confirmed

**No `confirmAlert` anywhere in the menu bar.** `confirmAlert` presents in the Raycast window, and a menu-bar command runs with the window closed — I have not verified it works there, and a silently-swallowed confirmation on a destructive action is unacceptable. Instead:

| Action | Menu bar |
|---|---|
| Kill, Restart, Start, Pause, Stash, Enqueue, set parallelism | plain one-click + `showHUD` echo |
| Remove, Clean | `alternate` only (⌥) — unreachable by accident |
| Reset, Remove Group | **not offered at all** — Tasks/Groups view, behind `confirmAlert` |

`showToast` falls back to `showHUD` when the window is closed, so `showFailureToast` is safe to call from a menu-bar action.

### 4.5 `isLoading` and refresh mechanics

Drive `isLoading` straight from `useCachedPromise` — never leave it unset (Raycast would render and immediately unload), never leave it true (the tree re-runs every tick until it goes false). `keepPreviousData: true` means the cached value paints instantly while `isLoading` is true, so there is no blank frame.

`interval: "1m"`. Docs contradict themselves on the floor (background-refresh page says `10s`, manifest page says `1m`); `1m` is the safe value and matches the shipping Brew extension. Scheduling is jittered by macOS energy policy and the command is auto-terminated on a timeout scaled to the interval — 22–44 ms per `status --json` is nowhere near it.

**Stale-restore mitigation.** When Raycast restarts, the menu bar item is restored from Raycast's database rather than by re-running the command, so a stale render survives until the next tick (upstream #14250, #20031, #14659). Three defences, all cheap:
1. The `Updated HH:MM` disabled item — makes staleness *visible* rather than misleading. This is the important one.
2. A `Refresh` item that `revalidate()`s.
3. On a failed fetch with cached data present: keep the data, tint `SecondaryText`, and set the tooltip to `Pueue — stale, last update HH:MM`.

`updateCommandMetadata`: **yes.** Call it inside the fetch's `onData`:
```ts
updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle: down ? "Daemon not running" : `${running} running · ${queued} queued` });
```
It only affects the calling command's own root-search subtitle, so `tasks.tsx` sets its own too.

### 4.6 Degradation

A `MenuBarExtra` cannot render a `List.EmptyView`, and returning `null` removes the item entirely — which is the wrong answer for a user who deliberately enabled a pueue menu-bar command. Render the error state:

```tsx
if (error && !data) {
  const d = describeError(error);          // shared descriptor, see §7
  return (
    <MenuBarExtra icon={{ source: Icon.XMarkCircle, tintColor: Color.Red }} tooltip={`Pueue — ${d.title}`}>
      <MenuBarExtra.Item title={d.title} />          {/* no onAction → disabled header */}
      <MenuBarExtra.Section>
        {d.actions.map(a => <MenuBarExtra.Item key={a.id} title={a.title} icon={a.icon} onAction={a.run} />)}
      </MenuBarExtra.Section>
    </MenuBarExtra>
  );
}
```

Binary missing → `Copy “brew install pueue”`, `Open Extension Preferences`, `Open Pueue Documentation`.
Daemon down → `Start Daemon` (only when brew-managed, see §7), `Copy “brew services start pueue”`, `Copy “pueued -d”`, `Open Tasks`.
