## 5. View commands

### 5.1 Tasks (`src/tasks.tsx`) — **v1**

```tsx
const [group, setGroup] = useCachedState("tasks.group", ALL_GROUPS);
const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
const stateAbort = useRef<AbortController>();
const groupsAbort = useRef<AbortController>();   // separate refs — look-up-word.tsx pattern

const st = useCachedPromise(
  (g: string, q: string) => status({ group: g === ALL_GROUPS ? undefined : g,
                                     query: q, signal: stateAbort.current?.signal }),
  [group, props.arguments?.query ?? ""],
  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: stateAbort },
);

const gr = useCachedPromise(() => groups(groupsAbort.current?.signal), [],
  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: groupsAbort });

// Log preview for the SELECTED row only — never per row.
const preview = usePromise(
  (id: string | null) => (id ? logs([Number(id)], { lines: prefs.detailLogLines }) : Promise.resolve({})),
  [selectedId], { execute: showDetail && selectedId !== null },
);

const isLoading = st.isLoading || gr.isLoading;
const error = st.error ?? gr.error;
```

- **Searching is client-side** via `keywords` per item (the `history.tsx` idiom): the whole state is already in memory, and the server-side DSL's `%=` only covers `command` and `label`. Keywords per row: `[String(id), command, original_command, label ?? "", group, statusKind, resultKind, path]`. The DSL stays available as the `query` **command argument**, so `Tasks` can be launched from root search with `status=failed order_by id desc first 20` — and note the DSL is applied by the pueue *client*, so it shrinks the JSON we parse, not the daemon traffic.
- **Group filter** is the single `searchBarAccessory` (Raycast allows only one), a `<GroupDropdown>` seeded with a static `["All Groups", "default"]` so it never paints empty, then swapped for the live map — and preserving an unknown current value as a synthetic item so a deleted group doesn't silently reset the filter. Lifted straight from `language-dropdown.tsx`.
- **Status filtering is by section**, not a second dropdown: `Running`, `Paused`, `Locked`, `Queued`, `Stashed`, `Failed`, `Done`. Sections give grouping for free and the search bar filters across all of them; typing "failed" narrows via keywords.
- **Detail pane**: `isShowingDetail` from `useCachedState("tasks.showDetail", prefs.showDetail)`, toggled by ⌘⇧D. `List.Item.Detail` with `metadata` (id, status, result + exit code, group, label, priority, path, dependencies, created / enqueued / started / ended, duration) and `markdown` = a fenced block of the last N log lines from `preview`.

Actions (ordering matters — the first is ⏎):

| Shortcut | Action | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ⏎ | Show Log | `Action.Push` → `<TaskLogView>` |
| ⌘⏎ | Follow Output | `Action.Push` → `<TaskFollowView>`, only when running |
| ⌘⇧D | Toggle Detail | |
| ⌘R | Restart | ⌥ alternate: Restart in Place (overwrites logs — say so in the title) |
| ⌘K | Kill | `confirmAlert` + `rememberUserChoice`, `Alert.ActionStyle.Destructive` |
| ⌘E | Enqueue / ⌘S Stash | rendered conditionally on `statusKind` |
| ⌘⌫ | Remove | `confirmAlert`; disabled with an explanatory toast for running/paused tasks — `pueue remove` refuses them and you must kill first |
| ⌘C / ⌘⇧C | Copy Command / Copy Task ID | |
| ⌘O | Open Working Directory | `Action.ShowInFinder path={t.path}` |
| ⌘N | Add Task | `Action.Push` → the Add form |
| ⌘⇧R | Reload | |

**Refresh after a mutation — the load-bearing detail.** The daemon processes requests asynchronously on its own update loop, so a state change may not be visible in the very next `status` call. `mutate`'s default `shouldRevalidateAfter: true` fires *immediately* after the promise resolves, reads pre-change state, and **visually undoes your optimistic update**. So:

```ts
/**
 * The daemon acknowledges a request before its update loop has applied it, so
 * the very next `status --json` can still show the old state. Revalidating
 * immediately (mutate's default) would therefore roll the optimistic update
 * back on screen and then flip it forward again a minute later. Suppress the
 * automatic revalidate and schedule one after the loop has had a turn.
 */
const RECONCILE_DELAY_MS = 700;

async function act(m: Mutation, opts: { verb: string }) {
  const toast = await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Animated, title: opts.verb });
  try {
    await st.mutate(mutate(m), {
      optimisticUpdate: (s) => applyMutation(s, m),   // pure, src/lib/optimistic.ts
      rollbackOnError: true,
      shouldRevalidateAfter: false,
    });
    toast.style = Toast.Style.Success;
    toast.title = `${opts.verb} — done`;
    setTimeout(() => st.revalidate(), RECONCILE_DELAY_MS);
  } catch (e) {
    await showFailureToast(e, { title: opts.verb });
  }
}
```

`src/lib/optimistic.ts` is pure and unit-testable:

```ts
/** Expected post-mutation State, for the optimistic paint. Never sent anywhere. */
export function applyMutation(s: State | undefined, m: Mutation): State {
  // kill    → Running/Paused ids become Done + Killed
  // start   → Queued/Stashed ids become Running; group.status = "Running"
  // pause   → Running ids become Paused;         group.status = "Paused"
  // stash   → Queued ids become Stashed(enqueue_at: null)
  // enqueue → Stashed ids become Queued(enqueued_at: now)
  // remove  → delete the ids
  // clean   → delete every Done task (successfulOnly → only Success)
  // parallel→ groups[name].parallel_tasks = count
  // add     → cannot be predicted (the id comes back from the CLI) → return s
}
```

Loading / empty / error:
- `isLoading` from the merged hooks.
- Empty: `<List.EmptyView icon={Icon.Tray} title="No tasks" description="Nothing queued. ⌘N adds one." />` with an Add action.
- Error: `isBinaryMissing(e)` → `<PueueNotFoundView/>`; `isDaemonDown(e)` → `<DaemonDownView/>`; `kind === "bad-query"` → a dedicated empty view echoing `cleanStderr` and the DSL grammar; else generic. **All rendered inside a `<List>`** — `List.EmptyView` is not standalone (the reference's `binary-not-found.tsx` has this constraint baked in).

### 5.2 Add Task (`src/add-task.tsx`) — **v1**

`Form` + `useForm`, `enableDrafts: true` so a half-typed pipeline survives a dismissal.

| Field | Component | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | `Form.TextArea`, required, autoFocus | Multi-line so a long pipeline fits. `info`: "Run by the daemon via `sh -c`. `&&`, `\|`, and `>` work. A trailing `&` detaches the process and the task finishes instantly." |
| `workingDirectory` | `Form.FilePicker` `canChooseDirectories canChooseFiles={false} allowMultipleSelection={false}` | Default from `LocalStorage("add.cwd")`, else `homedir()` |
| `group` | `Form.Dropdown` | Live from `groups()`, static `default` fallback so it never paints empty |
| `label` | `Form.TextField` | |
| `priority` | `Form.TextField` | `validation: (v) => v && !/^-?\d+$/.test(v) ? "Must be an integer" : undefined` |
| `dependencies` | `Form.TagPicker` | Options = current queued/stashed/running tasks, `title={`${id} · ${oneline(command)}`}`, `value={String(id)}`. Far better than a free-text id list. |
| `delay` | `Form.TextField` | `info`: "Seconds, or a date expression: `2h`, `18:30`, `2026-08-01T18:30:00`" |
| `startMode` | `Form.Dropdown`: Queued (default) / Stashed / Start immediately | **Collapses the mutually-exclusive `-s`/`-i` pair into one control.** Two checkboxes would let a user tick both. |
| `escape` | `Form.Checkbox`, default false | `info`: "Escapes shell metacharacters — this disables `&&`, `\|`, `>`" |

Submit → `mutate({op:"add", …})` → returns the new id from `--print-task-id`. Then:
```ts
await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Success, title: `Queued task ${id}`,
  primaryAction: { title: "Open Tasks", onAction: () => launchCommand({ name: "tasks", type: LaunchType.UserInitiated }) } });
await LocalStorage.setItem("add.cwd", values.workingDirectory[0]);
await LocalStorage.setItem("add.group", values.group);
popToRoot();
// Force the menu bar to catch up rather than waiting up to a minute.
launchCommand({ name: "queue-menu", type: LaunchType.Background }).catch(() => {});
```
That last line is the documented use of `launchCommand` — forcing a background refresh of a sibling command. It resolves when launched, not when the target finishes, so it must not be awaited for correctness.

**Escaping discipline**: `pueue add` takes `<COMMAND>...` variadic and joins with spaces; pass the whole command as **one argv element after `--`** via `execFile`. Never build a shell string, never `shell: true`. The user's text is already a shell command line — pueue runs it under `sh -c` itself.

When Add Task is pushed from Tasks (⌘N), thread an `onAdded` callback into it and call `revalidate()` — the `onRecorded → revalidate()` pattern from `look-up-word.tsx`, which lands while the pushed view is still open so the list is already fresh when it pops.

### 5.3 Groups (`src/groups.tsx`) — **v1**

Two `useCachedPromise`s with separate abort refs (`groups()` for authority on `status`/`parallel_tasks`, `status()` for per-group task counts), merged `isLoading`/`error`.

Row: `title={name}`, `accessories=[{ tag: {value: g.status, color: …} }, { text: `${runningIn(name)}/${g.parallel_tasks || "∞"}` }, { text: `${queuedIn(name)} queued` }]`.

Actions:
| Shortcut | Action | Copy that matters |
|---|---|---|
| ⏎ | Show Tasks in Group | `launchCommand({name:"tasks", context:{group}})` |
| ⌘P / ⌘S | Pause / Resume Group | ⌥ alternate on Pause: "Pause (let running tasks finish)" → `--wait` |
| ⌘⇧P | Set Parallelism | Push a one-field Form; `0` = unlimited |
| ⌘N | Add Group | Push a Form (name + parallel) |
| ⌘K | Kill Group | `confirmAlert`: **"This also pauses the group."** (verified from `kill --help`) |
| ⌘⌫ | Remove Group | `confirmAlert`, Destructive: **"All N tasks in this group will be moved to `default`."** (verified from `group remove --help`) |
| ⌘⇧⌫ | Reset Group | `confirmAlert`, Destructive, no `rememberUserChoice` — `reset` kills everything and wipes it |

**Parallelism is read from `group --json`'s `parallel_tasks`, never from `pueue parallel` with no args** — that path is broken in 4.0.4 (logs "Received unhandled response message", exits 0, prints nothing).

### 5.4 Quick Add (`src/quick-add.tsx`) — **v1**, `no-view`, ~35 lines

Reads the `command` (required) and `label` (optional) arguments, pulls group/cwd from `LocalStorage`, calls `mutate({op:"add", …})`, `showHUD(\`Queued task ${id}\`)`, and background-launches `queue-menu`. On error, `showHUD` the cleaned message (a `no-view` command has no window, so `showToast` degrades to HUD anyway). This is the highest value-per-line command in the extension.

### 5.5 Deferred to backlog

Edit Task (`pueue edit` needs a TOML/JSON editor round trip), Send Input (`pueue send` — no way to know whether the process is reading stdin), Switch queue positions (`pueue switch` — needs a two-selection UI), Environment editor (`pueue env set/unset`), a saved-query browser.

## 6. Log viewing — one source per situation

| Situation | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Detail-pane preview for the **selected** row | `pueue log <id> --json --lines 20` | One call returns task + output together; bounded; `envs` already blanked by pueue in this path. Never fetch per row — only on `onSelectionChange`. |
| Full log page for a **finished** task | Read `<pueue_dir>/task_logs/<id>.log` off disk, tailing the last 512 KB | `client.read_local_logs: true` here. Skips the JSON string-escape round trip, skips the `--full` RAM warning, and lets us tail instead of loading everything. Falls back to `pueue log <id> --json --lines 2000` when the file is absent (remote daemon, `read_local_logs: false`, or a non-default `pueue_directory` we couldn't resolve). |
| Live tail of a **running** task | `spawn(pueue, ["follow", id, "--lines", "200"])` | The only streaming surface pueue has (250 ms local disk poll). Exits by itself when the task stops. |

`pueue log <bad-id> --json` returns `{}` with **exit 0** — an empty result is not an error and must render as "No output yet", not as a failure.

**`<TaskFollowView>`** — the `stream-view.tsx` pattern (`useRef` accumulator + `spawn` + returning the cancel fn from `useEffect`) with four additions the reference doesn't need:

```tsx
const MAX_BUFFER_CHARS = 200_000;   // a long-running task would grow this forever
const FLUSH_MS = 200;               // follow polls at 250 ms; don't render per chunk

useEffect(() => {
  acc.current = "";
  setIsLoading(true);
  const flush = setInterval(() => setMd(acc.current), FLUSH_MS);
  const cancel = follow(task.id, 200, {
    onData: (chunk) => {
      acc.current += chunk;
      if (acc.current.length > MAX_BUFFER_CHARS) {
        acc.current = "… (earlier output trimmed) …\n" +
          acc.current.slice(-MAX_BUFFER_CHARS);
      }
    },
    onDone: (code) => {
      clearInterval(flush);
      // `follow` exits when the task stops — that is success, not failure.
      // Exit 1 + "The task to be followed doesn't exist." is the bad-id case.
      setMd(acc.current + "\n\n---\n\n_task finished_");
      setIsLoading(false);
    },
    onError: (e) => { clearInterval(flush); setMd(acc.current + `\n\n> ${e.message}`); setIsLoading(false); },
  });
  return () => { clearInterval(flush); cancel(); };
}, [task.id]);
```

Actions on both log views: Copy Output, `Action.Open` on the disk log path, `Action.ShowInFinder`, Copy Log Path, `Copy "pueue follow <id>"`, Show Full Log (re-fetch unbounded), ⌘R Reload. Render as a fenced code block so ANSI-ish content and markdown characters in program output don't get interpreted:

```ts
const markdown = "```text\n" + output.replace(/```/g, "``\u200b`") + "\n```";
```

## 7. Onboarding / failure states

One descriptor, three renderers — this is the fix for the reference's duplicated `errorMarkdown()` (`define-detail.tsx` and `translation-detail.tsx` each carry a copy).

```ts
// src/lib/error-states.tsx
export interface ErrorDescriptor {
  icon: Image.ImageLike;
  title: string;
  description: string;
  markdown: string;                 // for Detail
  actions: { id: string; title: string; icon: Icon; run: () => void | Promise<void> }[];
}
export function describeError(e: unknown): ErrorDescriptor;   // SINGLE source of truth

export function ErrorEmptyView({ error }: { error: unknown });  // renders inside a <List>
export function ErrorDetail({ error }: { error: unknown });     // a full Detail
// the menu bar consumes describeError() directly (§4.6)
```

**State A — `pueue` binary not found**

- title: `Pueue CLI not found`
- description: `Install pueue, then reopen. If it lives in a non-standard location, set its path in preferences.`
- actions: `Copy "brew install pueue"` · `Copy "cargo install --locked pueue"` · `Open Extension Preferences` (`openExtensionPreferences`) · `Open Pueue Documentation` (`https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue`)
- Detail markdown additionally explains *why*: Raycast runs extensions under launchd with no shell rc, so `~/.cargo/bin` and Homebrew are not on PATH; the extension probes `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`.

**State B — daemon not running** (covers both `config-missing` and socket-unreachable; the remedy is identical)

- title: `Pueue daemon not running`
- description: `pueue is installed but pueued isn't reachable. Start the daemon and reopen.`
- actions: `Start Daemon` (conditional, below) · `Copy "brew services start pueue"` · `Copy "pueued -d"` · `Open Extension Preferences` · `Retry`
- Detail markdown includes the cleaned stderr verbatim in a fenced block — the two messages are genuinely diagnostic (`Couldn't find a configuration file. Did you start the daemon yet?` means pueued has *never* run; `I/O error at path "…/pueue_<user>.socket" while connecting to daemon` means it ran and stopped).

**One-click "Start Daemon" — conditional, and here's why.**

Offer it **only** when the daemon is Homebrew/launchd-managed: `resolveBrew()` finds a brew binary **and** `~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.pueue.plist` exists. Then run `brew services start pueue`, toast, and revalidate after ~1.5 s.

Otherwise **copy-only**, with this note in the Detail:

> Starting `pueued -d` from Raycast would make the daemon a child of Raycast's launchd process, so **every task it later runs would inherit Raycast's minimal environment** — no `~/.zshrc`, a bare `PATH`. Start the daemon from a terminal or via `brew services` so your tasks get a usable environment.

This is a real hazard, not hypothetical: it's the same launchd-PATH problem as the extension's own binary resolution, except it silently poisons every future task instead of failing loudly once. Guessing `pueued -d` also risks a second daemon racing a launchd-managed one.

`showFailureToast(error, { title: … })` from `@raycast/utils` is the default for transient failures; the full-screen states are reserved for the two structural ones.

## 8. Store-readiness checklist

- [ ] `assets/extension-icon.png` — **512×512** PNG. Keep the SVG source beside it. Add an `extension-icon@dark.png` only if the mark reads poorly on dark.
- [ ] `assets/pueue-menubar.svg` — monochrome, single-path, sized for the menu bar; always rendered with `tintColor` so it adapts to light/dark and to the state tints in §4.2.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` — first entry exactly `## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}` (literal placeholder; the store substitutes it), then a bullet per command.
- [ ] `README.md` — must cover, in order:
  1. **Requirements**: `brew install pueue` (or `cargo install --locked pueue`) — the extension shells out, it does not queue anything itself.
  2. **Start the daemon**: `brew services start pueue`, or `pueued -d`. Include the warning that a daemon started from a GUI process gives its tasks a crippled environment.
  3. **Background refresh is disabled by default for store installs.** A fresh install shows *nothing* in the menu bar until you run **Queue Menu Bar** once from root search, or enable background refresh in the command's settings. This is the single most likely "it's broken" report.
  4. Binary-path preference and the probe order, with the launchd-PATH explanation.
  5. `pueue` runs commands via `sh -c` and inherits the **daemon's** environment, not your shell's — so `$PATH`-dependent commands may need absolute paths or a `daemon.env_vars` entry in `pueue.yml`.
  6. **Notifications** section: the `daemon.callback` recipe, presented as something *you* add to *your* `pueue.yml`, with the exact YAML offered as a copy-to-clipboard action inside the extension. State explicitly: **the extension never writes to your pueue.yml.**
     ```yaml
     daemon:
       callback: 'osascript -e "display notification \"{{ command }} → {{ result }}\" with title \"Pueue #{{ id }}\""'
       callback_log_lines: 10
     ```
  7. Screenshots, commands table, preferences table.
- [ ] `metadata/pueue-1.png … pueue-5.png` — 2000×1250, captured with Raycast's built-in *Save Screenshot* (⌘⇧… in dev mode) so the chrome is right. Slots: Tasks list · Tasks with detail pane on a failed task · Add Task form · Groups · menu bar open with sections.
- [ ] `package-lock.json` committed (`npm ci` must succeed on a clean checkout).
- [ ] `raycast-env.d.ts` committed, regenerated after **every** manifest edit. Committing it means `tsc` works before the first `ray build`; the cost is remembering to regenerate. Never edit it, and never hand-write a `Preferences` interface anywhere in `src/`.
- [ ] `npm run lint` clean. Expect one required suppression: `no-control-regex` on the ANSI regex in `errors.ts`.
- [ ] `npm run build` clean.
- [ ] `LICENSE` (MIT) present and `"license": "MIT"` in the manifest.
- [ ] `"platforms": ["macOS"]` — mandatory, `menu-bar` is macOS-only.
- [ ] Store rules sanity: "✅ Calling known system binaries" is explicitly allowed. "Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads" is soft guidance, and **brew** (which ships a `menu-bar` `services-menu` at `interval: 1m`), **colima**, **orbstack**, and **yabai** are all shipping precedents for requiring a pre-installed CLI/daemon. The mitigation the reviewer will look for is graceful onboarding — which §7 is.

## 9. Risks, open questions, backlog

### Risks / open questions

1. **`confirmAlert` from a `menu-bar` command is unverified.** The design avoids it entirely (§4.4). Verify during step 6 of the build order; if it *does* work, it changes nothing — ⌥-alternates are still the better menu-bar affordance.
2. **Store review pushback** on requiring a daemon. Mitigated by precedent + onboarding. If rejected, the fallback is a private/org store or a GitHub-hosted local install.
3. **Menu-bar stale-icon upstream bugs** (#14250, #20031, #14659) are outside our control. The `Updated HH:MM` item converts an invisible bug into visible information.
4. **Large queues.** `status --json` is ~2 MB for 400 tasks, virtually all `envs`. Stripping at parse fixes retention but not the parse cost. `menuQuery` (e.g. `last 100`) is the escape hatch — but note it's client-side filtering *inside the pueue binary*, so it shrinks stdout and `JSON.parse`, not daemon traffic.
5. **Version skew.** The `TaskStatus` shape here is v4.0.4. `statusKind` returns `"unknown"` rather than throwing on an unrecognised tag, and `probe()` warns below 4.0. The reference's own pitfall applies: *don't probe capability by exit status, check the shape of the output* — a published extension faces this skew permanently.
6. **`RECONCILE_DELAY_MS = 700`** is an estimate of the daemon's update-loop latency, not a measured constant. Verify with a real task during step 5; if the optimistic state flickers, raise it or add a short revalidate poll (3 tries at 300/700/1500 ms, stopping on first change).
7. **Node version.** Raycast's runtime is bundled Node 22 while this shell has 24.13.1 via mise. `@types/node: ^22` enforces the floor; don't reach for Node 23+ APIs.
8. **Dev-loop trap** (verbatim from the reference's pitfalls): a terminal inherits your full PATH and will happily find `pueue`, masking the launchd-PATH bug entirely. **Every PATH-related test must be run from Raycast**, not from `npm run dev`'s terminal output.

## 10. Build order

Each step is one commit and independently verifiable. `just` and `rsync` are on this host; `ray` ships inside `@raycast/api`, so every recipe self-bootstraps with `([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) &&` (the reference's convention).

| # | Step | Verify |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Scaffold.** `package.json` from §2, `tsconfig.json` copied verbatim from the reference, `eslint.config.js`, `.gitignore`, `LICENSE`, placeholder `assets/extension-icon.png`, empty `src/tasks.tsx` returning `<List/>`. `npm install`, commit the lockfile. | `npm run build` succeeds and writes `raycast-env.d.ts` containing `Preferences.Tasks` / `Arguments.Tasks`. `npm run lint` clean. |
| 2 | **`src/lib/pueue/types.ts` + `normalize.ts`.** Pure, no I/O. Add a `src/lib/__fixtures__/state.json` with one task per `TaskStatus` variant *including a `Locked` wrapping a `Done{Failed:127}`*, and a temporary `src/dev-check.ts` that asserts every normalizer. | `npx tsc --noEmit`. Run the assertions with `npx tsx src/dev-check.ts` (dev-only; delete before step 14). Specifically confirm: `enqueue_at: null` → `undefined` not 1970; `Locked` unwraps to `"done"`; `{Failed: 127}` → `exitCode 127`. |
| 3 | **`errors.ts` + `binary.ts`.** Feed `cleanStderr` the three verbatim stderr samples captured in §0. | Assert `cleanStderr` on the eyre sample yields `Failed to read configuration.\nI/O error at path …` with no `\u001b`, no `Location:`, no `Backtrace`. Assert `classify` maps all five samples correctly. `resolvePueue()` returns `/usr/local/bin/pueue` on this host. |
| 4 | **`transport.ts` + `cli-transport.ts` + `index.ts`.** Reads only (`readState`, `readGroups`, `readLogs`, `probe`); `mutate` throws `not implemented`. | From a terminal: a temporary `src/dev-check.ts` that calls `status()` and prints the task count — confirms parsing against the live daemon. Confirm `readGroups()` returns `{default: {...}}` and does **not** go through the State parser. |
| 5 | **Tasks view, read-only.** Sections by status, group dropdown, keywords search, detail pane, `query` argument. No actions but Copy and Reload. | `npm run dev`, then open **from Raycast root search** (not the terminal). Queue a few real tasks by hand in a terminal (`pueue add 'sleep 30'`, `pueue add 'false'`) and confirm each renders with the right icon, duration, and exit code. |
| 6 | **Mutations.** `argvFor` for all 15 variants, `optimistic.ts`, the `act()` helper with `shouldRevalidateAfter: false` + delayed reconcile. Wire Kill / Start / Stash / Enqueue / Restart / Remove / Clean into Tasks. | Manual from Raycast: kill a `sleep 30` and watch the row flip **immediately** and *stay* flipped. If it flickers back, `RECONCILE_DELAY_MS` is too low — that's the whole point of this step. Also confirm `remove` on a running task surfaces pueue's refusal as a readable toast, not a crash. |
| 7 | **`error-states.tsx`** + wiring into Tasks. | Test binary-missing by setting the `pueuePath` preference to `/nope`. Test daemon-down with `brew services stop pueue` — **and then restart it**. Confirm both render the actionable view, not a raw stack. |
| 8 | **Log views** — `task-log.tsx` (CLI + disk fallback) and `task-follow.tsx` (spawn + throttled flush + buffer cap). | `pueue add 'for i in $(seq 1 200); do echo line $i; sleep 0.2; done'`, follow it from Raycast, confirm live updates and that the view settles to `_task finished_` on its own. Confirm the disk path resolves to `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/task_logs/<id>.log`. |
| 9 | **Add Task form** + `quick-add`. | Submit a task with a working directory, group, label, priority, a dependency, and each `startMode`; verify against `pueue status` in a terminal. Test a command containing `&&`, quotes, and `$HOME` — confirm it isn't double-escaped. Test Quick Add from root search with an argument. |
| 10 | **Groups view.** | Add a group, set parallelism to 3, pause, resume, remove — cross-check each against `pueue group --json` in a terminal. Confirm the remove confirmation names the task-move behaviour. |
| 11 | **Menu-bar command.** Icon SVG, title modes, sections, caps, `Updated HH:MM`, error states, `updateCommandMetadata`. | Open it from Raycast once to register it. Verify the icon appears, `title` hides at zero running, an action fires and HUDs, and the item refreshes ~1 min later on its own. Stop the daemon and confirm the red error menu (not a disappearing icon). **Also: quit and relaunch Raycast** and confirm the restored item shows a plausible `Updated` time. |
| 12 | **Cross-command refresh.** `launchCommand(queue-menu, Background)` after Add / mutations; `launchCommand(tasks, context:{group})` from Groups and the menu bar. | Add a task from Quick Add; confirm the menu-bar count bumps within a couple of seconds rather than up to a minute. |
| 13 | **Docs + knowledge harness.** README, CHANGELOG, `docs/pueue-json-contract.md`, the five `pitfalls/` entries (each titled by *symptom* with a grep-able verbatim-error section), `TODO.md` seeded from §9, `backlog/socket-transport.md`, `Justfile`. | `just --list` shows the recipes; each runs from a clean `node_modules`-less checkout. |
| 14 | **Store polish.** Real 512×512 icon, five `metadata/` screenshots, delete `dev-check.ts` and the fixtures if unused, final lint/build, regenerate `raycast-env.d.ts`. | `npm run lint && npm run build` both clean. `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && npm run build` succeeds (proves the committed lockfile). **Do not run `npm run publish`** — publishing stays deferred per the brief. |

Proposed `Justfile`:

```make
default:
    @just --list

# run in Raycast dev mode (registers the extension; persists after you stop)
dev:
    ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run dev

# typecheck + bundle (regenerates raycast-env.d.ts; does NOT install into Raycast)
build:
    ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run build

lint:
    ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run lint

fix:
    ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run fix-lint

# lint + build, the pre-commit gate
check: lint build

# prove the committed lockfile still works from scratch
ci:
    rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build

# seed a local queue to exercise every status variant (needs a running daemon)
fixtures:
    pueue add 'sleep 120'
    pueue add -s 'echo stashed'
    pueue add 'false'
    pueue add 'echo ok'
    pueue status
```

**Testing note to carry into `pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-pueue-not-found.md`:** a terminal inherits your full PATH and will find `pueue` by bare name, so the launchd-PATH bug is invisible from `npm run dev`'s console. Every step above marked "from Raycast" must be exercised through Raycast root search or the menu bar, with the extension's own `resolvePueue()` doing the work.

# Pueue Raycast Extension — Implementation Plan

## 0. Corrections to the brief (verified on this machine)

These change the design, so they come first.

| # | Premise | Verified reality |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "`--color never` and `NO_COLOR=1` do NOT suppress ANSI" | **True, and worse**: `--color` is a *global* option. `pueue status --color never --json` exits **2** with a clap error (`error: unexpected argument '--color' found`). It must go **before** the subcommand: `pueue --color never status --json`. |
| 2 | "Exit codes are 0/1 only" | **False.** clap argument errors exit **2**. A third error shape exists and must be handled, or a flag typo surfaces as a confusing "command failed". |
| 3 | Query DSL `columns=[...]` | **Brackets are grammar meta-notation, not literal.** `columns=[id]` → `Failed to parse query … expected column`. The working form is `columns=id,status`. (Irrelevant for `--json` anyway — column selection does not trim the JSON.) |

304	Notes on choices:
305	- `@types/node` pinned to **`^22`** on purpose. Raycast's runtime is bundled Node 22 even though `node -v` in this shell is 24.13.1 — typing against 24 lets you write APIs that throw at runtime.
306	- No `interval` preference (§0 #4).
307	- No `subtitle` on commands — the extension is already titled "Pueue"; a `"Pueue"` subtitle on every row is pure noise here (brew needs it because "Search" alone is ambiguous).
308	- `tasks` takes a `query` **text argument**, not a dropdown: it's the escape hatch to the server-side DSL from root search, and the DSL values are unbounded.
309	- `quick-add`'s `label` argument is optional; the group and cwd come from `LocalStorage` written by the Add Task form.
310	- **Never hand-write a `Preferences` interface.** `ray build` generates `Preferences.Tasks`, `Preferences.QueueMenu`, `Arguments.Tasks`, etc. with required fields — so a code default that drifts from the manifest becomes a compile error. The reference's `lib/translate.ts` violates this with its local `interface Prefs`; do not copy that.

314	## 3. `src/lib/pueue/` — the transport seam
315	
316	### 3.1 Why a directory, not one file
317	
318	`translate.ts` is 612 lines and already at the edge. Pueue has ~15 mutations, 3 reads, a streaming surface, a 6-variant recursive enum, and a 4-way error taxonomy. More importantly, **the seam has to be a file boundary to be swappable**: `cli-transport.ts` is the only file a future CBOR socket transport replaces.

320	### 3.2 `types.ts` — the wire (1:1 with `pueue_lib` v4.0.4 serde)
321	
322	```ts
323	/** Externally tagged, and it mixes bare strings with single-field objects. */
324	export type TaskResult =
325	  | "Success"
326	  | "Killed"
327	  | "Errored"
328	  | "DependencyFailed"
329	  | { Failed: number }          // exit code
330	  | { FailedToSpawn: string };  // spawn error message
331	
332	/**
333	 * Externally tagged, recursive through `Locked`. There is NO flat
334	 * `"status": "Running"` string anywhere in a Task.
335	 *
336	 * NOTE the one-letter split: Stashed carries `enqueue_at` (when it WILL be
337	 * enqueued, nullable); every other variant carries `enqueued_at` (when it WAS).
338	 */
339	export type TaskStatus =
340	  | { Stashed: { enqueue_at: string | null } }
341	  | { Queued: { enqueued_at: string } }
342	  | { Running: { enqueued_at: string; start: string } }
343	  | { Paused: { enqueued_at: string; start: string } }
344	  | { Locked: { previous_status: TaskStatus } }
345	  | {
346	      Done: {
347	        enqueued_at: string;
348	        start: string;
349	        end: string;
350	        result: TaskResult;
351	      };
352	    };
353	
354	/** Exactly what `status --json` puts in `tasks["<id>"]`. */
355	export interface RawTask {
356	  id: number;
357	  created_at: string;
358	  original_command: string;
359	  command: string;
360	  path: string;
361	  /** A full snapshot of the submitting shell's environment. May contain secrets. */
362	  envs: Record<string, string>;
363	  group: string;
364	  dependencies: number[];
365	  priority: number;
366	  label: string | null;
367	  status: TaskStatus;
368	}
369	
370	/**
371	 * The app-facing task. `envs` is DROPPED at the parse boundary and never
372	 * reaches a component, a cache, or disk. See stripEnvs() for why.
373	 */
374	export type Task = Omit<RawTask, "envs">;
375	
376	export type GroupStatus = "Running" | "Paused" | "Reset";
377	export interface Group {
378	  status: GroupStatus;
379	  parallel_tasks: number;
380	}
381	
382	/** `status --json` top level. */
383	export interface State {
384	  tasks: Record<string, Task>;
385	  groups: Record<string, Group>;
386	}
387	
388	/**
389	 * `group --json` returns the INNER map only — `{"default": {...}}`, NOT
390	 * `{"groups": {...}}`. Different top-level shape from `status --json`.
391	 * Feeding one parser to both is the single easiest bug in this codebase.
392	 */
393	export type GroupMap = Record<string, Group>;
394	
395	/** `log --json` → `{"<id>": {task, output}}`. `task.envs` is blanked to {} here. */
396	export interface LogEntry {
397	  task: Task;
398	  output: string;
399	}
400	export type LogMap = Record<string, LogEntry>;
401	
402	/** Timestamped read, so the UI can say how stale it is. */
403	export interface Snapshot {
404	  state: State;
405	  fetchedAt: number;
406	}
407	```
408	
409	**Why `envs` is stripped at parse:**
410	1. `useCachedPromise` persists its result to the disk-backed `Cache`. Caching `envs` writes every secret in the submitting shell's environment to Raycast's cache directory in plaintext.
411	2. Upstream cites ~2 MB of state for 400 tasks, virtually all of it `envs`. The menu-bar command re-parses this every 60 s.
412	3. Nothing in the v1 UI needs it.
413	
414	Explicit opt-in accessor for the one place it matters (a "Show Environment" action in the task detail), uncached:
415	
416	```ts
417	/** Uncached, on-demand. Never call this from a render path. */
418	export async function taskEnvs(id: number): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
419	```

421	### 3.3 `normalize.ts` — flatten the enums (pure, no I/O, unit-testable)
422	
423	```ts
424	import type { Task, TaskStatus, TaskResult } from "./types";
425	
426	export type StatusKind =
427	  | "stashed" | "queued" | "running" | "paused" | "locked" | "done"
428	  | "unknown"; // a future pueue variant must degrade, not throw
429	
430	export type ResultKind =
431	  | "success" | "failed" | "failed-to-spawn" | "killed" | "errored"
432	  | "dependency-failed" | "unknown";
433	
434	const KINDS: Record<string, StatusKind> = {
435	  Stashed: "stashed", Queued: "queued", Running: "running",
436	  Paused: "paused", Locked: "locked", Done: "done",
437	};
438	
439	export function statusKind(s: TaskStatus): StatusKind {
440	  const tag = Object.keys(s)[0];
441	  return KINDS[tag] ?? "unknown";
442	}
443	
444	/** Locked wraps the status the task will return to. Unwrap it recursively. */
445	export function unwrapLocked(s: TaskStatus): TaskStatus {
446	  return "Locked" in s ? unwrapLocked(s.Locked.previous_status) : s;
447	}
448	
449	/** The kind a Locked task will resume as — what to show as a secondary badge. */
450	export function underlyingKind(s: TaskStatus): StatusKind {
451	  return statusKind(unwrapLocked(s));
452	}
453	
454	export function taskResult(s: TaskStatus): TaskResult | undefined {
455	  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
456	  return "Done" in u ? u.Done.result : undefined;
457	}
458	
459	export function resultKind(r: TaskResult | undefined): ResultKind | undefined {
460	  if (r === undefined) return undefined;
461	  if (typeof r === "string") {
462	    switch (r) {
463	      case "Success": return "success";
464	      case "Killed": return "killed";
465	      case "Errored": return "errored";
466	      case "DependencyFailed": return "dependency-failed";
467	      default: return "unknown";
468	    }
469	  }
470	  if ("Failed" in r) return "failed";
471	  if ("FailedToSpawn" in r) return "failed-to-spawn";
472	  return "unknown";
473	}
474	
475	/** The process exit code, only for `{ Failed: n }`. Success has none on the wire. */
476	export function exitCode(r: TaskResult | undefined): number | undefined {
477	  return r && typeof r === "object" && "Failed" in r ? r.Failed : undefined;
478	}
479	
480	export const isDone = (t: Task) => underlyingKind(t.status) === "done";
481	export const isRunning = (t: Task) => underlyingKind(t.status) === "running";
482	export const isSuccess = (t: Task) => resultKind(taskResult(t.status)) === "success";
483	/** Anything that finished without Success — including Killed and DependencyFailed. */
484	export function isFailed(t: Task): boolean {
485	  const k = resultKind(taskResult(t.status));
486	  return k !== undefined && k !== "success";
487	}
488	/** Not finished: the queue still owes you something. */
489	export const isActive = (t: Task) =>
490	  !isDone(t) && underlyingKind(t.status) !== "stashed";
491	
492	/* ---- timestamps -------------------------------------------------------- */
493	
494	/**
495	 * Guarded parse. `new Date(null)` returns 1970-01-01, NOT Invalid Date, so a
496	 * Stashed task with `enqueue_at: null` would render as 1970 without this.
497	 * Chrono emits RFC3339 with microseconds and a numeric offset
498	 * ("2026-04-27T11:01:06.893055+08:00") — never Z, never epoch. V8 parses the
499	 * extra fractional digits and truncates to ms; verified.
500	 */
501	export function parseTs(s: string | null | undefined): Date | undefined {
502	  if (!s) return undefined;
503	  const d = new Date(s);
504	  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? undefined : d;
505	}
506	
507	/** Handles the enqueue_at / enqueued_at split. Stashed may legitimately be undefined. */
508	export function enqueuedAt(s: TaskStatus): Date | undefined {
509	  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
510	  if ("Stashed" in u) return parseTs(u.Stashed.enqueue_at);
511	  if ("Queued" in u) return parseTs(u.Queued.enqueued_at);
512	  if ("Running" in u) return parseTs(u.Running.enqueued_at);
513	  if ("Paused" in u) return parseTs(u.Paused.enqueued_at);
514	  if ("Done" in u) return parseTs(u.Done.enqueued_at);
515	  return undefined;
516	}
517	
518	export function startedAt(s: TaskStatus): Date | undefined {
519	  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
520	  if ("Running" in u) return parseTs(u.Running.start);
521	  if ("Paused" in u) return parseTs(u.Paused.start);
522	  if ("Done" in u) return parseTs(u.Done.start);
523	  return undefined;
524	}
525	
526	export function endedAt(s: TaskStatus): Date | undefined {
527	  const u = unwrapLocked(s);
528	  return "Done" in u ? parseTs(u.Done.end) : undefined;
529	}
530	
531	/** Wall-clock runtime: end−start for finished tasks, now−start for live ones. */
532	export function durationMs(t: Task, now = Date.now()): number | undefined {
533	  const start = startedAt(t.status);
534	  if (!start) return undefined;
535	  const end = endedAt(t.status);
536	  return (end ? end.getTime() : now) - start.getTime();
537	}
538	
539	/** A short human label: "running", "failed (127)", "killed", "success". */
540	export function statusLabel(t: Task): string;
541	/** The token typed into the search bar to find this task — feeds List.Item keywords. */
542	export function statusKeywords(t: Task): string[];
543	```

561	### 3.4 `errors.ts` — taxonomy + stderr normalizer
562	
563	```ts
564	export type PueueErrorKind =
565	  | "binary-not-found"    // resolvePueue() failed, or spawn ENOENT
566	  | "config-missing"      // pueue has never run: no pueue.yml
567	  | "daemon-not-running"  // config present, socket gone or refused
568	  | "bad-query"           // the DSL string didn't parse
569	  | "bad-arguments"       // clap, exit 2 — an extension bug, surface verbatim
570	  | "timeout"
571	  | "command-failed";     // anything else
572	
573	export class PueueError extends Error {
574	  readonly kind: PueueErrorKind;
575	  /** ANSI-stripped, eyre-noise-stripped, ready to render. */
576	  readonly detail: string;
577	  readonly exitCode: number | null;
578	  readonly argv: readonly string[];
579	}
580	
581	export const isBinaryMissing = (e: unknown) =>
582	  e instanceof PueueError && e.kind === "binary-not-found";
583	/** True for both "never configured" and "socket unreachable" — both mean "start it". */
584	export const isDaemonDown = (e: unknown) =>
585	  e instanceof PueueError &&
586	  (e.kind === "daemon-not-running" || e.kind === "config-missing");
587	```
588	
589	The normalizer, driven by the three verified shapes:
590	
591	```ts
592	// eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex -- color_eyre emits raw SGR even when stderr is a pipe
593	const ANSI_SGR = /\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g;
594	
595	/**
596	 * Turn pueue's stderr into one renderable message.
597	 *
598	 * color_eyre writes SGR escapes to stderr even when it is a pipe: neither
599	 * `--color never` (which is a GLOBAL flag and must precede the subcommand, or
600	 * clap exits 2) nor NO_COLOR=1 suppresses them. Verified against v4.0.4.
601	 * It then appends a "Location:" block naming a Rust source file and two
602	 * RUST_BACKTRACE hints, none of which mean anything to a Raycast user.
603	 */
604	export function cleanStderr(raw: string): string {
605	  const lines = raw.replace(ANSI_SGR, "").split("\n");
606	  const kept: string[] = [];
607	  for (const line of lines) {
608	    if (/^Location:\s*$/.test(line)) break;
609	    if (/^Backtrace omitted/.test(line)) break;
610	    if (/^Run with RUST_BACKTRACE/.test(line)) continue;
611	    kept.push(line);
612	  }
613	  return kept
614	    .join("\n")
615	    .replace(/^Error:\s*\n?/, "")
616	    // eyre numbers its cause chain "   0: " / "   1: ". Pest's own diagnostic
617	    // uses "      1 | " (pipe, not colon), so this leaves it intact.
618	    .replace(/^\s*\d+:\s+/gm, "")
619	    .replace(/^Pueue:\s*/gm, "")
620	    .trim();
621	}
622	
623	export function classify(detail: string, exitCode: number | null): PueueErrorKind {
624	  if (/Failed to parse query/i.test(detail)) return "bad-query";
625	  if (exitCode === 2 && /^error:/im.test(detail)) return "bad-arguments";
626	  if (/Couldn't find a configuration file/i.test(detail)) return "config-missing";
627	  // The socket path ends in .socket; the config path ends in .yml. Discriminate
628	  // on the verb, which is unambiguous: "while connecting to daemon".
629	  if (/while connecting to daemon/i.test(detail)) return "daemon-not-running";
630	  if (/Did you start (it|the daemon)/i.test(detail)) return "daemon-not-running";
631	  if (/(ECONNREFUSED|ENOENT).*socket/i.test(detail)) return "daemon-not-running";
632	  return "command-failed";
633	}
634	```
635	
636	### 3.5 `binary.ts` — PATH resolution
637	
638	The #1 hazard. Raycast runs extensions under launchd with no shell rc, so bare `pueue` throws `spawn pueue ENOENT`. Modelled on brew's `paths.ts` (which I read from the installed sourcemap) plus the reference's `resolveBinary()`.
639	
640	```ts
641	const PROBE_DIRS = [
642	  "/opt/homebrew/bin",              // Apple Silicon Homebrew
643	  "/usr/local/bin",                 // Intel Homebrew — the one that exists on this host
644	  join(homedir(), ".cargo", "bin"), // cargo install pueue
645	  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
646	  "/usr/bin",
647	  "/bin",
648	];
649	
650	let cachedPueue: string | undefined;
651	
652	/**
653	 * Absolute path to the `pueue` client.
654	 * The preference is checked BEFORE the module cache on purpose: a cached probe
655	 * result must never outlive the user changing the preference mid-session.
656	 * The preference is existsSync-validated so a stale path falls through to the
657	 * probe rather than producing an ENOENT with no explanation.
658	 */
659	export function resolvePueue(): string {
660	  const { pueuePath } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
661	  if (pueuePath && existsSync(pueuePath)) return pueuePath;
662	  if (cachedPueue && existsSync(cachedPueue)) return cachedPueue;
663	  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
664	    const c = join(dir, "pueue");
665	    if (existsSync(c)) return (cachedPueue = c);
666	  }
667	  throw new PueueError("binary-not-found", "pueue CLI not found");
668	}
669	
670	/**
671	 * `pueued`, preferring the SIBLING of the resolved client — a Homebrew client
672	 * driving a cargo-built daemon is a version-skew bug waiting to happen.
673	 */
674	export function resolvePueued(): string | undefined {
675	  try {
676	    const sibling = join(dirname(resolvePueue()), "pueued");
677	    if (existsSync(sibling)) return sibling;
678	  } catch { /* fall through */ }
679	  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
680	    const c = join(dir, "pueued");
681	    if (existsSync(c)) return c;
682	  }
683	  return undefined;
684	}
685	
686	/**
687	 * Pass HOME through so pueue can find its config dir. On macOS that is
688	 * ~/Library/Application Support/pueue (NOT ~/.config/pueue), and it doubles as
689	 * the data, socket, and log dir. Deliberately NOT setting NO_COLOR: it does
690	 * nothing to color_eyre's stderr (verified), and setting it would imply it does.
691	 */
692	export function baseEnv(): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
693	  const { configPath } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
694	  return {
695	    ...process.env,
696	    HOME: process.env.HOME ?? homedir(),
697	    ...(configPath ? { PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH: configPath } : {}),
698	  };
699	}
700	
701	/**
702	 * The pueue data directory, for reading task_logs off disk.
703	 * 1. default macOS path
704	 * 2. if missing, one regex probe of pueue.yml for a non-null `pueue_directory`
705	 * 3. give up — callers fall back to `pueue log --json`
706	 * Deliberately no YAML dependency for one optional key.
707	 */
708	export function pueueDirectory(): string | undefined;
709	export function taskLogPath(id: number): string | undefined; // <dir>/task_logs/<id>.log
710	
711	/** Homebrew's brew binary, for the one-click daemon start. undefined if absent. */
712	export function resolveBrew(): string | undefined;
713	/** True when the daemon is brew-services/launchd managed on this host. */
714	export function isBrewManagedDaemon(): boolean; // ~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.pueue.plist
715	```
716	
717	### 3.6 `transport.ts` — the interface and the Mutation union
718	
719	**This is the actual seam.** If mutations are `string[]` argv, a socket transport has to parse argv back into intent. Model them as data:
720	
721	```ts
722	export type Mutation =
723	  | { op: "add"; command: string; group?: string; label?: string;
724	      priority?: number; workingDirectory?: string; after?: number[];
725	      delay?: string; stashed?: boolean; immediate?: boolean; escape?: boolean }
726	  | { op: "start";   ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean }
727	  | { op: "pause";   ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean; wait?: boolean }
728	  | { op: "kill";    ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean; signal?: string }
729	  | { op: "restart"; ids: number[]; inPlace?: boolean; stashed?: boolean; immediate?: boolean }
730	  | { op: "remove";  ids: number[] }
731	  | { op: "stash";   ids?: number[]; group?: string; delay?: string }
732	  | { op: "enqueue"; ids?: number[]; group?: string; delay?: string }
733	  | { op: "clean";   group?: string; successfulOnly?: boolean }
734	  | { op: "switch";  a: number; b: number }
735	  | { op: "parallel"; count: number; group?: string }
736	  | { op: "group-add"; name: string; parallel?: number }
737	  | { op: "group-remove"; name: string }
738	  | { op: "send"; id: number; input: string }
739	  | { op: "reset"; groups?: string[] };
740	
741	export interface StatusOptions { group?: string; query?: string; signal?: AbortSignal }
742	export interface LogOptions { lines?: number; full?: boolean; signal?: AbortSignal }
743	export interface FollowHandlers {
744	  onData(chunk: string): void;
745	  onDone(code: number | null): void;
746	  onError(e: Error): void;
747	}
748	
749	export interface PueueTransport {
750	  /** READ — `status --json`. The only call that returns tasks + groups together. */
751	  readState(o?: StatusOptions): Promise<State>;
752	  /** READ — `group --json`. DIFFERENT top-level shape; never route through readState's parser. */
753	  readGroups(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<GroupMap>;
754	  /** READ — `log --json`. Defaults to the last 15 lines; `full` can exhaust RAM. */
755	  readLogs(ids: number[], o?: LogOptions): Promise<LogMap>;
756	  /** WRITE — exit-code + prose only. Returns the new id for `add`, else void. */
757	  mutate(m: Mutation): Promise<number | void>;
758	  /** STREAM — the only push surface pueue has. Returns a cancel fn. */
759	  followLog(id: number, lines: number, h: FollowHandlers): () => void;
760	  /** Reachability + version, for onboarding and the >=4.0 guard. */
761	  probe(): Promise<{ version: string; reachable: boolean }>;
762	}
763	
764	let active: PueueTransport | undefined;
765	export function transport(): PueueTransport {
766	  return (active ??= createCliTransport()); // swap point for a future socket transport
767	}
768	```

51	    const { envs: _drop, ...lean } = t;

81	`run()` is the shared wrapper: `pexecFile` with `env: baseEnv()`, per-call `timeout`/`maxBuffer`/`signal`, and a catch that turns `err.code === "ENOENT"` into `binary-not-found` and everything else into `new PueueError(classify(cleanStderr(err.stderr), err.code), …)`.

83	`probe()` is the module-level cached lookup with the reference's swallow-and-fall-back discipline — but note the reference's own pitfall: **never probe capability by exit status alone**; parse the shape. `pueue --version` prints `pueue 4.0.4`; match `/^pueue (\d+)\.(\d+)/` and treat an unparseable result as "unknown, assume 4".

85	### 3.8 `index.ts` — the public API views actually import
86	
87	```ts
88	export * from "./types";
89	export * from "./normalize";
90	export { PueueError, isBinaryMissing, isDaemonDown, cleanStderr } from "./errors";
91	export { taskLogPath, pueueDirectory, resolveBrew, isBrewManagedDaemon } from "./binary";
92	
93	export const status  = (o?: StatusOptions) => transport().readState(o);
94	export const groups  = (s?: AbortSignal)   => transport().readGroups(s);
95	export const logs    = (ids: number[], o?: LogOptions) => transport().readLogs(ids, o);
96	export const follow  = (id: number, lines: number, h: FollowHandlers) =>
97	  transport().followLog(id, lines, h);
98	export const mutate  = (m: Mutation) => transport().mutate(m);
99	
100	/** Timestamped read for the menu bar — one cache entry holds data AND its age. */
101	export async function snapshot(o?: StatusOptions): Promise<Snapshot> {
102	  return { state: await status(o), fetchedAt: Date.now() };
103	}
104	
105	/** Read the merged stdout+stderr log straight off disk. Falls back to the CLI. */
106	export async function readLogText(id: number, maxBytes = 512 * 1024): Promise<string>;
107	
108	/** Uncached, on demand, never rendered by default. */
109	export async function taskEnvs(id: number): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
110	```

113	
114	## 4. The menu-bar command (`src/queue-menu.tsx`)
115	
116	### 4.1 Data
117	
118	```tsx
119	const { data, isLoading, revalidate, mutate: mutateState } = useCachedPromise(
120	  async (query: string): Promise<Snapshot> => snapshot({ query }),
121	  [prefs.menuQuery ?? ""],
122	  { keepPreviousData: true, failureToastOptions: { title: "Pueue" } },
123	);
124	```
125	
126	`useCachedPromise` is `Cache`-backed, so the first paint after a Raycast restart is the last successful state — no blank menu. Returning `{ state, fetchedAt }` from the fetch means **the age lives in the same cache entry as the data**; no second `Cache` mechanism, no drift between them.
127	
128	### 4.2 `title` / `icon` / `tooltip`
129	
130	```tsx
131	const running = tasks.filter(isRunning).length;
132	const queued  = tasks.filter(t => underlyingKind(t.status) === "queued").length;
133	const paused  = tasks.filter(t => underlyingKind(t.status) === "paused").length;
134	const failed  = tasks.filter(isFailed).length;
135	
136	// Hidden at zero — no badge API exists, the count IS the title, and
137	// `undefined` is what removes it (the Brew idiom).
138	const title =
139	  prefs.titleCounts === "none"           ? undefined
140	  : prefs.titleCounts === "running-queued" ? (running || queued ? `${running}/${queued}` : undefined)
141	  : prefs.titleCounts === "active"         ? (running + queued + paused || undefined) && String(running + queued + paused)
142	  : running > 0 ? String(running) : undefined;
143	```
144	
145	Order of precedence in the title: **running first**. Running is the only count that changes on its own; queued is a backlog you already know about.
146	
147	Icon — one glyph, four tints, so the shape never moves in the menu bar:
148	
149	| Condition | icon |
150	|---|---|
151	| binary missing / daemon down | `{ source: Icon.XMarkCircle, tintColor: Color.Red }` |
152	| any failed task | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.Red }` |
153	| every group paused | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.Orange }` |
154	| last fetch errored, showing cached data | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.SecondaryText }` |
155	| normal | `{ source: "pueue-menubar.svg", tintColor: Color.PrimaryText }` |
156	
157	`pueue-menubar.svg` must be a **monochrome template glyph** — a coloured asset looks wrong on a dark menu bar. `tintColor: Color.PrimaryText` is exactly what brew does.
158	
159	Tooltip: `"Pueue — 2 running, 5 queued, 1 failed"`, or `"Pueue — daemon not running"`, or `"Pueue — stale, last update 14:32"`.
160	
161	### 4.3 Structure
162	
163	```
164	<MenuBarExtra icon={…} title={…} tooltip={…} isLoading={isLoading}>
165	
166	  {/* only when errored — see 4.6 */}
167	  <Section>  Pueue daemon not running / Start Daemon / Copy … / Open Preferences </Section>
168	
169	  <Section title={`Running (${running})`}>
170	    {top(runningTasks).map(t =>
171	      <Submenu key={t.id} title={`${t.id} · ${oneline(t.command, 48)}`} icon={statusIcon(t)}>
172	        <Item title="Follow Output"  onAction={openTasksAt(t)} />
173	        <Item title="Kill"           icon={Icon.Stop}
174	              alternate={<Item title="Kill (SIGINT)" onAction={…signal:"int"} />}
175	              onAction={act({op:"kill", ids:[t.id]})} />
176	        <Item title="Copy Command"   onAction={() => Clipboard.copy(t.command)} />
177	      </Submenu>)}
178	    {more(runningTasks)}
179	  </Section>
180	
181	  <Section title={`Queued (${queued})`}>   … Start Now / Stash / Copy · ⌥ Remove </Section>
182	  <Section title={`Failed (${failed})`}>   … Show Log / Restart · ⌥ Restart in Place / Copy · ⌥ Remove </Section>
183	
184	  {prefs.showGroups && (
185	    <Section title="Groups">
186	      {groupEntries.map(([name, g]) =>
187	        <Submenu key={name} title={`${name} — ${g.status.toLowerCase()} (${runningIn(name)}/${g.parallel_tasks})`}>
188	          <Item title={g.status === "Running" ? "Pause Group" : "Resume Group"} … />
189	          <Submenu title="Parallelism">
190	            {[1,2,3,4,6,8,0].map(n =>
191	              <Item key={n} title={n === 0 ? "Unlimited" : String(n)}
192	                    icon={n === g.parallel_tasks ? Icon.Checkmark : undefined} … />)}
193	          </Submenu>
194	        </Submenu>)}
195	    </Section>)}
196	
197	  <Section>
198	    <Item title="Add Task…"  icon={Icon.Plus}          onAction={launch("add-task")} />
199	    <Item title="Open Tasks" icon={Icon.AppWindowList} onAction={launch("tasks")} />
200	    <Item title="Pause All"  icon={Icon.Pause}
201	          alternate={<Item title="Pause All (let running finish)" … wait:true />} … />
202	    <Item title="Start All"  icon={Icon.Play} … />
203	    <Item title="Clean Finished" icon={Icon.Trash}
204	          alternate={<Item title="Clean Successful Only" … />} … />   {/* ⌥-only, see 4.4 */}
205	  </Section>
206	
207	  <Section>
208	    <Item title={`Updated ${fmtClock(data.fetchedAt)}`} />   {/* no onAction → disabled label */}
209	    <Item title="Refresh" icon={Icon.ArrowClockwise} onAction={() => revalidate()} />
210	  </Section>
211	</MenuBarExtra>
212	```
213	
214	Rules honoured:
215	- **No two identical `Item`s at the same level.** Every title is prefixed with the task id, and the per-task actions live inside per-task `Submenu`s — which also keeps the top level short.
216	- **Empty submenus render disabled**, which is fine and self-documenting for an empty Groups list.
217	- `maxItemsPerSection` (default 7) with a trailing `…and N more` item that `launchCommand`s the Tasks view. A 400-task queue must not become 400 menu items on every 60 s tick.
218	- The `Updated HH:MM` disabled item is the mitigation for the restore-from-database problem (§4.5).
219	
220	### 4.4 One-click vs confirmed
221	
222	**No `confirmAlert` anywhere in the menu bar.** `confirmAlert` presents in the Raycast window, and a menu-bar command runs with the window closed — I have not verified it works there, and a silently-swallowed confirmation on a destructive action is unacceptable. Instead:
223	
224	| Action | Menu bar |
225	|---|---|
226	| Kill, Restart, Start, Pause, Stash, Enqueue, set parallelism | plain one-click + `showHUD` echo |
227	| Remove, Clean | `alternate` only (⌥) — unreachable by accident |
228	| Reset, Remove Group | **not offered at all** — Tasks/Groups view, behind `confirmAlert` |
229	
230	`showToast` falls back to `showHUD` when the window is closed, so `showFailureToast` is safe to call from a menu-bar action.
231	
232	### 4.5 `isLoading` and refresh mechanics
233	
234	Drive `isLoading` straight from `useCachedPromise` — never leave it unset (Raycast would render and immediately unload), never leave it true (the tree re-runs every tick until it goes false). `keepPreviousData: true` means the cached value paints instantly while `isLoading` is true, so there is no blank frame.
235	
236	`interval: "1m"`. Docs contradict themselves on the floor (background-refresh page says `10s`, manifest page says `1m`); `1m` is the safe value and matches the shipping Brew extension. Scheduling is jittered by macOS energy policy and the command is auto-terminated on a timeout scaled to the interval — 22–44 ms per `status --json` is nowhere near it.
237	
238	**Stale-restore mitigation.** When Raycast restarts, the menu bar item is restored from Raycast's database rather than by re-running the command, so a stale render survives until the next tick (upstream #14250, #20031, #14659). Three defences, all cheap:
239	1. The `Updated HH:MM` disabled item — makes staleness *visible* rather than misleading. This is the important one.
240	2. A `Refresh` item that `revalidate()`s.
241	3. On a failed fetch with cached data present: keep the data, tint `SecondaryText`, and set the tooltip to `Pueue — stale, last update HH:MM`.
242	
243	`updateCommandMetadata`: **yes.** Call it inside the fetch's `onData`:
244	```ts
245	updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle: down ? "Daemon not running" : `${running} running · ${queued} queued` });
246	```
247	It only affects the calling command's own root-search subtitle, so `tasks.tsx` sets its own too.
248	
249	### 4.6 Degradation
250	
251	A `MenuBarExtra` cannot render a `List.EmptyView`, and returning `null` removes the item entirely — which is the wrong answer for a user who deliberately enabled a pueue menu-bar command. Render the error state:
252	
253	```tsx
254	if (error && !data) {
255	  const d = describeError(error);          // shared descriptor, see §7
256	  return (
257	    <MenuBarExtra icon={{ source: Icon.XMarkCircle, tintColor: Color.Red }} tooltip={`Pueue — ${d.title}`}>
258	      <MenuBarExtra.Item title={d.title} />          {/* no onAction → disabled header */}
259	      <MenuBarExtra.Section>
260	        {d.actions.map(a => <MenuBarExtra.Item key={a.id} title={a.title} icon={a.icon} onAction={a.run} />)}
261	      </MenuBarExtra.Section>
262	    </MenuBarExtra>
263	  );
264	}
265	```
266	
267	Binary missing → `Copy “brew install pueue”`, `Open Extension Preferences`, `Open Pueue Documentation`.
268	Daemon down → `Start Daemon` (only when brew-managed, see §7), `Copy “brew services start pueue”`, `Copy “pueued -d”`, `Open Tasks`.

271	
272	## 5. View commands
273	
274	### 5.1 Tasks (`src/tasks.tsx`) — **v1**
275	
276	```tsx
277	const [group, setGroup] = useCachedState("tasks.group", ALL_GROUPS);
278	const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null);
279	const stateAbort = useRef<AbortController>();
280	const groupsAbort = useRef<AbortController>();   // separate refs — look-up-word.tsx pattern
281	
282	const st = useCachedPromise(
283	  (g: string, q: string) => status({ group: g === ALL_GROUPS ? undefined : g,
284	                                     query: q, signal: stateAbort.current?.signal }),
285	  [group, props.arguments?.query ?? ""],
286	  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: stateAbort },
287	);
288	
289	const gr = useCachedPromise(() => groups(groupsAbort.current?.signal), [],
290	  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: groupsAbort });
291	
292	// Log preview for the SELECTED row only — never per row.
293	const preview = usePromise(
294	  (id: string | null) => (id ? logs([Number(id)], { lines: prefs.detailLogLines }) : Promise.resolve({})),
295	  [selectedId], { execute: showDetail && selectedId !== null },
296	);
297	
298	const isLoading = st.isLoading || gr.isLoading;
299	const error = st.error ?? gr.error;
300	```
301	
302	- **Searching is client-side** via `keywords` per item (the `history.tsx` idiom): the whole state is already in memory, and the server-side DSL's `%=` only covers `command` and `label`. Keywords per row: `[String(id), command, original_command, label ?? "", group, statusKind, resultKind, path]`. The DSL stays available as the `query` **command argument**, so `Tasks` can be launched from root search with `status=failed order_by id desc first 20` — and note the DSL is applied by the pueue *client*, so it shrinks the JSON we parse, not the daemon traffic.
303	- **Group filter** is the single `searchBarAccessory` (Raycast allows only one), a `<GroupDropdown>` seeded with a static `["All Groups", "default"]` so it never paints empty, then swapped for the live map — and preserving an unknown current value as a synthetic item so a deleted group doesn't silently reset the filter. Lifted straight from `language-dropdown.tsx`.
304	- **Status filtering is by section**, not a second dropdown: `Running`, `Paused`, `Locked`, `Queued`, `Stashed`, `Failed`, `Done`. Sections give grouping for free and the search bar filters across all of them; typing "failed" narrows via keywords.
305	- **Detail pane**: `isShowingDetail` from `useCachedState("tasks.showDetail", prefs.showDetail)`, toggled by ⌘⇧D. `List.Item.Detail` with `metadata` (id, status, result + exit code, group, label, priority, path, dependencies, created / enqueued / started / ended, duration) and `markdown` = a fenced block of the last N log lines from `preview`.
306	
307	Actions (ordering matters — the first is ⏎):
308	
309	| Shortcut | Action | Notes |
310	|---|---|---|
311	| ⏎ | Show Log | `Action.Push` → `<TaskLogView>` |
312	| ⌘⏎ | Follow Output | `Action.Push` → `<TaskFollowView>`, only when running |
313	| ⌘⇧D | Toggle Detail | |
314	| ⌘R | Restart | ⌥ alternate: Restart in Place (overwrites logs — say so in the title) |
315	| ⌘K | Kill | `confirmAlert` + `rememberUserChoice`, `Alert.ActionStyle.Destructive` |
316	| ⌘E | Enqueue / ⌘S Stash | rendered conditionally on `statusKind` |
317	| ⌘⌫ | Remove | `confirmAlert`; disabled with an explanatory toast for running/paused tasks — `pueue remove` refuses them and you must kill first |
318	| ⌘C / ⌘⇧C | Copy Command / Copy Task ID | |
319	| ⌘O | Open Working Directory | `Action.ShowInFinder path={t.path}` |
320	| ⌘N | Add Task | `Action.Push` → the Add form |
321	| ⌘⇧R | Reload | |
322	
323	**Refresh after a mutation — the load-bearing detail.** The daemon processes requests asynchronously on its own update loop, so a state change may not be visible in the very next `status` call. `mutate`'s default `shouldRevalidateAfter: true` fires *immediately* after the promise resolves, reads pre-change state, and **visually undoes your optimistic update**. So:
324	
325	```ts
326	/**
327	 * The daemon acknowledges a request before its update loop has applied it, so
328	 * the very next `status --json` can still show the old state. Revalidating
329	 * immediately (mutate's default) would therefore roll the optimistic update
330	 * back on screen and then flip it forward again a minute later. Suppress the
331	 * automatic revalidate and schedule one after the loop has had a turn.
332	 */
333	const RECONCILE_DELAY_MS = 700;
334	
335	async function act(m: Mutation, opts: { verb: string }) {
336	  const toast = await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Animated, title: opts.verb });
337	  try {
338	    await st.mutate(mutate(m), {
339	      optimisticUpdate: (s) => applyMutation(s, m),   // pure, src/lib/optimistic.ts
340	      rollbackOnError: true,
341	      shouldRevalidateAfter: false,
342	    });
343	    toast.style = Toast.Style.Success;
344	    toast.title = `${opts.verb} — done`;
345	    setTimeout(() => st.revalidate(), RECONCILE_DELAY_MS);
346	  } catch (e) {
347	    await showFailureToast(e, { title: opts.verb });
348	  }
349	}
350	```
351	
352	`src/lib/optimistic.ts` is pure and unit-testable:
353	
354	```ts
355	/** Expected post-mutation State, for the optimistic paint. Never sent anywhere. */
356	export function applyMutation(s: State | undefined, m: Mutation): State {
357	  // kill    → Running/Paused ids become Done + Killed
358	  // start   → Queued/Stashed ids become Running; group.status = "Running"
359	  // pause   → Running ids become Paused;         group.status = "Paused"
360	  // stash   → Queued ids become Stashed(enqueue_at: null)
361	  // enqueue → Stashed ids become Queued(enqueued_at: now)
362	  // remove  → delete the ids
363	  // clean   → delete every Done task (successfulOnly → only Success)
364	  // parallel→ groups[name].parallel_tasks = count
365	  // add     → cannot be predicted (the id comes back from the CLI) → return s
366	}
367	```
368	
369	Loading / empty / error:
370	- `isLoading` from the merged hooks.
371	- Empty: `<List.EmptyView icon={Icon.Tray} title="No tasks" description="Nothing queued. ⌘N adds one." />` with an Add action.
372	- Error: `isBinaryMissing(e)` → `<PueueNotFoundView/>`; `isDaemonDown(e)` → `<DaemonDownView/>`; `kind === "bad-query"` → a dedicated empty view echoing `cleanStderr` and the DSL grammar; else generic. **All rendered inside a `<List>`** — `List.EmptyView` is not standalone (the reference's `binary-not-found.tsx` has this constraint baked in).
373	
374	### 5.2 Add Task (`src/add-task.tsx`) — **v1**
375	
376	`Form` + `useForm`, `enableDrafts: true` so a half-typed pipeline survives a dismissal.
377	
378	| Field | Component | Notes |
379	|---|---|---|
380	| `command` | `Form.TextArea`, required, autoFocus | Multi-line so a long pipeline fits. `info`: "Run by the daemon via `sh -c`. `&&`, `\|`, and `>` work. A trailing `&` detaches the process and the task finishes instantly." |
381	| `workingDirectory` | `Form.FilePicker` `canChooseDirectories canChooseFiles={false} allowMultipleSelection={false}` | Default from `LocalStorage("add.cwd")`, else `homedir()` |
382	| `group` | `Form.Dropdown` | Live from `groups()`, static `default` fallback so it never paints empty |
383	| `label` | `Form.TextField` | |
384	| `priority` | `Form.TextField` | `validation: (v) => v && !/^-?\d+$/.test(v) ? "Must be an integer" : undefined` |
385	| `dependencies` | `Form.TagPicker` | Options = current queued/stashed/running tasks, `title={`${id} · ${oneline(command)}`}`, `value={String(id)}`. Far better than a free-text id list. |
386	| `delay` | `Form.TextField` | `info`: "Seconds, or a date expression: `2h`, `18:30`, `2026-08-01T18:30:00`" |
387	| `startMode` | `Form.Dropdown`: Queued (default) / Stashed / Start immediately | **Collapses the mutually-exclusive `-s`/`-i` pair into one control.** Two checkboxes would let a user tick both. |
388	| `escape` | `Form.Checkbox`, default false | `info`: "Escapes shell metacharacters — this disables `&&`, `\|`, `>`" |
389	
390	Submit → `mutate({op:"add", …})` → returns the new id from `--print-task-id`. Then:
391	```ts
392	await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Success, title: `Queued task ${id}`,
393	  primaryAction: { title: "Open Tasks", onAction: () => launchCommand({ name: "tasks", type: LaunchType.UserInitiated }) } });
394	await LocalStorage.setItem("add.cwd", values.workingDirectory[0]);
395	await LocalStorage.setItem("add.group", values.group);
396	popToRoot();
397	// Force the menu bar to catch up rather than waiting up to a minute.
398	launchCommand({ name: "queue-menu", type: LaunchType.Background }).catch(() => {});
399	```
400	That last line is the documented use of `launchCommand` — forcing a background refresh of a sibling command. It resolves when launched, not when the target finishes, so it must not be awaited for correctness.
401	
402	**Escaping discipline**: `pueue add` takes `<COMMAND>...` variadic and joins with spaces; pass the whole command as **one argv element after `--`** via `execFile`. Never build a shell string, never `shell: true`. The user's text is already a shell command line — pueue runs it under `sh -c` itself.
403	
404	When Add Task is pushed from Tasks (⌘N), thread an `onAdded` callback into it and call `revalidate()` — the `onRecorded → revalidate()` pattern from `look-up-word.tsx`, which lands while the pushed view is still open so the list is already fresh when it pops.
405	
406	### 5.3 Groups (`src/groups.tsx`) — **v1**
407	
408	Two `useCachedPromise`s with separate abort refs (`groups()` for authority on `status`/`parallel_tasks`, `status()` for per-group task counts), merged `isLoading`/`error`.
409	
410	Row: `title={name}`, `accessories=[{ tag: {value: g.status, color: …} }, { text: `${runningIn(name)}/${g.parallel_tasks || "∞"}` }, { text: `${queuedIn(name)} queued` }]`.
411	
412	Actions:
413	| Shortcut | Action | Copy that matters |
414	|---|---|---|
415	| ⏎ | Show Tasks in Group | `launchCommand({name:"tasks", context:{group}})` |
416	| ⌘P / ⌘S | Pause / Resume Group | ⌥ alternate on Pause: "Pause (let running tasks finish)"

21	## 6. Log viewing — one source per situation
22	
23	| Situation | Source | Why |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| Detail-pane preview for the **selected** row | `pueue log <id> --json --lines 20` | One call returns task + output together; bounded; `envs` already blanked by pueue in this path. Never fetch per row — only on `onSelectionChange`. |
26	| Full log page for a **finished** task | Read `<pueue_dir>/task_logs/<id>.log` off disk, tailing the last 512 KB | `client.read_local_logs: true` here. Skips the JSON string-escape round trip, skips the `--full` RAM warning, and lets us tail instead of loading everything. Falls back to `pueue log <id> --json --lines 2000` when the file is absent (remote daemon, `read_local_logs: false`, or a non-default `pueue_directory` we couldn't resolve). |
27	| Live tail of a **running** task | `spawn(pueue, ["follow", id, "--lines", "200"])` | The only streaming surface pueue has (250 ms local disk poll). Exits by itself when the task stops. |
28	
29	`pueue log <bad-id> --json` returns `{}` with **exit 0** — an empty result is not an error and must render as "No output yet", not as a failure.
30	
31	**`<TaskFollowView>`** — the `stream-view.tsx` pattern (`useRef` accumulator + `spawn` + returning the cancel fn from `useEffect`) with four additions the reference doesn't need:
32	
33	```tsx
34	const MAX_BUFFER_CHARS = 200_000;   // a long-running task would grow this forever
35	const FLUSH_MS = 200;               // follow polls at 250 ms; don't render per chunk
36	
37	useEffect(() => {
38	  acc.current = "";
39	  setIsLoading(true);
40	  const flush = setInterval(() => setMd(acc.current), FLUSH_MS);
41	  const cancel = follow(task.id, 200, {
42	    onData: (chunk) => {
43	      acc.current += chunk;
44	      if (acc.current.length > MAX_BUFFER_CHARS) {
45	        acc.current = "… (earlier output trimmed) …\n" +
46	          acc.current.slice(-MAX_BUFFER_CHARS);
47	      }
48	    },
49	    onDone: (code) => {
50	      clearInterval(flush);
51	      // `follow` exits when the task stops — that is success, not failure.
52	      // Exit 1 + "The task to be followed doesn't exist." is the bad-id case.
53	      setMd(acc.current + "\n\n---\n\n_task finished_");
54	      setIsLoading(false);
55	    },
56	    onError: (e) => { clearInterval(flush); setMd(acc.current + `\n\n> ${e.message}`); setIsLoading(false); },
57	  });
58	  return () => { clearInterval(flush); cancel(); };
59	}, [task.id]);
60	```
61	
62	Actions on both log views: Copy Output, `Action.Open` on the disk log path, `Action.ShowInFinder`, Copy Log Path, `Copy "pueue follow <id>"`, Show Full Log (re-fetch unbounded), ⌘R Reload. Render as a fenced code block so ANSI-ish content and markdown characters in program output don't get interpreted:
63	
64	```ts
65	const markdown = "```text\n" + output.replace(/```/g, "``\u200b`") + "\n```";
66	```

70	## 7. Onboarding / failure states
71	
72	One descriptor, three renderers — this is the fix for the reference's duplicated `errorMarkdown()` (`define-detail.tsx` and `translation-detail.tsx` each carry a copy).
73	
74	```ts
75	// src/lib/error-states.tsx
76	export interface ErrorDescriptor {
77	  icon: Image.ImageLike;
78	  title: string;
79	  description: string;
80	  markdown: string;                 // for Detail
81	  actions: { id: string; title: string; icon: Icon; run: () => void | Promise<void> }[];
82	}
83	export function describeError(e: unknown): ErrorDescriptor;   // SINGLE source of truth
84	
85	export function ErrorEmptyView({ error }: { error: unknown });  // renders inside a <List>
86	export function ErrorDetail({ error }: { error: unknown });     // a full Detail
87	// the menu bar consumes describeError() directly (§4.6)
88	```
89	
90	**State A — `pueue` binary not found**
91	
92	- title: `Pueue CLI not found`
93	- description: `Install pueue, then reopen. If it lives in a non-standard location, set its path in preferences.`
94	- actions: `Copy "brew install pueue"` · `Copy "cargo install --locked pueue"` · `Open Extension Preferences` (`openExtensionPreferences`) · `Open Pueue Documentation` (`https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue`)
95	- Detail markdown additionally explains *why*: Raycast runs extensions under launchd with no shell rc, so `~/.cargo/bin` and Homebrew are not on PATH; the extension probes `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`.
96	
97	**State B — daemon not running** (covers both `config-missing` and socket-unreachable; the remedy is identical)
98	
99	- title: `Pueue daemon not running`
100	- description: `pueue is installed but pueued isn't reachable. Start the daemon and reopen.`
101	- actions: `Start Daemon` (conditional, below) · `Copy "brew services start pueue"` · `Copy "pueued -d"` · `Open Extension Preferences` · `Retry`
102	- Detail markdown includes the cleaned stderr verbatim in a fenced block — the two messages are genuinely diagnostic (`Couldn't find a configuration file. Did you start the daemon yet?` means pueued has *never* run; `I/O error at path "…/pueue_<user>.socket" while connecting to daemon` means it ran and stopped).
103	
104	**One-click "Start Daemon" — conditional, and here's why.**
105	
106	Offer it **only** when the daemon is Homebrew/launchd-managed: `resolveBrew()` finds a brew binary **and** `~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.pueue.plist` exists. Then run `brew services start pueue`, toast, and revalidate after ~1.5 s.
107	
108	Otherwise **copy-only**, with this note in the Detail:
109	
110	> Starting `pueued -d` from Raycast would make the daemon a child of Raycast's launchd process, so **every task it later runs would inherit Raycast's minimal environment** — no `~/.zshrc`, a bare `PATH`. Start the daemon from a terminal or via `brew services` so your tasks get a usable environment.
111	
112	This is a real hazard, not hypothetical: it's the same launchd-PATH problem as the extension's own binary resolution, except it silently poisons every future task instead of failing loudly once. Guessing `pueued -d` also risks a second daemon racing a launchd-managed one.
113	
114	`showFailureToast(error, { title: … })` from `@raycast/utils` is the default for transient failures; the full-screen states are reserved for the two structural ones.
